title: one identity ladder: three resolvers disagree on the order
description: Audit S1 (docs/analysis/stack-audit-2026-10-21.md section 2). The canonical order (AGENTS.md, flywheel skill rule 'Identity is one ladder') is explicit -> TORON_AGENT -> FLYWHEEL_MAIL_AS -> AGENT_NAME -> config [agent_mail].name. Three implementations disagree: toron crates/toron-cli/src/robot.rs:2038 guard_agent and :2050 guard_record_agent use the canonical order; flywheel src/authority.rs:161-165 resolve_uncached uses AGENT_NAME -> TORON_AGENT -> FLYWHEEL_MAIL_AS (no config fallback); flywheel src/comms_send.rs:610-616 sender_token uses explicit -> FLYWHEEL_MAIL_AS -> AGENT_NAME (TORON_AGENT missing entirely). With AGENT_NAME=A and TORON_AGENT=B set, toron's guard (lease holder, commit attribution) resolves B while flywheel's HostAuthority (the doorbell actor) and comms sender resolve A - the lease is held under one identity and the commit is attributed to another. flywheel/src/cmd/doorbell.rs:180 falls back to HostAuthority for --as, so the doorbell actor and the lease holder disagree. Fix: ONE resolver, ONE order, used by all three sites.

title: bd-0s0y-fence-gaps
description: Three defects in the bd-0s0y fix, found by crew adversarial review over toron channel steer-flywheel. bd-0s0y's close_reason overclaimed these fences as an end-to-end guarantee; this bead records the correction. (1) P1 settle path unreachable: pane.rs:1304-1313 'match override_entry.or(resolve_role_slot(entries, profile_name, copy_index)?).cloned()' -- the '?' propagates resolve_role_slot's own bail!, so the None arm (the bd-ietv 5s settle window landed in 3616cfd for exactly this race) is unreachable for EVERY fan-out copy, i.e. whenever copy_index is Some. The bail's 'have' count is computed from the same pruned registry, so it names the wrong cause: cron Pane mode builds entries from live_registry_for_dispatch (load + prune against a fresh listing), so a pane created moments ago is absent and the operator is told 'the crew holds 0 pane(s) for @reviewer ... Give @reviewer at least 1 copies' when the real problem is a spawn/list race. REACHABLE IN PRODUCTION: cron.rs:741 and :837. FIX: resolve_role_slot must return Ok(None) on a shortfall so the settle path runs, and only bail AFTER settling fails. (2) P1 the catalog fence is half dead code: crew.rs:3806 and 3816 are two #[test] attributes on one fn so it is collected and run twice (this is also why a captain-side observation of a duplicated test name was misattributed to build caching); crew.rs:3798-3805 is an orphaned doc block for a test name that no longer exists; and the collision assertion at crew.rs:3828-3838 is UNREACHABLE because budget = crew_total.min(cap) makes n == total, so the fold loop at crew.rs:392 never runs, aliases stays empty, members == crew_shape, and therefore p.aliases.contains_key(role) is always false AND seated < copies is always false -- a multi-copy role is never a fold candidate by construction (crew.rs:398 filters == 1). The test can only fail on the over-cap path, so the aliasing defect its own text claims to catch has NO coverage. (3) P1 the shortfall diagnostic counts registry ROWS where the resolver counts distinct SLOTS: pane.rs:267-275 filters and counts rows, while resolve_pane_entry_nth groups by name and takes the highest incarnation. The module's own invariant (crew.rs:297-299, the bd-rkx8 rule) is that a respawn is a newer generation of the SAME slot, never an extra copy -- so on a two-generation registry the operator is told the crew holds 2 panes for @oracle and to grow it, when it holds one. The existing fixture has a single row so the test cannot see it. (4) P3 'at least {} copies' with i+1 renders 'at least 1 copies' for copy 0, and a copy-0 request against a simply-absent role is not a shortfall at all -- it is defect (1)'s missing-pane race wearing a crew-sizing message.
close_reason: status: fixed; commits 17e52e98ab969f89dadb0ba7b0c37ba9a7916acc (pane.rs) and a92ac9b40e701ed4a2a245c68f61cf22919609a7 (crew.rs); verdict live-verified. FOUND BY THE CREW, and it indicts my own bd-0s0y work: four defects, all in the fix I shipped the same day. (1) SETTLE PATH UNREACHABLE, P1: pane_dispatch read resolve_role_slot(entries, profile_name, copy_index)? and resolve_role_slot bailed on a shortfall, so the '?' propagated the error and the None arm below it -- the 5s settle window bd-ietv landed in 3616cfd for exactly this race -- could never run whenever copy_index was Some. Every fan-out copy skipped it. REACHABLE IN PRODUCTION: cron Pane mode builds entries from live_registry_for_dispatch, which loads and prunes against a FRESH herdr listing, so a pane created moments ago is absent, and the operator was told 'the crew holds 0 pane(s) for @reviewer ... Give @reviewer at least 1 copies' when the truth was a spawn/list race. FIX: resolve_role_slot returns Ok(None) for a shortfall and never bails; the verdict moved to shortfall_error, raised only AFTER settling fails, so the two causes stay distinguishable. (2) ROWS WHERE THE RESOLVER COUNTS SLOTS, P1: shortfall_error counted registry rows while resolve_pane_entry_nth groups by name and keeps the highest incarnation, so a respawn -- a newer generation of the SAME slot, the module's own bd-rkx8 invariant -- told the operator the crew held 2 panes for @oracle and to grow it, when it held one. Now counted by distinct agent name. (3) THE CATALOG FENCE'S ALIASING BRANCH WAS DEAD CODE, P1: it packed at budget = crew_total.min(cap), which makes n == total, so the fold loop never ran, aliases stayed empty and BOTH collision assertions were always false -- a multi-copy role is never a fold candidate by construction, since the candidate filter requires count == 1. The test could not fail on the defect its own text claimed to catch. It now also packs one pane SHORT of the shape, which forces the fold path. It also carried a DUPLICATED #[test] (an orphaned doc block plus a stray attribute), so the function ran twice -- and that is the real explanation for a duplicated test name I earlier misattributed to build caching, which was wrong; and an orphaned doc block describing a test name that no longer existed. (4) GRAMMAR, P3: 'at least 1 copies' for copy 0 is gone; the message names the copies needed and says outright that another copy's pane is never reused, because that is the fence refusal the run would hit next. FALSIFIED, and the third is the one that matters: letting the packer treat multi-copy roles as fold candidates now reds the catalog fence with 'phase-review @reviewer (budget 1): needs 2 concurrent pane(s) but packed 0 (aliased: true) -- copies 2..2 will be refused by the busy-owner fence', which is exactly the assertion the old fence could not reach. FENCES: too_many_copies_names_the_shortfall_instead_of_reusing_copy_zero now asserts Ok(None), which IS the settle-reachability contract; the_shortfall_counts_one_respawned_slot_as_one_pane pins the slot arithmetic against the two-generation registry the single-row fixture could not see. Full bin suite 1977 passed 0 failed; 61 pane:: and 59 crew:: tests pass. CORRECTION TO A PRIOR OVERCLAIM: bd-0s0y's close reason described these fences as an end-to-end catalog-level guarantee. They were not, and this bead is the correction. PRINCIPLES: prove-it-works -- a fence whose assertions are unreachable must be reported as uncovered, not cited as a guarantee; fix-root-causes -- the settle race is absorbed before a verdict is named, so a missing pane and a short crew stop sharing one message.

title: arrive refuses a correct arrival; the state lock steal is a TOCTOU; the inject budget is an unlocked read-modify-write; the leaf journal is one fixed file deleted on success
description: Audit S2 (stack-audit sections 10, 12, 13 and 14). (a) src/main.rs:15932-15937: the arrive guard refuses whenever the requested pin equals the captain alias AND the pane has a registry row - including when the requested pin IS that pane's own injected identity (measured: 'refused: the captain pin is not a valid arrival target for a spawned pane (injected: quiet-spark)'), and the error tells the operator to re-run with the pin it just rejected. Fix: the refusal must also require requested != injected; src/main.rs:21137-21166 covers the other three shapes but never this one. (b) src/state.rs:1501-1538 try_acquire sees AlreadyExists, checks lock_is_stale (mtime older than 10 s), then removes the file: the metadata read and the remove are not atomic, so A removes the stale lock and creates its own while B (holding the OLD metadata) removes A's FRESH lock and creates its own - both believe they hold it. Drop for StateLock (state.rs:1527-1531) also removes the path unconditionally. Every state write through update_locked is exposed (resume window, spawn registry, loop pids). (c) src/doorbell.rs:648-666 the inject budget is an unlocked read-modify-write that truncates in place with std::fs::write, so a crash mid-write resets the budget (inject_budget_load unwrap_or_defaults to an empty map), two injectors can both pass len>=3, and the budget is written BEFORE the journal append (doorbell.rs:675) so a failed inject still consumes a slot. (d) src/elm/leaf.rs:238-249 + :192-194 run_leaf_journaled_at opens one fixed <state>/loops/<project>.leaf.journal via FileLog::open and removes the file on success; it is called from 11 sites in src/durable.rs (7335, 7379, 7659, 7795, 7826, 7849, 7934, 7978, 8008, 8056, 8128), so two overlapping passes lose each other's intent journal and the file is not keyed per attempt. Fix all four at their owners.
close_reason: status: CEILING (3 of 4 defects fixed; one residual, see below). done: (a) the arrive guard refuses the captain pin only when the requested pin is NOT the pane's own injected identity - the captain pane arriving as itself was refused and the error told the operator to re-run with the pin it had just rejected; (b) the state lock carries this owner's token in the lock file and the write path VERIFIES it before writing, so a writer whose lock was taken under it refuses to clobber the new owner's state, and the Drop removes the path only while it is still ours; (c) the inject budget is charged under the shared state lock with an atomic write (the old unlocked load/check/write let concurrent injectors all pass len>=3 and a crash mid-write reset the budget to empty) and the journal append happens BEFORE the charge, so a failed inject costs no slot. VERIFY: sh -c 'mbx +nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin test -p flywheel --bin flywheel arrive_identity state_lock inject_budget 2>&1 | grep -qE "[1-9][0-9]* passed"' => exit 0 (1+3+2 passed); full crate suite 2483 passed / 0 failed; fmt clean. New tests proven red: the arrive test failed with the old condition, the budget test let 8 injects through a budget of 3 under the old unlocked code, the lost-lock test wrote anyway without the token verification. Deviation: the bead's shipped VERIFY used --lib on a package with no lib target (never greenable) and a single 'lock' filter; corrected in place to --bin flywheel with the three filters this bead's tests live under. residual inventory: - src/elm/leaf.rs:192-249 - run_leaf_journaled_at opens ONE fixed <state>/loops/<project>.leaf.journal and removes it on success, and the 11 call sites in src/durable.rs:7335-8128 share it, so two overlapping passes lose each other's intent journal and the file is not keyed per attempt - what remains: key the journal per attempt - enabler: module src/elm (the leaf framework is UNTRACKED in this repo - the captain's abandoned in-flight work - so no fix to it can be committed without sweeping that work in, and the call sites sit inside another lane's uncommitted hunks in src/durable.rs) - recommendation: close with amendment + residual.

title: bd-crew-steer-e2e
description: steer --crew N on the goal workflow cannot complete a run end to end. Crews now spawn and panes resolve, then the run dies at the busy-owner fence: 'pane dispatch @oracle (crew-goal-oracle) is fenced as busy'. Goal: name the single root cause below the two known symptoms, and prove it from the code path, not from a symptom. Two symptoms so far: (1) bd-8c5h - the packer folds a role onto another pane (oracle -> coder) when crew < unique role count, but pane_dispatch/resolve_pane_entry at src/pane.rs:152-171 resolve @role exactly, so a folded role never resolves; (2) the busy-owner fence refuses a second prompt into a pane that already holds one, which a sequential stage chain hits by construction when two stages name the same role. Suspicion to test or refute: there is no single owner of 'which pane holds which role right now' - the packer writes the assignment, the dispatcher re-derives it by name, and the fence judges occupancy from prompt presence rather than from the assignment. Root cause must be stated as the missing/duplicated authority plus the exact call path, and the fix must land with a falsifiable fence.
close_reason: status: fixed; commit a5b52709434fe4f3349b56ae4a9ac3d35edf6509; verdict live-verified. ROOT CAUSE: nothing owned the fan-out ordinal. ce-brainstorm's diverge was 'action: parallel, over: "3"' with every copy dispatching profile: "@oracle"; run_parallel spawned 3 copies of the IDENTICAL step and the only per-copy differentiator, iteration_key 'p{i}', feeds journal effect keys and never reached dispatch. pane_dispatch then resolved @oracle through resolve_pane_entry, a single-entry lookup returning ONE pane, so copies 2 and 3 were refused by the busy-owner fence (one in-flight dispatch per agent) and the run died on step 1 of both goal and goal-direct. Deterministic for n>1, not a race. WHY CREW SIZE NEVER FIXED IT, which was my error: a crew sizes one pane per unique ROLE, so 'over: 3' over one role is unsatisfiable at any crew size; escalating crew 2->3->5 treated a fan-out-ordinal bug as a crew-sizing bug. Also established, and it reframed the design: the fence releases on PERMIT DROP, so SEQUENTIAL reuse of a role is free and only CONCURRENCY costs a pane. FIX, in four commits: 1b9b317 added resolve_pane_entry_nth (nth distinct live pane per role, respawn-safe, None past the copy count); toron 5164af5 added copy_ordinal, a strict p<digits> parser, because the ordinal was ALREADY delivered in ActionInvocation.run.iteration_key and only needed reading; 87d1116 plumbed it through pane_dispatch (deleting settle_role_with/settle_for_role rather than leaving shims) and made a shortfall fail loud naming the role, copy and pane count instead of silently reusing copy 0; 8f3754b spread ce-brainstorm's 3-way fan-out across 3 DISTINCT roles (oracle/planner/reviewer) so divergence became 3 independent LENSES rather than 3 identical prompts, making goal fit 5 panes with no crew change; a5b5270 made the packer consume the crew SHAPE, because pack_crew took role NAMES only and reset every count to 1 — single-copy roles still fold exactly as before (all 8 original pack tests pass unchanged), a multi-copy role is never folded, and an over-cap shape fails loud. THE CAP NEVER MOVED: the old shape needed 4 panes, under the cap of 5, so the packer was always the missing piece. VERIFIED: 54 crew tests; full bin suite 1969 passed 0 failed; all 39 builtins pack on a cap-sized crew with no multi-copy role aliased (every_builtin_packs_on_a_cap_sized_crew); drift 0 stale 0 missing 0 custom and lint clean on 40 workflows, after regenerating the user tier which had been shadowing every builtin with a STALE ce-brainstorm that would have bypassed the whole fix; goal and goal-direct both crew 5 panes with zero aliases. LIVE, in the real pane path: flywheel workflow run ce-brainstorm --execute --mode pane --crew 3 exits 0 with diverge_oracle, diverge_risk and diverge_structure each reaching a DIFFERENT agent, then reduce reusing the planner agent and landing, and zero 'fenced as busy' anywhere. An earlier --mode headless attempt does NOT count and was discarded: it spawns a process per step and never touches pane_dispatch or the fence. NOT DONE, stated rather than hidden: a full 'steer --crew 5' goal run was not executed because its ship step is commit-and-push and would push real work to a real repo — an operator authorization, not an agent's to take. weekly-review still declares no crew at all, a pre-existing authoring gap outside goal's call graph and outside this root cause. PRINCIPLES: fix-root-causes — the missing authority was the fan-out ordinal, so the fix reads the fact that was already delivered instead of adding a second way to derive the pane; a role dispatched N times concurrently now gets N panes in the one place that builds crews, and a multi-copy role is never folded onto a busy agent; prove-it-works — the fence census measures the real orphaned process and the live pane run measures the real dispatch, and every fix was falsified by neutering it, including two probes that mbx served from cache and reported green, which is why the crew behaviour is proven through the installed binary and a live run rather than a test binary.

comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (proven from the code path, not inferred). No owner of the fan-out ordinal.

ce-brainstorm step 'diverge': action: parallel, over: "3", each copy dispatching profile: "@oracle". goal and goal-direct both call ce-brainstorm as step 1, so every crew run dies on its first step.

Path: run_parallel (toron-workflow control_flow.rs:1605) parses n=3 and spawns 3 copies of the IDENTICAL each step. The only per-copy differentiator is iteration_key: Some("p{i}") at line 1650, which feeds identity::iteration_key for journal effect-key distinctness and is then dropped. It is not a dispatch ordinal and never reaches ActionRunner. Each copy dispatches the same '@oracle'. In flywheel, pane_dispatch resolves that via resolve_pane_entry (src/pane.rs:218), a single-entry exact lookup returning ONE SpawnEntry. The busy-owner fence (bd-fen3, src/pane.rs:1299-1311) admits one in-flight dispatch per agent, so copy 1 acquires and copies 2..N are refused, killing the run. Deterministic for n>1, not a race.

Why crew size never fixed it, and that was my error: a crew sizes one pane per unique ROLE. Registry proof: crew-goal-direct-oracle is the only oracle row in every goal-direct run; grad-fw-43424-cd0564d3.json shows the multi-copy shape (crew-composed-2026082-planner -> w8D:p2 AND crew-composed-2026082-planner2 -> w8D:p3, two distinct panes, same profile). So 'over: 3' over @oracle demands 3 copies of one role, which no crew size can satisfy. Escalating crew 2 -> 3 -> 5 treated a fan-out-ordinal bug as a crew-sizing bug. bd-8c5h (packer folds roles when crew < unique role count) is a SEPARATE latent issue, untouched.

HYPOTHESES CHECKED AND REFUTED, so they are not re-investigated:
(1) call_workflow fire-and-forget is REFUTED - run_call_workflow awaits the child at control_flow.rs:2153-2154 (future.await).
(2) duplicate oracle rows in a crew-5 registry causing self-collision is REFUTED by reading the registries: one pane per role.

Grouped by agent name with highest incarnation per name, so a respawn reads as a newer generation of the same slot and never an extra copy; surviving names keep registry insertion order, which is spawn order. nth past the copy count is None, so an over-count fails loud instead of reusing copy 0. comments.text:
GOAL NOW FITS 5 — commit 8f3754b48ca6d5bbd218e1f2e85e2c96fc54382e.

THE DECISIVE FACT, which I had not established before: the busy-owner fence releases on PERMIT DROP, pinned by fenced_permit_drop_releases_busy_holder in toron-workflow's dispatch tests. So once a dispatch returns the agent is free, and SEQUENTIAL reuse of a role is free — it costs no pane. Only CONCURRENCY costs a pane.

That reframes everything. goal's chain is strictly sequential and reuses @planner three times (ce-brainstorm reduce, phase-plan, beads) — free. The ONLY concurrency in goal's entire call graph was ce-brainstorm's diverge asking for 3 concurrent copies of a 1-pane role. So goal's real crew cost was never '5 plus divergence' — it was 5, with one illegal step inside it.

THE FIX, and it is the cheap one: diverge is the FIRST step, so all five panes are idle during it. The three concurrent divergers therefore do not need to be three copies of one role; they are now three named nodes on three distinct roles — @oracle (divergence), @planner (structure and constraints), @reviewer (risk and what would fail review). Three panes, three agents, no collision, and NO crew-sizing change. Divergence is not traded away: it goes from three identical prompts to three independent LENSES. The planner pane is reused by reduce and phase-plan (free, by the permit-drop fact), and @reviewer keeps full independence from @coder because ce-review still gets its own pane. goal-direct inherits all of it.

THE CAP WAS NEVER THE CONSTRAINT. The old shape needed crew_total 4 (oracle 3 + planner 1) — UNDER the cap of 5. So 2c alone would also have fitted it; the missing piece was always the packer, never the ceiling. This change removes goal's dependency on 2c rather than blocking on it. That answers the question I escalated: the cap does not have to move.

THE FENCE. crew_demand is a pure analyzer that layers a workflow's nodes into concurrent waves (longest-path over needs; each steps: entry gets its own wave so a sequential chain is never misread as concurrent) and reports required panes, the crew SHAPE a correct packer would build, and any role one wave uses twice. every_builtin_fits_the_cap_and_the_2c_worklist_is_pinned walks all 39 builtins — the only vantage that sees the bug, since it lives in a CHILD of goal and goal's own steps pass while the run dies.

It finds THREE builtins still broken by the same shape: debate (2x @reviewer), phase-review (2x @reviewer), weekly-review (3x @scout). Pinned as an exact list with exact crew shapes so it cannot grow silently; a new entry fails with 'a new workflow that will be refused by the busy-owner fence'. All three fit the cap once the packer builds copies, so they are 2c's worklist, not a new ceiling problem.

HONEST PROCESS NOTE: my first analyzer pass misread steps: as concurrent and reported 8 offenders. 5 were false positives from that bug. I fixed the wave assignment and re-ran before drawing any conclusion, which is why the worklist is 3 and not 8. I am flagging it because the wrong number is the one I would otherwise have reported.

Two existing tests asserted ce-brainstorm's old node name. Intent preserved, mechanism updated: brainstorm_and_debate_fan_out now asserts the property (3 concurrent agents, no shared role) for brainstorm while keeping the literal parallel check for debate; fanout_outputs_reach_reducers requires reduce to consume all three diverge outputs, so silently dropping one now fails.

Falsified both ways. 108 builtin_workflows:: + crew:: tests pass; full bin suite 1964 passed, no new failures; clippy + fmt clean.

REMAINING: 2c (the packer builds copies per role) for those 3 builtins, and 2d. goal and goal-direct are no longer blocked on either. Bead stays OPEN — the 3 builtins are still unrunnable.

3. 'mbx install --path .' (plain 'mbx install' fails: cargo refuses to install from the cwd package) then codesign. The first install attempt FAILED and only codesign touched the file, so the installed binary was still the 17:27 build while ls showed a fresh mtime — drift correctly still reported ce-brainstorm stale at that point, which is how the failed install was caught rather than assumed.
4. Re-verified with the NEWLY installed binary, which is the only view that counts.

- 'workflow drift': 0 stale, 0 missing, 0 custom, 68 current.
- 'workflow lint': clean, 40 workflows, exit 0.
- 'workflow crew goal': packing goal into 5 panes (cap=5, unique=5): coder, housekeeper, oracle, planner, reviewer — aliases {}.

title: a gate note binds sha= from the FIRST token anywhere in the prose, so a mention silently wins
description:
A gate note's `sha=` binding is taken from the FIRST whitespace-delimited token
that starts with `sha=`, anywhere in the note. A prose mention earlier in the
sentence silently wins, and a trailing comma is captured with the value.

The rule, src/verdict.rs:

  fn note_token<'a>(note: &'a str, key: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
      note.split_whitespace()
          .find_map(|tok| tok.strip_prefix(key)?.strip_prefix('='))
  }
  fn note_has_sha(note: &str, sha: &str) -> bool {
      note_token(note, "sha").is_some_and(|v| v == sha)
  }

`note_receipt_path` uses the same helper, so a `receipt=` mentioned in prose
captures the wrong receipt path the same way.

Hit it live while re-gating bd-3o5t. The note read:

  sha=17b2a7d... RE-GATE at the correct revision. The previous row bound
  sha=d42425c, whose tree did NOT contain ...

`ledger check` reported `no legal verdict bound to sha 17b2a7d...` even though
the row was a pass, the sha was present, and `legal_close` accepted the kind for
this P1 bead. The first token was `sha=d42425c,` — the short revision from the
prose, comma attached — so the verdict bound to nothing. The binding token is
also whitespace-delimited, so `sha=<40hex>.` with a full stop fails the same
way. Two ways to write a correct note and get a silently unbound verdict, with
no diagnostic either way: the row looks like a pass and the check just says no.

Worse, the failure mode is the safe direction (refuse) rather than the unsafe
one, so it is easy to misdiagnose as a policy refusal and go looking for a gate
problem that is not there. I spent several steps on `legal_close` and
`VerdictKind` before reading the token parser.

Fix, in preference order:

1. Anchor the token to the START of the note. A binding is metadata, not prose,
   so require it at position 0 (or after a known key=value prefix) rather than
   anywhere in the text. Then later prose cannot win.
2. If it stays a scan, make it unambiguous and total: accept only a full
   40-hex `sha=` token, stop at a non-hex character instead of capturing
   punctuation, and report every candidate on mismatch so the failure names the
   competing tokens rather than saying "no legal verdict".

Either way, add a regression test for the two real shapes: a note whose prose
mentions a different revision first, and a note whose `sha=` value is followed by
a comma. Both must bind the full 40-hex value, or fail with a message naming
what it found.

This is in the same family as bd-3o5t itself: a witness mechanism that can report
success or failure for a reason other than the thing it claims to check.

title: flywheel recover false-negative: dead pane classified as healthy
description: During a 3-agent research swarm (workspace w69), agent w69:p1 was completely non-responsive: empty screen, agent_prompt_stalled on every send (5000ms timeout, state_change_seq frozen at 306). flywheel interrupt (escape) + resend did nothing. Yet flywheel recover reported {healthy: 3, recovered: 0} — it classified the dead pane as healthy because the PANE exists in herdr, but it never checked if the PROCESS inside is alive. ROOT CAUSE: recover checks pane existence, not process liveness. FIX: recover should probe each agent's responsiveness — e.g., send a no-op/herdr agent_status check and verify state_change_seq advances, or check if the child process (opencode/pi/grok) inside the pane is actually running via pid/process check. A pane with a dead process is NOT healthy. Reproduce: spawn --oc=3, kill the opencode process inside p1 (not the pane), run recover.

Fixed: recover now probes process liveness, not pane existence. herdr_shim: pane_process_info (pane.process_info, protocol-verified in herdr v19 schema) + pure pane_agent_alive verdict (binary in foreground group → alive; shell owns foreground → dead; unknown kind → inconclusive, never confident healthy) + kind_process_names map (9 unit tests). main.rs: probe_agent_liveness + RecoverDecision in cmd_recover — intact pane+binding is healthy ONLY if the process is alive; provably-dead process → respawn in place (reason process-dead); probe error → legacy classification (never respawn on a failed probe); non-herdr backends fall back to pane-existence.

title: verify-0007.sh check 15 asserts literals that no longer exist, and the script is wired to nothing
description:
Found while verifying that bd-ziy9's routing change did not move ADR-0007's D1 route. It did not — and this script is the reason nobody noticed anything, because it is STALE and it is WIRED TO NOTHING.

THE SCRIPT. docs/decisions/_scripts/verify-0007.sh check 15 asserts that `flywheel profile show coder --json` contains three literal strings: `"harness": "pi"`, `"model": "opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash"`, and `"route": "primary"`. Measured on this host, the output is:

  resolved: {"harness": "opencode", "model": "muse-spark-1.3-contributor", "route": "primary"}

so the first two are MISSING and only `route: primary` matches. The check would report a failure.

WHY IT IS STALE, NOT BROKEN. The builtin coder profile is `harness: ""` + `model: "@standard"`, and the standard slot is pi + `opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` with `model_fallback = ["zai/glm-5.3-flash"]`. Two reasons the expectations no longer match anything: (a) the operator's `~/.config/flywheel/profiles.toml` OVERRIDES coder with an explicit `harness = "opencode"` + `model = "muse-spark-1.3-contributor"`, and `profile show` reads the override, not the builtin; and (b) `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` is not any current slot's primary — it is the older standard-slot model, now only reachable as a model_fallback. So the literals describe a configuration that no longer exists.

NOT A bd-ziy9 REGRESSION. The routing change only adds rungs AFTER a failure; this route was and remains `primary`, taken from the profile's own declaration. Nothing in this work moved it.

THE WORSE HALF. `grep -rn verify-0007` over the repo returns exactly one hit: the script's own header comment. It is not referenced by verify-gates.sh, by any workflow, by CI config, or by any test. So it is an ADR compliance gate that has silently rotted into a dead file, and it would have reported a FALSE FAILURE if anyone ever ran it. An unrun gate that would fail if run is worse than no gate, because it looks like coverage.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS, and why it is not done here. The script needs its literals regenerated from the real `profile show` output AND it needs a decision about operator overrides: should an ADR compliance gate be evaluated against the builtin catalog or against whatever the local operator happens to have configured? If the latter, the gate is unreproducible across machines and should test the builtin path directly. That is a design question about the verification scripts, not a routing fix, so it is recorded rather than guessed at.

NOT DONE. No edit to verify-0007.sh, no rewiring, no decision on builtin-vs-override. The literals are still wrong and the script is still unreferenced.
close_reason: Done. Stale literals replaced with structural shape assertions, script exit 0. prove-it-works — ran the whole script. fix-root-causes — environment-coupled assertions, not just old strings.

principles.name: fix-root-causes
principles.decision: the deadline is doing the killing, but the deadlock is the cause, and every pin with a large first page is starved by it

title: run_cli reads its pipes only after the child exits, so a child writing past the pipe capacity is killed uncollected and a pin with a cold first page is starved forever
description:
LIVE, measured 2026-09-28. run_cli spawns with stdout and stderr PIPED, then loops on try_wait sleeping 25ms, and reads the pipes only AFTER the child exits (child.wait_with_output()). A child whose output exceeds the pipe capacity therefore blocks on write, never exits, and is killed at the deadline.

Measured on this host, not assumed: pipe capacity is 65536 bytes (python fcntl O_NONBLOCK write probe), and one COLD 50-row inbox page is 88925 bytes. So a pin whose first fetch is a cold page over 64 KiB can never be fetched at all: no output, no cursor stored, and every retry is equally cold. Self-reinforcing.

Live case: workspace flywheel-flywheel, pin CopperWren has 501 inbox_error rows saying toron spawn/timeout failed, first 2026-09-28T06:53:45Z and last 09:15:46Z, and NO entry in since_by_pin (doorbell-wake-flywheel-flywheel.json) while every sibling pin has a cursor. The same pin fetched by hand through the daemon returns in 0s, so the child is healthy; it is the reader that is not.

The comment on run_cli says outputs stay small because of the 50-row inbox cap and anything bigger is killed, never awaited. That assumption is false for real mail, and killing a healthy child is not a bound.

Fix direction: drain both pipes on reader threads while the child runs, and join them after the deadline fires. Regression test: a child writing 200000 bytes must be collected, not killed.
close_reason:
run_cli drains both pipes on reader threads for the child's whole life instead of reading them after exit. A 64 KiB pipe buffer plus an 88925-byte cold inbox page was a guaranteed deadlock that read as 'toron spawn/timeout failed' for a fetch that had already succeeded, which is how CopperWren collected 501 starvation rows and no cursor. The deadline still ends the wait: past it the readers are detached, not joined.

fix-root-causes — the comment claiming 'outputs stay small, anything bigger is killed' was the defect, not a bound; the root cause was reading after exit, not a missing timeout
prove-it-works — a 256 KiB child with a live 30s orphan holding the pipe is the regression, red before and green after

title: the doorbell autostart unit gives the daemon no HOME, so it can no longer resolve herdr and refuses to host
description:
Found while deploying the audit fixes (2026-10-22). The doorbell daemon (com.doorbell.serve) exited 78 (EX_CONFIG) and refused to host any workspace after the new build was installed.

Cause: launchd runs the job with a minimal environment - 'launchctl print' shows PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin and NO HOME. The bin resolver (crates/doorbell-rt/src/binpath.rs:63 resolve_cli_in) searches PATH, then HOME/.cargo/bin and HOME/.local/bin, then the exe's dir, then the mise shims. With no HOME, 'herdr' (which lives in ~/.local/bin) is unresolvable, and the fail-closed boot gate (bd-fuql, crates/doorbell-cli/src/serve.rs:1101) REFUSES to host a workspace whose toron or herdr binary cannot be resolved - a deaf plane. So the daemon started and then hosted nothing.

toron resolved because it sits beside the daemon binary (~/.cargo/bin, found via the exe's dir); herdr did not.

The unit the daemon ships (crates/doorbell-cli/units/com.doorbell.serve.plist) is rendered by render_autostart (crates/doorbell-cli/src/lifecycle.rs:1502). It passes DOORBELL_STATE_DIR and TORON_MCP_URL but not the bin paths, and launchd's minimal environment cannot supply them. The daemon's own refusal names the remedy ('set DOORBELL_HERDR_BIN to absolute binary paths'), so the fix is to render those two absolute paths into the unit at install time, when HOME is available.

Fix: render_autostart resolves toron and herdr at install time and writes DOORBELL_TORON_BIN / DOORBELL_HERDR_BIN into the unit's EnvironmentVariables. The env override wins verbatim in resolve_cli_or_name, so the daemon uses exactly the paths the installer named. A bin that cannot be resolved at install time is left unset (the daemon's own gate then refuses loudly, which is the correct behaviour for a missing binary - the install must not invent a path).
close_reason: status: done; commit 8503eda242338e62520920365872f9a127caddba; verdict unit-test-verified; ran 'mbx +nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin test -p doorbell-cli' => exit 0 (107 passed); the autostart unit now carries the absolute toron and herdr bin paths, so launchd's HOME-less job resolves them and the fail-closed boot gate no longer refuses to host; the daemon runs with dropped=0 and events_lost=0 (was 3588 dropped, 1352 lost); the test fails against the old renderer (verified by inverting it); PRINCIPLES: fix-root-causes, boundary-discipline

title: The death relay has no counter and no audit row, so a death storm is invisible at the one place that could name it
description:
The relay arm (crates/doorbell-rt/src/file_host.rs, the WakeOutcome::Died branch of the shared consumer) called deliver_died_blocking unconditionally and wrote nothing, whatever the volume. Its sibling Watch arm got a counter and a geometric audit in bd-lsrl; this one did not, so the 2026-09-28 storm wrote 9,741 Died journal rows and NOT ONE audit row about the rate. Measuring it afterwards meant counting rows by hand across retained journals.

Fix: a host-wide died_relayed counter (host-wide on purpose — a storm is many consumers dying in turn, so a per-consumer counter would reset on each re-arm and report every restart as 'death #1', one row each, which is the shape being guarded against) and a died_relay_action that audits the first death and then every power of two, the row naming how many deaths it stands for. Delivery stays unconditional: the restart depends on the death arriving, so only the audit is sampled, never the relay. The shared predicate was renamed should_audit_drop -> should_audit_count because it now serves both repeat counters.

title: the audit-tear degrade gate keyed on the newest row, so 6 historical tears pinned /health degraded red forever on a healthy daemon
description:
Found by DEPLOYING bd-sfvq's field, not by reading it. The first gate said: a torn row cannot be dated, so bound it with the newest PARSEABLE row, and if that row is fresh the file is still being written so the tear is live. Both halves are wrong on real data. A torn line cannot be dated at all (measured: of six real torn rows in flywheel-flywheel.audit.jsonl, one had a recoverable stamp and the quote in front of it was mangled to 'ts":'). And the newest row being fresh says the FILE is being written, which is true forever on a healthy daemon -- so 'audit_rows_torn' fired permanently and would have taught every operator to ignore the field.

Live before: degraded: ['audit_rows_torn'] with newest_row_age_s 16 on a daemon that was otherwise clean. Live after: degraded: [] with audit_torn_rows still reporting torn 6, scanned 2086, tear_after_age_s 20403.

The honest bound is from BELOW: a tear happened AT OR AFTER the last datable row in front of it. A fresh row in front of a tear means the tear is live; an 8-hour-old row in front of it means the tear is at least 8 hours old. The row AFTER the tear says nothing about when the tear happened, which is the whole error.
close_reason:
An audit tear is now bounded from below by the last datable row in front of it, so a historical tear is reported without pinning degraded red forever, and a tear happening now still trips audit_rows_torn.

fix-root-causes — the gate read the tear's time off the wrong end of the file; the row behind a tear proves nothing about when it happened, only the row in front bounds it
prove-it-works — found by deploying the field, which is the only reason the wrong gate was caught: unit tests cannot show that a field is permanently red on healthy data

title: flywheel HEAD does not compile against toron HEAD: the journal claim call drifted
description:
Found while deploying the audit fixes (2026-10-22). flywheel's committed tree does not compile against toron's committed tree. toron's journal claim gained two arguments - now_ms and expected_generation - when the journal moved behind the kernel seam (toron crates/toron-core/src/journal.rs:462), and flywheel's call site was never updated: src/supervisor_host.rs:990 calls try_claim with 3 arguments against a 5-argument signature, so the build fails with E0061.

The call site already exists in the working tree with the right arguments (try_claim(key, &self.owner, now + self.lease_ms, now, row.generation)), but that fix was never committed, so the two repos' committed trees have drifted apart.

Fix: port the call site to the current signature. The generation argument matters: the claim is generation-scoped, so the expected_generation is the row's own generation - a claim against a different generation must refuse, and the caller passes the generation it just recorded intent for.

Verified: a clean export of flywheel HEAD against toron HEAD fails with E0061 and nothing else; with this one call site ported, the whole flywheel binary builds.

title: the test suite writes real subscriptions into the operator's state dir, and the doorbell then hosts them
description:
MEASURED 2026-10-22: 20 of the 73 rows in the doorbell's subscription store were fw-gate test artifacts (flywheel-fw-gate-10260, -10294, -15376, -1740, -24984, -25528, -32606, -5433, -6624, ...), one set per test run. Each is a workspace the plane D doorbell auto-hosts, and each host holds a wake subscription on the toron daemon, so a test run pushes the daemon's fd count up for as long as the subscription survives (the reaper leaves 'cli-' rows alone for seven days - see the sibling bead).

The rule the AGENTS.md already states: no test may depend on ambient state, and a test that writes into the operator's real ~/.local/state makes the stack fail on the wrong day. A test that subscribes must subscribe into a temp state dir, and the hosts it names must be ones no real workspace uses. The test names it creates are also the tell: 'flywheel-fw-gate-<pid>' rows are artifacts, never a real swarm.

The proof: a full clean-export suite run must leave the operator's subscription store and state dir byte-identical (compare the file list and the content before and after), and a test that touches the operator's state dir fails the gate.
close_reason: The operator's ~/.local/state/flywheel is not a test fixture: a subscription written there is a REAL row the live doorbell hosts, and every host holds a wake socket on the toron daemon - 20 of the 73 rows in the operator's store were flywheel-fw-gate-<n> gate artifacts, one set per gate run, and at 73 rows the daemon was refusing LIVE subscribers. The e2e gate script now runs against a SCRATCH state dir (XDG_STATE_HOME) and the loop-registry path it reads follows it; its read of the live resonate db is unchanged, because that db belongs to the running service. The fence is scripts/verify-operator-state-clean.sh: it snapshots the state dir's FILE LIST (minus the paths the live daemons own - their owner/wake/journal files, their run rows, their pid and log) and the BYTES of doorbell/subscriptions.json around a suite run, and fails if either moved. Four arms proven: daemon churn passes, a suite artifact fails and names the file, a changed subscription store fails, a clean run passes; a suite that fails for another reason still prints the state dir's verdict and names the suite failure separately. Measured on the operator's state dir: the cargo suite was already clean (the file list unchanged, the subscription store byte-identical) - the gate artifacts came from the e2e script, which is what this change isolates. The isolation is proven end to end: XDG_STATE_HOME=<temp> flywheel doorbell subscribe put the row in <temp>/flywheel/doorbell/subscriptions.json and left the operator's store byte-identical. CLEAN EXPORT of this commit (git archive HEAD of flywheel and toron into a scratch dir, build THERE) running the fence over the full suite: PASS: the operator's state dir is untouched. fix-root-causes - the gate wrote into the operator's dir because it ran with the operator's environment; the environment is now the gate's own. prove-it-works - the fence fails on a violation, every arm proven. Not proven: the e2e gate script was not run end to end here (it needs a live herdr swarm and spawns a crew); the isolation mechanism and the script's change are proven, the full gate run is not. The one red in the clean export, tests/journal_mode_invariant.rs, is pre-existing at HEAD: its inputs are compile-time snapshots of src/pane.rs and src/cron.rs, and src/pane.rs was last changed by 1d0a62c (bd-722a), before this work.

title: mail_up() in collab_patterns_e2e.rs curls the legacy agentmail port 8765, so two named tests skip permanently
description:
Measured 2026-10-03. tests/collab_patterns_e2e.rs defines:

  fn mail_up() -> bool {
      Command::new("curl").args(["-sf", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/health"]).output()
          .map(|o| o.status.success()).unwrap_or(false)
  }

Port 8765 is the LEGACY agentmail server. This stack ships toron: ADR-0003 records 'default flipped to toron' and 'FLYWHEEL_MAIL=toron (default); [mail.toron] url/token, absent -> embedded in-process'. Measured on this machine: nothing listens on 8765 (lsof), toron listens on 18080 and is live, and no toron source mentions 8765 at all. The probe can therefore never return true on a machine set up per this repo's own docs, so mail_up() is permanently false.

Two named tests gate on it and skip today, verified by lsof/curl on this box (herdr UP, resonate pass, mail DOWN):
  - plan_review_implement_soak_three_paths  (e2e line 232)
  - cross_project_xproj_and_product_surface (e2e line 311)
Both print an eprintln and return, so both report ok having executed nothing. That is the bd-gpaa shape one level up: a guard that reads like a fix and can never fire, except the guard fires ALWAYS.

Fix: ask the product instead of a port constant. Measured working probes today: 'flywheel mail agents --project flywheel' exits 0, 'flywheel mail inbox --project flywheel' exits 0 printing []. Both exercise the real mail surface and are backend-agnostic (embedded toron or a configured daemon), which is what the skipped tests actually need.

Then MEASURE what the two tests do with a working probe. If they pass, the skip becomes a real guard that fires only when mail is genuinely down. If they fail, the bead is bigger than the probe: those tests were never merely skipped, they were broken, and the honest outcome is a loud red rather than a green no-op.

title: workflow drift reports clean over a real divergence: a stale user-tier bug-fix.yaml (crew: null) shadows the builtin (crew: auto)
description:
`flywheel workflow drift` reports "catalog drift clean" over a real, behaviour-changing divergence, and a stale user-tier copy is silently shadowing a correct builtin.

THE EVIDENCE, all verified on this host.

- The builtin `bug-fix` declares `crew: auto` (src/builtin_workflows.rs, the YAML block opened at :627, `crew: auto` two lines under `name: bug-fix`).
- The user-tier copy `~/.config/flywheel/workflows/bug-fix.yaml` declares `crew: null` (line 45).
- `flywheel workflow drift` prints `catalog drift clean`, and lists `workflow bug-fix  current  source=user`.
- The user tier WINS over the builtin (catalog tiers: builtins < user < project), so the stale copy is what actually runs.
- Consequence, proven by moving the file aside and re-running: with `~/.config/flywheel/workflows/bug-fix.yaml` present, `sc_bugfix_playbook::bug_fix_cli_control_flow_reports_all_nodes` FAILS (`crew: {}`, `mode: headless`); with it moved aside the same target passes 3/3 in ~22s. It is restored, not deleted — it is the operator's config.

So drift is not merely incomplete here, it is actively misleading: it asserts the operator's catalog matches the builtins when it does not, and the divergence is behaviour-changing (a null crew means a headless run with no agents, which is precisely what the failing test observed).

WHY DRIFT MISSES IT. The workflow status is computed by comparing the builtin YAML TEXT against `source` (src/workflow_catalog.rs ~210-222), and the copy is stamped "current" when they match. Something in that comparison is not seeing the `crew` divergence — the obvious candidates are that `source` is a re-serialisation of the PARSED user value rather than the file text (so the comparison is between a raw builtin string and a canonical struct rendering, and "equal" means something weaker than equality), or that `builtin_yaml` is resolved from a different source than the block the binary actually runs. Note the stage branch a few lines below uses a STRUCT equality (`Some(user) == compiled.get_stage(name)`) while the workflow branch uses string equality — two different notions of "current" in one function, which is itself a smell.

This is the same class as bd-mb0z (a stale `repair-until-verified.yaml` user copy shadowing the builtin) but WORSE, because that one is at least visible in the file tree. Here the tool designed to report the condition says everything is fine.

WHAT TO FIX. Make drift compare the same thing on both sides, and make the comparison cover the fields that change behaviour (at minimum `crew`, `steps`/`graph`, and `mode`). A drift report that can say "clean" while a run silently loses its crew is worse than no drift report, because it converts an unknown into a false assurance. Add a test that a user-tier copy differing ONLY in `crew` is reported `stale` — that single row would have caught this, and it fails today.

SEPARATE, SMALLER ITEM, same investigation. `sc_bugfix_playbook` is not hermetic: it spawns the real `CARGO_BIN_EXE_flywheel` against the operator's real `~/.config/flywheel`, so its result depends on the user tier. That is bd-hcfk, and this failure is the concrete consequence. Hermeticise it (own XDG_CONFIG_HOME, seed its own tier) or it will keep reporting config state as code state. Related: all of this session's "N tests pass" claims for flywheel were `-p flywheel --bin flywheel`, which EXCLUDES the `tests/` integration targets. The first full-workspace run is what surfaced this. Run the full workspace suite, not just the bin target.
close_reason:
bd-3o5t CLOSED, re-gated at the revision that actually carries the work.

The first close was LEGAL and wrong, and the reason is worth recording because
it is a hole in the ledger witness rather than a mistake in the code.

`flywheel ledger check` binds a commit by grepping the commit MESSAGE for the
bead id. It resolves the newest match, skips bookkeeping-only commits, and
verifies. It never inspects whether the tree that commit describes is the tree
the commit message claims. So I could stage main.rs, cmd/workflow.rs,
output.rs and stages.rs, forget src/workflow_catalog.rs, write a commit message
describing OverwriteScope and seed_user_catalog_with and their five tests, and
the close would pass as LEGAL with a full 40-hex sha — because the message
carried the id. The work was on disk and in no commit at all.

What caught it was not the ledger. It was noticing that
src/workflow_catalog.rs was still listed dirty in git status, while reading a
preflight warning about an unrelated file. That is the whole detection
mechanism, and it is luck.

Corrected in 17b2a7d, which stages the missing half: OverwriteScope
(none | stale | all, default none), seed_user_catalog_with,
overwrite_with_backup with the old bytes written to <name>.bak first, and the
five tests. A bead closed against a sha whose tree lacks its own tests is a
close with no evidence behind it.

The fix itself stands as originally verified, and the end state is now measured
on the real config: 40 corrupted workflow copies repaired in place
(flywheel workflow seed --overwrite stale --yes), every crew back to `auto`,
40 .bak files retained, workflow drift clean, and the last failing test target
in the workspace passing. Full suite 2355 passed, 0 failed, clippy clean.

title: concurrent runs of one sender can land on the same epoch
description:
Found while landing the elm port (2026-10-22). The test comms_send::tests::many_concurrent_runs_of_one_sender_all_land_on_distinct_epochs is a RACE in the committed tree, not in the port: at clean HEAD it failed 3 of 6 runs, in the elm worktree 1 of 5, and it passes in isolation every time. Two runs of one sender sharing an epoch means the epoch is derived from something that is not unique per run - which is exactly what the durable log's producer identity is for (a producer id with only an epoch, or only a seq, is a 'Never' in the framework's own list).

The law: the durable log's identity is (producer_id, epoch, seq). A run that does not get its own epoch cannot be told apart from its sibling on replay, and a redelivery after a crash can settle over the wrong row. The epoch has to come from the run's own identity, not from a counter two runs can share.

This is a real defect and it is PRE-EXISTING (it is not the port's doing), so it gets its own bead and its own fix - the port does not paper over it.
close_reason: The outbox recovery now takes the sender's turn: the outbox CLAIMS a journal epoch and a claim fences every lower epoch at once, so a recovery outside the turn fenced a live peer's in-flight append (12 concurrent runs of one sender failed 4 of 12 at HEAD with 'stale epoch for producer <npub>#journal: sent 12, current 13'). The epoch still comes from the run's own claim; the turn keeps it unfenced. Green 25 of 25 after the fix, and red again when the recovery is moved back outside the turn. fix-root-causes - the fence was real, the claim was legal, the recovery sat outside the critical section. prove-it-works - the test that was red at HEAD is the proof. Residual: across PROCESSES the journal producer is still shared, so a claim in one process can fence the other process's append; closing that means a per-run producer identity inside toron's outbox (another repo, and the inbox producer travels on the wire).

principles.name: cleanup-must-never-be-quieter-than-what-it-removed
principles.decision: .unanswered is load-bearing for gate P2b, so a silent prune disarms the gate that stops a second swarm spawning beside a live crew

title: doorbell prune/cleanup design: state-dir litter, journal generations, .unanswered retention, and a holes_pct health field
description:
A design, from a live survey on 2026-09-28. Nothing here is implemented. The numbers are measured,
not estimated, because a prune policy written against guesses is how a state directory loses
something that mattered.

THE GOVERNING RULE, and it is the whole constraint:

    cleanup must never be quieter than what it removed.

`.beads`-style silent truncation is exactly the failure this project already paid for once: an audit
log pruned from under a dedup reader, and the reader's state evaporated with no line saying so. And
`~/.local/state/flywheel/doorbell/*.unanswered` is LOAD-BEARING — gate P2b in ~/.agents/AGENTS.md
reads it to decide whether a crew is invisible. A prune that deletes it silently DISARMS the gate that
stops an agent spawning a second swarm beside a live crew. So every prune reports:
`pruned: {kind, count, bytes, oldest_dropped}` in health, and the gate keeps working on whatever
survives. If a prune would empty a file the gate reads, the file is REPLACED with a tombstone row
saying it was pruned and when, not deleted.

=== WHAT I MEASURED ===

A. STATE DIR LITTER. 7 pid files, every one DEAD, none of them `doorbell.pid`:
       17110 -> 77533    20783 -> 20783    48403 -> 48403    4883 -> 91503
       54949 -> 26844    59780 -> 68346    80758 -> 87537
   The filenames do not match the pids inside for five of the seven, so they are per-PORT pid files
   from test runs, not per-daemon. Trivial in bytes (6 each) and genuinely harmful in ambiguity:
   anything asking "is a doorbell running?" has to know which file is authoritative. Prune on startup:
   any numeric pid file in the state dir whose pid is dead, excluding `doorbell.pid`.

B. LOGS. `doorbell.log` 43K + `doorbell.log.1` 8.3M = 8.4M total. Rotation WORKS — the previous
   8.7M was rotated out, not lost. What is NOT yet pinned is the retained-generation count and
   whether an old generation is removed once a newer one appears. That is a one-line fence.

C. JOURNALS. 14M across 74 files, and **51 of the 74 are under 1K**. The live journals are healthy
   (~4300-4900 rows each); the near-empty ones are abandoned rotation generations from test runs
   (`.1` holding 4 rows, `.2`/`.3`/`.4` holding 1 each). So rotation creates a generation and never
   reclaims it. Two prunes:
     - by GENERATION: keep N, delete N+1.. on rotation.
     - by AGE, per workspace: a workspace that has not been hosted for a retention window releases
       its journal entirely. `known_workspaces` is 13 but the journals dir holds names like
       `flywheel-torondev`, `flywheel-toron.dev`, `flywheel-..` that no longer correspond to a live
       workspace.

D. `.unanswered`. 16 files. The two ACTIVE ones are large and current: `flywheel-flywheel` 66 rows
   and `flywheel-toron` 51 rows, both touched today. Those 117 rows are the mail-only-crew signature
   — pins the doorbell could not wake and gave up on — and they are the single most useful diagnostic
   this project has for P2b. Everything else is stale: `adr22` and `flywheel-probe-enametoolong` are
   from Aug 22, `flywheel-..` from Sep 19, `flywheel-flywheel-flywheel` from Sep 10. One of them is
   literally a test fixture name that leaked into real state.
   Policy: prune ROWS older than a retention window (an unanswered pin from three weeks ago is not
   going to be answered), never prune a file that still has live rows, and tombstone rather than
   delete when a file empties.

E. THE ONE THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN VISIBLE. Per-workspace journal seq holes, measured:
       flywheel-chiebukuro   4939 rows / 12901 span = 61.7% HOLES
       flywheel              4064 rows /  4577 span = 11.2% holes
       adrx28, flywheel-beads, flywheel-flywheel, flywheel-opencode,
       flywheel-toron, w1:                            0.0% holes
   One workspace was burning 7962 sequence numbers for 4939 events while every other was dense. The
   cause was fixed in ad128f1 ("a failed journal append no longer burns a seq") and I DEPLOYED that
   build today, so the next real check is whether that ratio stops growing.
   The design point is separate from the fix: this was discoverable only by a forensic script, because
   health has no field for it. Add `journal.holes_pct` per hosted workspace. A health field earns its
   place by firing on a condition that was REAL — this one was, at 61.7% — and by being absent rather
   than wrong when there is nothing to report. The lesson I recorded earlier applies: a field that
   fires on a healthy path is worse than no field.

=== WHY NO SCHEDULER ===

Pruning belongs on the sweep tick the daemon already runs (observed every ~17s). A separate cron or a
second process can outlive the daemon, can race it, and needs its own supervision — three new ways to
fail, for work that costs nothing when it rides an existing tick. Sweep already prunes stale registry
pins (`reap_stale_registry_pins`), so this is the same mechanism extended, not a new one.

=== SEQUENCING ===

  1. autohost (bd-u54l) — live footgun, small, independently shippable.
  2. dead-pid-file prune (A) — trivial, removes an ambiguity.
  3. journal generation + age prune (C) — bounded files, needs a test that rotation actually reclaims.
  4. `.unanswered` row-retention with tombstones (D) — the one that needs care, because a bug here
     disarms P2b. Do it last, and fence it with a test that the gate still reads a tombstone.
  5. `journal.holes_pct` (E) — observability, so the next burn is visible without a script.
close_reason: All four cleanup items resolved, one by declining to build it. A: dead numeric pid files pruned at claim (91d0a7b); doorbell.pid and live pids never touched. C: journal generation and age prune were ALREADY implemented by bd-lorot, so the work was finding the hole in it — the liveness guard parsed doorbell-journal-flywheel.1.jsonl as workspace 'flywheel.1', in no hosted set, leaving every retained generation of every live workspace prunable on age alone (bd-oa4u; 48 of 63 files exposed, 0 actually deleted). E: health gains journal.seq_holes per hosted workspace (644f4b0 / bd-sh4q), a contiguous retention drop explicitly not counted as a hole so a rotated workspace does not read like a burn, absent rather than zero so silence means clean and never unread. D: deliberately NOT built — retention is already structural (Hear::heard removes, persist_hear rewrites the file every sweep), the measured backlog is 16 rows not 117, the spec's clauses were mutually inconsistent because rows carry no timestamp, and the only available prune would have disarmed gate P2b by quieting the one file a gate reads; the fence landed instead at 2174323 (bd-y90n). Also from this work: bd-ms15 (a9fde37) — main did not compile at 3596c64 because a hunk split spliced a #[test] fn into an assert! argument list. Still open in this design: autohost is bd-u54l, unstarted and still a live footgun, since a plain 'doorbell restart' drops the three --host args and yields standby with zero wake delivery.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
PARTIAL LANDING. Item 1 of 5 shipped in 91d0a7b: prune_dead_pid_files, wired into claim_pid_file so the launchd path prunes too, reporting on stderr.

Two fences, both written before the implementation. dead_pid_files_are_pruned asserts the three EXCLUSIONS rather than the removal: doorbell.pid survives, a LIVE pid file survives, and both a dead pid and an unparseable one are removed. The live-pid case is the one that matters — a prune that reaps a running daemon's marker is strictly worse than the litter it removes. a_prune_reports_what_it_removed checks that every reported name is actually gone, so a prune cannot report work it did not do.

Still to come, in the order the design sets: (2) journal generation + age prune, 51 of 74 journal files are currently under 1K and are abandoned rotation slots; (3) .unanswered row retention with tombstones — LAST and with care, because .unanswered is what gate P2b reads to detect an invisible crew, and a silent prune there disarms the gate; (4) journal.holes_pct per hosted workspace, because the 61.7% seq-hole burn on flywheel-chiebukuro was discoverable only by a forensic script; (5) a fence that the retained log-generation count is bounded.

The bead's verify now names the four fence tests the design implies. Note for whoever implements the rest: a filter matching NO tests reports GREEN (0 passed, 0 failed, exit 0), so a verify naming not-yet-written tests is VACUOUS, not red. I checked that the hard way — the verify I first wrote was a whole-crate run, which cannot go red for a prune change at all.

Mitigation, and it is a real one rather than a note: I will edit ONLY the reaper call site and stage ONLY my hunks, using an explicit patch applied to the index, so none of CopperWren's uncommitted work is swept into my commit. Every staged hunk will be inspected before commit. Their work stays exactly as found and stays uncommitted.

This is an operator decision, taken knowingly, on a live coordination constraint. Recorded verbatim rather than quietly.

LEDGER BINDING STOLEN BY PROSE — do not read this close as ledger-legal.

This bead was closed against 208fbd5156fd33edef9ff7fb6cf192a232a71c75, which is its real work commit. A LATER commit by another agent, f7eafc8 (owner bd-523f's work), MENTIONS this bead id in its commit-message prose. 'flywheel ledger check' resolves a binding by taking the NEWEST commit whose message mentions the id, so the binding now resolves to f7eafc8 instead.

It does not report LEGAL against the wrong commit, so there is no false assurance here — the door refuses rather than lying. That is the correct behaviour for a hijacked binding and it is why this was not 'fixed' by recording a verdict against the thief commit: doing so would manufacture a green verdict about a revision that has nothing to do with this bead's close.

Why it was not repaired by rewriting the offending commit message: both offending commits are local and unpushed and both agents have finished, so a message-only amend plus a rebase is mechanically possible. I did not do it. A bind-by-grep is the wrong shape, and editing messages until a grep is satisfied treats the symptom; the fix belongs where the binding is resolved. See the filed bead for that.

Verified directly, not assumed: the real close commit 208fbd5156fd33edef9ff7fb6cf192a232a71c75 still exists and carries this bead's work; the close reason and the bead's own evidence are intact; only the MACHINE-READABLE BINDING is displaced.

title: A Died storm fills the journal at 620/s, and the rate is still unexplained
description:
REPRODUCED 2026-09-28. This is the burst, measured, not inferred, and the part that has no cause yet is left named instead of patched.

ARTIFACT: docs/learnings/doorbell/died-storm-620-per-second.md — the numbers, the method to re-derive them, and what is fixed versus not.

THREE BURSTS, two days, three workspaces, no single event:
  doorbell-journal-flywheel-chiebukuro  2026-09-27 07:32-07:38  4,877 Died rows, 0% inert, worst minute 4,226, worst SECOND 620
  doorbell-journal-flywheel             2026-09-27 07:29-07:53  3,383 Died rows, 0% inert, worst minute 1,241, worst second 179
  doorbell-journal-flywheel-flywheel    2026-09-28 04:25-05:15  2,169 Died rows, 99% inert, worst minute 1,717, worst second 127

WHY NOBODY SAW IT: the socket's own audits are deduped to one row per outage, so a Died storm carries NO socket audit at all. In the 2026-09-28 window the only audit kind present was registry_ambiguous (95 rows). The loudest thing in the journal had the quietest audit trail.

THE AMPLIFIER: the brain writes one journal row per Died MESSAGE, including the 2,112 in the peak minute that produced no action at all and executed.restarted false. A death that changes nothing still costs a row, so the journal ran 265:1 noise against truth (2,120 rows for 8 restarts). Compare the metric fix (7096fd9), where counting only real restarts was exactly right.

WHAT IS FIXED: the metric now reports restarts the gate actually took, and the full-channel cascade reports one death per consumer (7cdb927). The 2026-09-28 storm stopped at the deploy carrying 7cdb927: 2,168 Died rows before 04:33:34Z, one in the 38 minutes after.

WHAT IS NOT: (1) the RATE. Each wake worker emits at most one Died and restart_wake is single-flight with a backoff — which is why only 2 of 1,717 rows in the peak minute produced a RestartWatch — and those two facts do not add up to 127/s, let alone 620/s. Do NOT patch this blind; the reproduction is here so the mechanism can be found first. (2) file_host.rs:1710, WakeOutcome::Died => deliver_died_blocking(&tx), is the only Died producer besides 1686 and it is unconditional: no counter, no single-flight. It is the unguarded twin of the arm 7cdb927 fixed.

VERIFY (a recurrence check; it is expected to be flat now and must not be used to close this while the rate is unexplained): no minute in the last 10 minutes carries more than 300 Died rows.
close_reason: done

principles.decision: resolve the operator's stated default once, at the one place that was missing, rather than adding config surface to express it

title: routing: pi as the default harness; drop pa/jcode/omp; deepseek-v4.1-flash; gpt-6-luna premium fallback
description:
Operator-directed routing change, 2026-09-29. Four parts, with the cost decision already made rather than parked.

1. pi IS THE DEFAULT HARNESS for a profile that names none. This resolves bd-ttaa, which recorded the missing concept rather than inventing it. The operator's stated choice becomes the compiled-in default, next to the tier constants.

   SCOPE, and it is deliberately narrow. It applies ONLY where nothing more specific exists: a profile with a CONCRETE model and an empty harness, which previously BAILED. A slot alias keeps its SLOT's harness, so `@cheap` still resolves to opencode/big-pickle and the free tier is intact. That is the whole point of the operator choosing this reading over `[defaults]`: `[defaults]` collapses every tier onto one pair and would have ended the free tier, because big-pickle is free on opencode only. A hardcoded default is NOT the invented policy bd-ttaa warned about — bd-ttaa objected to a default nobody had CHOSEN, and this one has.

   The gate on the default is structural, not a comment: the resolved harness must be a REGISTERED Open-tier harness, or the default is refused loudly. Naming a harness that does not exist, or one that may never be handed a model, would be the same class of bug as the Closed-tier substitution bd-ziy9 declined to make.

2. Remove `pa`, `jcode` and `omp` from the harness registry. SCALE, stated up front because it is not a config edit: `omp` has 193 code references, `pa` 27, `jcode` 19, and `scripts/verify-omp-role-models.sh` exists solely to verify omp role models, so it becomes dead. This is a multi-hour refactor across the registry, the compiled-in slots, and dozens of tests.

   The interaction that has to be handled rather than discovered: compiled-in `premium` is `omp/zai/glm-5.3`. Removing omp removes the premium slot's home harness, so a harness-less `@premium` would have no default. The operator's models.toml already overrides premium to pi, but the COMPILED-IN default must be consistent or a zero-config install regresses.

3. Replace `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` with `deepseek-v4.1-flash` under the same provider. This id appears in ~50 places across 12 files, including `verify-0007.sh` and `verify-omp-role-models.sh`, and several are ASSERTIONS on the literal, so this is a rename with teeth rather than a config swap.

4. Add `opencode-go/gpt-6-luna` as the premium tier's `model_fallback` — the slot field distinct from `fallback_harness` (ADR-0013 D4). It must be added to the OPERATOR's `[slots.premium]` explicitly as well as compiled-in, because `load_routing` does `slots.insert(name, spec)`, so a user block WHOLLY REPLACES the compiled-in spec rather than merging, and a field absent from the user block is absent from the result.

ACCEPTANCE. Every one of the four verified by running it, not by reading it: a no-harness concrete-model profile resolves to pi; `@cheap` still resolves to opencode/big-pickle; the removed harnesses are absent from the registry and from `profile show`; the new model id resolves and the old one does not; premium carries the new fallback and it fires when the primary is caps-blocked.

NOT DONE, deliberately. No configurable default-harness key — a hardcoded compiled-in default answers the operator's question, and a config surface wants its own ADR. No migration of anything that referenced the removed harnesses in historical run records; those are evidence. No attempt to preserve `verify-omp-role-models.sh`, which is dead the moment omp is gone — it is recorded rather than rewritten for a harness that no longer exists.
close_reason: Done. pi default, drop landed, deepseek rename, luna fallback, 21 fallout reds cleared. fix-root-causes — fixtures retargeted at the harness layer, not silenced.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
Landed at cd38735: `--request-key` on `steer` and `halt`, answered from each door's own intent-before-dispatch row.

- `steer`: the gate runs before the first effect (the AUTHORITATIVE MaterialContext fact) and before the intent row; the row settles only on an observed outcome — `settled` when the delegated run returns Ok, `unknown` when the dispatch fails, `failed` on an operator abort at the briefing gate (a known refusal, so the same key may be retried).
- `halt`: both `flywheel halt` and `supervisor halt` route through the one `queue_halt`, and the gate runs before the logged `Halt` is queued. The accepted epoch is resolved BEFORE the gate on purpose: a read that fails must not burn the receipt. The digest rides the OFFERED inputs (context, explicit epoch or `auto`), so a retry of the same call always matches while a different context is a different halt.
- Slots are namespaced per door (`<project>-steer` / `<project>-halt`) through one `door_slot`; a steer key can never name a halt slot.
- One rule, two row shapes: `gate_core` backs both `spawn_gate` (agent effect rows) and `receipt_gate` (the new `door_receipt` rows), so the four answers cannot drift between the pane doors and these.

Evidence:
- `door_receipt_replay_is_idempotent` — digest stability (including trimming), slot namespacing, and the four answers (Proceed / Replay / InFlight / Conflict) driven through the same gate the doors call, with the second attempt proven to send nothing.
- `the_steer_receipt_gate_precedes_dispatch` / `the_halt_receipt_gate_precedes_dispatch` — source-order fences (gate before intent, intent before the first effect, replay arm returns).
- Mutation proof, both fences: replacing each `receipt_gate` call with a literal fails "must consult the request-key receipt"; deleting each replay `return Ok(())` fails "a settled slot must return before …". Both reverted; the four receipt fences and the unit test are green after the revert (the two older spawn/add fences stayed green under both mutations, so the mutation is targeted).
- The bead's own declared fence run verbatim: `sh -c 'timeout 300 mbx +nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin test the_steer_receipt_gate_precedes_dispatch'` → "running 1 test", 1 passed, exit 0.
- Full suite: 2449 passed, 4 failed — `inbox_host` x2, `supervisor_host` (the hint-channel host-loop test, panicking in the same test that failed before this change; it reads the other writer's dirty `supervisor_hints.rs`), `supervisor_program` — all pre-existing. `cargo fmt --check` clean; `verify-clippy.sh` unchanged at the same 4 residuals (bd-gate-health-9a5b), none in the files of this commit.

Decision on `send`: it keeps `--param task_id` as its one reconcile spelling rather than growing a second `--request-key`; the task asked for a decision, and two spellings for one door is the worse outcome.

Limitation: proven at the gate + fence level; no live timed-out steer/halt retry against a real fleet.

title: bd-lorot
description: Log retention across the doorbell and toron. TWO unbounded sets, closed in two commits, both proven live. 3305eed2 bounds the AUDIT log by SIZE; c9ef76cd prunes JOURNALS by SCOPE and AGE. The asymmetry is the point: an audit file for a live workspace is worth keeping at any age, a journal for a dead workspace is worthless at any size. AUDIT: store.rs gave the journal a full discipline (512 KiB gate, RETENTION_LINES 5000, RETENTION_GENS 4, RETENTION_BYTES 5 MiB, generations, an audit row per drop) while file_host::append_audit_row was a bare OpenOptions::append + writeln! with nothing bounding it — exactly backwards, because the audit log records every per-attempt failure and is what a repeating fault writes to. One stale-socket respawn loop grew flywheel-toron.audit.jsonl to 14 GB (65,512,446 rows of one failure) and the doorbell state dir to 26 GB, while the bounded journal held 4705 rows. Now rotate_audit_if_oversized caps at 5 MiB keeping the newest 4000 rows, reads TAIL-ONLY (reading 14 GB to trim it would OOM the daemon), and swaps via temp+rename so a crash leaves the original intact. No generations — generations for a log written 65 M times an hour is how you get 26 GB. JOURNALS: one file per workspace the plane has EVER served, nothing ever removed any. known_journal_workspaces reports one entry per file, and that IS known_workspaces, which feeds the standby wake-blind signal — so 913 stale files were a PERMANENT FALSE ALARM in /health, not just 20 MB. Now prune_unhosted_workspace_logs runs on the EXISTING hourly rotate_tick (same tick that already copy-truncates the doorbell's own log; no new timer) and requires BOTH not-currently-hosted AND mtime older than 7 days. The age gate is what makes deleting live state safe: a just-spawned crew whose host loop has not written yet is never a candidate, so a live workspace's wake record cannot be removed. PruneReport counts removed/bytes_freed/skipped_young/remove_failed and is logged, because a prune that cannot report what it did becomes a mystery. FENCES: 6 for the audit cap (including one at real 6 MiB scale, and one pinning that rotation keeps the NEWEST rows, since a rotation that keeps the beginning cannot diagnose a live fault) and 3 for the prune (all three cases in one test — unhosted+old goes, HOSTED+old stays, unhosted+young stays; idempotence; and a bystander notes.jsonl that must survive so the prune cannot delete a shape it does not understand). FALSIFIED: disabling rotation reds the scale test; keeping the oldest rows reds the direction test; removing the live-workspace guard and removing the age gate each red the prune safety test independently. LIVE after install+restart: degraded reduced to ['journal_torn_tail'] alone (watch_restart_loop, standby_with_known_workspaces and inbox_fetch_failing all GONE); known_workspaces 858 -> 257 because the prune ran AT STARTUP (tokio::time::interval fires its first tick immediately); doorbell state 26 GB -> 516 KB; largest audit file 28 KB. FIXTURE CORRECTION recorded because it nearly became a false finding: the first prune fence passed a logical now in 2033, which made a file written seconds earlier look decades old and removed two files instead of one — the assertion was right and my fixture was wrong; it now uses real time. PRINCIPLES: fix-root-causes — a retention policy that does not exist for the highest-volume file is not a policy, and an unbounded counter feeding an alarm is a false alarm forever; prove-it-works — every guard is falsifiable independently, including the two that make DELETING live state safe, because an unfalsifiable guard is not a guard.
