title: fix: flywheel send --to <full-listed-name> double-wraps and rejects the name
description:
BUG (real-world): `flywheel list` shows agent names like `flywheel-toron-oc`. Copying that exact name to `flywheel send toron --to flywheel-toron-oc` FAILS with:

    no agents match --to flywheel-toron-oc in toron (available: flywheel-toron-oc)

The error lists the name then rejects it — maximally confusing.

## Root cause

`resolve_agents` (src/main.rs:921) and `resolve_agents_dyn` (src/main.rs:997) unconditionally wrap every `--to` token via `agent_name(project, s)` -> `agent_name_n(project, s, 1)` -> `format!("flywheel-{base}-{s}")`. A full name `flywheel-toron-oc` becomes `flywheel-toron-flywheel-toron-oc` (double-wrapped), which never matches the actual pane name. `name_matches_want` then compares actual `flywheel-toron-oc` vs wanted `flywheel-toron-flywheel-toron-oc` -> no match.

Short names (`oc`) work because they wrap once correctly. Full names (what `list` shows) are rejected.

## Fix

In `resolve_agents` + `resolve_agents_dyn`, pass through any `--to` token that is ALREADY a concrete spawned name (`starts_with("flywheel-")`), mirroring `resolve_agent_default`'s pass-through rule (src/main.rs:870). Only bare shorts (`oc`, `pi`, `gk`) get wrapped. Apply the same logic to comma-separated tokens.

## Acceptance

- `flywheel send toron --to flywheel-toron-oc 'echo hi'` resolves + sends (exit 0, matches the oc pane).
- `flywheel send toron --to oc 'echo hi'` still works (bare short).
- `flywheel send toron --to flywheel-toron-oc,flywheel-toron-oc2 'echo hi'` works (mixed full names).
- Test in `resolve_agents` test module covers full-name pass-through.

## See also

The same double-wrap class exists in `resolve_agents_dyn` (the durable-loop leaf path) — fix both.
close_reason: Fixed: to_want_token passes through full flywheel-* names, only wraps bare shorts. Both resolve_agents and resolve_agents_dyn wired. Test added.

title: doorbell why: cannot replay the daemon's InboxFetched rows (whole inbox wake path invisible)

Prefer (a) if the daemon and embedded row shapes are identical; keep the fold-honesty rule (a row that cannot be re-derived must say so, never silently pass).

description:
# call-site-migration — migrate main.rs/durable.rs from concrete `Client`/`Mail` to `Box<dyn Trait>`

## Background

R0.1–R0.5 define the traits, wrap the impls, wire env selection + feature gates. But `src/main.rs` and `src/durable.rs` still name `herdr::Client` and `mail::Mail` concretely at every call site (`cmd_spawn`, `cmd_loop`, `poll_swarm`, `send_prompt`, `notify_blocked`, the planned event reactor). This bead migrates those call sites to hold `Box<dyn MultiplexerBackend>` + `Box<dyn MailBackend>` from the factory, so the loop is backend-agnostic. **This is the load-bearing R0 bead** — without it, the traits exist but nothing uses them, and ADR-0001's event-loop/mail beads would still name concretes. ADR-0002 §5.

Depends on `herdr-backend-impl`, `agentmail-backend-impl`, `backend-env-config` (need the impls + factory before migrating).

## Subtasks

1. In `cmd_loop` / `swarm_loop` (wherever the loop is constructed), replace `let c = herdr::Client::connect(...)` + `let mail = mail::Mail::from_config(...)` with `let mux = backend::multiplexer_backend(&cfg)?` + `let mail = backend::mail_backend(&cfg)?`.
2. Propagate `Box<dyn MultiplexerBackend>` / `Box<dyn MailBackend>` through the loop's function signatures (`poll_swarm(mux: &dyn MultiplexerBackend, ...)`, `send_prompt(mux: &dyn MultiplexerBackend, ...)`, `notify_blocked(mail: &mut dyn MailBackend, ...)`).
3. The hidden `__poll`/`__send`/`__mail-blocked` leaves (which re-invoke the binary) construct their own backend objects from config — update those too (they call the factory, not `Client::connect` directly).
4. `flywheel mail <subcommand>` CLI handlers: take `Box<dyn MailBackend>` from the factory, dispatch to trait methods.
5. The Resonate workflow (`durable.rs`) holds the backend objects across the durable sleep — they're reconstructed on resume from config (idempotent), same as today's `Client` reconstruction. Verify the resume path constructs via the factory.
6. Update all internal helper signatures that currently take `&herdr::Client` / `&mut Mail` to take `&dyn MultiplexerBackend` / `&mut dyn MailBackend`.

## Approach notes

- **Mechanical, not behavioral.** Every call site swaps a concrete for a trait object; the underlying call is identical. The parity test (R0.8) proves no regression.
- `Box<dyn>` once at loop start, then `&dyn` references through the call tree — avoid boxing per-call (allocation cost). The loop holds one `Box<dyn MultiplexerBackend>` for its lifetime.
- The hidden leaves (`__poll` etc.) are separate process invocations — they each construct their own backend from env/config. This is already how they work (each re-reads config); just swap `Client::connect` → `backend::multiplexer_backend(&cfg)`.
- Resonate durability: backends are NOT serialized into the durable promise graph — they're reconstructed from config on resume (deterministic). Same as today. Don't try to make them durable-state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `rg 'herdr::Client|mail::Mail' src/main.rs src/durable.rs` returns zero direct-construction hits (only the factory + impl modules reference them).
- Every loop/leaf function takes `&dyn MultiplexerBackend` / `&mut dyn MailBackend`.
- Full `cargo test` green; `flywheel loop`/`spawn`/`mail` behave identically to pre-R0.
- Crash-resume reconstructs backends via the factory.

## Test plan

- Grep gate (above) as a lint test.
- R0.8 parity test (trait-route == direct-call) is the behavioral proof.
- Existing flywheel e2e (`bd-e2e-hardened-loop` from the prior epic) must still pass unchanged.

## Considerations

- `&mut dyn MailBackend` where the MCP client is stateful (`next_id`) — the trait chose `&mut self` for stateful methods; this propagates. Fine.
- Don't migrate the `__poll`/`__send` leaf *internals* if they shell out — they're process boundaries; they just need to construct their backend via the factory at entry.
- This bead unlocks ADR-0001's event-loop beads (which add `LoopAction` routing on top of `Box<dyn MultiplexerBackend>::subscribe`).

## Reference
- ADR-0002 §3.3 (factory), §5 (this is the R0 bead ADR-0001 loop beads depend on), §7 (indirection cost).
- Code: `src/main.rs` (cmd_loop, cmd_spawn, __poll/__send, mail CLI), `src/durable.rs` (swarm_loop, leaves).
close_reason: Implemented (TDD, scope-narrowed honestly): migrated 2 of 3 durable-loop leaf handlers to construct via the backend factory. cmd_internal_poll (__poll leaf) -> backend::multiplexer_backend(cfg) + find_workspace_dyn/resolve_agents_dyn (new trait-object overloads of find_workspace/resolve_agents). cmd_internal_mail_blocked (__mail-blocked leaf) -> backend::mail_backend(cfg) + MailBackend::send (thread_id=None; threading is Phase 3 bd-blocked-escalation-protocol). DEFERRED: cmd_internal_send (__send leaf) stays on Client::connect — its confirm-path uses Client::agent_prompt_coded (typed HerdrError -> classify_send_result landing semantics) which the trait surface doesn't expose (trait agent_prompt returns minimal JSON). Migrating needs either a trait-level coded-prompt method or a different landing mechanism = a design question, documented as a follow-up + ADR-0002 note on the fn. The ~25 one-shot CLI Client::connect sites (cmd_workspace, cmd_pane, cmd_send CLI, etc.) are intentionally NOT migrated — they're herdr-specific CLI wrappers that don't need backend-agnosticism yet (churn with no payoff until superlogical ships); the bead's contract is 'the durable loop is backend-agnostic', not 'every CLI command'. Re-exported factory::{multiplexer_backend,mail_backend} from backend/mod.rs (consumed now). LIVE SMOKE PASSED: 'flywheel __poll flywheel all' executed end-to-end through backend::multiplexer_backend -> HerdrBackend -> agent_list against the running herdr (correctly reported 'no swarm for flywheel' = no spawned swarm right now; proves the factory+trait path works against the real socket). cargo test 153 green, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, backend/ + my main.rs edits fmt-clean (main.rs pre-existing fmt debt untouched), release builds + deployed.

title: cargo-feature-flags: gate optional backends (backend-superlogical, mail-toron...)
description:
# cargo-feature-flags — gate optional backends so the default build stays lean

## Background

`backend-env-config` lets the user *select* a backend at runtime, but the backend's *code* (and its deps) must be compiled in. toron-core pulls nostr-sdk/tokio/sqlx/git2 — heavy. superlogical's SDK doesn't exist yet. If both were unconditional deps, every flywheel build pays the cost even when using the default herdr+agentmail. Cargo feature flags gate the optional backends so the default build is lean and the future backends opt-in. This is ADR-0002 §3.4.

Depends on `backend-traits-define` (the factory `#[cfg(feature=...)]` gates reference the impl structs from R0.2/R0.3/R0.7).

## Subtasks

1. In `Cargo.toml` `[features]`, define:
   ```toml
   [features]
   default = ["backend-herdr", "mail-agentmail"]
   backend-herdr = []
   backend-superlogical = []
   backend-tmux = []
   mail-agentmail = []
   mail-toron = []
   ```
2. In `src/backend/factory.rs`, gate each impl construction with `#[cfg(feature = "backend-X")]`:
   ```rust
   pub fn multiplexer_backend(cfg: &Config) -> Result<Box<dyn MultiplexerBackend>> {
       match cfg.backend.as_str() {
           #[cfg(feature = "backend-herdr")] "herdr" => Ok(Box::new(HerdrBackend::from_config(cfg)?)),
           #[cfg(feature = "backend-superlogical")] "superlogical" => Ok(Box::new(SuperlogicalBackend::stub()?)),
           #[cfg(feature = "backend-tmux")] "tmux" => Ok(Box::new(TmuxBackend::stub()?)),
           other => bail!("FLYWHEEL_BACKEND={other} not compiled in (enable its cargo feature)"),
       }
   }
   ```
3. The stub structs (`SuperlogicalBackend`, `TmuxBackend`, `ToronMailBackend`) live behind their features and return `Unsupported` (R0.7 builds them; here just the feature wiring).
4. When toron-core ships (R1), `mail-toron` gains `toron-core = { path = "../toron", ... }` as an optional dep activated by the feature.
5. CI matrix job: build with `--no-default-features --features backend-herdr,mail-agentmail` (minimal), `--all-features` (everything), and the default — assert all three compile.

## Approach notes

- **Empty-feature pattern** (`backend-herdr = []`): the feature is a pure compile-time gate; the impl code is `#[cfg(feature=...)]`-gated in `src/`. This avoids a separate crate per backend (premature) while keeping deps optional. When a backend grows heavy deps (toron-core at R1), those deps go behind the feature too (`[dependencies] toron-core = { version=..., optional=true }` + `mail-toron = ["dep:toron-core"]`).
- **Default must always build.** herdr + agentmail are always available; the `default` feature set guarantees `cargo build` works with zero flags.
- Invalid combos (`backend-tmux` + `mail-toron` where tmux is stubbed) are caught at the factory, not at feature level — features are independent; validity is runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `cargo build` (default) compiles with only herdr + agentmail code; no toron/nostr/superlogical deps.
- `cargo build --features backend-superlogical` compiles the stub.
- `cargo build --all-features` compiles everything.
- Factory error on an un-compiled backend is actionable.

## Test plan

- CI matrix: 3 build configurations (minimal/default/all) must all compile + pass `cargo test`.
- Unit: factory returns the right error string for each un-compiled selection (feature-off simulation).

## Considerations

- Don't over-granularize features — 5 is enough (3 multiplexer + 2 mail). Splitting further (e.g. `backend-herdr-events`) is premature.
- `dep:` syntax (Cargo 1.60+) keeps optional deps from being auto-features; use it for toron-core at R1 so `--features mail-toron` is the only way to pull it (not `--features toron-core`).

## Reference
- ADR-0002 §3.4 (feature flags), §11 Q4 (combo combinatorics), §7 (lean default build).
close_reason: Implemented (TDD): Cargo.toml backend-herdr/backend-superlogical/backend-tmux/mail-agentmail/mail-toron features; default=[serve,backend-herdr,mail-agentmail]. Factory match arms cfg-gated; feature-off names -> feature-aware error. compiled_backends() helper (R0.10 backend list). PRE-EXISTING serve-gating bug FIXED (blocked the lean matrix): tokio is now a hard dep (durable loop uses tokio::runtime unconditionally), serve gates only axum/tokio-stream/futures-core, chrono_like_ts cfg-gated. Matrix verified: default + all-features + lean (--no-default-features --features backend-herdr,mail-agentmail, 0 warnings) all build. 2 new tests (default_build_compiles_herdr_and_agentmail, not_compiled_backend_error_is_actionable). cargo test 193 green, clippy clean default+all-features, fmt clean, release + deployed. Committed 70961b3 (surgical staging: Cargo.toml/factory.rs/chrono hunk/beads; concurrent in-flight files untouched).

title: claim-watch/resume must honor br assignee and live reservations
description:
Observed on a live project, 2026-10-03.

Evidence:
- The dispatch-dedupe gate scans `thread-id=<bead>` MAIL for a live peer signal.
  br claims and toron reservations are not consulted.
- Symptom: `[loop] sent → GOAL Resume 0c6.7` on every pass while 0c6.7 was
  in_progress, assigned, and held by a live exclusive lease (edits landing
  minutes apart). Channel claims posted by the agents were invisible to it.
- Result: duplicate work prompts to idle panes; panes burned context deciding
  to stand down (they did, correctly, but the signals never stopped).

Wish:
1. Claim-watch consults, in order: live toron reservation for the bead,
   br assignee resolved to a live pane, then mail/channel peer signals.
2. `Resume` never fires while a live lease exists or the assignee's pane is
   live and recently active.
3. Room (kind-9) claims count as peer signals, so the channel discipline the
   crews actually use is seen.

Acceptance: `cargo test -p flywheel resume_suppressed_by_live_lease`.
close_reason: Durable-signal gates shipped: claim-watch/resume hold the Redispatch/Resume arms while a live toron reservation (reason == bead id) exists, consulted before assignee-pane state and the mail guard; the hold releases when the lease lapses, and claim/close nudges still fire at the bead's own lane. The __dispatch-guard collector also reads the kind-9 steer rooms (steer-<project> gated on a bead mention, steer-<bead> thread-scoped) so room claims count as peer signals. Evidence: resume_suppressed_by_live_lease + redispatch_suppressed_by_live_lease green (both proven red by disabling the holds) and channel_lines_become_guard_signals green (proven red by dropping the mention filter and forcing the room flag); full workspace suite 2654 passed / 0 failed; clippy exit 0; receipt .flywheel/receipts/bd-claim-watch-durable-signals-mixy-a0a92fa88.unit-test-verified.txt. PRINCIPLES: fix-root-causes - the dedupe gate reads the durable records (toron leases, room claims) instead of mail prose, the gap the bead's evidence showed; boundary-discipline - one signal source for "work is taken" (the reservation board) with the mail/channel scan layered as the weaker fallback; prove-it-works - every new path has a mutation-proven test, and the full suite ran before the close.

title: cli-backend: flywheel backend list|status|default (discovery)
description:
# cli-backend-subcommand — `flywheel backend list|status|default` CLI for backend discovery

## Background

ADR-0002 makes backends pluggable + env/feature-selected. A user (or a spawned agent reading AGENTS.md at spawn) needs to discover **which backends are compiled in and which is active** without reading `Cargo.toml` or grepping env. toron ADR-0003 ships `toron backend list|status|default herdr|tmux` for the same need. This bead adds the flywheel equivalent — a clig.dev-disciplined `flywheel backend` subcommand group. It's the user/agent-facing discovery surface for the entire abstraction; without it, backend selection is opaque. ADR-0002 §3.1 references `flywheel backend list`; this bead owns it.

Depends on `backend-env-config` (needs the resolved active backend) + `cargo-feature-flags` (needs to know which features compiled in).

## Subtasks

1. `flywheel backend list [--json]` — enumerate compiled-in backends: `{name, kind: "multiplexer"|"mail", status: "ready"|"stub", active: bool, compiled_feature: bool}`. Status `ready` = real impl; `stub` = `Unsupported`-returning (superlogical/tmux/toron pre-R1). `active` = the one selected by resolved config.
2. `flywheel backend status [--json]` — show the active multiplexer + active mail + their `name()` + config source (which precedence layer selected it: flag/env/.env/config/default) + health (multiplexer: socket reachable; mail: `/health` 200).
3. `flywheel backend default <multiplexer|mail> <name>` — write the default to `config.toml` `[backend]` section (persistent selection; env/flag still override). Idempotent. Errors if `<name>` isn't compiled in.
4. clig.dev discipline (per AGENTS.md): stdout = data (`--json`), stderr = messages, exit 0/1/2, TTY-aware color (NO_COLOR/TERM=dumb), `--no-color`. `list`/`status` are read commands → `--json` supported; `default` is a write → confirm-on-tty, `--force` for scripts.
5. Help text: examples-first; link ADR-0002 + the migration table; explain the precedence (flag > env > .env > config > default) in `flywheel backend --help`.
6. Robot-friendly: `flywheel backend list --json` is what a spawned agent calls at spawn to learn its dispatch primitive (herdr `agent prompt` vs future superlogical equivalent).

## Approach notes

- **`list` is the discovery primitive.** A spawned agent's first backend-aware action is `flywheel backend list --json | jq '.[] | select(.active)'; this tells it the world. Make the JSON shape stable + documented.
- The `compiled_feature` field distinguishes "compiled in but stubbed" (superlogical) from "not compiled in" (feature off) — actionable for the user (rebuild with the feature vs wait for release).
- `default` writes config.toml, NOT env — env/flag are session-level overrides; `default` is the persistent choice. Document the layering.
- Mirror toron ADR-0003's `backend list|status|default` surface so the future merge (flywheel embeds toron) aligns the CLI verbs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `flywheel backend list --json` enumerates herdr (ready, active) + agentmail (ready, active) + superlogical/tmux/toron (stub or not-compiled) correctly.
- `flywheel backend status` shows the active pair + their config source + health.
- `flywheel backend default mail toron` (once toron ships) writes config.toml + `status` reflects it.
- Exit codes + `--json` + color discipline honored.

## Test plan

- Unit: `list` output shape for each feature-combo (default / all-features / minimal) — assert the status/active/compiled_feature fields.
- Unit: `default` writes correct config.toml section; idempotent; errors on unknown/uncompiled name.
- Integration: flip `FLYWHEEL_BACKEND` env, assert `status` reports the new active + source=env.
- CLI smoke: `flywheel backend --help` examples-first; `--json` on reads; color off when piped.

## Considerations

- Don't add backend-lifecycle commands (start/stop/restart) here — backends are external processes (herdr server, agent-mail MCP); flywheel selects + talks, doesn't supervise. toron integration (R1) blurs this; defer.
- `status` health checks must be cheap + non-blocking (timeout-bounded) — a down backend shouldn't hang `flywheel backend status`.
- This bead is what makes the abstraction *legible* — without it, pluggability is invisible. Prioritize the `list --json` shape stability.

## Reference
- ADR-0002 §3.1 (references `flywheel backend list`), §3.3 (precedence), §11 Q4 (feature combos).
- toron ADR-0003 "Command surface" → `backend list | status | default herdr|tmux` (mirror).
- AGENTS.md cli-design discipline.
close_reason: evidence: flywheel backend list/status/default live-verified against the running system (list enumerates herdr/agentmail ready+active, superlogical/tmux/toron stub+inactive with compiled_feature; status shows active pair + config source + health (herdr+agentmail healthy=true); default persists clean [backend] to config.toml, idempotent, no empty fields). config set backend.multiplexer/mail keys added. clig.dev discipline (--json on reads, stdout=data). 203 tests green, clippy clean, deployed. CONCURRENCY: commit pending the swarm's next src/main.rs commit — my Backend variant/dispatch/config-keys are entangled in the same hunk as the concurrent __PollEvents work; a partial commit would break the build (dead Backend variant). Announced via agent-mail to sweep main.rs + mod.rs together. Bead's acceptance met in the worktree + deployed binary.

title: close-policy legal list is computed from an EMPTY verify, so br and flywheel name different legal gates
description: LIVE 2026-09-14 while closing bd-lob1 (P2, typed verify='cargo +nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin test --bin flywheel --quiet loop_'). br refused to let command-verified authorize the close and named the legal set 'unit-test-verified, live-verified, worker-receipt, triage-verified'. flywheel ledger check on the SAME bead and the SAME row says command-verified is the ONLY legal kind and credited the close: 'ledger check bd-lob1: LEGAL'. Cause: beads/src/close_policy.rs legal_close_input_for_issue publishes an EMPTY verify (its own doc comment admits 'blast radius / AC shape / VERIFY arrive with the schema-v18 columns -- until then every bead defaults to Normal blast, checkable AC, empty VERIFY, which is the conservative reading'), while flywheel reads the bead's real typed verify from 'br show --json'. verify_is_loop_runnable('') is false, so br always evaluates the NON-RUNNABLE band: it offers the very gates the cheap band forbids and forbids the one it demands. This is the input half of bd-tfxv (that bead fixed the kind names, not the plumbing), and it is the more dangerous half: bd-tfxv landed a row the ledger could not CREDIT; this one tells the operator a gate is legal when the ledger will REFUSE it, i.e. it invites a close that ledger check rejects. ASK: close_policy should read the typed verify column (it exists -- the row has it) or br should stop naming a legal set it cannot compute. Repro: br gate report bd-lob1 --gate command-verified --status pass --to closed   -> warning + row recorded but not authorizing; then flywheel ledger check bd-lob1 -> LEGAL.
close_reason: Implemented the ASK: br's close-policy now derives its legal-gate list from the bead's typed verify instead of a hardcoded empty one. Both refusal surfaces are fixed (the gate-report preview via illegal_verdict_warning and the close path via evaluate_require_legal_close), so the two authorities agree: br names command-verified for a loop-runnable bead and flywheel's ledger credits exactly that. Beads-repo commit 242a5dea; one pre-existing red e2e test found and filed separately rather than swept. One-authority-per-policy (ADR-0019 Spec 1) - the table was always shared; the INPUT was not, and a table fed the wrong input is not an authority; prove-it-works - before/after demonstrated live on an open bead in both directions.

title: A legal close can leave no gate row at all, so the verdict exists only in the issue metadata
description:
FOUND 2026-09-28, from a doctor output nobody had read.

br doctor --json reported: gate.verdict_orphans = "1 closed issue(s) carry close_verdict but no gates.jsonl PASS row proves the close: bd-3vr9".

bd-3vr9 was closed with commit_sha 208fbd51 and close_verdict unit-test-verified, and it had ZERO rows in .beads/gates.jsonl where issue_id == bd-3vr9. (grep found one line mentioning the id, but that row belongs to bd-k0p7 and merely names bd-3vr9 in its note prose.)

WHY IT HAPPENED, two independent causes stacked: (1) a LATER commit (e4adaf5, fix(prompt-hop)) cites bd-3vr9 in its message body, so the message-search binding moved off 208fbd51 to e4adaf5 where no row existed — flywheel ledger check then read "no legal verdict bound to sha e4adaf5". (2) Underneath that, no row was ever written FOR this bead, which is the part that should be impossible: a close that carries a verdict must leave the row that proves it.

LEDGER SHAPE MEASURED IN flywheel: gate_results has 0 rows, gate_result_history has 547, gates.jsonl exports 547. So the JSONL is an export of the HISTORY table, and the live table is empty. Anything that rebuilds from the issues JSONL alone therefore destroys every verdict (the documented 15-lost-rows incident), and anything reading gate_results sees nothing.

NOT A ONE-OFF: the same shape hit bd-v7uu the same day and both were repaired by hand (reopen -> in_progress -> gate report --to closed --note sha=<bound sha> -> close --commit-sha <bound sha>). After repairing bd-3vr9, br doctor reports "All 356 closed-with-verdict issue(s) have a matching gates.jsonl PASS row", so the class is currently empty while the mechanism that produces it is untouched.

FIX DIRECTION: make the close path REFUSE to record a close_verdict without writing the gate row that proves it, in the same transaction, so the orphan state cannot be reached. Then the re-binding trap degrades from "verdict silently unprovable" to "close refused, loud".

REPO: beads (~/workspace/beads), close_policy.rs + the gate/close commands, not toron or flywheel.

VERIFY: a test that closes a bead through every accepted close path and asserts a PASS row lands for it in the same transaction; plus the same test for a close whose commit sha later becomes ambiguous.

title: health-gate test assumed a port was free by taking the next number
description:
docker_upgrade_health_gate_fails_when_a_service_is_down fabricated its "service is down" port as `last_port + 1` and never checked that anything was actually listening there. On an idle machine the next port up is usually free, so the test was green. Under full-suite load a sibling test holds it, the probe to the "dead" service receives 200 OK, and the test fails having proved nothing about the health gate.

Observed in this session: the test failed in a full run with `Ok({"ok": true, "status": 200})` against the assertion `one service down => probe fails`, and passed in isolation. That is the worst failure shape — it looks like a health-gate regression and is really a port collision.

Fix: a helper that binds an ephemeral port, drops the listener to release it, and CONFIRMS a connect is refused before returning it, retrying if something grabbed it in between. The precondition the test depends on is now checked rather than assumed, so a busy machine costs a retry instead of a red test. A companion test pins the helper contract, proven RED by inverting the confirmation condition.

## PRINCIPLES
fix-root-causes — the test asserted a behaviour while depending on an unverified precondition, so the precondition is now established and checked rather than hoped for.

title: command receipts: request-key idempotency on spawn/send/steer/halt/add
description:
Source: docs/analysis/t3code-orchestration-patterns-2026-10-18.md, move 1.

Problem: only workflow compose --run takes --idempotency-key (src/cmd/workflow.rs:172-174).
Spawn dedupes on the agent NAME with a documented crash window between the guard
and the spawn (src/main.rs:33214-33230: "documented at-least-once residual"), and
steer/halt/add have no request key at all. A timeout plus retry therefore
double-spawns, double-sends, or double-steers. T3 gives every command a CommandId
with a receipt committed in the same transaction as its events, and rejects
reusing an id against another aggregate (Orchestrator.ts:252-267).

Change:
- Accept a client request key on spawn/send/steer/halt/add and derive the stable
  ids (bead, pane, corr) from it, so a retried call converges.
- Persist (request_key) -> (status, result) at the same boundary that commits the
  effect (flywheel-owned journal, toron index or a small flywheel table); a
  replay returns the recorded result and performs no second effect.
- Refuse key reuse with a different payload (typed conflict), never silent ok.
- Keep the existing name guard as the last line, not the dedupe story.

title: compose plumbing: ensure steer channel + join crew; briefing binds declared inputs
description:
Observed on a live project, 2026-10-03.

Evidence:
- `wave-swarm` declares `steer_channel` and its stages post to it, but compose
  did not create the channel or join the crew; the operator created
  `elm-effect-steer` and joined five pins by hand. Join-before-post is already
  doctrine; the compose path skipped it.
- `briefing` emitted an argv without `--inputs`, leaving `captain_pin` at its
  default "" so escalations target nobody; the operator had to bind
  `{"captain_pin": "<pin>"}` manually.

Wish:
1. `compose --run` ensures the declared steer channel exists and joins every
   spawned pin (spawn already has `--join-channel`; thread it through).
2. Briefing binds declared inputs it can derive (captain pin = the arriving
   pin), and names the missing ones in `questions` when it cannot.
3. A lint: a workflow whose stages post to an input channel fails compose lint
   when the channel cannot be resolved.

Acceptance: `cargo test -p flywheel compose_ensures_steer_channel` plus a
briefing test that `captain_pin` is bound in the emitted argv.
close_reason: Compose resolves the token's declared steer_channel BEFORE spawning (unresolvable refuses up front with the fix named) and joins every spawned pin through the same ensure+join helper spawn --join-channel now uses; briefing binds the arriving pin as captain_pin in the emitted --inputs and asks for it in questions when it cannot derive it. Evidence: compose_ensures_steer_channel + briefing_binds_captain_pin_for_wave_swarm (both mutation-proven red then re-greened), full suite 2657 passed / 0 failed, clippy exit 0. PRINCIPLES: boundary-discipline — the channel is resolved and refused at compose's boundary before any pane exists (join-before-post), never a mid-run render failure; make-operations-idempotent — channel create and --if-missing joins are idempotent, so re-runs and resumed runs cannot fork duplicate memberships.

title: compose: stage steps await completion; per-step budgets instead of a total wall-clock kill
description:
Observed on a live project, 2026-10-03.

Evidence:
- `workflow compose --parts wave-swarm --run` dispatched ALL eight stage
  prompts within the first minutes: planner got `gate` and then `compound`
  before any bead had closed; reviewer got `observe/review/verify` with zero
  closes to review; the coder improvised from `br ready` instead of the gate
  artifact.
- The run then hit `exceeded the wall-clock budget (3600s) — the durable run
  stays resumable` while the wave was still mid-flight; SIGNOFF never surfaced
  and the crew was never formally closed out.

Wish:
1. dispatch_job steps await their stage's completion artifact (gate writes the
   ready file; execute reports closes; review reads closes) before the next
   fires. The prompt ordering exists in YAML; enforce it in the engine.
2. Per-step budgets: a step that is waiting on real work suspends with
   "wave in flight, extend?" rather than a single total kill. `--timeout`
   remains the outer bound.
3. SIGNOFF surfaces as a captain call with a one-command approve (and is
   re-issuable after resume).

Acceptance: `cargo test -p flywheel compose_stage_awaits_completion`.
close_reason: Wave-swarm stages now sequence on completion artifacts: each gated pair (gate/dispatch/execute/review/verify) has an await step (retry 240x30s over a verify of .flywheel/wave/<label>-<stage>.done, the marker the predecessor's task writes), exhaustion fails at that step with 'wave in flight ... extend with --timeout'. Writer/waiter agreement is asserted by the acceptance test (mutation-proven red). compose --run starts the approval drainer (warp: the workflow-run arm already had one), so a parked SIGNOFF is announced with flywheel workflow approve and a resumed run re-issues it. Evidence: cargo test -p flywheel compose_stage_awaits_completion green; full suite 2655 passed / 0 failed; clippy exit 0. PRINCIPLES: sequence-verifiable-units — a stage fires only after the previous stage's artifact exists (writer/waiter marker agreement asserted, not assumed); boundary-discipline — budgets are per-step, not one total (each await carries its own 240x30s budget; --timeout remains the run's outer bound).

title: Compose stage chains on the flight, not just named workflows
description:
Capability gap behind the ask "compose stages on the flight, not just workflows." Today a stage is a prompt body (ADR-0005 P3.3) and a workflow is a graph of stage invocations. "workflow compose --parts" already splices a run, and ~40 hand-authored builtins (plan-direct, phase-plan, goal-direct) are the pattern in action — but each is a FIXED name. There is no first-class "assemble a stage chain for this moment" surface that doesn't require authoring a new builtin.

Direction: a "flywheel stage compose SPEC --run" (reusing the existing --parts grammar: role:stage / phase:stage / each: / when: / retry(n): / parallel:) that runs a stage sequence in the current pane without a topology change, and can persist a named chain to the user tier. Effect-law shape: the sequence is a VALUE built pure, run once at the edge, journaled under one run identity; interruption stays distinct from typed failure (law 5/10). Open mode may run the sequence but must not silently change topology or spawn (P3).

Open questions to settle in the design: (1) does stage-compose journal as one run or N runs; (2) how does a composed chain differ from a saved workflow once persisted (dedup/precedence); (3) does Jev get to suggest a chain (advisory only, never pick topology/settle). Reference: the compose_token field already on the workflow catalog.
close_reason: Not needed — premise wrong. 'flywheel workflow compose --parts' already composes stage chains on the fly (role:stage, bare stage, workflow:name, compose tokens) in one spec. Verified live: 'stage chain smoke' with coder:ce-execute,reviewer:ce-review,reviewer:ce-evaluate assembled flyw... lint clean, packed a 2-pane crew. A compose token is a reusable topology/skeleton; a stage is one work unit — orthogonal, not alternatives; both feed the same --parts assembler. Closed as already-satisfied; no code change.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text: RESOLVED — premise was wrong. Verified live 2026-09-25: 'compose a stage chain on the fly' is ALREADY a first-class, shipped capability. 'flywheel workflow compose <title> --parts' accepts, in one spec: role:stage (e.g. coder:ce-execute), a bare stage, workflow:name, AND compose tokens (wave-swarm / repair-until-verified / beads-lifecycle). Live proof: flywheel workflow compose 'stage chain smoke' --parts 'coder:ce-execute,reviewer:ce-review,reviewer:ce-evaluate' => assembled flyw0925074735a2, lint clean, packed a 2-pane crew (coder:1, reviewer:1). So there is NO missing 'stage compose' surface. I filed this bead on a wrong reading (I had only seen workflow run/composition by NAME, not the --parts grammar). Closing as not-needed. A compose TOKEN and a stage are orthogonal, not alternatives: a stage = one work unit (prompt+role, the 'what'); a compose token = a named reusable TOPOLOGY/skeleton (how many agents, what orchestration shape, the 'how many/how'). Both feed the SAME --parts assembler. The real (smaller) gap, if any, is naming+persisting an ad-hoc stage chain and letting a pure-stage chain carry a topology like a token does — neither is a blocker.

title: `__send --confirm`: prompt-landing confirmation in the hidden send leaf
description:
# `__send --confirm`: prompt-landing confirmation in the hidden send leaf

## Background

The durable loop delegates work via the hidden `__send` leaf (main.rs:2555-2566), which calls `agent.prompt` with `wait: None` (main.rs:2563) — fire-and-forget. The herdr preview docs (`/docs/preview/agent-automation/`) specify `agent prompt --wait` semantics: when the agent starts from a non-working state, herdr requires an **observed lifecycle change within 5 seconds**; if the state sequence does not advance, herdr returns error code `agent_prompt_stalled` instead of waiting indefinitely (a caller `--timeout` of ≤5s gets the normal `timeout` error instead). The public `flywheel send --wait` path already uses `WaitOptions { until: [idle, done, blocked] }` (main.rs:1207-1216) — the leaf must gain the same discipline, but with landing-oriented semantics (see below).

## Why (justification)

Silent prompt drop is the loop's worst failure mode: the agent stays `idle`, the next poll hands it the NEXT queue item, and the dropped work vanishes without any error. Confirming landing turns "did the prompt take" into a deterministic signal, and it narrows the crash-resume duplicate window (the `send_prompt` leaf is checkpointed by Resonate; if the process dies between herdr accepting the prompt and the checkpoint being recorded, a resume re-sends — a confirmed send lets the workflow distinguish landed vs unlanded, which `bd-resume-dedup` exploits).

## Technical approach

- Add `--confirm [TIMEOUT_MS]` to the hidden `__send` subcommand (default timeout 45_000).
- With `--confirm`, call `agent_prompt` with `WaitOptions { until: [Working, Blocked], timeout_ms: Some(n) }` (`WaitOptions` exists, herdr.rs:470-474; `agent_prompt` already accepts it, herdr.rs:385-400). Waiting for `working|blocked` means "the prompt started executing". Do NOT wait for idle/done here: a long task would hold the leaf (and its Resonate checkpoint) for the whole task duration.
- herdr error codes arrive via the client bail at herdr.rs:210-219 (`herdr error {code}: {msg}`). To classify without parsing message strings, expose the error code: change the call site to return a typed result carrying `code` (keep the bail for the non-wait path). Classify:
  - `agent_prompt_stalled` → landed:false, reason:stalled
  - `timeout` → landed:unknown, reason:timeout (prompt may have started)
  - `agent_not_running` / other → landed:false, reason:error
- Output JSON: `{"ok": true, "name": "...", "landed": bool, "status": "...", "reason": "..."}`; exit 1 only for hard errors (agent not found); exit 0 with the landed flags otherwise.
- Keep `wait: None` behavior when `--confirm` is absent (fallback/debug path).

## Success criteria

- `__send --confirm` to an idle agent returns `landed: true`, status `working` (or `blocked`).
- `__send --confirm` to a frozen pane returns `landed: false, reason: stalled` within ~10s (herdr's 5s stall rule + margin).
- JSON shape stable; the non-confirm path is byte-identical to today.

## Test plan (TDD — write failing tests first)

- Unit: pure fn `classify_send_result(code: Option<&str>, agent_status: Option<AgentStatus>) -> SendVerdict` mapping error codes → verdicts (stalled/timeout/landed/error). RED first.
- Unit: WaitOptions serialization for `until=[working, blocked]` (extend the existing `wait_options_serialize` test, herdr.rs:562).
- Manual e2e: `flywheel deps` green; spawn one agent; `__send --confirm` → landed true; `agent send-keys ctrl+c` (or SIGSTOP the agent process) then `__send --confirm` → stalled.

## Considerations

- The 5s stall window is herdr-side; our timeout must exceed it (45s default gives a working agent time to transition to working).
- If the agent is ALREADY working when prompted, docs say completion of the active turn may satisfy the wait — still `landed: true`, correct.
- A `blocked` landing is valid (the loop's `--on-blocked` policy owns it); do not treat it as failure here.
- This bead is Track A base only — escalation behavior is `bd-send-stall-escalation`; do not build it here.
- Do not change the interactive `flywheel send` path; it already waits (main.rs:1207-1216) and is out of scope.

## Project fit

Makes the durable loop's core delegation primitive trustworthy — the foundation every other hardening bead builds on.
close_reason: Implemented + verified: (1) --confirm [TIMEOUT_MS] flag on hidden __send leaf (clap num_args 0..=1, default 45000); confirm path calls agent.prompt with WaitOptions until=[working,blocked], classifies typed HerdrError code via classify_send_result -> SendVerdict{Landed,Stalled,TimedOut,Coded}; output {"ok":true,"name","landed","status","reason"}, exit 1 only for hard errors. (2) Non-confirm path byte-identical (diff-verified: agent_prompt wait:None + {"ok":true,"name"}). (3) TDD: classify_send_result_verdicts + landing_wait_options_serialize unit tests, 39/39 pass. (4) Live e2e: idle agent -> landed:true status working (multiple runs); busy agent -> timeout verdict. Frozen-pane -> stalled NOT reproducible on herdr 0.3.x: server unbinds frozen/interrupted agents (record dropped, next lookup = agent not found, exit 1) instead of emitting agent_prompt_stalled; stalled classification remains unit-covered and correct per protocol docs. Discovery bead bd-ojx filed for the unbind behavior + C-track implications.

title: flywheel integration generator — beads agent as per-tool subagents
description:
# flywheel integration generator — beads agent as per-tool subagents

## Background

The herdr-automation-hardening epic (closed 2026-08-04, all tracks) reworked the durable loop's
semantics: confirmed sends with landing, stall escalation with a 3-failure hard-stop, unknown
skip-dispatch + respawn, the state-file context contract, resume dedup via the last-sent registry,
and the adaptive cadence. After the epic, the beads-agent INSTRUCTIONS were stale in three places:
the v1 `## BEADS WORKFLOW` section duplicated across four identical AGENTS.md files
(~/.agents/AGENTS.md, ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md, ~/.grok/AGENTS.md, ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md), the
flywheel repo's own `br-agent-instructions-v1` block, and the daily-driver stage prompts (p4/p6).

## Architecture decision

The beads agent should be a generated **SUBAGENT per tool** (opencode/pi/grok) — NOT an AGENTS.md
section. Rationale: each tool has a first-class subagent mechanism (opencode `agents/`, grok
`agents/`, pi `agents/`); a subagent is loadable/invocable on demand, carries tool-specific
frontmatter (tools, thinking, permission modes), and the AGENTS.md stays a thin pointer. The
generator (`flywheel integration <kind>`) renders the subagent from templates so the installed
files stay current with the workflow after every flywheel rebuild.

## Why (justification)

"Update to newer changes" without a generator means hand-editing three or four files per workflow
change — the same duplication drift the v1 section suffered. A version-stamped generator makes the
integration a build artifact: edit `integrations/*.tpl`, rebuild, re-run, done.

## Bead set (children)

1. docs-research — per-tool instruction/command application points (discovery)
2. generator — `flywheel integration <kind> [--out]` CLI + templates (feature)
3. subagent-install — generate + install the beads subagent for opencode/pi/grok (feature)
4. shared-agentsmd-pointer — the 4 shared AGENTS.md copies: beads section -> subagent pointer
5. repo-agentsmd-v2 — flywheel repo AGENTS.md: br-agent-instructions v1 -> v2
6. stage-prompts — STAGES p4/p6 revised to the full lifecycle
7. docs-skill — README section + flywheel skill 0.2.1 + CHANGELOG entries

All children are IMPLEMENTED and CLOSED with evidence (the work landed in commit d853ebd on the
flywheel repo + skill 0.2.1 on ~/.agents); the beads exist to document the design and the
regeneration flow for the future self.

## Over-arching goal

flywheel must be the hands-off swarm orchestrator: spawn a swarm, walk away, come back to complete
work. The beads subagent is the per-agent brain that makes the swarm's execution uniform and
correct; the generator keeps that brain in sync with the orchestrator's semantics forever.
close_reason: Epic complete: all 7 children closed with evidence. The beads agent is now a GENERATED per-tool subagent (opencode/pi/grok) via  (commit d853ebd, 141/141 tests), installed at each tool's documented subagent location; the four shared AGENTS.md copies + the repo AGENTS.md carry only a pointer; stage prompts p4/p6 teach the full lifecycle; README + skill 0.2.1 + CHANGELOG document the regeneration flow. The regeneration loop (edit integrations/*.tpl -> rebuild -> re-run) keeps the beads agent current with the orchestrator's semantics forever.

title: opencode pane/agent seats never start: --model is a run-only flag but herdr launches the root command
description:
headless::model_args("opencode", ..) emits ["--model", <m>]. That is correct for the headless one-shot (`opencode run --format json --model X`) but INVALID for the opencode root/TUI command, which is what herdr's `agent.start --kind opencode` runs (herdr agent start takes only [AGENT_ARG].. and uses the canonical executable for the kind).

Verified against opencode v2.0.16 on this host: `opencode --help` root flags are --standalone, --server, --auto, --continue/-c, --session/-s, --prompt. There is no --model and no -m. `opencode run --help` DOES have `--model, -m string` (format provider/model#variant). https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/models/ confirms --model is documented only for `opencode run`; the TUI model comes from opencode.json's `model` key or in-session `/models`.

Observed live on run fw-composed-2026-09-26T01:42:42Z: the coder seat (pi) landed, the reviewer seat (opencode) printed "Unrecognized flag: --model in command opencode", so herdr readiness reported agent_not_running, and the step failed permanently with "agent crew-...-reviewer not found in toron". Every opencode pane seat is dead on spawn for this reason.

Compounding factor: pane.rs degraded the failed readiness wait to "dispatching anyway" (now removed by bd-d7zu, which made that gate fail closed), which laundered this flag bug into the mailbox error and hid the real cause across many runs.

Fix needs a decision (see bead comments): the opencode TUI has no CLI model override, so the pin must move to config (pane env OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, matching the existing OPENCODE_API_KEY pane-env precedent) or be dropped. OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT merge-vs-replace semantics are NOT documented, so it may clobber the user's opencode.json (agents/mcp/permissions).
close_reason: bd-crlx fixed in bc1866c. Every opencode pane/agent seat had always died on spawn: model_args emits --model, valid for 'opencode run' but rejected by the opencode ROOT command, which is what 'herdr agent start --kind opencode' runs (herdr takes only [AGENT_ARG].. and uses the kind's canonical executable). v2.0.16 root flags are --standalone --server --auto --continue/-c --session/-s --prompt; --model gives 'Unrecognized flag: --model in command opencode', then agent_not_running, then the permanent 'agent not found in toron' that misdirected the operator to the mailbox. The TUI's model is config, so it now travels by pane env as OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, which MERGES: measured with 'opencode api --standalone GET /api/config', the pin adds a third document source and the operator's permissions/agents/mcp survive, with the pinned model winning. The pin is refused for a non-provider/model id (opencode would silently drop it) and refuses rather than overwriting unparseable existing content. profile_launch_plan now returns ProfileLaunchPlan{args,model,env_model_pin} so the type forces callers to handle an env pin, and the argv-only profile_launch_args refuses rather than silently dropping the model. Wired: compose crew, flywheel spawn (including the root pane's workspace env), crew control relaunch. Live: fw-composed-2026-09-26T02:33:51Z landed BOTH seats, status=succeeded. Principles: fail-closed - the argv-only view and the pin itself both refuse rather than starting a seat on the wrong model; prove-it-works - the only things that found this were reading the real binary's help and running the real config API, since a --help probe short-circuits and validates nothing. STILL OPEN, tracked in the bead comments: pane.rs spawn_launch_plan/SpawnJobLaunch, the main.rs profile-spawn path, the reroute fallbacks in start_agent_with_retry_profile, and the ~29036 helper still use the argv-only view and now REFUSE for opencode rather than running unpinned. Also noted: model_args falls through '_ => vec![]' for claude/codex, so those pin no model today (pre-existing, untouched).

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
DESIGN DECISION: option (a) chosen, and the merge-vs-replace question is now MEASURED, not assumed.

The operator chose 'try (a) then (b)'. (a) is viable, proven by measurement.

PROOF that OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT merges rather than replaces. Measured on opencode v2.0.16 with 'opencode api --standalone GET /api/config', which returns the RESOLVED config as a list of sources:

  baseline                        -> 2 sources; model=None; permissions/agents/mcp present
  OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT={model} -> 3 sources; model={'providerID':'deepseek','model':'deepseek-flash'}; permissions/agents/mcp STILL present
  OPENCODE_CONFIG=/path/pin.json  -> 3 sources; identical result

So the pin adds a third 'document' source, the operator's global opencode.json keeps its permissions/agents/mcp, and the pinned model WINS (last document wins per key). The binary's own loader agrees: it parses the env var into its own type:'document' entry and returns it alongside the global/direct/project sources. This is the same pane-env channel apply_opencode_go_api_key_alias already uses for opencode-go auth. OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT is preferred over OPENCODE_CONFIG because it needs no temp file and nothing to clean up.

Note: 'opencode debug config' does NOT show the env-var source (it reports only discovered files), so that probe is inconclusive and must not be used to conclude the var is ignored.

IMPLEMENTED so far:
- headless::InteractiveModelPlan + interactive_model_plan(harness, model, effort): opencode's interactive entrypoint emits NO model argv and routes the pin to env; every other harness routes to the existing model_args unchanged, so this cannot become a second arg builder that drifts. 6 tests.
- herdr_shim::apply_opencode_model_pin(env, model): merges the model into any existing OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, refuses a non-provider/model id (opencode silently drops such a reference, which would leave the seat unpinned), and REFUSES rather than overwriting unparseable or non-object pre-existing content. 7 tests.
- profile_launch_plan now returns ProfileLaunchPlan { args, model, env_model_pin } instead of a 2-tuple, so the type forces every caller to decide what it does about an env-delivered pin.
- profile_launch_args (the argv-only view) now REFUSES when the plan carries an env pin, instead of silently dropping the model. A seat with no way to honour the pin now gets a loud, actionable error rather than a wrong model.
- Wired: the compose crew path (src/pane.rs), the flywheel spawn path including the root pane's workspace env (src/main.rs), and crew control relaunch (src/cmd/crew.rs). The crew path additionally refuses to reuse a pre-existing pane for an env-pinned seat, because those panes were created by workspace_create with a different env and a process env is fixed at its start.
- Three existing tests asserted opencode's --model in argv; they were pinning the bug and now assert the corrected behaviour.

13 new tests, all mutation-verified (neutering the opencode carve-out fails 2; making the pin clobber instead of merge fails 3; 8 unaffected tests still pass).

STILL TO WIRE (these now REFUSE for opencode rather than running unpinned — loud, but not yet working):
- pane.rs spawn_launch_plan / SpawnJobLaunch: needs an env-pin field carried into launch_spawn_job.
- main.rs profile-spawn path (~22685) which finds or creates a workspace.
- main.rs reroute fallbacks inside start_agent_with_retry_profile: these launch into an EXISTING pane, so a changed model cannot be re-pinned. Note the pane's shell env already carries the ORIGINAL split's pin, so a same-model reroute is actually fine; only a model CHANGING reroute is unsatisfiable.
- main.rs ~29036 helper.

Also recorded, pre-existing and NOT changed here: model_args falls through '_ => vec![]' for claude/codex, so those harnesses pin no model at all today.

title: Crew dispatch fails permanently: agent.start failure yields a not-found reason the transient classifier rejects
description:
Every crew dispatch fails at its first step. Reproduced 5x on 2026-09-26 with
freshly installed binaries; the chain is fully evidenced.

(1) pre_spawn_crew creates the crew workspace, whose pane shell is not yet AT AN
INTERACTIVE PROMPT. herdr's own contract: "An available shell pane must be at
its interactive prompt, with the shell itself in the foreground and no foreground
command, editor, or agent running", and "agent start requires an existing
available shell pane". So agent.start fails with
  backend error agent_pane_busy: agent target pane wN:p1 is not an available shell

(2) pane.rs:724 then calls c.agent_wait(name, [Idle], 90s), which fails because
the agent was never started:
  readiness wait failed (dispatching anyway): backend error agent_not_running

(3) The code at pane.rs:717-719 documents the intent: on a wait failure,
degrade to the __send landing semantics, "which classify not-ready as a per-step
error".

(4) THAT DEGRADATION IS UNSOUND. is_transient_dispatch_reason (pane.rs:782)
matches only "agent_not_ready" and "agent_pane_busy". But when agent.start ITSELF
failed there is no agent to be not-ready, so the first dispatch instead fails
with "flywheel: agent <name> not found in toron". That reason is classified
NON-transient, so the step fails permanently on the first attempt and the
documented retry never engages.

Net effect: a pure boot race is reported as a permanent failure, no crew can
ever start, and each attempt leaves dead-pane registry rows behind (panes_missing
grew 12 -> 16 across my attempts).

This is the SAME class as the pi harness bug: a helper well tested in isolation
while the integration around it was never exercised.

Fix: either treat an agent-not-found immediately after a failed readiness wait as
transient, or refuse the spawn when agent.start failed, instead of proceeding
past a check that just failed.

SEPARATE BUG, same area: pre_spawn_crew creates the workspace with cwd
"<project_dir>/workspace dir", which DOES NOT EXIST. The pane's cwd silently
falls back to /Users/bangedorrunt instead of the project repo, so even a started
agent would work in the wrong directory. Verified directly: creating a workspace
with that cwd yields a healthy zsh whose cwd is /Users/bangedorrunt, not toron.
acceptance_criteria: A dispatch whose agent.start failed is either retried as transient or refused, never dispatched into; the workspace cwd is the project repo, not a non-existent 'workspace dir'; a test reproduces the chain without a live herdr
close_reason: bd-d7zu fixed in 4fa7c8b (gate) + c310f17e (fail closed). Root cause corrected on this bead: not the transient classifier, which returns reroute_eligible=false and never gave up — a missing shell-readiness gate. herdr types AGENT_ARG into the pane PTY at agent.start; the peer-aware template is ~2.6KB single-quoted; spawn_crew_into fired agent.start milliseconds after pane_split returned, so the arg split mid-quote, zsh parked at PS2, and the agent never started. cmd_crew_control has always gated on wait_shell_prompt, which is why relaunch survived and compose did not. Measured: a real split pane needs 769ms to reach a prompt (E2E real_pane_reaches_a_detected_prompt), so the old code was firing ~700ms early. Principles: fail-closed — the warn-and-continue first cut reproduced the very defect (readiness failed, dispatch proceeded anyway, surfaced as the permanent 'agent not found in toron'), so the gate now refuses and names the shell; prove-it-works — only a real pane and a real dispatch found this, and unit-testing the classifier had already cleared the innocent path. Live: fw-composed-2026-09-26T01:19:12Z landed with status working. Separate opencode flag bug filed as bd-crlx.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED (was wrong) + FIXED in 4fa7c8b.

The recorded root cause on this bead was WRONG. It claimed the transient/permanent classification of agent_pane_busy gave up too early. It did not: failure::classify on that error returns kind=Unknown with reroute_eligible=false, so the 30x3s retry loop in start_agent_with_retry_profile was never the thing that bailed.

Actual root cause: a missing shell-readiness gate. herdr types AGENT_ARG into the pane PTY the instant agent.start is called, and the peer-aware launch template renders to a ~2.6KB single-quoted arg. spawn_crew_into fired agent.start milliseconds after pane_split returned, while the fresh pane shell was still booting (zsh running .zshrc, prompt unrendered, PTY still CANONICAL). The arg split mid-quote, zsh parked at PS2, the agent never started — the exact failure herdr_shim.rs documents as the 2026-08-18 coder2/coder3 dead-on-spawn.

Why the asymmetry explained the symptom: cmd_crew_control (flywheel crew control relaunch) has always called wait_shell_prompt before starting an agent, so relaunch kept working. The compose crew path in pane.rs never did, so workflow compose --run dead-on-spawned. I had wrongly cleared pane.rs earlier by diffing against f4c9f2a, where the gate was also absent — but absence there only means compose was riding the timing margin, not that there was no bug.

Measured, not assumed: a live E2E probe (real_pane_reaches_a_detected_prompt, 4fa7c8b) splits a real pane and drives the real gate. A fresh pane reaches a detected prompt in 769ms, matched on a bare U+276F, so the gate is a genuine readiness signal and not a sleep that always hits its 15s deadline. Without the gate, agent.start was firing roughly 700ms too early.

Fix: gate the crew path on wait_shell_prompt (15s, warn-only) exactly as the relaunch path does, so a slow shell degrades to the old race rather than to a hard failure.

Verified live: the first dispatch in five attempts to land, with send receipt landed=true, status=working; run fw-composed-2026-09-26T01:19:12Z reached status=succeeded. Full bin suite 1871 pass / 0 fail, clippy clean. Mutation-verified: neutering shell_prompt_rendered makes the E2E fail with 'gate never detected a prompt on a real pane in 15s'.

title: pi harness emitted --thinking=<level>, which pi's parser rejects
description: Every pi-spawned agent with an effort was launched with an argument pi's own parser rejects, so the agent died at startup with 'Error: Unknown option: --thinking'. Found by dispatching a crew on the pi harness and reading the pane. Reproduced against pi 0.87.1: 'pi --print --model bogus/m --thinking=high x' -> Error: Unknown option: --thinking (arg parse fails), while 'pi --print --model bogus/m --thinking high x' -> Error: Model not found (args parsed fine). So pi accepts the SPACE form and rejects the EQUALS form, even though pi --help advertises '--thinking <level>'. src/headless.rs model_args pushed format!("--thinking={e}") for the pi harness; the 'pa' arm directly below already used the correct two-entry form, so the shapes were inconsistent. WHY IT SLIPPED THROUGH: the existing test jev_effort_pi_thinking_native_opencode_loud_degrade asserted ["--model","glm-5.2","--thinking=high"] - it pinned the equals form because that is what the code emitted, and its doc comment claimed bd-ulzi had 'verified pi --help'. A test that only confirms what the code already says cannot catch the code being wrong about the world. omp's --thinking= form was left alone: different binary, not tested here.
acceptance_criteria: New test pi_emitted_effort_arg_form_is_accepted_by_the_real_binary runs the emitted argv against a bogus model so pi fails at model resolution (no network) and 'Unknown option' is the only signal the ARG FORM was wrong; verified RED before the fix, GREEN after; skips loudly when pi is absent; the old test now asserts the two-entry form; 39 headless tests pass; verify-clippy.sh exits 0
close_reason: model_args now emits --thinking and the level as two argv entries for the pi harness; a new test asks the pi binary whether it accepts what we emit instead of asserting our own output. This unblocked pi-spawned dispatch: crew dispatch went from 0/3 agents started to 3/3 dispatched.

title: deps-protocol-check: version-pin herdr dep + CI protocol gate
description:
# `flywheel deps` warns on herdr protocol mismatch

## Background

`bd-protocol-v18` makes the documentation truthful. This bead makes drift visible AUTOMATICALLY: `flywheel deps` must flag when the installed herdr speaks a protocol the client was not verified against. Today `deps` reports `herdr socket: idle` — a green checkmark with no version awareness (gap #6 in the epic table).

## Why (justification)

"Trust but verify" for the runtime contract: the orchestrator's single most important dependency is the herdr socket protocol. A schema bump that adds required fields would break the client at runtime; a warning at `deps` time turns a confusing mid-loop failure into a five-second diagnosis.

## Technical approach

- herdr.rs: `pub const HDR_PROTOCOL: u64 = 18;` (single source of truth; `bd-protocol-v18` establishes the verified value).
- `flywheel deps` (cmd_deps in main.rs): additionally query the server's protocol — prefer a socket call if `schema`/`api.schema` exists as a protocol method in v18 (check `herdr api schema --json` for the method list; herdr CLI itself is guaranteed present since deps already checks it, so falling back to `herdr api schema --json` subprocess is acceptable — pick the socket call if available, document why).
- Output: add a `protocol: 18 (expected 18) OK` line, or `protocol: X (expected 18) WARN` — colored per the output.rs TTY rules. Decision: deps keeps exit 0 for a protocol mismatch (services are UP; only the contract version differs) — the WARN line is the signal. Document this choice in the code comment.
- Keep the existing per-line `name: state` shape; the protocol line is informational + warning.

## Success criteria

- `deps` prints the protocol line with the actual server value.
- Mismatch → visible WARN line (and stderr note), exit stays 0.
- No change to the other deps checks.

## Test plan

- Unit: constant sanity; warn-formatting helper (output.rs) test.
- Manual: expected=18 vs live v18 → OK; temporarily change the constant → WARN; restore.

## Dependencies

Depends on: `bd-protocol-v18` (establishes the verified constant).

## Considerations

- The socket-schema query is one extra round trip per `deps` run — negligible (deps is interactive/diagnostic, not hot-path).
- If v18 has NO schema method and the CLI fallback is used, note that the CLI itself may drift from the socket (same binary, so acceptable).
- Future-proof: when the server bumps to v19, this line turns red immediately — that is the point.
close_reason:
Runtime contract drift is now visible at deps time. herdr.rs: HDR_PROTOCOL = 18 (single source of truth, doc'd) + pure parse_protocol(raw) -> Option<u64> (top-level `protocol` field of `herdr api schema --json`). cmd_deps runs the schema query (herdr CLI subprocess — the socket has no protocol method in v18; same binary as the server so CLI-vs-socket drift is a non-concern) and prints `herdr protocol: 18 (expected 18)` — the value painted green via new output::ok() when matching, yellow via output::warn() when not, plus a stderr WARNING naming both versions. Unreadable schema -> `protocol: unknown (expected 18)` + stderr note. Exit stays 0 on mismatch BY DESIGN (services are up; only the contract version differs — the WARN line is the signal; commented in code). No other deps checks changed.

122/122 tests (3 new: parse_protocol reads the field, parse failures -> None, warn() marks text with NO_COLOR plain form).

Live verification: v18 vs live v18 -> green `herdr protocol: 18 (expected 18)`. Temporary const bump to 19 -> yellow `18 (expected 19)` + stderr WARNING, deps continued, exit 0; const restored, green line back. (Learned: output::ok must be aliased on import — cmd_deps's local `ok` bool shadows it.)

title: ledger: derive_head_sha binds the close ceremony's own bookkeeping commit — skip bookkeeping-only matches
description:
The close ceremony writes .beads/* and that bookkeeping commit routinely cites the bead id, so derive_head_sha (git log --all -1 --grep=<id>) picked the BOOKKEEPING commit rather than the revision the gate row was bound to — the row just bound read clean-false, and it is unrepairable by policy once the bead is closed (closed -> closed is not a legal gate transition). Confirmed live: bd-workflow-catalog-read-doors-project-tier-jah1 reads clean-false today.

FIX (landed): derive_head_sha walks the --grep candidates newest-first and SKIPS bookkeeping-only commits (.beads/**, .flywheel/** — the same two ADR-0006 D3 names), binding the newest commit that carries the id AND carries work. Fail-closed: an empty path list is NOT bookkeeping (a merge commit prints no paths without -m, an empty commit has none — skipping on absence would silently retarget the bound revision), and when every candidate is bookkeeping-only the newest one is still returned, because "no commit carries the id" would be a lie that reopens a legal close.

Belt and braces pinned in AGENTS.md: keep the bead id out of the bookkeeping commit message anyway (a skip is a heuristic, a token-free message is a fact).

VERIFY: cargo test --bin flywheel verdict (derive_head_sha skips a bookkeeping-only newest match; empty-path and all-bookkeeping fallbacks).
close_reason: done

title: dispatch cap must account for profile conditioning; over-cap must degrade, not kill the loop
description:
Observed on a live project, 2026-10-03.

Evidence:
- Every composed pane (profile coder/planner/reviewer) was undispatchable:
  `dispatched prompt for bead ... is 4587 bytes — over the 4096 byte cap (loop
  bug; NOT sent, never truncated)`.
- Arithmetic from source: `BRIEF_TEMPLATE` fills to 3226 bytes with a 38-char
  bead id; planner/coder/reviewer behavior preambles are 1357/1550/1492 bytes.
  Template + preamble is always over 4096. The long id appears ~11 times in the
  template.
- After 4 consecutive rejects the loop treats the agent as dead and aborts
  (`failed to accept 4 prompts in a row`), so ONE oversized brief class kills
  the whole supervisor.
- Workaround was destructive: strip `profile` from the spawn-registry entry so
  sends go raw (loses behavior conditioning), or spawn bare panes.

Wish:
1. Size the whole send (behavior + skills prefix + brief) before dispatch, and
   make the template cheap: compress repeated ids (one id line, `{id}` refs),
   or reference the brief by `br show <id>` instead of embedding.
2. Over-cap degrades: send a short pointer brief naming the bead and the exact
   `br show`/receipt path, with a WARN, instead of failing the agent and the
   loop. Fail loud once, never fail-deadly.
3. `br create` warns when a project id prefix + title length will push dispatch
   briefs over budget (cheaper to fix at authoring time).

Acceptance: `cargo test -p flywheel dispatch_cap_accounts_for_conditioning`
covers: template+preamble sizing, degrade-on-over-cap, and a loop that survives
one over-cap dispatch.
close_reason: Dispatch cap now sizes the whole send: the compacted template (2437 B w/ 37-char id) fits under the cap with the worst built-in preamble, and an over-cap brief degrades to a pointer brief (bead id + br show path + report contract) in both the queue and __send instead of rejecting; the agent is never failed over brief size. PRINCIPLES: boundary-discipline — one sizing decision (build_brief/pointer_brief) owns both loop and send paths. prove-it-works — dispatch_cap_accounts_for_conditioning pins template+preamble sizing, degrade-on-over-cap, and a queued degraded dispatch.

title: docs-backend: AGENTS/README Backends section + .env.example
description:
# docs-backend-abstraction — AGENTS.md/README "Backends" section + `.env.example` + ADR cross-links

## Background

R0.1–R0.8 ship the pluggable-backend abstraction. The docs (AGENTS.md, README) currently describe a herdr+agent-mail-only swarm. After R0, they must document: the two traits, the env/`.env`/config selection, the feature flags, the stubbed future backends (superlogical/toron/tmux), and the migration path to toron embedding. The `.env.example` is the user-facing quickstart. Docs are load-bearing — agents read AGENTS.md at spawn, and the captain/future-self needs the migration map. ADR-0002 §7 (neutral consequence) + §11 Q3 (`.env` security).

Depends on `call-site-migration` (document what shipped, not what's planned).

## Subtasks

1. **AGENTS.md** "Backends" section:
   - The two traits (`MultiplexerBackend`, `MailBackend`) + the impl matrix (herdr/superlogical/tmux × agentmail/toron).
   - Env/config contract: `FLYWHEEL_BACKEND`, `FLYWHEEL_MAIL`, precedence (flag > env > `.env` > config.toml > default), cargo features.
   - The migration path table (R0 now → R1 toron → R1.5 trait-merge → R2 superlogical) from ADR-0002 §4.
   - Cross-links to ADR-0002, ADR-0001, toron ADR-0003.
2. **README.md** "Backends" section: one-paragraph overview + the `.env.example` quickstart + the `flywheel backend list` discovery command.
3. **`.env.example`** (shipped, gitignored-real-`.env`):
   ```
   # flywheel backend selection (defaults: herdr / agentmail)
   # FLYWHEEL_BACKEND=herdr          # herdr (default) | superlogical (future, unreleased) | tmux (legacy)
   # FLYWHEEL_MAIL=agentmail         # agentmail (default) | toron (future, ADR-0003 R1)
   # agent-mail MCP (used by the agentmail backend)
   # FLYWHEEL_AGENTMAIL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765
   # FLYWHEEL_AGENTMAIL_TOKEN=       # never commit real tokens
   ```
4. **CHANGELOG.md** entry for the R0 abstraction release.
5. Add `// governed-by: ADR-0002` headers to `src/backend/*.rs` per the ADR-linkage convention (verified by `verify-adr-links.sh`).
6. Update ADR-0001's "Governs" field to note its beads now target the ADR-0002 traits.

## Approach notes

- Agents read AGENTS.md at spawn — the "Backends" section must tell a spawned agent which backend is active (so it knows whether `herdr agent prompt` or a future superlogical equivalent is the dispatch primitive). Bake `flywheel backend list` into the spawn-time context if cheap.
- De-slopify per AGENTS.md RULE 0: terse, technical, exact. The migration table is the highest-value artifact for "future self".
- `.env.example` uses `#` comments (sourced by shell/dotenvy as disabled) — copy, uncomment, edit. Never ship a real token.
- The `governed-by: ADR-0002` header on `src/backend/*.rs` is verified by the existing `verify-adr-links.sh` — don't skip it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AGENTS.md + README have a "Backends" section consistent with the shipped R0 code.
- `.env.example` shipped; real `.env` gitignored; lint test asserts `.gitignore` contains `.env`.
- `flywheel backend list` documented + works.
- ADR-0001 updated to reference ADR-0002 (beads target traits).
- `governed-by: ADR-0002` headers present + verified.

## Test plan

- Doc lint: grep asserting `.env.example` exists + is referenced from README; `.gitignore` contains `.env`; no stale "herdr-only" framing remains in AGENTS.md (the abstraction is now described).
- `verify-adr-links.sh` passes (ADR-0002 linkage).

## Considerations

- Docs lag code — land this bead *last* in Phase 0 so it documents what shipped. But update AGENTS.md incrementally as each R0 bead lands (don't batch to the end).
- The migration table (R0→R1→R1.5→R2) is the "future self" reference — keep it accurate as phases complete (update the table in each phase's docs bead).

## Reference
- ADR-0002 §4 (migration path table), §7 (neutral: docs rewrite), §11 Q3 (`.env` security).
- ADR-0001 (update Governs field).
- toron ADR-0003 (the R1/R1.5 target the table points to).
close_reason: AGENTS.md + README Backends sections; .env.example; CHANGELOG R0 entry; ADR-0001 Governs→traits + Depends on ADR-0002; governed-by on backend/*; env_example lint test. verify-adr-links.sh N/A (missing); verify-0002 if green.

# docs-collab-spine-recipes — rewrite AGENTS.md + README for the collaboration spine + recipe catalog

## Background

`AGENTS.md` and `README.md` currently describe a poll-based, orchestrator-only swarm: "protocol v18", "serve SSE on real herdr events (currently state-poll stream)", the 8-tool mail surface. After Phases 1-5 land, every one of those statements is stale. This bead ships the docs rewrite: the new event-driven model, the full mail surface, the four recipe catalog, the verification script, and the ADR cross-links. Docs are how the "future self" (and the swarm agents themselves, who read AGENTS.md at spawn) understand the system. This is ADR-0001 §10's third pillar + §6 neutral consequence.

Depends on all four pattern beads (recipes must exist to document them).

## Subtasks

1. **AGENTS.md** rewrite:
   - Session facts: herdr protocol v19, event-driven loop (primary) + poll heartbeat (fallback), full agent-mail surface (enumerate the wrappers), pane-identity bridge, escalation protocol.
   - New "Collaboration patterns" section: the four recipes (debate / plan-review-implement / peer-triggered / cross-project) with one-paragraph contracts + pointers to the recipe beads + ADR-0001 §9.
   - Update the "Rules" / architecture diagram to reflect `mail.rs` (14 wrappers) + event reactor in `durable.rs`.
   - Cross-link ADR-0001 + `verify-0001.sh`.
2. **README.md** rewrite:
   - Replace "socket protocol v18" → v19; "serve SSE on real herdr events (currently state-poll stream)" → "event-driven (events.subscribe primary, poll heartbeat fallback)".
   - Update the mail surface table (`mail inbox/send/locks/unlock/conflicts/agents` → full list).
   - Add a "Collaboration" section with the 4 patterns + a quickstart for each.
   - Update the architecture diagram (event channel into the loop).
3. **Recipe catalog** (`docs/collab/recipes.md` or in AGENTS.md): one page per pattern with the full contract (from the pattern beads), spawn commands, prompt-template references, gotchas. The "future self" reference.
4. **CHANGELOG.md** entry for the spine release.
5. Add `// governed-by: ADR-0001` headers to the rewritten files per the ADR-linkage convention (AGENTS.md ADR section).

## Approach notes

- Agents read AGENTS.md at spawn — the docs are *load-bearing for behavior*, not just human reference. The ack contract, the lease-renew clause, the build-slot-before-cargo clause, the "don't close peers' panes" safety rule all live in AGENTS.md so spawned agents see them. Get these right.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A spawned agent reading AGENTS.md understands the ack/lease/build-slot/safety contracts without external docs.
- `verify-0001.sh` referenced from both files.
- Recipe catalog covers all four patterns with runnable commands.

## Test plan

- Doc lint: a script (or `grep`) asserting no stale tokens (`protocol v18`, `state-poll stream`, the old 8-tool list) remain in AGENTS.md/README.
- Human review: captain signs off the recipes match intent.

## Considerations

- Docs lag code is the classic failure — land this bead *last* in the dependency chain so it documents what shipped, not what was planned. But also update it incrementally as each phase lands (don't batch all docs to the end and risk drift).
- The "governed-by: ADR-0001" header is verified by `docs/decisions/_scripts/verify-adr-links.sh` (per AGENTS.md ADR section) — don't skip it.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §6 (neutral: docs rewrite), §10 (docs), §7 Phase 6, §11 verification.
- Stale anchors: `AGENTS.md` (protocol v18), `README.md:168,195`.

title: recover does not restore workspace doorbell dispatchers; liveness invisible in status
description:

title: doorbell status reports alive:false for a live daemon when the caller's state dir differs from the daemon's
description:
# `doorbell status` reports `alive:false` for a daemon that is up and serving

## Symptom

`lifecycle::status()` builds `alive` as `pid.is_some() && health.is_some()`, where
`pid` comes from `managed(cfg)` = `read_pid(cfg.pid_file())`. The pid file is read
from the **caller's** `--state-dir`, not the daemon's. The daemon only writes its
pid file under its own state dir, so any caller configured with a different one
prints a null pid and `alive:false` for a daemon that is answering on the port.

## Reproduction (live, 2026-09-28, one daemon, two callers, same port)

    $ doorbell status --state-dir ~/.local/state/doorbell --port 18980
    {"alive":true, ... "owner":{"pid":7765} ...}

    $ doorbell status --state-dir ~/.local/state/flywheel --port 18980
    {"alive":false, "pid":null, ... "owner":{"pid":7765} ...}

Same daemon, same health body, opposite `alive`. The second form is not
hypothetical: `flywheel doorbell status` executes exactly it, because it passes
`config::state_dir()` (the *flywheel* state dir) rather than the doorbell's.

Impact: `alive` is the first field a script or an operator reads. Anything gating
on it treats a healthy doorbell as down — and the plane has spent this whole day
removing exactly this class of lie (`stale_build` crying wolf on a quiet tree was
fixed the same way: ask the question that actually has an answer).

## Root cause

`managed()` answers "did WE start this, and is our pidfile current" — a true and
useful question, but not the question `alive` is read as answering. Liveness is
proven by the health probe. The pidfile only ever proves attribution.

## Fix

`alive` derives from the probe that reached the daemon. `pid` prefers the local
pidfile (attribution) and falls back to the daemon's own pid from the health body
(`owner.pid`), with the source named so the two can never be silently confused.

Decision core stays pure: a `status_liveness(local_pid, health)` fold, no IO, so
the rule is testable without a server.

## VERIFY

```bash
mbx test -p doorbell-cli status_liveness
```
