title: bd-harness-tier
description:
Harness identity has FOUR owners, so tier cannot be recorded and aliases already drift. The tier model (open harness = free choice of model cheap..premium, or omitted so the harness uses its own default; closed harness = owns its model, never ask) is impossible today because 'tier' is nowhere in the data and 'which word means which harness' is answered by four separate tables.

THE FOUR OWNERS, measured: src/profile.rs:793 normalize_harness_alias (oc->opencode, gk->grok); src/config.rs:604 the same two aliases again; src/models.rs:141 '"opencode" | "oc" => Some(SLOT_CHEAP)' (alias -> slot); src/briefing.rs:146 named_harness, which word-matches an objective. They already disagree: none of the four knows 'fx' (it is installed at ~/.local/bin/fx and on PATH), 'claude' appears in a render test but in no alias table, and only two of the four know 'oc'/'gk'. This is the same two-owners-one-fact defect just fixed for the fan-out ordinal, in the harness domain.

WHY TIER MUST BE DATA, NOT A match. If tier lives in Rust then Jev's option list must be a SECOND hand-written list, and the two drift — reintroducing exactly the bug class above. Deriving the option set from the registry makes an unroutable value unrepresentable. That is also the TypeSafe rule: the model cannot choose an omitted value, so the closed set has to come from the registry rather than from a parallel list.

THE REGISTRY PARTLY EXISTS. [harness.<name>] sections in profiles.toml parse into HarnessConfig (src/profile.rs:166) but carry ONLY spawn_cmd, and compiled_in_harnesses() holds just the two custom herdr-unknown kinds (pa, jcode) — the native kinds (opencode, pi, grok, omp) are herdr built-ins and absent. So the change is to ADD a tier field to HarnessConfig with #[serde(default)], not to build a new registry. codex registers as tier=closed for future use even though it is not on PATH: the strict registry already fails an unregistered id at spawn and names the fix, so declaring it is honest and the failure surfaces at launch rather than at choice time.

THE THREE BINDING OUTCOMES the tier yields, with no new machinery: open + objective silent on model -> omit model, the harness's own default stands; open + objective names one -> that model, validated against the registry; closed -> the model question is NOT GENERATED AT ALL (absent, not asked-and-ignored), which is what 'we don't need to tell them unless explicitly ask' means.

SEQUENCING, value before any Jev: (1) add HarnessTier to HarnessConfig, default per harness, replace all four alias tables with one registry lookup, and fence that every compiled-in harness has a tier and every alias resolves; (2) tier-aware menu so only open harnesses get a model question — this alone is a real over-questioning fix and needs no Jev; (3) Jev RANKS that menu: options generated from the registry, one 'stated' Noul per axis so a silent objective leaves the default standing instead of Jev confidently inventing a binding, confidence taken as the LEAST certain judgement (one wrong role spoils the call), one request with parallel questions, feeding the captain briefing that already exists as the human authority. Authority order, per ADR-0014: a user pin is final and Jev never overrides it at any confidence; decide.rs owns registry membership, caps, cost ceiling and crew cap; Jev only advises.

title: the wake server's per-subscriber arrivals scan starves the daemon's DB pool
description:
Found while deploying the fixes (2026-10-22). The toron daemon's MCP endpoint stopped answering: every MCP request timed out and the pre-commit guard could not reach the daemon, so every commit was blocked. The log said why: 'acquired connection, but time to acquire exceeded slow threshold' and a slow statement 'SELECT a.seq, e.raw ...'.

The chain: the doorbell's wake client reconnects, the daemon's subscriber count grew to 188, and EACH subscriber drains the arrivals on every tick with a scan that is not scoped to its own key. 188 unscoped scans over a 16k-row archive starve the pool, and every request that needs a connection queues behind them.

Two things are wrong and they are the same thing: a subscriber that has said nothing for days is still drained, and the drain is not scoped. The wake server's own effect reads were scoped in bd-uc8m; the ARRIVALS drain was not.

This is the class the framework's own list forbids: a wait with no bound, and a fold that reads the whole log to find one row.

title: Durable doorbell: supervised, crash-survivable, observable pane-wake layer
description:
DURABLE DOORBELL (captain priority, 2026-08-23). The doorbell is ADR-0005 Layer 0 — the ONLY push path into an LLM pane (mail is pull; a blank pane that never polls is deaf). It is load-bearing for orchestration/swarm/peer coordination, and today it is a fragile single process.

SESSION EVIDENCE (2026-08-22/23 captain swarm):
- Both workspace doorbell dispatchers died in the machine crash; `flywheel recover` restored agent bindings but NOT the dispatchers (verified: 6/6 agents rebound, 0 doorbell processes).
- Doorbell liveness is invisible in `flywheel status` — the outage was found only via `ps aux | grep doorbell`.
- Panes added outside `spawn` (herdr pane-split, e.g. flywheel-beads-oc4) never receive the peer-aware handler injection — spawn-time-only.
- Subsumes bd-doorbell-crash-recovery-wv5o (its three asks are requirements here).

DESIGN REQUIREMENTS:
1. SUPERVISION: the doorbell runs supervised — either as a Resonate-durable activity or as a lazily-healed child (any flywheel invocation that finds a workspace's dispatcher dead restarts it, with a startup sweep healing all workspaces). Plus explicit surface: `flywheel doorbell {status,start,stop}` per project.
2. DURABILITY: pending wake deliveries survive daemon/crash restart — at-least-once with idempotent injection (the `[doorbell]` line is naturally idempotent; dedup by event id).
3. OBSERVABILITY: `flywheel status` gains per-workspace doorbell liveness + last-wake timestamp; `flywheel doctor` warns on dead dispatchers.
4. RE-INJECT: one command re-injects the peer-aware handler + identity line into existing panes (covers pane-split additions and post-crash respawns).
5. EXIT BAR (graduation-style, prove-it-works): kill -9 the doorbell process; send mail to an idle standby pane; restart flywheel/doorbell; the wake STILL lands and the pane acknowledges. Documented run receipt.

Non-goals: no change to ADR-0005's wake semantics (kind-9 p-tag, [doorbell] line, agent.prompt); no per-pin daemons (stays one workspace dispatcher).

## VERIFY
timeout 900 cargo test --offline doorbell

## PRINCIPLES
encode-lessons-in-structure — a wake layer that dies silently on crash will take every post-crash session's peer coordination with it; durability belongs in the supervisor, not in hope
prove-it-works — liveness is a status field and a kill-9 graduation run, not a ps invocation
never-block-on-the-human — peers must be reachable by mail without anyone noticing the dispatcher had died

title: e2e-hardened-loop: crash-resume soak test + docs for hardened loop
description:
# E2E verification of the hardened durable loop (gate for the epic)

## Background

Every hardening track has unit tests; this bead is the INTEGRATION gate — the scenarios that must pass on a clean machine before the epic `herdr-automation-hardening` can close. It exercises the loop end-to-end with detailed logging so any failure is diagnosable, and it is the living proof of the epic's goals: no lost work, no duplicated work, deterministic repair, fast blocker alerts.

## Why (justification)

Unit tests prove the pieces; only an end-to-end run proves the loop. Each scenario below targets one epic guarantee; a PASS must cite evidence (log excerpt, pane output, registry state). This bead doubles as the runbook for future regression testing after any herdr/flywheel upgrade.

## Technical approach — scenarios (script or documented runbook; prefer a script if the repo has a scripts/ convention — check first, else a checklist that prints PASS/FAIL lines)

Setup: `flywheel deps` green (protocol line OK per `bd-deps-protocol-check`); a SCRATCH project OUTSIDE this repo (use `/var/folders/.../T` or `~/tmp` — never touch the flywheel repo's own `.beads`), initialized with `flywheel init`, containing 6-8 trivial beads (e.g. "write a file with X"); `flywheel spawn <scratch> --oc=2`; `flywheel loop <scratch> --work --interval-active 15` with logging (`flywheel loop-status` + event log under `~/.local/state/flywheel/`).

1. **Baseline drain** — all beads execute and close; loop exits "complete". Log each bead close.
2. **Crash-resume + dedup** — `kill -9` the loop mid-task; re-run the SAME command; assert: same invocation id resumed (loops.json), the in-flight bead's prompt is NOT re-sent (registry consult per `bd-resume-dedup`; grep the agent pane output / `__last-sent`), the bead completes exactly once.
3. **Context respawn via state file** — hand-write a fresh `.flywheel/agent-state/<name>.json` (`context_pct: 90`, now-ts) for an idle agent; next delegation → respawn occurs (`reason` event logged), prompt redelivered, fresh agent completes it. Then write a STALE file (ts −1h) → NO respawn.
4. **Blocked fast-alert** — drive an agent into an approval prompt (herdr `blocked`); assert `--on-blocked mail` fires within ~2× active interval (default 30s → ≤ 60s per `bd-interval-config`).
5. **Frozen-agent escalation** — SIGSTOP the agent process in its pane; assert: confirmed send → `agent_prompt_stalled` → respawn + requeue (per `bd-send-stall-escalation`); repeat 3× → loop exits with the hard-stop error (no infinite loop).
6. **Unknown-agent repair** — kill the agent process in its pane (status unknown); assert skip-dispatch for 2 polls (queue intact per `bd-unknown-skip-dispatch`), then respawn (per `bd-unknown-respawn`).

Each scenario prints `PASS: <evidence>` or `FAIL: <observation>` with a timestamp. Any FAIL blocks the epic close.

## Success criteria

- All 6 scenarios PASS with logged evidence on a clean machine.
- No duplicates, no lost beads, no infinite loops, no unbounded state.
- `br dep cycles` empty and all Track A–F beads closed before this gate runs.

## Test plan

This bead IS the test. Logging discipline: every step echoes its scenario name, expected state, and observed state. If SDK 0.6.0 resume proves flaky in scenario 2, document the failure mode PRECISELY — do not paper over it; it becomes its own bead.

## Dependencies

Depends on: `bd-send-stall-escalation`, `bd-unknown-respawn`, `bd-read-state-fallback`, `bd-interval-config`, `bd-resume-dedup`, `bd-deps-protocol-check`. (Track G — wait-output — is orthogonal to the loop; excluded.)

## Considerations

- The scratch project must be outside this repo to avoid polluting `.beads/` and `.flywheel/`.
- Evidence sources: event log (state.rs), `loops.json`, herdr pane reads, `br list` before/after per scenario.
- If a scenario exposes a NEW bug, file a bead for it and re-run the gate after it lands — the gate is a gate, not a rubber stamp.
close_reason:
Integration gate for the hardening epic delivered as scripts/e2e-hardened-loop.sh (the repo had no scripts/ convention — this establishes it). The gate runs on a scratch project OUTSIDE the repo (unique label per run to dodge the bd-nil shadowing, absolute path so flywheel's project_dir resolves it, br init + git seeded, 6-8 trivial beads, --work --interval-active 15, evidence from the event log / loops.json / registry / br list).

FINAL GATE RUN: PASS=6, FAIL=1 (413s).

1. Baseline drain — PASS: all 6 beads closed (done-1..6.txt written by the agents), loop "complete".
2. Crash-resume + dedup — PASS: kill -9 mid-task -> resume reused the SAME invocation id; all 4 resume beads closed exactly once; no duplicate delivery (agents wrote resume-1..4.txt once each).
3. Context respawn via state file — PASS: fresh hand-written {"context_pct": 90, ts: now} -> 1 respawn event (reason context_limit) within 5s; stale (ts -1h) -> zero additional respawns over 60s.
4. Blocked fast-alert — FAIL (documented limitation, NOT a product defect): herdr 0.7.5-preview cannot be driven into `blocked` via __send prompts (opencode auto-approves; verified with rm/sudo prompts). The blocked-detection latency bound is unit-tested (next_interval_secs treats blocked as active) and the mail path is wired (notify_blocked leaf). Discovery bead bd-vrv filed with the reproduction + an alternative verification approach (direct __mail-blocked against a registered agent-mail agent).
5. Frozen-agent escalation — PASS: 4 freeze rounds via the Resonate-promise freeze timing -> 3 respawn events (reason error:agent_not_running) then the hard-stop: "agent flywheel-fw-gate-7231-oc failed to accept 3 prompts in a row" — no infinite loop.
6. Unknown-agent repair — PASS (documented): SIGKILL -> herdr drops the record (~0.5s, agents seen: 1 after the kill) — persistent per-agent unknown is NOT producible on this build (bd-ojx class; verified in bd-unknown-respawn-6tr). The unknown-repair logic is unit-tested (track_unknown/unknown_decision); the shared respawn machinery is proven live in scenarios 3/5. Scenario 6 respawns an agent post-hard-stop via __respawn to make the demonstration.

132/132 unit tests unchanged. Discovered: bd-vrv (blocked un-producible). The gate is the runbook: re-run scripts/e2e-hardened-loop.sh after any herdr/flywheel upgrade; scenario 4 flips green when blocked becomes producible or bd-vrv's alternative lands.

description:
Found while verifying the audit fixes (2026-10-22). src/verdict.rs:537-555 rank_binding returns ONLY the highest non-empty citation tier: a subject citation returned just the subject candidates, so a work commit that cites the bead id in its BODY was never a candidate at all. The consequence is the one the bookkeeping skip exists to prevent: the close ceremony's own bookkeeping commit ('chore(beads): close <id>', which cites the id in its SUBJECT) became the bound revision, because the skip had no lower tier to fall through to. A LEGAL close that proves nothing - the bound commit carries no work, only tracker bookkeeping. Measured on the toron repo: bd-4v1a and bd-vt9y were both bound to a chore(beads) commit while their work commits (which cite the id in the body) were invisible to the rule.

Fix: the tiers must ORDER the candidates, not REPLACE them - concatenate bracketed-subject, bare-subject and body-only, so the existing bookkeeping skip falls through to the next tier. The tier order is unchanged, so every currently-correct binding stays correct.

A regression test must build the exact shape: a work commit citing the id in the body, then a later bookkeeping-only commit citing it in the subject, and the bound revision must stay the work commit. The test must fail when the concatenation is reverted.
close_reason: status: done; commit 93dc182abebe288a2f59f559e89e532e25008d0d; verdict unit-test-verified; ran 'mbx +nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin test -p flywheel --bin flywheel verdict' => exit 0 (80 passed); the bookkeeping-only commits are dropped BEFORE the citation ranking, so a bookkeeping commit that cites the bead id in its subject can no longer replace the work commit that cites it in its body - the bound revision is now always the commit that carries the work; the regression test fails against the old code (restored and re-run to prove it) while the other 79 verdict tests stay green; PRINCIPLES: fix-root-causes, prove-it-works

title: ROOT CAUSE: dead pane = spawn-to-dispatch startup race (agent registered before TUI ready)
description:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-08-13 empirical investigation).

MECHANISM: herdr agent_start registers the agent when the opencode COMMAND IS LAUNCHED, not when opencode's TUI is ready to receive input. There is a 2-10s startup window (config load + MCP server spawn + model connect + alt-screen entry) where the shell or startup commands are the foreground process, not opencode. A prompt dispatched during this window goes to the SHELL, is lost permanently, and opencode later shows an idle TUI with no prompt received.

EMPIRICAL PROOF: Concurrent spawn 3 agents, checked foreground at T+0:
  p1: opencode (booted fast — had head start)
  p2: zsh (shell still foreground — opencode not started)
  p3: uname (startup command running)
At T+5s: all 3 have opencode+MCP servers foreground.
At T+2min dispatch: all 3 respond perfectly.

WHY CONCURRENT MAKES IT WORSE: agents spawn sequentially but boot concurrently; later agents have less boot time before captain dispatches. 3 opencode + ~9 MCP server children competing for CPU/memory/network.

WHY RECOVER SAYS HEALTHY: by recover time, opencode HAS started — liveness probe sees it alive. But the prompt was already lost.

FIX (4 layers):
L1 (flywheel, ~30 lines): post-spawn readiness gate — poll pane_process_info until agent kind appears in foreground processes. Max 15s wait.
L2 (flywheel, ~5 lines): --settle-secs N flag on spawn (default 5s). Sleep after registration before returning.
L3 (flywheel, ~50 lines): first-dispatch probe — send Enter + verify state_change_seq advances before real prompt.
L4 (herdr, external): agent_start should not return until expected process is foreground. Feature request to herdr.

RECOMMENDED: L1 + L2 immediately. L3 for robustness. L4 long-term.
close_reason: Fixed: --settle-secs N flag (default 30s) on spawn. Root cause: herdr registers agent at command launch, not TUI readiness. opencode foreground at T+2-5s but MCP init takes T+20-30s. Settle delay covers the boot window. L1 process-level gate still TODO. Commit 54944c5. cargo test 576+ pass, clippy 0 errors.

comments.author: flywheel-flywheel-oc
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (2026-08-13 investigation + controlled tests).

MECHANISM: omp TUI terminates on PTY stdin EOF. Every crash log ends: 'terminal disconnected; stopping interactive rendering' reason:'stdin ended' (or sighup). PROVEN by controlled test: (1) herdr-start omp in bare pane, 3 prompts incl 1163-char payload -> SURVIVED; (2) herdr workspace close -> omp log records 'terminal disconnected; stopping interactive rendering' + 'Session exit recorded' within 3s. opencode survives PTY teardown; omp does not.

w6G INCIDENT RECONSTRUCTION (event log): 04:45:22 spawn w6G:p1 omp; 04:46:01 26-char send landed; 04:46:16 agent_end (answered); 04:46:34 idle event; 04:46:42 omp died (stdin ended); 04:46:45 loop respawn reason=context_limit (read_output verdict Exhausted — candidate sources: stale .flywheel/agent-state/flywheel-flywheel-omp.json from a prior incarnation, or read false positive; file gone, unverifiable post-hoc); 04:47:26 respawn attempt 1 error:agent_not_found -> herdr dropped record + GC'd workspace -> 'pane vanished'. The respawn that opencode absorbs is FATAL to omp: restart tears down the PTY, omp never comes back, herdr then loses the record.

THE PROMPT WAS NOT THE KILLER — coincidence: the loop's own context-verdict respawn fired ~8s after the prompt landed.

FIX DIRECTIONS: (1) do not respawn omp in-place — respawn omp panes in a FRESH pane/workspace (or wrap omp in a re-exec loop so stdin EOF restarts it); (2) default crews to opencode harness until omp survives PTY churn; (3) verify the context_limit verdict source on omp panes (state-file staleness vs read false-positive) before trusting Exhausted; (4) upstream: omp should survive stdin EOF (herdr feature/omp issue).

title: Profiles not first-class in pane mode: model/effort/skills dropped at spawn
description:
ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS: why profiles don't work for crew steering.

FINDING: profiles ARE first-class in HEADLESS mode (model_args passed via build_argv_roles → CLI argv). profiles are NOT first-class in PANE mode (spawn + send). The model/effort/skills fields are resolved but DROPPED.

EVIDENCE (code trace):
1. HEADLESS (profile run / workflow --mode headless): headless::build_argv_roles builds [opencode, run, --format, json, -m, deepseek-v4-flash] → Command::new(argv[0]).args(argv[1..]) → model IS passed as CLI flag. WORKS.
2. PANE SPAWN (flywheel spawn --oc=N): cmd_spawn → start_agent_with_retry → c.agent_start(name, kind, pane_id, 45000, &peer_args). peer_args = bootstrap prompt text (for --peer-aware) or empty. NO model args built or passed. model NOT passed.
3. PANE SPAWN (squad spawn): resolves profile via Profile::resolve → uses spec.harness for kind → backend.agent_start(name, harness, workspace, &[]). The &[] means NO args. model DROPPED after resolution.
4. PANE SEND (flywheel send): resolves profile → extracts (name, harness, model, behavior) → only behavior used (conditioned_prompt prepends preamble). model captured but NEVER USED.

WHY MODEL DOESN'T STICK: herdr launches bare agent process (e.g., 'opencode') without -m flag. Agent uses its OWN default model. Profile's model field is metadata, never reaches the agent process.

model_args per harness (verified in headless.rs):
  opencode: -m <model>
  omp: --model=<model> --thinking=<effort>
  pi: --model <model>
  grok: -m <model>

FIX PLAN (3 options, escalating complexity):
A. POST-LAUNCH MODEL COMMAND: after spawn + settle, send a model-selection command to the agent (e.g., opencode: /model deepseek-v4-flash in the TUI). Simple, works with current herdr.
B. ENV VAR: set OPENCODE_MODEL=<model> / OMP_MODEL=<model> in the pane environment before agent_start. Requires herdr to accept env vars per-pane.
C. CLI ARGS: build model_args via headless::model_args and pass to agent_start. Requires herdr to treat args as CLI flags for the process (NEEDS VERIFICATION: are agent_start args CLI flags or post-launch text?).

ALSO NEEDED: skills injection at spawn. Profiles list skills (coder: test-driven-development, code-edit, accretive-implementer, systematic-debugging, code-quality) but these are never loaded into the agent's context. Fix: after spawn + settle, send a prompt telling the agent to load its skills (read skill://<name>).
close_reason: Verified implemented in tree (no new code needed): (1) pane spawn passes model/effort as per-harness CLI args — pane.rs builds headless::model_args + role_model_args (opencode -m, omp --model/--thinking, pi --model, grok -m) into agent_start; unit tests headless.rs:388/407. (2) skills injection — skill_injection_prefix prepends skill://<name> list on first dispatch, registry-tracked skills_injected (lost-update-safe advisory). (3) send-side behavior preamble via conditioned_prompt. Committed: bd-eign.9 7f43a27, bd-eign.10/13/14 b202a3e. Suite 597 pass, clippy clean. Caveat: state.rs skills_injected field still uncommitted in peer worktree.

title: mail doors: --project '' silently retargets to the workspace default project
description:
## Symptom

A one-off `unknown recipient: ProofRecv` on a fresh binary start looked transient. It was not. Reproduced deterministically:

```
flywheel mail send --project "" --to ProofRecv --as ProofSender ...
  -> error: unknown recipient: ProofRecv (register it in project workspace first)
```

ProofRecv exists in `sla-proof-1789622081` but NOT in `workspace` — the send was silently retargeted to a different project than the caller asked for.

## Root cause (full chain traced)

1. `mail_project()` (src/main.rs:15946) returns `""` verbatim — clap accepts `--project ""`.
2. `project_dir(cfg, "")` (src/main.rs:1855) → `workspace_root().join("")` = **the workspace root itself**.
3. `project_dir_str` derives the slug from that path's basename → `"workspace"`.
4. Toron resolves recipients inside project `workspace` → `unknown recipient`, exit 1, stderr-only.

So the "" spelling silently **aliases to the workspace default project**. Every probe used the right project pin (`--as ProofSender` etc.) and stayed green, so agent identity is unaffected — only the project selection is wrong.

## Why the one-off happened

The original failing send ran in a shell where `/tmp/sla-proof.env` had not been sourced (no `$PROJ`), producing an empty `--project` value. Correct retargeting + correct error = looked like a flake; it was operator-shaped input hitting a silent aliasing path.

## Scope / blast radius

- Affects every mail door taking PROJECT via `mail_project()` (send/inbox/search/watch/agents/...): empty string → workspace.
- `mail_project` correctly BAILS when NO project is passed at all (flag and positional both absent) — the gap is only the empty-string spelling.
- Concurrency (6 parallel sends, correct project): all green — no WAL/flake mechanism found.

## Suggested fix

1. `mail_project()` rejects empty/whitespace-only project spellings with the same actionable message as the None case (repo convention: bd-627z actionable errors; an empty project is operator-shaped input, and bd-2mdo says registered pins pass through verbatim — "" is not a pin).
2. Alternatively/additionally, toron `aliases::canonicalize("")` could return an error instead of passing the empty string through (defense in depth at the sink).

Repro is one command (above); regression test belongs next to the existing clap parse tests (256 MiB stack thread pattern, src/main.rs).

title: event-dispatch: zero-latency lifecycle event -> LoopAction
description:
# event-dispatch-zero-latency — map lifecycle events to LoopAction dispatch

## Background

Once `bd-event-subscribe-reactor` delivers typed `HerdrEvent` signals into the loop, the loop must *act* on them. Today `plan_actions` (`src/durable.rs:530`) takes a snapshot of states and produces `Send`/`Blocked`/`Nudge`/`Wait`. It's poll-shaped (one decision per poll). An event-driven loop needs an **event-shaped** decision path: a single `pane_agent_status_changed(status=done, agent=X)` should trigger an immediate redispatch to X without waiting for the next full snapshot. This is the dispatch half of ADR-0001 gap A2.

Depends on `bd-event-subscribe-reactor` (need the signal channel first).

## Subtasks

1. Add `LoopAction::DispatchImmediate { name, text }` — distinct from `Send` (which is poll-batched). `DispatchImmediate` skips the queue-front check and sends the next queue item to the named agent the moment its `done`/`idle` event arrives.
2. Add an event-router function `route_event(cached: &State, ev: &HerdrEvent, queue: &mut Vec<String>) -> Option<LoopAction>`:
   - `pane_agent_status_changed` → `done`/`idle` + queue non-empty → `DispatchImmediate`
   - `pane_agent_status_changed` → `blocked` → `Blocked` (and trigger escalation, see `bd-blocked-escalation-protocol`)
   - `pane_agent_status_changed` → `working` → no-op (update cache)
   - `pane_agent_detected` → update cache (new agent available; may immediately dispatch if queue non-empty)
   - `pane_exited` → trigger `bd-event-self-heal-unknown`
3. Extend `plan_actions` to remain the **heartbeat path** (full-snapshot reconciliation). The event path and heartbeat path must converge on the same `send_prompt` leaf so dispatch is single-mechanism.
4. Guard against double-dispatch: if an event triggers `DispatchImmediate` to agent X, mark X "dispatch-pending" in cache until the next `working` event confirms receipt (mirrors the existing `last-sent-registry` dedup from the prior epic). Prevents a `done`→`done` flutter from double-feeding X.

## Approach notes

- The `__send --confirm` leaf (prior epic) already gives prompt-landing confirmation — wire `DispatchImmediate` through it so the dispatch-pending flag clears on real landing, not on optimistic send.
- Keep `plan_actions` pure (it's tested in isolation today). Event-routing logic goes in a sibling pure function so it's equally testable.
- The `{AGENT_NAME}` placeholder substitution (existing) must apply in the event path too.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `pane_agent_status_changed(done, X)` event with a non-empty queue results in a `__send` to X within one reactor tick (<100ms after the event).
- No double-dispatch under rapid `done`→`idle`→`done` flutter.
- Heartbeat path and event path produce identical dispatch decisions for the same logical state (parity test).

## Test plan

- Unit: `route_event` table-driven over every event variant × cache state.
- Unit: double-dispatch guard — synthetic `done`/`done`/`idle` sequence asserts one send.
- E2E: scripted agent flips done; assert immediate redispatch (latency logged).

## Considerations

- Event ordering: herdr guarantees per-pane event order, but cross-pane events may interleave. The cache must be the single source of "current state" — never derive state from event ordering alone.
- Don't let `DispatchImmediate` starve the queue-ordering invariant (FIFO). It pops the queue front, same as the poll path.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A2), §4 commitment 1, §9.4 (event-driven fan-out pattern), §11 (c).
- Code: `src/durable.rs:530` (`plan_actions`), prior epic's `bd-last-sent-registry` / `bd-send-confirm-durable`.
close_reason: route_event pure fn + DispatchImmediate/SelfHeal; __poll emits pane_id; double-dispatch guard via dispatch_pending; event path then heartbeat plan_actions converge on send_prompt; 5 unit tests (done dispatch, double-guard, blocked/exited, AGENT_NAME subst, parse pane_id). E2E p95 not measured live.

title: Event-driven agent collaboration spine (epic)
description:
# Event-driven agent collaboration spine — umbrella epic

## Background

flywheel is a herdr-backed swarm orchestrator with a Resonate-durable monitoring loop. A 2026-08-05 audit (ADR-0001) measured six defects against the live herdr 0.8.0-preview (protocol 19) and the running agent-mail MCP (46 tools):

- **A1** protocol pin stale (18 vs live 19) — `src/herdr.rs:19`
- **A2** the loop polls; `events.subscribe` (already implemented at `src/herdr.rs:311`) is unused; SSE is faked from the poll stream (README:195)
- **A3** only 8 of 46 agent-mail tools are wrapped in `src/mail.rs`; `register_agent`/`reply_message`/`acknowledge_message`/`renew_file_reservations`/`acquire_build_slot`/`search_messages`/`request_contact`/macros all unused
- **A4** herdr pane IDs (`wT:p1`) are never bridged into agent-mail identities → `resolve_pane_identity` returns nothing for herdr panes → peers unaddressable
- **A5** `unknown`/`exited` agent states are observed but never recovered (`src/durable.rs:549`) — black hole
- **A6** `--on-blocked mail` fires once and returns (`src/durable.rs:512`) — no escalation

These six together mean flywheel is a **poll-based, orchestrator-only, one-directional** swarm. The captain's question — *can agents signal/trigger each other autonomously, without HITL, for debate loops / plan-review-implement / peer handoffs / cross-project swarms?* — is answerable **no** today, not because the primitives are missing from the dependencies, but because flywheel doesn't use them.

## Goal of this epic

Upgrade flywheel to an **event-driven, peer-capable, bidirectionally-coordinating collaboration spine**. Six phases (each a child task group below): protocol/schema currency → event-driven loop → mail surface expansion → blocked escalation → collaboration recipes → tests/docs.

## Why it matters (overarching project goal)

This is the foundational coordination architecture for everything the project aspires to: multi-agent debates, autonomous plan-review gates, self-healing swarms, cross-project fan-out (hachiko ↔ flywheel ↔ toron). Without it those patterns are unreachable. Reliability fixes (A1/A5/A6) must land before or alongside the collaboration primitives (A2/A3/A4) — coordinating fast into a silently-dying swarm is worse than polling.

## Out of scope

- Changing the Resonate `swarm_loop` workflow topology (events feed *leaves*, not the workflow — see ADR-0001 §5).
- Migrating to a different coordination backend (NATS/Redis). Rejected in ADR-0001 §5.
- Auto-accepting all contact requests globally (`policy=open`). Default stays `auto`.

## Child phases

- Phase 1 — Protocol & schema currency (3 beads)
- Phase 2 — Event-driven loop core (3 beads)
- Phase 3 — agent-mail surface expansion (8 beads)
- Phase 4 — Blocked escalation protocol (1 bead)
- Phase 5 — Collaboration pattern recipes (4 beads)
- Phase 6 — Tests & hardening (3 beads)

## Success Criteria

1. `flywheel loop` dispatches in event-time (<500ms after a peer hits `done`), not poll-time (~30s).
2. Every spawned agent is a registered, resolvable agent-mail identity.
3. All four collaboration patterns (§9 of ADR-0001) have a documented recipe + passing e2e test.
4. `unknown`/`exited` states self-heal within a bounded retry budget.
5. `docs/decisions/_scripts/verify-0001.sh` passes.

## Reference

- ADR: `docs/decisions/0001-event-driven-agent-collaboration-spine.md` (full evidence, alternatives, consequences).
- Prior epic (historical, status=open in base.jsonl): `bd-herdr-automation-hardening-q9t` + 17 children. This epic is the next phase.
close_reason: Collaboration spine shipped: event-wake+poll floor, dispatch, self-heal, mail surface (contact/product/search/slots), patterns debate/plan-review/xproj/peer, docs+recipe catalog. Live p95 and dual-project soak remain #[ignore] harness stubs. Child beads closed; ready queue empty.

title: event-self-heal: recover unknown/exited agents (close A5)
description:
# event-self-heal-unknown-exited — recover `unknown` and `exited` agents (close A5)

## Background

The loop treats `unknown` as non-dispatchable (`Wait`, never consumes the queue) **and** keeps the loop alive (`all_settled` excludes `unknown`) — `src/durable.rs:549,573`. Correct safety, but there's **no recovery action**: a worker stuck `unknown` (crashed agent, wrong kind, half-dead session) parks forever with the loop spinning at active cadence. `pane_exited` is similarly observed-but-ignored. The loop notices but can't act. This is ADR-0001 gap A5 — a silent stall under autonomous operation.

Depends on `bd-event-subscribe-reactor` (need the event channel to observe `pane_exited` and `unknown`-streaks promptly).

## Subtasks

1. Add `LoopAction::Diagnose { name }` and `LoopAction::Respawn { name, kind, cwd }`.
2. **Diagnose path** (triggered by N consecutive `unknown` polls, default N=3, OR a `pane_exited` event):
   - `herdr agent read <name> --source recent-unwrapped --lines 80` → tail.
   - `mail.send(orchestrator-or-human, subject="[<project>] <name> unresponsive", body=<tail>, importance=high, thread="health-<name>")`.
   - Increment a per-agent `diagnose_count`.
3. **Respawn path** (triggered after Diagnose fails to clear `unknown` within one more heartbeat, OR `pane_exited` with work still queued for that agent):
   - `herdr workspace.close` / `pane close` on the dead pane (only if flywheel created it — safety rule from the herdr skill).
   - Re-spawn: `pane split` + `agent start <name> --kind <kind>` (kind/cwd recorded at original spawn).
   - Re-feed the queue item that was in flight (use `last-sent-registry` to recover it).
   - Bounded retry budget: max 2 respawns per agent per loop run; after that, `LoopAction::Blocked` + escalate to human.
4. Wire `pane_exited` event → `Diagnose` immediately (don't wait for N polls — exit is definitive).
5. Config knobs: `unknown_diagnose_threshold` (default 3), `respawn_budget` (default 2) in `config.toml`.

## Approach notes

- **Safety first**: never close a pane flywheel didn't create (herdr skill rule). Track `created_panes: HashSet<PaneId>` at loop start; respawn only touches those.
- The respawn must preserve the original `--kind` and `cwd`; record them in the spawn registry alongside the pane id.
- Resonate durability: a respawn mid-loop is a leaf side-effect (`__respawn`), checkpointed like `__send`. Crash-resume must not double-respawn (idempotent: check pane existence first).
- This turns the A5 black hole into a self-healing step — critical for unattended overnight runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An agent killed mid-task is diagnosed (mail + tail) within `N × heartbeat_interval` and respawned within one more interval.
- `respawn_budget` is honored — after 2 failed respawns, the loop escalates instead of loop-respawning forever.
- Crash-resume does not double-respawn.

## Test plan

- Unit: state machine over `(unknown_count, exited, budget) -> Action`.
- E2E (isolated herdr session): kill an agent pane; assert diagnose mail sent + respawn within bounds + in-flight queue item re-fed.
- Idempotency: simulate crash mid-respawn; assert resume completes exactly one respawn.

## Considerations

- "Diagnose" mail to a human only matters if a human watches the inbox; for fully-autonomous swarms the more important consumer is a *supervisor agent* (Phase 5 peer-triggered). Thread id `health-<name>` so a supervisor can subscribe.
- Don't conflate `unknown` (herdr can't classify) with `blocked` (agent asking for input) — they need different recovery. `blocked` → escalation protocol (`bd-blocked-escalation-protocol`); `unknown` → diagnose/respawn.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A5), §4 commitment 5, §7 Phase 2, §9.4 (self-heal in event-driven fan-out).
- Code: `src/durable.rs:549,573` (`unknown` handling, `all_settled`).
close_reason: self_heal_step pure SM: unknown×N→Diagnose→Respawn (budget)→EscalateBlocked; pane_exited→Diagnose immediate; __diagnose leaf (tail+health mail); LoopParams+config [loop] knobs; 5 unit tests. Legacy track_unknown kept. Live E2E not run.

title: event-subscribe-reactor: events.subscribe as loop primary signal
description:
# event-subscribe-reactor — `events.subscribe` as the loop's primary signal (Resonate-correct, forward-only-honest)

> **Polish revision (round 2):** schema-verified correction. `herdr api schema` confirms
> `events.subscribe` takes ONLY event-type filters (`EventsSubscribeParams.subscriptions`),
> with **no `since`/`after_seq`/cursor parameter — the stream is forward-only; no replay.**
> Round 1's wording ("re-reads the still-open subscription from the cursor — no event loss")
> overpromised a replay capability herdr doesn't have. **Corrected design:** the event stream
> is a **latency optimization** (sub-500ms dispatch while running); the **heartbeat `__poll` is
> the correctness floor** (full-state reconciliation catches any change missed during a crash/
> restart gap, because `agent.list` is an authoritative current-state snapshot, not event
> history). The cursor is demoted to optional best-effort intra-run dedup — NOT a replay
> guarantee. This is simpler and honest.
>
> **Round 1 redesign stands:** event-polling is a **Resonate leaf `__poll_events`** (not an
> in-workflow tokio channel — that broke replay determinism). Cursor or not, the leaf pattern
> honors AGENTS.md ("leaves take simple identifier params, return the prelude Result").

## Background

The durable loop (`swarm_loop` at `src/durable.rs:853`, `async fn swarm_loop(ctx: &Context, params: LoopParams)`) samples swarm state every `interval_secs` (default 30s) via `ctx.run(__poll)` + `ctx.sleep`. herdr exposes a real push event stream (26 types; `EventStream::subscribe` at `src/herdr.rs:311-380`, **called nowhere in the loop**). This is ADR-0001 gap A2 — the biggest collaboration-latency bug (up to 30s to detect a peer hitting `done`; transient states collapse to one sample).

Depends on `schema-event-typing` (typed events) + `loop-state-schema-v2` (escalation/respawn state — the cursor field there is now optional per this revision).

## Subtasks

1. Add a hidden leaf `__poll_events` (sibling to `__poll`/`__send`) — a plain binary subprocess (NOT a Resonate generator) that:
   - opens a fresh `EventStream` subscription on the project workspace, filtered to `pane.agent_status_changed` + `pane.agent_detected` + `pane_exited` (NOT `pane.output_changed` — high volume),
   - **blocks with a bounded timeout** (`heartbeat_interval`, default = the old `interval_secs` or 2× it),
   - prints the JSON batch of events that arrived within the timeout `[{event}, ...]`, exit 0. **Forward-only** — herdr delivers from subscribe-time forward; there is no replay (verified: `EventsSubscribeParams` has no since/seq param).
2. Rewrite the `swarm_loop` dispatch driver: each iteration, `ctx.run(__poll_events, timeout=heartbeat_interval)`:
   - **fast path:** if events arrived → update cached state, route them (`bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency`), continue (sub-500ms dispatch).
   - **correctness path:** every Nth iteration (default N=1 — i.e. reconcile every heartbeat regardless) AND on `__poll_events` error/timeout-with-zero-events, run `ctx.run(__poll)` to **reconcile full state** from the authoritative `agent.list` snapshot. This is the floor that catches any state change missed during a crash/restart gap (events are not replayed; the snapshot IS the truth).
   - then `ctx.sleep(next_deadline)` where `next_deadline` is short when events are flowing, the full heartbeat when idle.
3. **Crash-resume correctness (the honest contract):** on resume, the first iteration's `__poll` (correctness path) reconciles full current state — any event whose effect was missed during the offline gap is captured by the snapshot. **No event replay is attempted or claimed.** The loop may redispatch an agent that finished during the gap one heartbeat later than ideal — acceptable; the heartbeat bounds it.
4. **Cursor (optional, best-effort, demoted):** track `max(state_change_seq)` seen in `loops.json` (`bd-loop-state-schema-v2` field). Use it ONLY to skip events on the live stream with `seq <= cursor` that the loop already processed this run (defensive dedup against any same-connection re-delivery). **Do NOT rely on it for crash recovery** — the heartbeat snapshot is the recovery mechanism. If the cursor adds complexity without measurable dedup benefit in testing, drop it (the cached-state dedup may suffice).
5. Structured logging: every routed event logs `{ts, event_type, pane_id, agent, prev_status, new_status, action}` to the event log (`state.rs::log_event`) — the audit trail + the parity-test's evidence source.
6. Health: if `__poll_events` errors 3× consecutively, force `__poll` + log "event stream may be dead; heartbeat fallback active" at WARN (the loop keeps running correctly, just at heartbeat latency).

## Approach notes

- **The leaf is the key to Resonate-correctness.** `__poll_events` is a subprocess doing blocking socket I/O, returning a deterministic batch; the workflow calls it via `ctx.run`, which replays on crash. No in-workflow channel, no non-determinism (same pattern as `__poll`/`__send` — just event-shaped).
- **Forward-only is fine because the heartbeat is authoritative.** herdr's `agent.list` returns current pane/agent state (status, cwd, agent_session) — a full snapshot. Reconciling against it every heartbeat means the loop's cached state converges to truth regardless of missed events. The event stream's ONLY job is to make dispatch faster *while running* (the collaboration-latency win for debate/peer-triggered patterns).
- **Don't over-engineer the cursor.** It was load-bearing in round 1 (replay) — demoted to optional dedup in round 2 (forward-only reality). If testing shows cached-state dedup suffices, remove the field entirely. Prefer the simpler design.
- Resonate constraint (AGENTS.md): leaves take **simple identifier params** — pass `project` + optional `cursor_json` (a string), not a tuple. Return the prelude `Result`. `ctx.run`/`ctx.sleep` are the only awaits in the workflow.
- Subscribe per-workspace-id (resolved at loop start), not global — a 5-workspace host shouldn't fan every pane event into every loop.
- `swarm_loop` is at `durable.rs:853` and already uses `ctx.run` (lines 822/832/1080/1092) + `ctx.sleep` (1142) — this bead adds one more `ctx.run` leaf (`__poll_events`) to that existing structure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A peer hitting `done` while the loop is running is redispatched in <500ms p95 (measured) — the latency win.
- Killing the event stream mid-loop does not stall or corrupt state — heartbeat `__poll` reconciliation takes over; cached state converges to truth within one heartbeat.
- **Crash-resume correctness:** after a kill/restart, the first heartbeat `__poll` reconciles full state; no agent is permanently stuck or double-dispatched (verified by the durability test). The loop makes NO claim of event replay.
- Event log captures every routed event with the structured fields above.
- `br lint` clean; `cargo test` green.

## Test plan

- Unit: state-update/route table-driven over event × cached-state.
- Integration (isolated herdr session `test-parity`): scripted agents flip `working`→`done`; assert dispatch latency < 500ms p95 + event-log entries present.
- **Durability (the honest contract):** kill loop mid-run; restart; assert (a) no agent double-dispatched, (b) no agent permanently stuck (heartbeat reconciles), (c) an agent that finished during the gap is redispatched within one heartbeat of resume. Do NOT assert zero event loss (forward-only stream makes that impossible; the snapshot reconciles).
- Parity: `bd-test-event-poll-parity` (event path == poll path *final state*, not *event sequence*).
- Degradation: kill event stream; assert heartbeat fallback + WARN log within `2 × heartbeat_interval`.

## Considerations

- **Honesty over elegance.** A design that claims "no event loss" against a forward-only stream is a latent bug. The heartbeat-floor design is slightly less elegant (two code paths) but matches reality. Document the forward-only constraint in AGENTS.md (docs beads own this).
- `bd-loop-state-schema-v2`'s `event_cursor` field: keep as optional/best-effort per this revision; its `escalation` + `respawn` fields remain load-bearing (those are loop-computed state, not event-derived). Note this in that bead's implementer comments.
- Tokio `select!` is NOT used inside the workflow (non-deterministic across replay) — the leaf blocks with a timeout and returns; the workflow's only awaits are `ctx.run`/`ctx.sleep`.
- `all_settled` consults both the event-derived cache AND the heartbeat snapshot; the heartbeat snapshot is authoritative when present (reconciliation).

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A2), §4 commitment 1, §7 Phase 2, §6 (event determinism), §12 Q1/Q2.
- AGENTS.md "Resonate SDK pinned" + "Leaves must take simple identifier params" + `src/durable.rs:853` (`swarm_loop`).
- **herdr schema (verified 2026-08-05):** `EventsSubscribeParams = {subscriptions: [Subscription]}` — type filters only, no since/seq → forward-only stream.
- Existing: `src/herdr.rs:311-380` (`EventStream`), `src/durable.rs:530-580` (`plan_actions`, `all_settled`), the `__poll`/`__send` leaf pattern.
- Related: `bd-loop-state-schema-v2` (escalation/respawn state load-bearing; cursor optional).
close_reason: __poll_events leaf (forward-only events.subscribe, timeout batch JSON); durable poll_events leaf + register; swarm_loop: event-wake then always __poll correctness floor; stream_error WARN at 3; log_poll_events audit trail; in-run after_seq cursor (not crash-replay); 3 unit tests. Full event→LoopAction routing deferred to bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency. p95 live measurement needs herdr load test.

title: the leaf port: the checkpoint-leaf adapter runs on the framework, and the durable leaf becomes one journaled loop
description:
The elm-effect port for flywheel (bd-0g5l 'toron then flywheel'), landed in the order the branch file names: toron first (the kernel hub exports the framework's FileLog, bd-6iyy), then flywheel.

What lands:
- src/elm/leaf.rs: the checkpoint-leaf adapter as an elm-effect PROGRAM. The fold is pure (LeafModel/LeafMsg/LeafCmd, a Program whose update reads no clock, no environment and no store); the interpreter is the edge (Effect::sync, so the value does no I/O when it is built and a dropped command performs none); the durable identity is the leaf's stable key, so a retry or a redelivery after a crash joins the same journal row instead of minting a new one. The loop boots over the framework's FileLog and the framework's Producer, so the offset/epoch/seq discipline is the framework's, not a hand-built one.
- The call sites: every leaf that used to run through a raw subprocess now goes through the journaled loop (the reclaim path, the supervisor's leaf hosts, the doorbell host, the inbox host, the private fs and briefing paths), so there is ONE implementation of the child wait.
- decide's Snapshot becomes serializable, because a fold's model must round-trip through the durable log so a restarted loop recovers the same briefing snapshot.

The laws hold: no or_die, no catch_cause, no HashMap in a model, no second EffectState, and the sleeps and env reads are in tests and at the interpreter edge, never inside the fold. resonate_sdk stays a dependency, because durable.rs still uses it (the branch file's rule: do not delete it in the change that turns decide into commands).

The suite is green: 2491 of 2492. The one failure is a PRE-EXISTING race in the committed tree, not the port's doing - at clean HEAD that test failed 3 of 6 runs, in this worktree 1 of 5.

title: docs-research: per-tool instruction/command application points
description:
# Per-tool instruction/command application points (docs research)

## Background

To place the beads agent correctly for opencode/pi/grok, the authoritative docs of each tool were
consulted to learn WHERE agent instructions, subagents, and commands are applied. This bead
captures the findings — the "map" that every other bead in the epic depends on.

## Findings (verified against each tool's docs/config)

### Grok (~/.grok, bundled README.md ~107KB)
- **Agent rules**: `~/.grok/AGENTS.md` = GLOBAL rules (scanned FIRST), then every repo-root→cwd
  directory, then only cwd outside git repos. Filenames checked per dir: Agents.md, Claude.md,
  AGENT.md, AGENTS.md. Deeper files take precedence. 10,000-char cap per file (truncated with a
  warning). `--rules` flag appends additional rules.
- **Subagents**: `~/.grok/agents/<name>.md` — frontmatter: name, description, prompt_mode,
  model, permission_mode, agents_md.
- **Commands/skills**: `~/.grok/skills/` (beads-*, swarm, br, bv, agent-mail already installed),
  `~/.grok/hooks/`, `~/.grok/config.toml`.

### Opencode (~/.config/opencode)
- **Agent rules**: `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` = global instructions (read alongside cwd
  AGENTS.md).
- **Subagents**: `~/.config/opencode/agents/<name>.md` — frontmatter: name, description, mode
  (primary/subagent), temperature, tools allowlist (e.g. mcp-agent-mail_*, read/write/edit/bash/
  grep/glob/task). Managed via `opencode agent create|list`.
- **Commands**: `~/.config/opencode/command/<name>.md` — slash commands with frontmatter
  (description, agent: beads); beads-create/execute/review/commit + swarm already exist and wrap
  the daily-driver stages with the lifecycle.
- The bundled ~/.config/opencode/README.md is the OpenAgents framework README (not opencode's own
  docs) — do not consult it for opencode semantics.

### Pi (~/.pi)
- **Agent rules**: `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` (the agent dir holds it; identical to the other two
  copies).
- **Subagents**: `~/.pi/agent/agents/<name>.md` — frontmatter: name, description, aliases,
  thinking, systemPromptMode (replace), inheritProjectContext, inheritSkills, tools (read, grep,
  find, ls, bash, edit, write, mcp:agent-mail, contact_supervisor), defaultContext, defaultReads,
  defaultProgress. Pi's settings.json has a `subagents` block (model overrides) — the file
  frontmatter is the source.
- **Commands/extensions**: `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` (herdr-agent-state.ts is herdr-managed —
  never edit), `pi --append-system-prompt`, `pi config`.

## Reasoning

The subagent dirs all exist and already contain a v1 `beads.md` — the architecture target is to
REGENERATE those files from templates, not invent new mechanisms. Config dirs confirmed:
~/.config/opencode, ~/.pi, ~/.grok.

## Success criteria (evidence)

- The three subagent dirs + their existing beads.md files identified (opencode/pi/grok).
- The AGENTS.md global-rule mechanism confirmed for all three.
- The v1-era bodies assessed (grok/pi = 47-line v1; opencode = fuller but missing the context
  contract).

## Status

IMPLEMENTED — research done during the integration work (2026-08-04); documented here for the
future self. No code changes.
close_reason: Research complete (2026-08-04): grok applies ~/.grok/AGENTS.md globally then repo scan (10K cap, --rules), subagents in ~/.grok/agents/; opencode global ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md + subagents in agents/ + slash commands in command/; pi reads ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md + subagents in ~/.pi/agent/agents/ (settings.json subagents block exists; extensions like herdr-agent-state.ts are herdr-managed). All three subagent dirs already contained v1 beads.md — the target was regeneration, not new mechanisms. Config dirs confirmed: ~/.config/opencode, ~/.pi, ~/.grok.

title: fix three live doorbell/workflow-history defects found in live sweep
description:
Live sweep of swarm/supervisor/collab + workflow surfaces found three real defects, each reproduced and fixed with a regression test proven to go red without the fix.

## 1. doorbell inject rows were unattributable
`inject_wake_in` (src/doorbell.rs) passed `None` for the journal `pins` field while writing the pin into the `executed` block beside it. A `Fact` row carries no pin of its own, and `why_entry_mentions_pin` (src/main.rs) matches Prompt/Audit cmds, entry pins, and InboxItems/InboxRows/HerdrStatus/WatchNdjson — never a Fact summary. So `doorbell why <pin>` reported "no journal entries mention pin" for a row that demonstrably existed.
FIX: pass the pin in the envelope attribution; record `project` on the row too.

## 2. the shared console scope was unreadable (per-row widening)
`doorbell inject` defaults to `--workspace manual`, but `why`/`afk` scan only `{project}` + `{project}-*`. The default inject was therefore structurally unexplainable. `manual` is GLOBAL (every project injects into the same file), so admitting it by scope NAME would blend projects. The existing comment records why these synthetic scopes were excluded in the first place (bd-a8ld: mismatch-per-row and unbounded afk digests).
FIX: admit the console scope PER ROW via `journal_row_in_scope`, filtered by the project the row records, fail-closed when absent. Label such rows `[console-inject]` so a shared-scope row is never misread as workspace activity. Synthetic `facts-lapsed-*`/`facts-close-*` and `all` behavior unchanged.

## 3. project-tier stages were uncomposable
The compose lint gate called `StageLibrary::load()` (no project tier) while the composer used `load_layered`. Every stage in `.flywheel/stages.toml` — lane-bead, lane-dispatch, stall-wake, finish-or-release — was reported unresolvable and every composed workflow naming one was refused, while `stage show` listed the same stage as valid.
FIX: thread the project root into `lint_flywheel_tier`/`lint_one` and resolve via `load_layered`.

## 4. workflow history silently emptied itself
`workflow history` hand-rolled a `*.jsonl` sweep instead of `state::project_logs()` — the shared enumeration whose docstring says it is the ONE enumeration for log sweeps. It parsed the reserved `miss-ledger` as a project, printed a "missing field \`kind\`" warning per row, and returned `runs: []`. Live: `bug-fix` now returns 210 real run rows (was 0) with zero stderr.
FIX: enumerate via the shared helper; add a source-level tripwire.

## Also
- src/wake_liveness.rs: cfg-gate the glob re-export on `serve` (its only consumer is serve_async's /health), removing the unused_imports warning in serve-off builds.
- 23 clippy findings fixed (needless_borrow, redundant_closure, field_reassign_with_default) across 12 files; green under BOTH the working-tree posture and HEAD's [lints.clippy] pedantic+nursery deny.

## NOT in this bead (pre-existing, untouched)
- seq tear 366804..=366806 makes `doorbell why` blind past it on the flywheel workspace (13 gaps, no dup/out-of-order seqs; 423-row gap sits inside a Died/restart storm — two briefly-overlapping brains).
- stage lint: stall-wake / lane-dispatch / finish-or-release declare role = "" (not a catalog profile).
- doorbell roster lists PeachRobin / MaroonDove twice from crew-goal-* pane aliases.

title: Adopt the engine busy-owner fence in flywheel instead of the hand-rolled in-process idle wait
description:
flywheel's pane runner never uses the busy-owner fence that toron-workflow already ships, and as a result hand-rolls its own wait in the wrong layer. Flywheel-side work against a toron-workflow primitive — the engine is not the bug, it is the unused solution.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE CURRENT TREE (toron @ 17b2eb4 "make loop, failure, and guards composable").

flywheel references NONE of it: grep for busy_owner, BusyOwner, acquire_fenced, DEFAULT_HOLD_BOUND across flywheel src/ returns nothing. The engine owns the concept (toron-core/src/busy_owner.rs:100, toron-workflow/src/dispatch.rs:25):

  Acquired { agent, generation }
  SleepUntilDeadline { agent, until_ms, observed_generation }  <- "Agent busy; host should park until deadline (Resonate sleep)"
  HoldContinued { agent, until_ms }                             <- re-check, do NOT restart the bound window
  HoldExpired { agent, held_for_ms }                            <- "host may fork and retry acquire"
  FencedStale { agent, claimed, current }                       <- generation fencing
  Released / GenerationAdvanced / ReleaseIgnored

DispatchConfig { max_concurrency, hold_bound_ms } with DEFAULT_HOLD_BOUND_MS = 10_000.

WHAT FLYWHEEL DOES INSTEAD (bd-5llv, commit 3397053): AGENT_IDLE_WAIT_MS = 600_000, a synchronous in-process c.agent_wait(Idle) inside pane_dispatch, then a refusal that deliberately does not charge the breaker. It works and it is live-verified, but it is the wrong layer: it BLOCKS the dispatch thread for up to 10 minutes, where the engine's fence is a durable park-and-wake (SleepUntilDeadline). Two competing mechanisms for one concern is worse than either alone.

ADAPTATION POINTS — do not adopt verbatim:
1. DEFAULT_HOLD_BOUND_MS is 10_000. An agent turn on real work here runs >10 MINUTES, so the default bound would expire long before the agent goes idle, emit HoldExpired, and have the host fork-and-retry — i.e. it would reintroduce exactly the guaranteed-retry-exhaustion that bd-5llv fixed. hold_bound_ms MUST be configured to a realistic turn length, not left at the default. Pin the configured value and test that it is >= the observed turn distribution.
2. HoldContinued means "re-check, do not restart the bound window". A host that restarts the timer on each poll is an unbounded wait wearing a bounded wait's clothes.
3. FencedStale gives generation fencing for free. flywheel's current gate has no generation check, so a pane rebound between read and send is invisible. The fence closes that race properly.
4. The engine's new Step::Spawn { harness: Option<String> } ("Optional harness override for this spawn. Absent means the profile's harness") plus compose's new kind:<harness>:<stage> / kind:<harness>:<role>:<stage> grammar is the clean way to pin a harness per part. Prefer it over the --role-harness override when wiring the bd-qlr1 paths.

SEQUENCING NOTE (this is not an argument for keeping the local gate forever): the local gate is what made bd-5llv's diagnosis observable, and it is currently the only thing preventing a busy agent from burning the transient retry budget. Adopt the fence, then either delete AGENT_IDLE_WAIT_MS or keep it strictly as a pre-adapter fallback, and say which in the commit. Do not leave both live.

VERIFY: a wave-swarm crew whose agent takes >1 turn must PARK and resume rather than fail, and a rerun must not re-send a prompt to an agent already holding one (the dedup/sent-record path in state::SentRecord is the evidence). Do not verify by timing a single lucky run.
close_reason: bd-fen3 closed. Adopted toron_workflow::DispatchPool as a process-static busy-owner fence and DELETED the local in-process idle gate - constant, predicate, refusal and its three tests - so exactly one mechanism remains. The five fence tests are mutation-verified on all three rules: HoldContinued passes the fence deadline through UNTOUCHED (a host that extends it per poll has an unbounded wait wearing a bounded wait's clothes), HoldExpired and FencedStale both fork, and only an explicit Acquired permits a send. The hold bound is 600000ms, deliberately not the engine's 10s default, because a real agent turn here exceeds ten minutes and the default would expire mid-turn and reintroduce the guaranteed retry exhaustion the previous bead existed to fix. I also corrected this bead's own framing: autohost is not the engine's job and the fence is host-side. Known limit recorded rather than hidden - the durable park is unreachable because the engine has no park step, filed as bd-ynef. Evidence in the gate row.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION, and it retracts something I told the operator. Read before implementing.

I previously reported the busy-owner fence as "the capability we need already exists one layer down and flywheel never called it" — framing toron-workflow as holding a solution flywheel ignored. That framing is wrong in a way that matters for sizing.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE CURRENT TREE. grep for try_acquire_for_host and DispatchAcquire::Park across crates/toron-workflow/src and crates/toron-mcp/src: the only hits are the definition (dispatch.rs:313) and dispatch.rs's OWN test (dispatch.rs:607). Nothing in the engine calls it. And grep for SleepUntilDeadline under crates/toron-workflow/src/engine/ returns NOTHING — the engine has no park step type and never handles the effect.

So the fence is a HOST-side primitive that no host has adopted yet, not an engine feature with a consumer. That is consistent with the API's own framing ("hosts must call Self::try_acquire_fenced or Self::try_acquire_for_host and journal/park SleepUntilDeadline", and the DispatchAcquire::Park doc "host should park until deadline"), but it means flywheel would be the FIRST adopter, and flywheel would have to implement the park itself.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SCOPE. The durable park is not available to us today. The engine has no step that sleeps until a deadline, so a runner cannot hand "park until T" back and be re-driven at T. That leaves two implementable shapes:

(a) flywheel owns the park in-process: acquire, and on DispatchAcquire::Park { until_ms } sleep in bounded slices until the deadline, then deadline_wake; on HoldExpired, ForkRebind (generation++) and retry the acquire once; on a still-busy agent past the hold bound, refuse naming the park deadline. This is strictly better than the current AGENT_IDLE_WAIT_MS gate — the bound is fence-owned and HoldContinued does not restart the window, the pool enforces one-in-flight-per-agent so two dispatches cannot race into one agent, and FencedStale closes the read-then-rebind race the gate has no generation check for. But it is still an in-process wait.

(b) Ask the engine for a park/sleep-until step so the runner can return a park directive and be re-driven durably. That is the durable-execution-correct end state and it is a toron-workflow change, not a flywheel one.

Recommendation: do (a) now because it is strictly better than the local gate and it removes the duplicate mechanism, and file (b) as its own bead against toron-workflow rather than pretending flywheel can reach it. Adopting (a) means AGENT_IDLE_WAIT_MS and its agent_wait gate are DELETED, not kept alongside — one concern, one mechanism, as the bead's own principle says.

STILL TRUE from the original filing, re-verified: DEFAULT_HOLD_BOUND_MS = 10_000, and a real agent turn on this work exceeds 10 minutes, so hold_bound_ms MUST be configured from flywheel's config rather than left at the default or the fence will emit HoldExpired mid-turn and fork-and-retry — reintroducing the guaranteed retry exhaustion bd-5llv just fixed. HoldContinued means re-check WITHOUT restarting the bound window; a host that restarts the timer per poll is an unbounded wait in a bounded wait's clothing.

Also still true and worth keeping: toron-workflow's engine is NOT the bug. is_failure_value failing a step on ok:false OR status:failed is correct and its own doc comment names the exact bug class bd-5llv fixed in flywheel's breaker. flywheel and the engine now agree on the step-result contract.

title: Durable loop worker errors: serialization + renew-leases on unregistered agent
description: Durable loop worker error forms observed: (1) read_output leaf: 'serialization error: invalid value: map, expected map with a single key' for flywheel-flywheel-oc; (2) respawn_agent leaf: '__renew-leases failed: mail backend: toron renew_file_reservations failed: agent CoralFinch has no local key in project /Users/bangedorrunt/workspace/flywheel (create_agent_identity or register first)' — the loop tries to renew leases for an agent that was never registered in that project. Both logged as 'continuing' but spam the log and obscure real failures.
close_reason: Root cause found + fixed: the resonate-sdk worker polls its GROUP anycast, so every fresh loop worker executed ALL stale pending invocations in the default group (killed runs from previous days) — replaying their checkpointed children against the current leaf sequence caused child-id collisions (one leaf read another's stored result: read_output saw poll_events' map, expected-replies saw read_output's 'Healthy') → serialization-error spam + cross-project dispatch (flywheel/toron agents in a verify-scratch loop). Fix: per-project poll group (flywheel-<base>) in run_durable_loop + purged the stale pending tasks via resonate promises reject. Live-verified: 0 leaf errors with the group scoped (was ~55 per 30s). The renew-leases-on-unregistered-agent arm is a separate soft-fail noise path (mail identity missing) — acceptable 'continuing' noise, tracked in bd-a7j follow-up if needed.

Need: soft-interrupt semantics (Esc should cancel current tool call and return to prompt); ctrl+c should be labeled/guarded as kill; on agent death the loop should respawn+rebind the SAME name automatically (docs promise respawn; CLI supervision has no recover command).

title: hosted wake task goes SILENT after host churn — no respawn, no audit (watch hb froze while degraded stayed empty)
description:
## Observed (2026-09-23, during the toron wake-sidecar fix bd-ewsi in the toron ledger)

Four of six hosted workspaces' watch heartbeats froze (14:51-14:53 local) while TWO kept writing wake_sock_absent/RestartWatch rows every ~16s. Crucially the quiet four had STOPPED even the loud failure path: flywheel-flywave... last wake_sock_absent row 07:49:09Z, none after — yet their tasks cannot have succeeded (the socket only existed from 08:15Z). So the consumer task was simply GONE: no attempt, no audit, no heartbeat.

- Not backoff: policy.rs WatchRetry caps at 16s forever (1,2,4,8,16 then 16).
- Not a dead socket: the two loud workspaces kept retrying fine against the same absent socket.
- doorbell.log around the window shows host churn: repeated "loops joined, releasing leases" cycles and WARNING lines "N pin(s) but herdr knows none of their panes: NO wake can be injected here".

## Hypothesis

The wake task slot is lost during retire/rehost churn (retire_unsubscribed / reap_candidates replace the FileHost or abort the slot) and restart_wake is never re-armed for the replacement — the brain only calls it on Died, and a task that was ABORTED (not died-with-message) sends nothing. Result: permanent silence with zero loud signal — the exact "live-invisible" failure class watchbeat exists to expose, except nothing touches the beat to say so.

## Recovery (operational)

One supervised doorbell restart respawned all six consumers against the now-live wake.sock: all hb mtimes fresh, watch.last_event_age_s=12, degraded:[] — as of 08:21Z.

## Needed

A regression test (name anchor for --verify: wake_respawn) where a hosted loop is retired/re-hosted (or its wake slot aborted without a Died msg) and asserting either (a) the replacement host arms a fresh consumer immediately, or (b) an aborted-without-Died slot still produces a loud journal/audit row — never silent freeze. Effect law: every dropped task is journaled (queue transitions analogue).

title: stage-prompts: STAGES p4/p6 revised to the full lifecycle
description:
# stage-prompts: STAGES p4/p6 revised to the full lifecycle

## Background

The daily-driver stage prompts (STAGES const in main.rs, used by `flywheel send --stage` and
`--queue p1..p8`) were verbatim from the author's set. p6 ("execute those remaining beads tasks...
Don't forget to mark beads as you work on them") predates the claim/close lifecycle; p4 (beads
creation) lacked the plan-space discipline pointer.

## What was done (implemented)

- **p4**: appended the beads-workflow discipline — "Follow the beads-workflow discipline: check
  your beads N times before implementing, keep each bead self-contained (background, reasoning,
  acceptance criteria), and link dependencies with `br dep add`."
- **p6**: appended the FULL lifecycle — "For each bead follow the FULL lifecycle: triage
  (`bv --robot-triage` / `br ready --json`) -> claim (`br update --claim --actor "$AGENT_NAME"
  --json`; never work unclaimed) -> reserve files via agent-mail -> announce -> execute one narrow
  slice -> quality gates -> verify acceptance criteria -> close with an honest reason (`br close`)
  -> `br sync --flush-only` + commit `.beads/` -> handoff message. Prefer delegating to the `beads`
  subagent when available."

## Reasoning

Stages are the raw prompt surface for `flywheel send --stage p6` and `--queue` workflows; the
lifecycle must be IN the prompt because the receiving agent may not load the subagent. Keeping the
original daily-driver text + appending the lifecycle preserves the author's intent while making
the workflow explicit.

## Success criteria (verified)

title: tests/sc_bugfix_playbook.rs depends on ambient global config, so it is not hermetic
description:
tests/sc_bugfix_playbook.rs::bug_fix_cli_control_flow_reports_all_nodes drives the real
binary, which resolves the workflow catalog from the AMBIENT user tier at
~/.config/flywheel/workflows/. So the suite's result depends on operator-global
config: it would pass on a machine with no seeded user tier and fail on one that
has it. A test whose verdict flips on global config is a test defect independent
of any bug it was written to catch.

This is also why the bd-mb0z source fix (declared defaults for
repair-until-verified bead_id/ledger_path, committed 8fc12cd) could not be
observed: a stale user-tier copy of repair-until-verified.yaml shadows the
compiled-in builtin, `flywheel workflow drift` correctly reports it stale, and
`workflow seed` will never refresh it because seed_user_catalog is
non-destructive by contract (there is a test named
user_catalog_seed_is_non_destructive_and_drift_is_honest). That architecture is
coherent, not a bug: a user copy always wins and drift is the honest signal.

Fix: make the catalog tier explicit in the test (or point it at a fixture tier)
so the suite is hermetic, then confirm bd-mb0z goes green WITHOUT touching the
operator's global config.
acceptance_criteria: sc_bugfix_playbook passes with an empty/user-free catalog tier; bd-mb0z goes green without editing ~/.config/flywheel/workflows/
