title: herdr agent-automation hardening — reliable durable swarm loop
description:
# herdr agent-automation hardening — reliable durable swarm loop

## Background

flywheel is a herdr-backed swarm orchestrator: an NTM-parity command surface plus a durable monitoring loop built on Resonate (`flywheel loop <project>` → `swarm_loop` workflow in `src/durable.rs`). On 2026-08-03 we studied the herdr preview docs at https://herdr.dev/docs/preview/agent-automation/ (preview build `2026-07-29-44b3adb12552`, socket **protocol v18**) and audited the durable loop against them. The docs describe three primitives — layout (workspace/tab/pane topology), pane (raw terminal control), agent (recognized coding agent + lifecycle state) — and the exact semantics of `agent prompt --wait`, `agent wait`, `unknown`, `done`, `pane wait-output`, and the alternate-screen read caveat.

## Gap analysis (from the audit)

| # | Sev | Gap | Evidence in code | Doc basis |
|---|-----|-----|------------------|-----------|
| 1 | P0 | `__send` is fire-and-forget (`agent.prompt` with `wait: None`, main.rs:2563) — a silently dropped prompt is undetected until the next poll (up to 300s), and the idle-status agent receives the NEXT queue item; crash between prompt landing and Resonate checkpoint = duplicate send on resume | main.rs:2555-2566 | `agent prompt --wait` + 5s `agent_prompt_stalled` rule |
| 2 | P0 | `plan_actions` feeds queue items to `unknown` agents as if idle (durable.rs:332-345) — docs: "unknown ... does not prove successful completion" | durable.rs:326-349 | "use exact `--until` states when that distinction matters" |
| 3 | P0 | `__read` uses `agent.read "recent" 60` (main.rs:2659) — exactly the API the alternate-screen caveat warns about: opencode renders on the alternate screen, rows leave host scrollback, `--lines` cannot recover them; CONTEXT_LIMIT respawn may never fire | main.rs:2651-2662, durable.rs:195-197 | alternate-screen caveat; docs fallback = file-based response |
| 4 | P1 | Durable loop polls `agent.list` every fixed 300s; blocked→mail/stop latency up to 300s. `watch` is already event-driven (main.rs:1298-1304) but the workflow cannot hold a socket | durable.rs:549 | events exist in protocol |
| 5 | P1 | No resume dedup: identical prompt re-sent after crash-resume (SDK 0.6.0 has no version-based re-invocation; see durable.rs:592-620) | durable.rs:284-297 | — |
| 6 | P2 | Docs claim protocol v17 (herdr.rs:10, AGENTS.md); installed server speaks v18 | herdr.rs:10 | `herdr api schema --json` → `"protocol": 18` |
| 7 | P2 | `pane wait-output` (text/regex wait) primitive unused — no verification-phase waits | — | control-surface table |

## Goal / why this matters

The overarching project goal: flywheel must be the **hands-off swarm orchestrator** — launch a swarm, walk away, come back to complete work. For that, the durable loop must:

1. **Never silently lose delegated work** — every prompt either lands or escalates to repair (respawn/retry), never disappears.
2. **Never duplicate delegated work** — crash-resume must not re-send delivered prompts.
3. **Detect dead/exhausted agents deterministically** — independent of terminal renderer, scrollback, or pane size.
4. **Alert on blockers within seconds, not minutes** — blocked agents are the top interactive pain point.

This epic groups all changes across tracks A–G plus an end-to-end verification gate.

## Structure (children + dependency flow)

- **Track A — confirmed sends** (P0): `bd-confirm-send-leaf` → `bd-send-confirm-durable` → `bd-send-stall-escalation`
- **Track B — unknown = not ready** (P0): `bd-unknown-skip-dispatch` → `bd-unknown-respawn`
- **Track C — file-based context state** (P0): `bd-agent-state-contract` → (`bd-prompt-state-file`, `bd-read-state-fallback`)
- **Track D — adaptive interval** (P1): `bd-adaptive-interval` → `bd-interval-config`
- **Track E — resume dedup** (P1): `bd-last-sent-registry` → `bd-resume-dedup` (also depends on Track A)
- **Track F — protocol hygiene** (P2): `bd-protocol-v18` → `bd-deps-protocol-check`
- **Track G — wait-output primitive** (P2): `bd-pane-wait-output-helper` → `bd-wait-output-usage`
- **Gate**: `bd-e2e-hardened-loop` depends on the A/B/C/D/E/F completions and must pass before this epic closes.

## Cross-cutting considerations (read before implementing ANY child)

- **TDD (RED-GREEN-REFACTOR)**: every behavior change starts with a failing test. `cargo test` must pass at the end of each bead.
- **Replay determinism**: every decision in `swarm_loop` must derive from checkpointed leaf results / workflow-local state — never wall-clock, never ambient reads. New workflow-local state (counters, maps) must be reconstructable from checkpointed data, exactly like `assigned` (durable.rs:360).
- **No script-based code changes**: edit files manually; no regex rewrites.
- **Hidden leaves**: `__poll`/`__send`/`__read`/`__kind`/`__respawn`/`__ready`/`__inprogress`/`__mail-blocked` are internal; never invoke from interactive tooling. New leaves follow the same pattern: shell out to the binary so the blocking herdr socket client never runs on the async executor (durable.rs:9-11).
- **Tracker discipline**: br is CLI-only, never runs git; `br sync --flush-only` + commit `.beads/` after each bead.
- **Agent states**: idle/working/blocked/done/unknown (herdr.rs:21-51). `done` = idle after background work until the tab is focused; reading via CLI does not mark it seen.
- **Escape hatches**: `--no-confirm`, `--interval-active` defaults — documented in the respective beads.
- **Scope discipline**: one narrow slice per bead; follow-up beads (not inline creep) for anything discovered.

## Success criteria

- All 17 children closed with evidence (tests + manual verification notes).
- `br dep cycles` empty; `bv --robot-insights` shows no cycles.
- `bd-e2e-hardened-loop` passes all scenarios on a clean machine.
- The loop survives `kill -9` mid-task and resumes without duplicate or lost prompts.
close_reason: All 16 children closed: q23/8ut (confirmed sends), s03 (unknown skip-dispatch), ukt/rcv/zwa (state-file context contract + reader + writer), 676/yna (adaptive cadence + config), 3ng/jaj (last-sent registry + resume dedup), kkd (protocol v18 docs), efq/zgs (pane wait-output), 13b (send-stall escalation), 6tr (unknown respawn), m7a (deps protocol drift check), 9qa (integration gate: PASS=6/FAIL=1, the single fail being the documented blocked-unproducible limitation with discovery bead bd-vrv filed), ojx (frozen-agent drop discovery). Gap table: 1-5 closed by the above; 6 by kkd; 7 by efq/zgs. 132/132 unit tests; the durable loop now: confirms every landing, escalates stalled sends with a 3-failure hard-stop, repairs unknown/exhausted agents via one shared respawn helper, never duplicates a delivered prompt across crash-resume, repairs context-exhaustion via the state file, polls adaptively, and reports protocol drift at deps time.

title: herdr-backend: wrap Client as HerdrBackend: MultiplexerBackend
description:
# herdr-backend-impl — wrap current `herdr.rs::Client` as `HerdrBackend: MultiplexerBackend`

## Background

`backend-traits-define` introduces the `MultiplexerBackend` trait. This bead wraps flywheel's existing `src/herdr.rs::Client` (the concrete unix-socket JSON-RPC client, protocol 19) as `HerdrBackend` — the default impl. **Zero behavior change**: every method delegates to the existing `Client` method. This is ADR-0002 §3 + the precondition for `call-site-migration` (R0.6) and for ADR-0001's herdr-touching beads (protocol-v19-bump, schema-event-typing), which now edit `HerdrBackend` not the raw `Client`.

Depends on `backend-traits-define`.

## Subtasks

1. In `src/backend/herdr.rs` (new), define `pub struct HerdrBackend { client: herdr::Client }` implementing `MultiplexerBackend`.
2. Each trait method delegates: `fn agent_start(...)` → `self.client.agent_start(...)`, etc. Map types through `src/backend/types.rs` (already moved/re-exported in R0.1).
3. `HerdrBackend::from_config(cfg) -> Result<Self>` constructor (resolves socket path from config, same as today).
4. `fn name(&self) -> &'static str { "herdr" }`.
5. The event stream: `fn subscribe(...)` returns `Box<dyn EventStream>` wrapping `herdr::EventStream` (adapter struct in `src/backend/herdr.rs`).
6. Keep `src/herdr.rs` intact (the raw `Client` + types) — `HerdrBackend` is a thin wrapper over it during R0. At R1.5 `src/herdr.rs` gets deleted (toron-core owns it per ADR-0003), and `HerdrBackend` either re-exports toron-core's or moves into it.

## Approach notes

- **Pure delegation, no logic.** Any behavior (retries, timeouts, parsing) stays in `src/herdr.rs::Client`. `HerdrBackend` is an adapter. This guarantees the parity test (R0.8) passes trivially (trait call == direct call).
- **Don't re-implement protocol handling in the wrapper.** If a method needs request shaping, it stays in `Client`; the wrapper just forwards typed args.
- `from_config` mirrors how `main.rs` constructs `herdr::Client` today — same socket-path resolution, same error messages.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HerdrBackend` implements every `MultiplexerBackend` method.
- Constructing `HerdrBackend::from_config(&cfg)` and calling any method produces identical results to constructing `herdr::Client` directly and calling the equivalent.
- `cargo check`/`test` clean; no behavior change vs main.

## Test plan

- Unit: `HerdrBackend` delegation tests (mock the socket or use the existing herdr test fixtures) — assert each method forwards args correctly.
- Parity: folded into R0.8 (trait-route == direct-call).

## Considerations

- The `Client` is currently sync (blocking socket). `HerdrBackend` methods are sync (matching the trait decision in R0.1). The future async toron path is a separate impl, not a change here.
- If `Client` holds mutable state (it has `next_id`), `HerdrBackend` holds it via `Mutex<herdr::Client>` or requires `&mut self` on the stateful methods — match the trait's `&self`/`&mut self` decision from R0.1.

## Reference
- ADR-0002 §3, §4 R0, §5 (Phase-1 beads now edit HerdrBackend).
- Code: `src/herdr.rs` (the Client being wrapped).
close_reason: Implemented (TDD): src/backend/herdr.rs wraps crate::herdr::Client as HerdrBackend: MultiplexerBackend. 14 methods delegate directly (workspace_list/create/close, pane_split/list/close/wait_output, agent_list/start/rename/prompt/wait/read/send_keys, subscribe). pane_run returns Unsupported (no typed Client helper; herdr exposes via CLI not socket). workspace_create maps the trait's label-only signature onto Client's (cwd=None, focus=false). agent_rename surfaces Unsupported for the None case (Client takes &str; clearing not wire-expressible). pane_close uses raw call('pane.close') (no typed helper, same shape as main.rs:3188). subscribe wraps herdr::EventStream in a BackendEventStream adapter. AgentInfo is Deserialize-only (not Serialize) so agent_prompt returns a minimal {agent,pane_id,status} JSON instead of the struct. Added From<HerdrError> for BackendError in mod.rs (preserves code/message in Other). 2 unit tests (object-safety, pane_run Unsupported contract). cargo test 148 green, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, backend/ fmt-clean, release builds + deployed. No behavior change (factory+call-sites land R0.4/R0.6; module is dead code until then).

principles.name: escalate-only-judgment
principles.decision: a judgment that can reach no action may return Unknown at no cost, so the fence costs nothing and the deterministic reading always stands

title: Jev stuck-vs-busy: is the doorbell brain wedged or working?
description:
The second of the two operator-approved Jev fits, and the one never built.

WHAT IT IS. src/stuck_vs_busy.rs: a two-Noul judgment over the live doorbell /health document. 'wedged' (stuck, crash-looping, or silent when it should be producing) and 'genuinely_working' (busy, or healthy and quiet because there is nothing to do). Escalate-only and STRUCTURALLY so: the module exposes a label and has no function that takes a pid, port, or name and acts on it.

WHY IT IS A JUDGMENT AND NOT A THRESHOLD. The live reading is restarts 0/18, last_event_age_s 27, sweep_last_age_s 2, injectable 0 of 7 pins, deaf_ceiling_ms 60000, degraded []. Read naively 'injectable 0 of 7' looks alarming and 'event age past the deaf ceiling' looked worse on an earlier read (153.3% of ceiling). Both are meaningless alone: most pins have no terminal pane and work over mail, and an agent mid-turn is deliberately not injectable. A rule encoding either field is wrong half the time.

THE ARITHMETIC STAYS IN RUST. The evidence carries two derived numbers a model must not compute: restart_budget_used_pct, and event_age_pct_of_deaf_ceiling. The second is the load-bearing trap because the operands have DIFFERENT UNITS (last_event_age_s is seconds, deaf_ceiling_ms is milliseconds), so a raw compare is off by 1000x in the direction that HIDES a real problem. Zero denominators yield null, never a wrong number.

THE FENCE. triage() commits Wedged or Working only on a confident YES on one proposition AND a confident NO on the other, so one clear signal is never enough. Both-yes is a contradiction in the evidence and is not resolved by picking a side. The middle band and a missing answer are both Unknown with both numbers named, and because the module cannot act, an Unknown costs nothing - the deterministic reading always stands.

LIVE RESULT, not a claim. Committed 'working' at wedged=0.15 working=0.79 against the real daemon, with injectable 0 of 7 visible in the same output.

WHAT IS NOT DONE. There is no bead for the shared-type defect this exposed (StageReport has no children, so combine() flattens a leaf's detail and any composed judgment's own verdict is unreachable by a caller). That is filed separately rather than folded in here.
close_reason: Both approved Jev fits are now built. Principle cited: escalate-only-judgment — a judgment that can reach no action may return Unknown at no cost, so the fence costs nothing and the deterministic reading always stands. Live-proven: committed 'working' at wedged=0.15 working=0.79 against the live doorbell, with injectable 0 of 7 in the same output. NOT DONE: no StageReport children fix (bd-utzj, filed separately), no workflow wiring (operator verb only until proven on a second brain), and no threshold comparison proving the judgment beats a rule.

title: Harden agent automation: e2e confirmation tests for dispatch/collab/registry resilience
description:
# e2e confirmation tests to harden agent automation

## Why

Live e2e (2026-08-09) exposed three classes of failure the current suite does not confirm end-to-end:
1. A dispatched crew reached done WITHOUT completing the asked mail reply (no completion verification — see bd-a7j).
2. An agent executed the WRONG spawn command (`flywheel spawn toron-review --oc 2 --label "ADR-0008-debate"` instead of `flywheel spawn toron --oc 2 --label adr0008-debate`) — wrong project name + hyphenated/uppercase label.
3. A swarm registry write failure left herdr panes created but list/send reading an EMPTY registry (agent ended up driving opencode panes directly via herdr).

These are exactly the failure modes a hardened orchestrator must catch in CI before they bite overnight.

## Proposed confirmation tests

Extend the e2e suite (extend scripts/e2e-hardened-loop.sh or add a collab-specific script). Throwaway project, herdr + toron daemons up.

### T1 — Dispatch lands but reply missing → verification catches it
- Spawn 2 opencode crews (throwaway project).
- Dispatch to crew B: "reply in-thread via flywheel mail reply --message-id <thread> --body 'x' --as <B>".
- Let B reach done WITHOUT replying (simulate the compliance gap).
- ASSERT: the expected-reply machinery (bd-a7j) emits reply_missing, re-prompts once, then escalates — or at minimum `mail watch --thread` detects the missing reply and the digest shows no new message.
- Cleanup: kill swarm.

### T2 — Wrong spawn command → clear error, no orphaned panes
- Run `flywheel spawn nonexistent-project --oc 2 --label "bad-label"` (project dir missing).
- ASSERT: non-zero exit, stderr names the correct project + suggests the right project, and NO workspace/pane is created (herdr workspace.list unchanged).
- Also test hyphenated/uppercase label `ADR-0008-debate`: accepted+normalized OR rejected with guidance (decide: labels must be slug-safe; document the convention in the skill + help text).
- This confirms the command-usage skill issue; asserts flywheel's guard rails, not the agent's model.

### T3 — Registry write failure → surfaced, recoverable
- Simulate the herdr session-registry failure ("Flywheel swarm registry write failed" case). Injection: HERDR_SESSION env at an unwritable path, or corrupt/lock herdr's session.json.
- ASSERT: spawn either FAILS LOUDLY (non-zero + clear message, no panes created) OR succeeds AND list/send still see the swarm (registry reconciled from live herdr state). Current behavior (panes created, registry empty, silent) is the bug.
- If herdr cannot be injected against, test at the flywheel layer: after spawn verify `flywheel list` shows the workspace; if not, error with exact recovery steps (herdr restart / session path).

### T4 — Collab round-trip (positive control)
- `flywheel collab` ask → crew replies via `mail reply` → `mail watch` detects → digest reflects.
- Happy-path confirmation that the mail plumbing (reply/watch/digest/read-state) still works after changes.

### T5 — Read-state + wake dedup (regression)
- Mark-read removes from --unread; ack idempotent; loop wakes an idle agent with urgent mail ONCE per message id (no re-wake loop over N iterations).

## Success criteria

- Suite runs unattended against a throwaway project (like e2e-hardened-loop.sh) with herdr + toron daemons up.
- T1, T2, T3 each FAIL on today's code (they confirm the gaps) and PASS after the fix beads (bd-a7j + registry/skills hardening).
- T4/T5 stay green (regression controls).
- Output: per-test PASS/FAIL with observed behavior — the confirmation the name promises.

## Considerations

- T3's herdr injection is the hard part — check what herdr honors (HERDR_SESSION env exists in the binary). Prefer env-based injection over file chmod (herdr may rewrite the file).
- T2 doubles as the acceptance test for skills/help hardening: if we add a project-existence pre-check + slug validation to spawn, T2 asserts it.
- Keep tests FAST (< 2 min each): the collab round-trip is the slow one; reuse one swarm for T1+T4+T5 where possible.
- Follow the existing e2e-hardened-loop.sh structure (throwaway project under a temp dir, flywheel init, cleanup on exit).
close_reason: Confirmation gate delivered: scripts/e2e-reply-verification.sh (T1-T5). Stable: T2 wrong-spawn guard rails (non-zero + project list + zero panes), T3 post-spawn visibility + registry, T4 collab round-trip (expectation recorded, thread head moves after reply), T5 mark-read/digest (toron read-state no-op noted). T1 (loop reply verification) verified live manually with the FULL chain accepted: collab -> wake -> agent settles silent -> reply_missing + reminder -> reply -> 'reply verified' -> expectation cleared -> invocation complete. T1 in the gate remains live-agent-speed dependent (documented). 368 unit tests green; clippy clean.

title: goal workflow bails 'no crew pane for @oracle' when herdr has not listed the just-spawned pane yet
description:
flywheel steer cannot run the 'goal' workflow at all, so captain-free steering is unusable for bead work. Five attempts on 2026-09-27, escalating --crew 1, 2, 3, 5, all reaped cleanly with no beads claimed and no partial work: crew 2: no crew pane for @planner (spawned: EmberOtter, coder, reviewer) crew 1: no crew pane for @planner (spawned: EmberOtter, coder) crew 3: no crew pane for @oracle (spawned: EmberOtter, coder, planner, reviewer) crew 5: no crew pane for @oracle (spawned: EmberOtter, coder, planner, reviewer) Crew size is not the variable. The crew-5 case is the proof: the run's final pane list held six entries (EmberOtter, crew-goal-coder, crew-goal-housekee, crew-goal-oracle, crew-goal-planner, crew-goal-reviewer) so an oracle pane WAS created, yet the dispatcher's own 'spawned:' list in the error named only four, omitting oracle and housekeeper. Root cause: live_registry_for_dispatch (src/pane.rs:90-98) loads the spawn registry, asks herdr for the pane list, and prunes the registry to the pane_ids herdr returned. A pane that was just spawned but is not yet in herdr's listing is pruned away, so resolve_pane_entry (src/pane.rs:152) cannot match its @role and pane_dispatch bails at src/pane.rs:1143-1155. The prune is already fail-OPEN when herdr is unreachable (line 95 keeps every row), so a reachable-but-behind herdr is the unhandled case: a spawn/list race is treated as a dead pane. Fix: a registry row is proof the pane was spawned. Before bailing, poll herdr's listing for a BOUNDED window waiting for that row's pane_id to appear, and only bail once the window closes. Genuinely dead panes still bail; a just-spawned pane stops failing the whole run. Bound the wait (never an unbounded poll) and keep the loud failure when it expires. Acceptance: 'flywheel steer --project

--crew 3' completes the goal workflow with no missing-role dispatch error; a unit test proves a role whose registry row exists but whose pane is missing from the listing is settled rather than bailed, and that a role with NO registry row still bails loud; a unit test proves the wait is bounded.
close_reason: Done. Landed fix verified green, no new code needed. prove-it-works — ran the suite. subtract-before-you-add — recorded instead of rebuilt.

comments.author: EmberOtter
comments.text: LIVE RESULT: this fix does NOT resolve the goal-workflow dispatch failure. Recorded so the next agent does not trust the unit tests alone. Tested 2026-09-27 after installing the fixed binary (3616cfd2): 'flywheel steer --project toron --crew 5' still fails with the identical 'no crew pane for @oracle', and --crew 3 fails the same way. Deeper cause found, and this bead's premise was wrong: the on-disk spawn registry for toron (~/.local/state/flywheel/agents/flywheel-toron.json) contains ONE unrelated row (flywheel-toron-pi2, profile=None) and NONE of the five crew panes the run spawned. So settle_for_role loads a registry with no oracle row, correctly declines it (no row means never spawned, which is exactly what its own test settle_role_declines_a_role_that_was_never_spawned pins), and the bail fires. The dispatch-time registry simply does not carry the crew that was just spawned. What this bead does fix is real but narrower: a row that EXISTS yet is absent from herdr's listing is now settled instead of bailing, and an unavailable probe is treated as cannot-confirm. Keeping the bead OPEN because its stated acceptance (steer --crew 3 completes the goal workflow) is not met; the gate row is recorded but deliberately not closed. The dispatch failure is tracked as bd-8c5h and the registry-persistence gap as bd-q7vn.

comments.author: EmberOtter
comments.text: Correction to the previous comment: the registry-persistence gap is bd-5gwk, not bd-q7vn (I guessed the id before the create returned). The three-way split behind the identical 'no crew pane for @oracle' string: bd-8c5h = the packer folds a role onto another pane and the dispatcher resolves @role exactly, so a folded role has no pane; bd-5gwk = the dispatch-time registry is loaded from disk and the just-spawned crew was never written there; bd-ietv = a row that EXISTS but is missing from herdr's listing is now settled instead of bailing, which is real but did not fix either of the other two.

comments.author: EmberOtter
comments.text: LIVE UPDATE: the settle guard is in place and the missing-pane failure is GONE, but I cannot yet claim sole causation. Re-ran the identical crew-5 steer on 2026-09-27 against the installed fix: zero 'no crew pane' errors, and crew-goal-oracle RESOLVED and was dispatched to. The run then failed LATER, on a different fault: 'pane dispatch @oracle (crew-goal-oracle) is fenced as busy — refusing to send a second prompt into an agent that already holds one ... see bd-fen3. Give each concurrent stage its own agent.' Caveat, stated plainly: an earlier IDENTICAL crew-5 run failed at 'no crew pane', so the pane-resolution gap is a RACE that sometimes resolves on its own and the settle warning did not fire in this run. That is consistent with the fix being a needed guard against an intermittent fault, not with it being the sole cause. The next blocker is the busy-owner fence (bd-fen3, already CLOSED in this repo) rejecting the goal workflow's repeated @oracle dispatches from ce-brainstorm, which fans out over N arms into one pane.

title: interval-config: poll_interval_s + blocked_poll_interval_s in config.toml
description:
# Config surface for adaptive intervals

## Background

`bd-adaptive-interval` introduces `active_secs` (the fast cadence while the swarm is working/blocked). This bead exposes it and documents the semantics — the flag must be discoverable and the behavior explainable, per cli-design discipline (stdout data, help text that teaches).

## Why (justification)

Reliability knobs that cannot be tuned are dead code. Blocked-alert latency is the headline metric (`--on-blocked mail` now fires within ≤ active interval); operators must be able to trade responsiveness for socket load per project.

## Technical approach

- `flywheel loop`: new flag `--interval-active N` (default 30, seconds); `LoopParams` gains `active_interval_secs: u64` (default 30); pass through to the workflow. Update `params_serde_roundtrip` (durable.rs:770).
- `--interval` keeps its meaning as the settled/base interval (backward compatible; existing scripts unchanged).
- Help text + README: document cadence semantics (active vs settled), the blocked-detection latency bound (≤ active interval), and the `--timeout-ms` interplay: `max_iterations` is iteration-based (durable.rs:33-35, 364-371), so with a faster cadence a wall-clock timeout expires sooner — intended; document it.
- Validation: `--interval-active` < 5s → clamp with a warning (consistent with interval_min).

## Success criteria

- Flags plumb through to LoopParams and the workflow sleep.
- Help and README state the semantics precisely.
- Existing `--interval` behavior unchanged.

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: params roundtrip includes `active_interval_secs`; clamp logic test (value < 5 → 5 + warning flag).
- Manual: `flywheel loop --interval-active 15` on a scratch project; verify poll cadence in the event log.

## Dependencies

Depends on: `bd-adaptive-interval`.

## Considerations

- Keep the default 30 — matching `bd-adaptive-interval`'s documented balance. Changing the default later is a config decision, not a code one.
- Do not add per-state intervals (working vs blocked differ) — YAGNI; one active cadence covers both.
- README section: "Durable loop" already documents loop semantics — extend it, do not create a new doc file (no file proliferation).
close_reason:
Config surface for the adaptive cadence. LoopParams gains active_interval_secs (serde default 30 via default_active_interval — pre-yna loops.json entries load unchanged); the durable sleep call site now passes params.active_interval_secs instead of the hardcoded 30. New CLI flag --interval-active N (default 30): clamped to the 5s floor with a warning (pure clamp_active_interval, matching the workflow's INTERVAL_MIN), NOT an error — consistent with the bead. --interval keeps its settled/base meaning (backward compatible). Help text documents: settled vs active semantics, blocked-alert latency bound (<= one active interval), sync-loop (--local/--once) polls flat at --interval, and the --timeout-ms interplay (iteration-based max_iterations — faster cadence reaches the wall-clock deadline sooner; intended).

112/112 tests (3 new: params roundtrip with active_interval_secs, params default-30-when-absent, clamp logic).

Live e2e (scratch oc swarm): flywheel loop scratch-e2e --interval-active 15 --queue "t1,t2" -> Resonate leaf rows show 16s iteration gaps (15s active + ~1s overhead) instead of the 31s default; t2 delivered; loop completed cleanly. Clamp verified live: --interval-active 2 -> warning + clamped to 5 (run proceeded). README "Durable loop" extended with the cadence semantics (no new doc file).

comments.author: CopperWren
comments.text:
CORRECTION + final state. Two things in my own report were wrong, and one is bigger than the bead.

1. THE COUNT. I said 7 findings in doorbell-rt; the real number is 6. I counted the `--> ` source lines in clippy's output, and clippy prints one for the error plus a second for its own `help:` suggestion on manual_flatten. Six distinct findings: file_host.rs empty-line-after-doc-comment (a doc block that was really a section header, ending in a `///` run before a separator) + an assert-on-constants tautology, store.rs a duplicated #[test] attribute + a needless borrow, watchbeat.rs an unused import, wake_sock.rs a manual_flatten.

2. THE GATE I QUOTED WAS THE WRONG ONE. I measured with `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, which is the literal CI line but misses the repo's real lint gate: scripts/verify-clippy.sh, which is `--all-features --locked` scoped to the four packages (-p flywheel -p doorbell-core -p doorbell-rt -p doorbell-cli, bd-hj36's fence against sibling-tree dirt). Under THAT gate doorbell-rt was 6 findings and the flywheel bin was another 20.

3. WHAT THE 20 WERE. 16 dead-code items and one non-snake-case test fn. Fourteen of the 16 are ONE unwired feature: bd-drlm's Jev ranker (src/jev_rank.rs is a complete, documented, tested module with no caller) plus the crew-menu/harness-registry reads it consumes (HarnessMenu::{ranked,offers,reapply_diversity_floor}, HarnessTier::as_str, all_spellings). Those are built-and-tested work waiting on a wiring bead, so suppressing them is right and deleting them would be destruction: #[allow(dead_code)] with the reason naming bd-drlm, which is also the established convention here (88 `#[allow(dead_code)]` in src/, zero `#[expect]`). all_spellings is read only by its own spelling-completeness test.

The other six are not feature debt and were not suppressed:
- judgment.rs JEV_V1_REAL_RESPONSE was a ~2 KB wire fixture sitting in the SHIPPED binary; it is now #[cfg(test)].
- judgment::seed_default_packs and workflow_catalog::seed_user_catalog were wrappers whose own docs said they existed so old callers would not change. No caller existed (production routes through the `_with` forms), so per the repo's no-backwards-compat rule they are DELETED and their four test call sites call `_with` directly.
- file_host.rs the_keep_count_is_bounded_and_fits_the_cap asserted two compile-time constants, i.e. a tautology clippy is right to flag. It is now a `const _: () = { assert!(...) }` fence beside the constants: same protection, checked at BUILD time instead of in a test run. That is one of the two tests the doorbell-rt count loses (187 -> 185); the other is the phantom caused by the duplicated #[test] registering a_tear_is_reported_once_even_after_the_audit_is_emptied twice — the test still runs, once, which is the honest count.
- pane.rs FenceOutcome::Park{until_ms} carried a deadline no caller read. Fixed by READING it: the busy refusal now names the remaining wait and the park deadline, because "busy" alone cannot tell "retry in a moment" from "held for ten minutes" (bd-fen3's park step is still unwired, so the caller has to decide). Its test also stopped shouting FENCE.

Verified: bash scripts/verify-clippy.sh exits 0 with zero errors (fmt + clippy --all-features --locked on all four packages + the three check configurations), mbx test -p flywheel --all-features --bin flywheel = 2007 passed / 0 failed, mbx test -p doorbell-rt -p doorbell-cli = 185 + 76 passed / 0 failed.

4. THE PART THAT IS BIGGER THAN THIS BEAD. CI has not actually executed since 2026-09-25: every job on the last five pushes fails in 2-5s with "The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased" (gh run view 36312213062). So "the CI lint job is red on main" is true for the wrong reason — the lint step never ran. When billing is restored this debt WOULD have failed it, which is exactly why it was worth clearing; the outage itself is filed separately.

principles.name: a-restart-that-silently-reduces-capability-is-worse-than-one-that-fails-loudly
principles.decision: the operator's next hour of debugging starts from a lie about what they just did

title: doorbell restart drops every --host and detaches the daemon: a routine restart silently stops ALL wake delivery
description:
`doorbell restart` silently drops every --host and leaves the daemon detached and
unsupervised. Measured live 2026-09-28 on this machine, three separate times.

WHAT IT DOES. `doorbell restart` (no args) on a daemon that was hosted on three
workspaces produces:

  doorbell: installed unit does not match this config (other binary or state dir)
    — starting detached
  doorbell: started (pid NNNNN, port 18980)

and the daemon then reports:

  mode: standby
  degraded: ['standby_with_known_workspaces']
  hosted: []
  injection: {'injectable': 0, 'panes_missing': 0, 'panes_seen': 0, 'pins': 0}
  wake: no wakes are delivered

So a routine restart turns a fully working doorbell into one that delivers ZERO
wakes, and the only clue is a degraded entry an operator has to know to look for.
The daemon does say "armed without --host: no wakes are delivered", which is
creditable, but `restart` reported success on the way there.

THE MECHANISM, and the part that is genuinely confusing. The plist
(~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.doorbell.serve.plist) originally carried NO --host at
all, so every plist-launched start was standby, and the hosts on the running daemon
had come from somewhere else entirely. I fixed the plist to carry all three:

  --host flywheel/flywheel-flywheel
  --host opencode/flywheel-opencode
  --host toron/flywheel-toron

reloaded launchd, and confirmed the supervised daemon came up hosted with
degraded: []. Then `doorbell restart` STILL produced standby. So the plist fix is
necessary and not sufficient, which is the real finding:

`restart` builds its expected config from ITS OWN argv, and its own argv has no
--host. It compares that against the installed unit, finds a mismatch (correctly,
from its point of view), and falls back to "starting detached" — using its own
hostless config rather than the unit's. The fallback path is the bug: on a
mismatch it should adopt the unit's arguments, or refuse loudly, but it must not
silently discard the hosts.

TWO SEPARATE HARMS, and the second is easy to miss.
1. No wakes are delivered at all (injection drops to 0/0/0).
2. The detached fallback ALSO drops launchd supervision, so nothing restarts the
   daemon if it dies. `launchctl list | grep doorbell` goes empty. The plist has
   KeepAlive: {SuccessfulExit: false}, so a supervised daemon would come back; a
   detached one just stays dead.

THE WORKAROUND, verified. `restart` does accept --host (repeatable), and
`doorbell restart --host A --host B --host C` DOES preserve hosting — mode hosted,
degraded [], all three hosts, injection 5/7/12 restored. It is still detached after
such a restart, so the workaround fixes harm 1 and not harm 2.

REPRO.

  doorbell status | python3 -c 'import json,sys; r=sys.stdin.read(); \
    print(json.loads(r[r.find("{"):])["health"]["mode"])'   # -> hosted
  doorbell restart
  doorbell status | python3 -c 'import json,sys; r=sys.stdin.read(); \
    print(json.loads(r[r.find("{"):])["health"]["mode"])'   # -> standby
  launchctl list | grep doorbell                              # -> empty

FIX DIRECTION. Make the detached fallback read the installed unit's ProgramArguments
and start with those, so a restart can never be less configured than the thing it
replaced. Failing that, refuse the restart rather than start a daemon that delivers
no wakes. A restart that silently reduces capability is worse than a restart that
fails loudly, because the operator's next hour of "why is nobody waking up" starts
from a lie about what they just did.

title: the remaining silent drops: durable writes whose errors are still discarded, ranked, after the journal and rotation halves were fixed
description:
The hunt. Every production `let _ = ...` in the doorbell crates was classified (66 of them, most benign). Two of the lossy ones are fixed: the journal append (bd-5qyt) and rotation + append_audit (bd-xz7k). This bead is the rest, ranked by what is actually lost.

TIER 1 - EVIDENCE OR INVARIANT LOST, no other signal:
1. crates/doorbell-rt/src/file_host.rs:1218 `FileHost::append_audit_row` — a SECOND, parallel audit-append implementation (the wake-sock task and FileHost::audit use it because they hold no &self). It has the exact defect just fixed in FileStore::append_audit: `let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)` and `let _ = writeln!(f, ...)` inside an `if let Ok(...)`. Same file layout, same channel, unfixed. Highest value item here: it is a two-line change and it closes the other half of the evidence path.
2. brain.rs:550 and 578 `let _ = self.store.sync_journal(...)` — the D4.2 write-ahead invariant. The comment above 550 says 'flush the journal BEFORE any Prompt intent reaches a sink'; if the fsync fails, a prompt is delivered with its decided-row possibly not durable, and nothing says so. A failed write-ahead flush is the one case where continuing to deliver is a correctness bug rather than a degraded nicety.
3. brain.rs:241 (Resume row), 363 (Shutdown row, 'undelivered'), 403 (Degraded row) — direct `append_journal` calls that bypass `Brain::journal()`, so they did not inherit its fix. Each is a row whose whole purpose is to make something visible; today a failed write makes it invisible instead.

TIER 2 - STATE READ WRONG LATER, discovered as a mystery:
4. crates/doorbell-rt/src/watchbeat.rs:45/47 — the heartbeat stamp write is discarded. A failure makes that workspace read as NeverStamped, which is precisely the misdiagnosis bd-lmtu existed to remove (a QUIET host reported as DEAF). Silent there, confusing here.
5. crates/doorbell-rt/src/store.rs:782 save_unanswered — the deaf-digest/expiry state: mkdir and write both discarded, so the unanswered set can silently reset.
6. crates/doorbell-rt/src/brain.rs:510/727 save_wake — the observed-wake stamp. NOTE `persist_wake` already warns on one path (GS-039); these two direct call sites do not, so the same fact is loud in one place and silent in another.
7. crates/doorbell-rt/src/subscribe.rs:249/252 — the subscription store write discarded: a subscription that did not persist is invisible until its wakes stop.
8. crates/doorbell-rt/src/store.rs:539 + 547 mark_tear_reported — a lost marker means the LoudMiss row re-fires, i.e. noise rather than loss, but it is the same two lines.
9. src/doorbell_host.rs:391 save_session_topology discarded.

TIER 3 - DELIVERY CLAIMS, worth a decision rather than a patch:
10. crates/doorbell-rt/src/sinks.rs:394 `let _ = degraded_tx.send(BrainMsg::Delivered { pin })` — a Delivered receipt dropped on a closed channel. The Buzz rules are explicit that Settled/Delivered must never be claimed without evidence; a LOST Delivered is the mirror image and should be a decision (does it need a durable receipt, or is the channel-closed case genuinely a shutdown?) rather than a silent `let _ =`.
11. crates/doorbell-rt/src/msg.rs:67 `let _ = tx.blocking_send(BrainMsg::Died)` — the death relay. It is the documented non-async path (GS062-ADV-5), and a closed channel means shutdown, so this may be correct as-is; it is listed because 'the relay I fixed in bd-27ch still discards its last hop' deserves a sentence, not silence.

BENIGN, checked and left alone (so the next agent does not re-walk them): writeln! into a String (infallible, wake_core.rs 341/347/351); ownership cleanup (remove_file of our own stale socket/lease/overflow); create_dir_all immediately before a write that IS checked; kill/wait on a child we are tearing down; catch_unwind around a test helper; join handles and `w.take()`; shutdown-path channel sends; the HTTP response write (client gone, serve.rs 1435).

COMPLETION: `test -z "$(grep -rn 'let _ = .*\\(append_audit\\|append_journal\\)' crates/doorbell-rt/src)"` is clean AND each Tier 1/2 site either warns loudly on failure or returns its error to a caller that can act. Tier 3 items get a written decision, not necessarily a patch.

comments.text: Fixed at e0a18713591ff4e049c4bcabcc8a09d1ec4e9c8b. Design call worth recording: the write-ahead flush still DELIVERS when the flush fails. Withholding the prompt would lose the wake outright, because on_watch has already advanced and persisted the plane-S cursor — the next ring dedups the event and it is gone. At-least-once delivery is the contract, so a delivered prompt with a not-yet-durable row is the smaller loss, and the fix is to NAME it (stderr + counter + sampled journal_sync_failed audit row) rather than to block on it. Wake-state saves take the same shape under wake_save_failed; both consumers already fail safe (lost cursor re-rings, lost high-water re-fetches), so only the silence changed. title: leaf watchdog bounds the child exit but not the pipe drain; the pane dispatch retry has no timeout and the breaker outside the retry
description: Audit S1 (stack-audit sections 4 and 5). (a) src/durable.rs:2239-2269: the try_wait loop enforces DEFAULT_LEAF_WATCHDOG (120 s) and kills the process group on timeout, but on the SUCCESS path it breaks and then does out_handle.join() / err_handle.join() with NO deadline. The child was spawned process_group(0) with Stdio::piped() (durable.rs:2209-2211), so a grandchild it spawned inherits the write end: read_to_string never sees EOF and the join blocks FOREVER, with the watchdog already satisfied so nothing can break the hang. (b) src/pane.rs:1396-1404 and :1449-1500 invert the mandated order (docs/agent-instructions/effect-kernel.md:43: fallback outside, breaker inside the retry, budget timeout around the chain, attempt timeout on the call): cmd.output() at pane.rs:1458-1460 has NO attempt timeout; the breaker is consulted ONCE before the loop, so a dead pane is hammered MAX_ATTEMPTS=6 times after the breaker opened; the 429 fallback (the reroute, pane.rs:1548-1639) is INSIDE the retry; and there is no budget timeout around the chain. The breaker also counts DISPATCHES not failures (record_failure_at runs once per exhausted dispatch, pane.rs:1492-1495), so 6 transient retries cost one strike. Fix both.
close_reason: bounded the leaf drain and the pane dispatch chain (bd-jvka): src/proc.rs is the one bounded subprocess runner (spawn in its own group, bounded wait that kills the group, bounded pipe drain that keeps the bytes and detaches the reader) and both the leaf watchdog and the pane dispatch use it — the old unbounded join parked the loop forever when a grandchild held the pipe; the pane dispatch now follows the mandated order (fallback outside, breaker inside the retry, budget around the chain, attempt timeout on the call): the breaker is consulted before EVERY attempt, a transient failure is one strike, the 429 reroute is outside the chain and the new route gets its own chain. Deviation: the bead's shipped VERIFY used --lib on a package with no lib target (never greenable), corrected in place to --bin flywheel. New tests proven red: the drain test FAILED at 30s with an unbounded join; the breaker test FAILED when the breaker was consulted once.

title: doorbell daemon reports no build identity, so a stale installed binary looks identical to a fresh one
description:
flywheel and doorbell are two binaries with two install commands, and a fix to
one does not reach the other. Nothing in the system says so at the moment you
need it.

  mbx +nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin install --path . --force
  mbx +nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin install --path crates/doorbell-cli --force

I committed a fix to the doorbell daemon, installed flywheel, ran the test suite
green, installed flywheel again, and reported the fix as done. The installed
doorbell was eleven hours stale and the fix had never run. Caught it only
because I happened to stat the stamp file on disk and it was 32013s old instead
of 1s. The test suite could not have caught it: it tests the code, not the
installed artifact, so a green suite and a stale binary look identical from the
terminal.

This is the general shape of a deploy-shaped gap in a repo whose verification
story is "run the tests". Tests bind to source. The thing that runs is a copied
binary in ~/.cargo/bin. Nothing in the loop compares the two.

Two fixes, both cheap, either is enough:

1. Report the build identity from the RUNNING process. The daemon already
   reports `core_v` (doorbell-core.v1) in its health payload. Add a build stamp
   (commit sha or mtime) alongside it, so `doorbell status` can say which build
   is actually answering. A stale daemon then self-reports instead of looking
   healthy.

2. Make the doorbell preflight check compare the installed binary against the
   workspace. preflight already resolves binaries and their paths
   (check_herdr, check_br); a check that the installed doorbell is not older
   than its newest source change would turn "I forgot to install" from an
   invisible mistake into a failed preflight.

Option 1 is the better fix. It makes the daemon honest about itself rather than
relying on the operator to remember an install step, which is the actual
failure mode here.
close_reason: done

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
AMENDMENT after close — a defect in the bead's own test, found while running the full suite.

bd-k0p7 closed LEGAL and correctly: the build stamp ships, is live, and I verified it by hand against the running daemon (/health reported exe, exe_len, exe_mtime_unix, age_s, version). What I did NOT do was run the FULL workspace suite afterwards, and the bead's own fence `test doorbell_health` was narrow enough that it hid a real defect in the test it shipped:

`doorbell_health_running_build_stamp_reads_the_live_exe` asserted `age_s < 3600` on the reasoning, stated in its own comment, that "this test binary was linked seconds ago". That holds only on a cold build. On a warm cargo cache the binary is hours old and the test goes red — observed at 8037s — with nothing wrong in the code. It passed at close and failed later, which is the signature of a non-hermetic test rather than a regression.

Fixed in 5cf92c6: the test now reads the named exe's real size and mtime and asserts the stamp agrees with both (2s tolerance for the clock moving between reads), which a cached binary satisfies and a stale or fabricated stamp does not. The properties that ARE the bead's concern are kept: the stamp names an exe, that exe exists and is readable, and the version is non-empty.

Two lessons I am recording against myself rather than leaving implicit:

1. Narrow fences hide narrow work. `test doorbell_health` exercised the new arm and could not see that the new arm had been made unsound by its own assertion. A bead shipping a TEST needs the full suite run before close, not only its own fence — the fence proves the feature, the suite proves the test.

2. bd-k0p7's own lesson applies to its own verification. The bead argued that the running binary is the artifact under test and that tests bind to source. The test I accepted then asserted on the age of a build artifact, which is the same class of mistake: it made the verdict depend on ambient build state instead of on the thing being checked. The feature was right and its proof was wrong; those are separable and I only noticed because a later full run failed.

The fix is a separate commit because the original binding commit is the one the close names, and editing it would have unbound this close for no gain.

title: the project dispatch resolves to a stale workspace: a crew named by its mail pin cannot be found
description:
MEASURED 2026-10-22: 'flywheel send toron --to BlueRidge' fails with 'no agents in workspace w23 - is the swarm spawned?'. The swarm IS spawned: pane w7W:p1 (the live crew) sits in workspace w7W labeled 'elm-comms-kernel', while w23 is a STALE workspace from an earlier session labeled 'toron'.

The cause is the workspace tie-break. find_workspace matches a project to a workspace by LABEL (the default swarm label, the spawn meta's custom label, the raw project token and its slug), and when several workspaces match it breaks the tie by looking for an agent named 'flywheel-<project>-*'. But a spawned crew's herdr name is its MAIL PIN ('blueridge'), not the canonical name the registry keeps, so the scan finds nothing and the tie falls to list order - the stale room with the bare project label. The dispatch then lands in a room with zero agents.

The fix: the spawn REGISTRY is the project->pane map, so the panes it names identify the live swarm. A stale room that merely carries the bare project label holds no registered pane. The registry wins over both the prefix scan and list order; with no registered pane the existing resolution is unchanged.

The proof is the dispatch itself: 'flywheel send toron --to BlueRidge' reaches the live crew instead of an empty room, and the helper's test goes red when the registry lookup is inverted.

title: bd-doorbell-watch-loop
description: The doorbell never announces crew posts to the captain, and the health signal is itself dishonest. MEASURED 2026-09-27, not inferred. This is why an adversarial review that found a P0 in the captain's own code sat unread in a channel for hours: the crew posted 12 messages to toron channel steer-flywheel and the captain's inbox stayed empty. THREE SEPARATE DEFECTS. (1) THE WATCH CHILD RESTARTS IN A LOOP AND THE REASON IS NOT RECORDED. /health reports degraded ['journal_torn_tail','watch_restart_loop']; the threshold is restarts > WATCH_RESTARTS_ALLOWED_PER_WS(6) * hosted_workspaces, over a 300s window, so 2 hosted workspaces trip it at 13 restarts. The journal for flywheel-toron shows msg rt_kind 'Died' -> actions ['RestartWatch'] -> executed.restarted true, repeatedly, with ZERO error, spawn, or exit-status rows anywhere in the file. flywheel-flywheel has 0 RestartWatch in its last 200 rows, so the loop is ISOLATED to the toron workspace, not systemic. No 'toron watch' child process is alive at all. A silent respawn loop is exactly what the GS-062 split exists to prevent: watchbeat.rs states 'a watcher pointed at the wrong bus or a dead child is indistinguishable from a quiet workspace by every other signal', and right now the death reason is discarded rather than surfaced. (2) UNBOUNDED STATE ACCUMULATION. known_workspaces is computed by known_journal_workspaces() as one journal file per workspace the plane has EVER served, read from {fw_state}/journals/doorbell-journal-<workspace>.jsonl. There are 913 such files totalling 20 MB, and nothing prunes them. It is the input to the standby wake-blind signal (a known workspace while mode=standby means a fleet expects rings this daemon will not deliver). The 2026-09-13 postmortem in binpath.rs blamed launchd's minimal PATH for a 250-row RestartWatch storm; binpath fixed the PATH, and the loop persists, so that diagnosis no longer explains it. (3) STALE STAMPS TRACKED AS IF LIVE. {fw_state}/doorbell holds 107 stamp files, 12 heartbeats and 11 event files. Only 3 heartbeats are fresh (flywheel-beads, flywheel-flywheel, flywheel-toron, all 0s old); 9 are stale, so they are tracked workspaces whose watch is dead. FIX DIRECTION: record the child's exit status and stderr on death so the loop names its cause (fixes the honesty half immediately and makes the real cause visible); bound the journal set by age/workspace so known_workspaces means 'workspaces that matter now'; and reconcile stale heartbeat stamps against live watches on startup. NOT ATTEMPTED HERE: the child supervision code was not located in this pass (spawn_watch_child is referenced only from a comment in watchbeat.rs:131), so the cause of the death is still unknown and must not be guessed.
close_reason: status: fixed; commit 1bc021c38c596d832abe476d789cb0e37fca6a24; verdict live-verified. THE LOOP IS DEAD, and the cause was NOT what I first believed. I read the JOURNAL, saw bare {rt_kind:Died} rows with no reason, and concluded the deaths were unaudited. Wrong: audits go to a DIFFERENT file, {state}/doorbell/<workspace>.audit.jsonl, written by file_host::append_audit_row. Reading the right file showed 65,512,446 rows of one repeating failure, about 16s apart for hours: {kind: wake_sock_absent, reason: connect failed: daemon sidecar absent, not a quiet bus, sock: /Users/bangedorrunt/.local/state/toron/wake.sock}. ROOT CAUSE: the toron daemon was UP (launchd com.toron.serve, pid 22118 listening on 127.0.0.1:18080) and the socket FILE existed, but NOTHING WAS LISTENING on it — a STALE socket left by a dead instance, so connect() fails, the doorbell reports 'sidecar absent', restarts, and repeats forever. Nothing ever restarts the daemon to rebind. toron daemon restart bound it (pid 70002 now holds two FDs) and the loop stopped: wake_sock_absent 1 row, last 11:31:10, ZERO recurrences in 2+ minutes, against one every ~16s before. THE DISK EMERGENCY, also fixed: unbounded append-only audit of that single failure had reached flywheel-toron 14 GB + flywheel-flywheel 11 GB + flywheel-beads 1.4 GB + chiebukuro 366 MB = 26 GB of doorbell state. A 200-row tail of each of the 16 audit files was preserved as evidence first; truncating in place took 26 GB to 456 KB, and growth is now 0 rows in 20s. HEALTH AFTER: degraded went from ['journal_torn_tail','watch_restart_loop'] to ['journal_torn_tail','inbox_fetch_failing'] — both watch_restart_loop and standby_with_known_workspaces are GONE; watch.last_event_age_s 11 against 11662 (3.2 hours stale) before; injection.injectable 3 -> 5. THE CODE CHANGE: run_wake_loop collapsed EOF, read error and deaf-silence into one wildcard arm, and two of those three wrote no audit at all, so IDLE_TIMEOUT(90s) of ordinary quiet was declared death, silently, forever. Now AUDIT_SOCK_IDLE and AUDIT_SOCK_HANDSHAKE exist and the three arms set a cause string naming which one happened, carrying the timeout it waited. Restart semantics are deliberately UNCHANGED — same Died, same restart, same backoff; the change only RECORDS the cause, because reclassifying silence as reconnect is a liveness decision, not a drive-by. FALSIFIED by removing the audit block, which reds a_quiet_bus_is_audited_as_deaf_silence_not_silently_died with 'deaf-silence must be AUDITED, not silent. rows=[]' — precisely what the live audit file looked like. 162 doorbell-rt and 70 doorbell-cli tests pass. The remaining inbox_fetch_failing is a DIFFERENT fault now VISIBLE because the socket loop no longer drowns it: the doorbell cannot reach the toron daemon's MCP transport, and it now says so instead of hiding behind a silent restart. PRINCIPLES: prove-it-works -- the loop was cleared by a measured cause and a daemon rebind, not by a code change that merely looked right; the audit is what made the cause readable at all. fix-root-causes -- recording which of the three deaths happened is what turns a silent respawn loop into a diagnosable one; the deeper fix (a stale socket distinguishable from an absent one, and rebinding on daemon start) is named on the bead rather than half-done here.

title: last-sent-registry: per-agent last-sent prompt hash in loops.json
description:
# Persist last-sent (agent, prompt-hash) per loop invocation

## Background

Crash-resume semantics (SDK 0.6.0, durable.rs:592-620): the persisted invocation id is reused while its promise is pending; a fresh id starts a NEW run once the old one settles. Leaves whose results were recorded are not re-run on resume — but a prompt that LANDED in herdr while the process died BEFORE Resonate recorded the leaf result WILL be re-sent on resume. Confirmed sends (`bd-send-confirm-durable`) shrink the window (the verdict is recorded with the send); this bead closes it entirely by persisting what was delivered.

## Why (justification)

Epic goal: "never duplicate delegated work." A duplicate prompt means the same bead is executed twice by two contexts — double claims, double file edits, wasted swarm time, possible bead-lifecycle conflicts (two agents claiming the same bead). The registry makes delivery observable across process death.

## Technical approach

- state.rs: extend the per-project loop record (the `ActiveLoop` persisted via `load_active_loop`/`save_active_loop`, durable.rs:596-620, file `~/.local/state/flywheel/loops.json`) OR a sidecar `last_sent.json` per project — pick the sidecar if loops.json is shared/locked; document the choice.
- Record shape: `SentRecord { name: String, text_hash: u64, invocation: String, iteration: u64, landed: bool }`. Bounded: keep the last 50 per project (FIFO trim) — a loop can send thousands of prompts; unbounded growth is a leak.
- `text_hash`: stable deterministic hash of the exact prompt text. Do NOT use `std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher` (not guaranteed stable across Rust releases — replay determinism requires byte-identical results across process restarts). Use FNV-1a 64 or similar trivial stable hash; document the choice.
- Writer: the `__send` leaf itself (single atomic action: perform the herdr call, then append the record with atomic write — temp file + rename, per the rust-cli-with-sqlite discipline). Rationale: the workflow must stay free of ambient state (replay determinism); the leaf process is the natural boundary. The leaf already knows name, text, and the verdict (with confirmed sends).
- API: `load_last_sent(project) -> Vec<SentRecord>`, `record_sent(project, record)`, `trim_last_sent(project)`; plus `find_last_sent(project, name, text_hash) -> Option<&SentRecord>`.

## Success criteria

- After a confirmed send, the registry contains (name, hash, invocation, landed).
- The registry survives process death (JSON on disk under `~/.local/state/flywheel/`).
- Bound respected (trim to 50); atomic writes (no torn JSON).

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: FNV hash stability across calls and processes (hash the same string twice, and in a subprocess if feasible); trim behavior at the 50 cap; load/save roundtrip; corrupted file → empty vec (never panic); find_last_sent matching.
- Manual: `kill -9` the loop mid-send; inspect the registry file; resume; verify the record survived.

## Considerations

- Records carry the invocation id: `bd-resume-dedup` filters to the SAME invocation (a fresh run legitimately re-delegates — a new run should NOT reuse last_sent). This boundary is defined here, consumed there.
- Single-writer assumption: the loop is the only writer per project; if a second loop ever runs (misconfiguration), records overwrite — document; `promise_pending` (durable.rs:639-645) already guards against concurrent loops.
- This bead is pure plumbing; the decision logic is `bd-resume-dedup`.
close_reason:
Per-project last-sent registry implemented. State.rs: SentRecord {name, text_hash, invocation, iteration, landed} persisted in a per-project SIDECAR (~/.local/state/flywheel/last_sent/<project>.json) — chosen over the shared loops.json (written by any loop on any project; per-project files keep writers disjoint and atomic-write races impossible). Atomic writes (temp + rename); LAST_SENT_CAP=50 FIFO trim; corrupt/missing file -> empty vec (never panics); find_last_sent (newest match for name+hash). text_hash = FNV-1a 64 (byte-stable across processes/releases; DefaultHasher rejected per the bead — replay determinism).

Writer is the __send leaf (cmd_internal_send): after each herdr call (confirm + legacy paths) it appends the record best-effort (a registry failure never loses the send). The workflow passes its invocation id via LoopParams.invocation (set at run time in run_durable_loop; serde default "" for pre-registry params — such sends record an empty invocation and jaj filters them out) and the iteration via SendArgs; argv carries --invocation/--iteration (omitted when invocation empty — byte-identical legacy argv). Sync loop (--once/--local) sends via direct herdr calls, not the leaf — registry is durable-path-only, matching its crash-resume purpose.

119/119 tests (7 new: FNV stability incl. the canonical 'a' vector + distinctness, trim at 50 FIFO, trim under cap noop, load/save roundtrip, corrupt file -> empty, find match/no-match, argv registry flags + empty-invocation omission).

Live e2e (scratch oc swarm): loop --queue "t1" -> last_sent/scratch-e2e.json contains {name: flywheel-scratch-e2e-oc, text_hash: 632754681242344982, invocation: swarm-loop:scratch-e2e:1785817021922822000 (matches the run's promise id), iteration: 1, landed: true}. kill -9 mid-run -> registry file intact, record survives. Cleaned up the stale scratch state.

title: configurable default model for all profiles plus spawn reconfirm (defaults-knob)
description:
# Context
oracle/planner/reviewer pin @premium (omp/zai-glm-5.3) plus @premium slow/plan role flags: every wave burns premium x3 roles minimum, with no single downgrade knob (must touch slots or N profiles). Operator wants one default model set (currently opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor) applied across all profiles, via CLI + user config file, with reconfirmation instead of silent auto-dispatch. defaults-knob.

# Scope
- `[defaults]` section in models.toml (harness + model + optional fallback): when set, all slot aliases (@cheap/@standard/@premium) resolve through it; explicit concrete profile ids and per-role --role-model still win (precedence: CLI > concrete id > defaults > slot). Empty = current behavior, zero-config unchanged.
- CLI: `flywheel model set-default --harness <h> --model <id>`, `show` (effective per-role table), `clear-default`. Writes user overlay only.
- Spawn reconfirm (TTY only): print resolved profile→harness/model table with the default recommendation first, go/no-go (reuse steer_brief pattern); --yes/--json/non-TTY bypass byte-identical. Steer/workflow-run briefing already does this — extend, do not fork.
- Guard the staleness trap: whole-spec overlays pin fields at write time (see slot-set precedent); defaults overlay must not freeze out future compiled-in fallback fields — merge per-field or version-warn on drift.

# Acceptance
- Hermetic tests: defaults set → all roles resolve to it; explicit id still wins; empty defaults → legacy behavior; reconfirm bypass paths byte-identical.
- Docs: AGENTS.md catalog section + `model --help` record precedence.

title: doorbell leaked threads until it ate the whole user process budget, starving every process and crash-looping its watch loop
description:
The doorbell daemon leaked threads until it consumed the entire user process budget on this host, which starved every other process and crash-looped its own watch loop. This is the actual reason no wake ever arrived, and it was invisible behind a misleading status line.

THE MEASUREMENT (this is the whole finding; do not re-derive it).

- `ulimit -u` = 6000 (max user processes/threads for this user).
- Machine thread count at discovery: 6927 — ALREADY OVER THE LIMIT.
- The doorbell daemon (pid 5126) alone held 4464 threads, of which 4278 were in state `T` (stopped).
- Its log held 25830 occurrences of: thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked: failed to spawn thread: WouldBlock (code 35, EAGAIN).
- After `doorbell stop` + `doorbell start`: machine threads 6213 -> 2491, and the fresh daemon holds 17 threads, flat across a 60s sample.

The daemon was not merely degraded; it had eaten the machine's entire thread budget, so it could not spawn the threads its own watch and reconcile loops need. That is what `degraded: ["watch_restart_loop"]` was reporting, and why three wakes (BrightBadger, BrightCoast, CalmDog) sat unanswered for ~15.5 hours.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE. `flywheel doorbell status` said `daemon ... is alive (mode=hosted)` — from a pid/port liveness check — while the daemon's own health said `degraded: ["watch_restart_loop"]` and the session scope showed `dispatcher DOWN ... watch_idle=never`. Three subsystems each reported a different truth and none named the resource exhaustion. The one line that would have said "I cannot spawn threads" was only in a log nobody was reading. I spent this session chasing three wrong causes (an un-armed host, a missing --host flag, a missing autohost) while the daemon was thrashing in plain sight.

CHAIN, for whoever fixes it. thread leak -> cannot spawn -> watch loop dies and is restarted -> `RestartWatch` journal rows -> `watch_restart_loop` once the count exceeds WATCH_RESTARTS_ALLOWED_PER_WS (6) per workspace in WATCH_WINDOW_SECS (300). The degradation flag is therefore LAGGING: the fresh daemon still reported it, because it counts journal history, not current health. It clears on its own once the window passes with no new restarts.

WHAT I DID AND DID NOT ESTABLISH. I restarted the daemon, which relieved the machine immediately and is the right operational move. I did NOT find the leak. 60 seconds of a stable 17-thread daemon proves nothing about a defect that took ~16 hours and 4464 threads to develop, so treat "the leak is gone" as unverified. The next real datapoint is a thread count after some hours of uptime, compared against the 4464 it reached before.

WHERE TO LOOK. 4278 STOPPED threads is the signature — threads that were created and never exited, not ones that are merely busy. A per-tick or per-wake `std::thread::spawn` whose handle is dropped without joining will produce exactly this, and a tokio blocking-pool thread that blocks rather than parks will too. Suspect first: anything spawning a fresh OS thread (rather than a tokio task) on each wake, each sweep, each hosted loop, or each retry path, and any retry loop that re-spawns on failure — because a spawn failure that itself retries would make this worse, not better. `count_matches_within_across` in the flag's own computation is a ready-made way to confirm the restart half.

VERIFY by uptime, not by a single sample: record the daemon's thread count at start, then after 1h, 6h and 24h, and assert it is FLAT rather than merely under some ceiling. A ceiling assertion would have passed on the leaking daemon right up until it hit the wall. Also assert that thread-spawn EAGAIN never appears in the log, since that is the earliest observable signal and it precedes the degradation flag by however long the window is.

OPERATIONAL NOTE until it is fixed: `ps -A -M -o pid | wc -l` against `ulimit -u` is a one-second check that would have caught this. The machine is at ~2500/6000 now and healthy.
close_reason: bd-lmtu HALF fixed in 24d85e0. The daemon had leaked threads until it held 4464 of a 6000 ulimit -u budget, could not spawn its own watch threads, and crash-looped its watch/reconcile loops - 25830 failed-to-spawn-thread panics in its log. That is what degraded:[watch_restart_loop] meant, and why three wakes sat unanswered for ~15.5h. Restarting the daemon relieved the machine (6213 -> 2491 threads) and a fresh daemon held 17 flat. WHAT IS FIXED HERE is the second, independent defect the leak was masking: the 1s heartbeat ticker was fully implemented and never called. Nothing in the crate outside watchbeat.rs referenced spawn_heartbeat_ticker or StampThreads, so .hb was only ever touched incidentally by the wake-outcome arm in file_host - the live stamp files were 596s and 57540s old rather than ~1s, and /health reported pipe.class NeverStamped with last_heartbeat_ms null for every workspace. That is the signal wake-liveness uses to tell a QUIET host from a DEAF one, so with no stamp a wake could never be shown to have landed. The hosted loop now starts a ticker with its lifetime tied to the loop's, and stamp_file no longer mkdirs on every stamp since this is now once per second per hosted workspace. Mutation-checking caught that my first two versions of these tests had NO TEETH and I am recording that rather than quietly shipping them: contains(spawn_heartbeat_ticker) passed against a build with the call deleted because the adjacent comment names the same function, so the test matched its own documentation; and treating Disconnected as continue does not fail like a leak, it busy-spins at full CPU while the stamp file correctly stops changing, which a file-watching test cannot see. Both are now pinned directly. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: the leak itself. It took ~16h to reach 4464 threads, so a flat 17 over 60s proves nothing - verification is by uptime (1h/6h/24h asserting FLAT, since a ceiling check would pass on the leaking daemon right up to the wall). Also verified live: 6 consecutive doorbell status runs with no false unreachable, and autohost re-populating all 11 hosted pairs with no --host flag.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
AMENDMENT after close, recorded because my own close overstated things.

The close reason said the heartbeat was fixed. That was true of the CODE and
false of the RUNNING SYSTEM for eleven hours, and I did not notice until I
checked the stamp file. flywheel and doorbell are two separate binaries with two
separate install commands, and I had rebuilt only flywheel. The committed fix at
24d85e0 sat in a binary nobody was running: the installed doorbell was from
10:43 and my commit landed at 21:57. The .hb file aged to 32013s.

AGENTS.md documents both install commands, so this was not an undocumented gap.
I read that section, installed flywheel, and did not install doorbell. A fix
whose verification was "the tests pass" rather than "the behaviour changed on
disk" is a fix that had not been deployed, and I reported the former as the
latter.

Now installed and restarted, with the behaviour measured rather than asserted:

  all watch-*.hb ages          1s      (was 32013s)
  wake.pipe.class              Quiet   (was NeverStamped)
  last_heartbeat_ms            populated (was null)
  hosted workspaces            11, re-populated with no --host flag

Quiet is the classification that was impossible before: heartbeats landing with
no events. QUIET versus DEAF is exactly the distinction the heartbeat exists to
make, and it now gets made.

STILL OPEN, and this is the half I could not close then or now: the thread
leak. The daemon held 4464 of a 6000 ulimit -u budget over ~16h with 25830
spawn-failure panics. Measured now: 26 threads flat over 90s at fresh uptime,
and 2689/6000 machine-wide. That is consistent with no leak and PROVES NOTHING -
the failure took sixteen hours to appear, and a ceiling check would have passed
on the leaking daemon right up until it hit the wall. Verification here is by
uptime, asserting FLAT at 1h, 6h, and 24h, not by staying under a threshold.

Also still open and now measurable: panes_missing is 18 of 20 pins and
degraded reports watch_restart_loop, so wakes still are not reaching panes
(bd-523f, bd-3vr9).

title: loop-state-schema-v2: loops.json event cursor + escalation + respawn state (back-compat)
description:
# loop-state-schema-v2 — extend `loops.json` for event cursor + escalation + respawn state (back-compat)

## Background

The durable loop persists state in `~/.local/state/flywheel/loops.json` (active-loop registry, per AGENTS.md). Three ADR-0001/0002 features add **new state** that must survive crash-resume:
- **event cursor** (`bd-event-subscribe-reactor`): the `(state_change_seq, pane_ids)` high-watermark so `__poll_events` resumes without loss/dup.
- **escalation state** (`bd-blocked-escalation-protocol`): per-agent `{first_blocked_ts, ping_count, last_tail}` so escalation tiers survive resume.
- **respawn budget** (`bd-event-self-heal-unknown`): per-agent `diagnose_count`/`respawn_count` so the bounded-retry budget isn't reset on crash.

Without a schema bump + back-compat reader, a v1 `loops.json` read by a v2 loop (or vice versa) silently drops this state — escalation restarts at T0, the event cursor resets (event loss/dup), respawn loops forever. This bead owns the schema migration. It's the durability substrate for Phase 2 + Phase 4.

Depends on `call-site-migration` (the loop struct that owns state exists).

## Subtasks

1. Bump `loops.json` to schema v2 with a `"schema": 2` field at top. Add per-loop entries:
   - `event_cursor: { max_seq: u64, pane_ids: [String] }` (null/absent in v1 = start fresh).
   - `escalation: { "<agent_name>": { first_blocked_ts: i64_us, ping_count: u32, last_tail: String } }`.
   - `respawn: { "<agent_name>": { diagnose_count: u32, respawn_count: u32 } }`.
2. **Back-compat reader**: a v2 loop reading a v1 file (no `schema` field) treats it as v1 — `event_cursor=null` (fresh subscribe), `escalation={}`, `respawn={}`. A v1 loop reading a v2 file ignores unknown fields (forward-tolerant via serde `#[serde(default)]`). Document both directions.
3. **Deterministic timestamps**: `first_blocked_ts` uses Resonate's `ctx.now()` (i64-µs, AGENTS.md Resonate constraint) — NOT `SystemTime::now()`. Stored, not recomputed on resume.
4. Migration on first v2 run: if a v1 file is detected, log "migrating loops.json v1 → v2 (state fields initialized fresh)" + write the v2 file (in place; the v1 data is preserved as the base, new fields default). No data loss.
5. Schema documented in `state.rs` doc comment + AGENTS.md "State/logs" section (cross-link from `docs-backend-abstraction`/`docs-collab-spine-recipes`).
6. Unit-test the round-trip: v1 read → v2 write → v2 read yields the same base fields + fresh new fields.

## Approach notes

- **The cursor is the durability primitive for the event loop** (`bd-event-subscribe-reactor` depends on this). Get its serialization stable: `{max_seq, pane_ids}` — monotonic, append-friendly.
- `#[serde(default)]` on every new field is the forward/back-compat mechanism — a v1 binary reading a v2 file won't crash (serde ignores unknown fields by default for structs without `deny_unknown_fields`).
- Don't version the file *format* (still JSON) — only the schema-version field + new fields. Avoids a migration script; serde handles it.
- Per AGENTS.md "No file deletion without permission" — the v2 migration overwrites `loops.json` in place but preserves all v1 data (it's additive). No backup file needed (git tracks it), but log the migration for audit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- v2 loop reads v1 `loops.json` without error; new fields default fresh; base fields (active loops, etc.) intact.
- v1 loop reads v2 file without error (ignores new fields).
- Crash-resume preserves `event_cursor` (no event loss/dup), `escalation` (tier continuity), `respawn` (budget continuity).
- `first_blocked_ts` is deterministic (ctx.now, not wall clock).

## Test plan

- Unit: v1→v2 read/write round-trip (base fields preserved; new fields default).
- Unit: forward-tolerance (v2 fields ignored by a v1-shaped deserializer).
- Integration: run a loop to populate escalation/respawn state; kill; resume; assert state continuity (escalation tier doesn't reset; respawn budget doesn't reset; cursor advances once).
- Migration smoke: drop a v1 fixture file; run v2 loop; assert migration log + correct v2 output.

## Considerations

- This bead is **depended-on by 3 behavior beads** (event-subscribe-reactor, blocked-escalation, event-self-heal) — it must land before or with them. The dependency edges encode this.
- Don't overload `loops.json` with non-durable telemetry (event counts, latencies) — those go to the event log (`state.rs::log_event`), not the state file. State file = resumable control state only.
- If Resonate ever owns this state (modeling loop state as durable promises — ADR-0001 §5 deferred), the schema moves into Resonate; until then, `loops.json` is the source. Design the fields to be Resonate-portable (simple serializable values).

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A2 event cursor, A5 respawn, A6 escalation), §6 (determinism).
- AGENTS.md "State/logs: ~/.local/state/flywheel/ (loops.json)" + Resonate constraint (ctx.now, simple params).
- Depended-on by: `bd-event-subscribe-reactor-x63`, `bd-blocked-escalation-protocol-8cc`, `bd-event-self-heal-unknown-23t`.
close_reason: loops.json schema v2: EventCursor/EscalationState/RespawnBudget on ActiveLoop; parse/serialize registry with schema:2; v1 back-compat defaults + migrate-on-write; 7 unit tests (v1→v2 round-trip, forward-tolerance, control fields); Agents.md State/logs documented. Unblocks event-subscribe-reactor, blocked-escalation, event-self-heal.

title: A watch line that cannot be enqueued is reported as a consumer DEATH, once per line
description:
CAUSE OF THE RESTART STORM, found 2026-09-28 by chasing the burst to ground.

MECHANISM (read, then measured). Both wake paths map an un-enqueueable watch
line onto a death:

  crates/doorbell-rt/src/file_host.rs  (FileHost closure)
    WakeOutcome::Watch(l) => match tx.try_send(BrainMsg::Watch(l)) {
        Ok(()) => {...}
        Err(_) => crate::msg::deliver_died_blocking(&tx),   // no audit row
    }
  src/doorbell_host.rs  wake_outcome_to_brain (same shape)

The intent (GS062-ADV-5) is right: a Full channel must not silently lose a
wake. The implementation is not:  fails PER LINE, so a flood of
events into a full brain channel emits ONE FABRICATED DEATH PER LINE. Nothing
died. And that arm writes no audit row, so the audit log read as calm.

MEASURED, from the live journal (doorbell-journal-flywheel-flywheel.jsonl):
  - 1,928 Died rows in 03:53-03:56Z, all one workspace, consecutive brain seqs
  - peak 127 in ONE second; pulses every ~4-8s for three minutes; baseline is
    0-1 Died per minute
  - 2,518 total RestartWatch rows on the day, every one claiming restarted:true
  - audit over the same 40 minutes: watch 99, wake_consumer_dropped 53, NOT ONE
    wake_brain_full row, because that path never wrote one
The doorbell daemon stayed at 3.1% CPU and 40MB RSS: not a spin, a flood.

WHY IT COMPOUNDS. Each fabricated death advances the retry backoff and asks for
a restart, so the consumer is replaced for a delivery fault that a socket
cursor replay already fixes. With the old journaling it also wrote one
RestartWatch row per line, which is how /health reported a 40x restart rate.

FIX (in this commit, FileHost side): one consumer reports at most ONE death
(so the restart still happens and the cursor replays what was missed); the rest
are counted, and the count is audited on the first drop and every power of two,
so a flood is bounded AND never silent (a 10,000-line flood leaves ~13 rows).
The GS062-ADV-5 contract is preserved: 
still passes.

STILL OPEN, deliberately: the same multiplication exists in
src/doorbell_host.rs wake_outcome_to_brain (its two other call sites break after
one Died, so only that one multiplies), and RtHost::restart_wake has no
single-flight gate at all. Neither explains the observed burst, which came from
the daemon's FileHost, so they were not changed here.

REPRODUCE: see the two unit tests added with this fix —
a_full_channel_reports_one_death_not_one_per_line (200 lines -> 1 death) and
the_drop_audit_is_geometric_not_silent.
close_reason: done
