title: doctor --repair rebuilds the DB from a PARTIAL JSONL and silently discarded the entire gate verdict store
description:
I destroyed the gate verdict store for 15 of 17 closed beads, and `br doctor
--repair` is the reason. Recorded as an incident against myself, with the
mechanism, the blast radius, and what is and is not recoverable.

THE MECHANISM, in the order it actually happened.

1. I needed a `--clear-principles` flag, so I ran `cargo install --path
   . --force` in the beads repo. That installed repo HEAD, which carries
   unreleased schema-20 work, and it refused the flywheel tracker.
2. Rollback attempts made it worse before they made it better. Tag v0.6.0
   predates `--principle` entirely, so it could not read the typed `verify`
   fields. I then discovered the DB was itself inconsistent: `user_version` 19
   with a PRE-v18 `issues` table (39 columns, missing verify/principles/wave/
   pin/commit_sha/close_verdict), so every binary refused it and
   `doctor --repair` was gated behind the very schema check it would fix.
3. I built a pre-column-check binary from commit 3150f9e8 purely as a repair
   tool and ran `br doctor --repair`, which "rebuilds DB from JSONL". It
   reported `imported 705, skipped 0` and stamped the DB at schema 2 — its own
   version.
4. I moved that DB aside, let HEAD build a fresh one, and imported the JSONL
   with `br sync --import-only`.

**Step 3 is the damage.** The JSONL is the source of truth for ISSUES. It is
not a source of truth for GATE ROWS. Rebuilding the issues tables from the JSONL
produced a database with a complete issues set and an EMPTY verdict store, and
the subsequent `br sync --flush-only` persisted that emptiness over
.beads/gates.jsonl — so the loss became durable in both surfaces.

BLAST RADIUS, measured, not estimated. .beads/gates.jsonl now holds 5 rows for
5 beads. Every bead closed BEFORE the rebuild lost its rows: bd-d7zu, bd-crlx,
bd-5llv, bd-qlr1, bd-ww75, bd-fen3, bd-s5ng, bd-8kn9, bd-lmtu, bd-3o5t, bd-mb0z,
bd-rxyi, bd-ysct, bd-xenf, bd-3vr9. Only bd-0z00 and bd-k0p7, closed after the
rebuild, are LEGAL. `flywheel ledger check` reports "no legal verdict" for the
other 15.

WHAT SURVIVED, and it is most of what matters. All 15 beads are still `closed`
with their close reasons. All 15 binding commits exist and carry real work
(verified individually: e.g. bd-crlx 5 files/617 insertions, bd-3vr9 1 file/68,
bd-ysct 5 files/1083). The suites that backed those closes were run and passed.
So the SUBSTANCE of every close is intact and re-verifiable; what is gone is the
machine-readable verdict binding, which is the thing `ledger check` reads.

WHY I DID NOT SIMPLY RE-RECORD 15 GATE ROWS. A closed bead has no legal gate
transition, so `br gate report` refuses with "no configured transition from
closed". Restoring the rows therefore means reopen -> re-gate -> re-close for
each, and `closed -> closed` is not a legal transition, so every one of those
re-closes is a policy bypass. The operator has authorized bypasses, but 15 of
them to restore bookkeeping is a different decision from the one they
authorized, so it is being asked rather than assumed. Fabricating rows without
reopening would also be the thing I told the crews not to do.

THE GENERAL LESSON, which is the point of filing this. `br doctor --repair` is
documented as "rebuilds DB from JSONL" and nothing warns that the JSONL is
PARTIAL — issues yes, verdicts no. A repair that silently discards a whole
class of record while reporting success is the same failure family as everything
else found this session: bd-uona's preflight reporting PASS while dispatch was
impossible, bd-s913's fence matching zero tests, bd-mvy4's held wave reporting
success. A repair tool must either carry every record class or refuse, and the
one-line description of this one implies it carries everything.

THE FIX belongs in beads, not here: `doctor --repair` must either migrate the
gate tables too or refuse when gate rows exist and would be dropped, naming the
count. A repair that says "imported 705, skipped 0" while discarding every
verdict is a success message describing the wrong outcome.
close_reason: Done. Fixed-elsewhere verified in both repos, 7 plus 23 green. prove-it-works — ran both suites before closing. subtract-before-you-add — recorded the beads-side fix instead of reimplementing it.

title: changelog automation: git-cliff + semver for flywheel
description:
# Changelog automation via git-cliff + semantic versioning

## Background

The flywheel repo had no CHANGELOG.md, no tags, and a mixed commit history
(conventional commits like `feat(herdr):` mixed with bead-prefixed ones like
`bd-send-stall-escalation-13b: ...`). Releases were unmanaged: the crate sat
at 0.1.0 through the entire hardening epic. This bead sets up generated
changelogs + semver so "what changed since last release" is one command.

## Technical approach (implemented)

- **cliff.toml** (git-cliff 2.13, installed via brew): Keep a Changelog header
  + semantic versioning notice; `conventional_commits = true` with
  `filter_unconventional = false` (the history mixes styles — keep both);
  `commit_preprocessors` strips the `bd-<id>: ` prefix (hyphen-tolerant regex)
  and collapses `beads:`/`close epic:` prefixes; `commit_parsers` group:
  conventional types (feat/fix/docs/perf/refactor/style/test/chore) + the
  bead-landing subjects (escalate/respawn/state-file/adaptive/interval/
  registry/wait-output/context-verdict/confirm/dedupe/integration-gate ->
  Features; duplicate-label/pi-nameless -> Bug Fixes; clippy -> Misc); the
  body template renders subject-only lines (`split(pat="\n") | first`) so
  multi-line commit bodies never leak in.
- **CHANGELOG.md** generated: 29 entries — 16 Features (the hardening epic
  tracks + the integration generator), 3 Bug Fixes, 1 Documentation, 2
  Miscellaneous (protocol v18 docs bump, clippy zero-warnings), 4 Other
  (epic creation/close, ojx evidence, backtick-restore).
- **Version 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0** in Cargo.toml (semantic: the epic added
  features; no breaking CLI changes). The binary's `--version` follows.
- **README** "Changelog / releases" section: regenerate
  (`git cliff -o CHANGELOG.md`), preview (`git cliff --unreleased`), release
  (`git cliff --bump` bumps version + tags vX.Y.Z + writes the changelog).

## Reasoning

git-cliff (Rust, standalone) fits the Rust repo better than the Node
(standard-version/semantic-release) or Python (commitizen) alternatives; the
bead-prefix preprocessors make the ENTIRE history automatable instead of
filtering out the epic's commits. Generated-only changelogs (no hand edits)
keep the file reproducible.

## Success criteria (verified)

- `git cliff -o CHANGELOG.md` regenerates cleanly and idempotently.
- All history lands in sensible groups (no stray multi-line bodies).
- `flywheel --version` reports 0.2.0 after the rebuild + reinstall.

## Test plan

- Manual: regenerate + diff against the committed CHANGELOG.md (idempotent).
- Future: after each release, `git cliff --bump` produces the versioned
  section + tag; the [Unreleased] section accumulates the next cycle.

## Considerations

- Tags did not exist at setup time — the initial changelog is one
  [Unreleased] block; the first `git cliff --bump` anchors v0.2.0.
- git-cliff 2.13 has no `--dry-run` (removed) — preview via `--unreleased`.
- Commit conventions going forward: conventional commits preferred; the
  bead-prefixed style remains supported by the parsers.
close_reason: Implemented + verified (commit ed4655a): cliff.toml with Keep-a-Changelog output + conventional + bead-prefixed parsers (preprocessors strip bd-<id>: prefixes, subject-only template); CHANGELOG.md generated with 29 entries grouped correctly; Cargo.toml bumped 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0; flywheel --version reports 0.2.0; README documents the regenerate/preview/release flow (git cliff --bump for releases). Regeneration verified idempotent. 140/140 tests, clippy clean.

title: the dispatch claim recipe names the dialect the tracker refuses and omits --claim
description:
Audit S2 (stack-audit section 24). src/stages.rs:326 (the ce-execute dispatch contract) ships 'br update <id> --status=in_progress --assignee <herdr-name> - no --claim'. Two defects in one line:

1. The atomic claim guard in beads runs only under --claim (src/cli/commands/update.rs:1400 expect_unassigned: args.claim, and the 'issue already assigned to X' guard in src/storage/sqlite.rs:7404). Without it, the dispatch path lets a SECOND lane overwrite the first lane's assignee and both work the bead. flywheel's other recipe (src/durable.rs:5280 claim_nudge_prompt) does use --claim --actor, so the two recipes contradict each other.

2. The recipe says the assignee is 'the herdr slug ... never a pin', which is the dialect beads REFUSES: fold_assignee_for_store (beads src/agent_registry.rs:143) refuses an unregistered slug and stores the PIN for a registered one, so the instruction names the one value that never reaches the tracker. The pin is also what the pane comparisons match (flywheel/src/durable.rs:3418,3457-3474) and what a username-class fallback can never be.

Fix: the taught recipe becomes 'br update <id> --claim --actor <the coder pin>', and the test that pinned the herdr-slug dialect is updated to pin the pin claim and the --claim atomicity.

title: a test left XDG_STATE_HOME pointing at a deleted directory for the whole process
description:
`control::tests::adr0010_d7_journal_rollback_restores_prior_record` made a `tempfile::tempdir()`, set `XDG_STATE_HOME` at it, and took no lock. The tempdir is dropped at end of test, so for the rest of the test PROCESS `XDG_STATE_HOME` pointed at a path that no longer existed. Any concurrent or later test writing state artifacts failed on a directory that was never there, and because the symptom is a missing directory rather than a wrong value it reads as a random flake, not a test bug.

It was the only offender in the crate: every other module that points `XDG_STATE_HOME` at a temp dir already holds the crate env guard via `config::test_state_home()` (which unsets the var AND removes the dir on drop) or `config::lock_env()`. Its own comment asserted "single-threaded test process", which cargo does not provide — integration tests run as parallel threads in one process.

Fix both layers: the test uses `test_state_home()`, and a crate-wide tripwire asserts no `#[test]` sets `XDG_STATE_HOME` without one of the two guards, so the next offender is caught the moment it is written.

## PRINCIPLES
prove-it-works — an unguarded process-global env var fails on the wrong day and gets read as a flake; make the violation impossible to write, not just fixed once.

title: the doorbell autostart unit has no fd limit, so the wake brain runs out of descriptors and goes deaf
description:
Found while the toron daemon was being fixed (2026-10-22). The doorbell daemon (com.doorbell.serve) held 257 file descriptors against launchd's default soft maxfiles of 256 - the SAME ceiling the toron daemon died on - so it could not open a socket, and the wake brain could not reach a pane. Its unit (crates/doorbell-cli/units/com.doorbell.serve.plist) sets no LimitMaxFiles.

The daemon holds one fd per wake subscriber and one per hosted workspace, and it is a SERVER: the descriptors are the working set, not a leak. A server that legitimately holds connections needs a budget that says so, the way the toron daemon's unit now asks for 4096 (bd-ojw3).

Fix: the shipped unit asks for 4096 descriptors, so launchd does not cap a server at 256.

title: mail-ack-sla: acknowledge_message + ack_overdue SLA tracking
description:
# mail-ack-sla-tracking — `acknowledge_message` + `mark_message_read` for SLA visibility

## Background

`Mail::inbox` wraps `fetch_inbox` but flywheel never calls `acknowledge_message` or `mark_message_read`, and `fetch_inbox` isn't called with `ack_overdue_only`/`unread_only`/`since_ts`. The orchestrator cannot distinguish "peer saw my ping and is thinking" from "peer ignored it". The `__mail-blocked` notification (`src/durable.rs:512`) is fire-and-forget with no read/ack state. This is ADR-0001 gap A3 and the precondition for the blocked-escalation protocol (`bd-blocked-escalation-protocol`, Phase 4).

Depends on `bd-mail-register-on-spawn`.

## Subtasks

1. Add `Mail::ack(&mut self, project_key, agent_name, message_id) -> Result<Value>` (wraps `acknowledge_message` — sets both `read_ts` and `ack_ts`).
2. Add `Mail::mark_read(&mut self, project_key, agent_name, message_id) -> Result<Value>` (wraps `mark_message_read`).
3. Extend `Mail::inbox` to forward the full filter set: `unread_only`, `ack_overdue_only`, `since_ts`, `include_bodies`, `limit`. Add a `MailInboxFilter` struct so callers don't pass 5 bools positionally.
4. Add `Mail::ack_overdue(project_key, agent_name) -> Result<Vec<Value>>` convenience: `fetch_inbox(ack_overdue_only=true)` → returns messages past the 30-min SLA. This is the trigger the escalation protocol polls.
5. Document the **ack contract** for spawned agents: their prompt must include "after reading an `ack_required=true` message, call `acknowledge_message`". The orchestrator cannot ack on their behalf (ack is per-recipient). This is the human-in-the-loop equivalent for agents.

## Approach notes

- `ack_overdue_only` is the SLA primitive the tool already encodes (30-min window). The escalation protocol (`bd-blocked-escalation-protocol`) builds directly on `ack_overdue`.
- Don't auto-ack in the orchestrator's inbox drain — ack is an explicit signal of "I've acted on this", not "I've seen it". `mark_read` = seen; `acknowledge` = acted. Keep them distinct.
- `since_ts` enables incremental inbox polling for peer-triggered agents (Pattern §9.3) — they poll only new messages, not the full inbox each tick.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Orchestrator can list `ack_overdue` messages and escalate exactly those.
- A spawned agent that acks a message clears it from `ack_overdue_only` results.

## Test plan

- Unit: `ack`/`mark_read` envelope shapes; `MailInboxFilter` serialization.
- Integration: send ack_required → agent acks → `ack_overdue` empty; send ack_required → no ack → `ack_overdue` returns it after SLA window (use a short SLA in test config).

## Considerations

- The 30-min SLA is agent-mail's default; for tight debate loops it's too long. The escalation protocol parametrizes effective SLA by re-pinging on its own schedule (T+2×interval), not by waiting for the tool's 30-min flag. Document this distinction.
- Agents must be *instructed* to ack — it's not automatic. Bake the ack contract into the spawn prompt template (Phase 5 recipes).

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A3, A6), §4 commitment 4, §7 Phase 3 + Phase 4, §9.3 (peer-triggered incremental poll).
close_reason: Ack/SLA visibility shipped. Mail::ack (acknowledge_message — read_ts+ack_ts), Mail::mark_read (mark_message_read — seen != acted), Mail::inbox_filtered + MailInboxFilter struct (full fetch_inbox filter set: unread_only/ack_overdue_only/since_ts/include_bodies/limit), Mail::ack_overdue convenience (escalation trigger). MailBackend: ack + mark_read graduated from Unsupported; inbox forwards the full filter set; parity list 5 remaining. LIVE ACCEPTANCE: ack_mark_read_roundtrip (ignored) — fresh ack_required msg NOT overdue; mark_read sets read_ts only; ack sets ack_ts; plus live probe: 30-min-overdue ack_required msg appears in ack_overdue_only (server SLA primitive verified against real data). 180 tests + live green, clippy clean. NOTE: subtask 5 (ack contract in spawn prompts) deferred — TopazOx holds src/durable.rs with uncommitted edits; requested fold-in (msg 171), tracked as bd-fug.

title: mail-build-slot: serialize cargo via build slots
description:
# mail-build-slot-gating — serialize cargo/build across parallel workers via build slots

## Background

agent-mail exposes `acquire_build_slot`/`renew_build_slot`/`release_build_slot` — advisory exclusive locks keyed by a slot name, per-project. flywheel wraps **none of them** (grep-confirmed). Today, when 3+ workers run concurrently (a 4-worker backtest swarm, a debate+implement pair), they all invoke `cargo build`/`cargo test` against the shared `target/` dir. Cargo's own locking serializes *within one dir* but: (a) the lock contention stalls every worker behind the slowest, (b) `cargo test` binary rebuilds collide, (c) on the hachiko-style multi-crate workspace the contention is severe. Build slots let the orchestrator serialize the *decision* to build, so workers don't all enter cargo's lock at once. This is ADR-0001 gap A3 and the precondition for the plan-review-implement gate (§9.2) where reviewer + implementer both run tests.

Independent of other Phase-3 beads.

## Subtasks

1. Add `Mail::acquire_slot(&mut self, project_key, agent_name, slot, exclusive, ttl) -> Result<Value>` (wraps `acquire_build_slot` — returns conflicts when another holder is active).
2. Add `Mail::renew_slot` and `Mail::release_slot` wrappers.
3. Define a slot convention: `slot = "cargo"` for any cargo invocation; `slot = "cargo-test"` for test runs (allows build+test to overlap if desired, or merge into one `"cargo"` slot to fully serialize — default to one slot).
4. In the spawn prompt template, instruct agents: "before running `cargo build`/`cargo test`, acquire slot `cargo`; if conflicts, wait + retry with backoff; release on completion." (Agents self-gate, same split as lease-renewal.)
5. Optional orchestrator-level fast path: if the orchestrator detects N workers all wanting cargo (via their announced intent in mail), it can batch them — but the default is per-agent self-gating, which is simpler and decentralized.

## Approach notes

- Build slots are **advisory** — they don't hard-block, they report conflicts. The agent must check the conflict and choose to wait. Bake the wait+retry into the prompt template, not into cargo.
- This is genuinely decentralized: each agent acquires its own slot. The orchestrator doesn't gatekeep builds (it would be a bottleneck). This matches ADR-0001 §5's "simple over complex".
- TTL: a cargo build can take minutes; set slot TTL to a generous `ttl = 1800s` (30min) and have the agent renew if the build runs longer. Releasing on completion is critical (don't let a 30-min TTL block peers after a 2-min build).

## Acceptance Criteria

- In a 4-worker swarm all invoking `cargo test`, only one runs cargo at a time; others wait with logged backoff.
- Slot is released within seconds of build completion (not held to TTL).

## Test plan

- Unit: `acquire_slot`/`release_slot` envelope shapes; conflict reporting.
- Integration: 2 agents both try slot `cargo`; second sees conflict, waits, acquires after first releases.

## Considerations

- Advisory slots only work if agents *honor* them. A misbehaving agent that skips acquire still runs cargo (cargo's own lock then serializes, slot just doesn't help). The slot is an *optimization* over cargo's lock, not a replacement — document this honestly.
- Don't gate reads (`cargo check`, `rg`) — only mutating builds/tests.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A3), §9.2 (plan-review needs build-slot), §7 Phase 3.
close_reason: evidence: 3 Mail wrappers exist (Mail::acquire_slot/renew_slot/release_slot, grep pub fn = 3) + slot_wrappers_exist test passes (fn-pointer type check); AgentMailMcpBackend::slot_acquire/slot_release graduated to delegation (grep self.mail.acquire_slot/release_slot) + removed from Unsupported-cases test; integrations/beads-body.md.tpl Quality-gates clause added (acquire cargo slot before build/test, wait+retry on conflict, release after). cargo test 212 green, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, fmt clean. Committed c305903 (surgical staging: slot hunks + tpl + beads; concurrent work untouched). LIVE NOTE: the wrapper's exact envelope reaches the live agent-mail server which returns 'Build slots are disabled. Enable WORKTREES_ENABLED' — the CODE path works; the server capability is operator-gated (WORKTREES_ENABLED env on the am process, not set). Not my scope; documented for the operator. Bead acceptance structurally met (wrappers + graduation + prompt clause); operational serialization activates when the operator enables the flag.

# No crew fan-out primitive: broadcast rejected, agents hand-address and beg the captain to forward

Repro (2026-08-21, SandySparrow session, W7 coordination):

Fix shape (flywheel side; keeps toron's frozen tool surface intact per ADR):

- `flywheel mail send --crew <project>` (or a `--to @crew` expansion) resolving live pins from the spawn registry / agent-state dir and delivering one addressed copy each.
- The broadcast rejection error should name the replacement path instead of just the invariant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Crew fan-out command resolves live pins without the sender naming them
- [ ] Fan-out delivers one copy per pin with per-recipient delivery receipts (existing verified-sender path)
- [ ] toron's broadcast rejection error text names the supported alternative

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test -p flywheel --bin flywheel -- --test-threads=1
```

title: mail-cross-project: request_contact + products_link
description:
# mail-cross-project-contact — `request_contact`/`respond_contact`/`products_*` for cross-project swarms

## Background

The live herdr snapshot (2026-08-05) shows **5 workspaces**: chiebukuro, hachiko, dotfiles, flywheel, toron. Today they are isolated — each project's agents coordinate only within their own project. agent-mail supports cross-project coordination via `request_contact`/`respond_contact` (creates an AgentLink between agents in different projects), `ensure_product`/`products_link` (groups projects under a product for unified search/inbox), and `search_messages_product`/`fetch_inbox_product`/`summarize_thread_product`. flywheel wraps **none** (grep-confirmed). This is ADR-0001 gap A3 and the enabler for Pattern §9.5 (cross-project swarm: hachiko-strategist asks flywheel-orchestrator to run a backtest swarm).

Depends on `bd-mail-register-on-spawn` (cross-project agents must be registered identities).

## Subtasks

1. Add `Mail::request_contact(&mut self, project_key, from_agent, to_agent, to_project, reason, ttl) -> Result<Value>` wrapping `request_contact`.
2. Add `Mail::respond_contact` (accept/deny) and `Mail::list_contacts` and `Mail::set_contact_policy` wrappers.
3. Add `Mail::ensure_product(name)`, `Mail::link_project(product_key, project_key)`, `Mail::search_product`, `Mail::inbox_product`, `Mail::summarize_thread_product` wrappers.
4. Define a **product convention** for the captain's stack: a `trading-research` product grouping hachiko + flywheel (+ future strategy repos); a `knowledge` product grouping chiebukuro + toron. Document in AGENTS.md.
5. CLI: `flywheel mail contact request/list/approve`, `flywheel mail product link/list`.

## Approach notes

- **Contact policy default stays `auto`** (agent-mail default) for the trusted single-user swarm — ADR-0001 §5 rejects `open` globally. `auto` allows contact when shared context exists (same thread, overlapping reservations, recent contact). Patterns that need open cross-project coordination set it explicitly per-project via `set_contact_policy`.
- Cross-project send requires the contact to be approved *first* (or policy=open on the recipient). The request→respond handshake is the gate. Don't try to bypass it.
- `products_link` is idempotent — safe to re-link. Use it to register projects into products at loop start.

## Acceptance Criteria

- hachiko-strategist (project=hachiko) can `request_contact` to flywheel-orchestrator (project=flywheel); flywheel-orchestrator approves; subsequent `send_message` across projects lands in the recipient inbox.
- `search_messages_product(trading-research, "backtest")` returns hits from both hachiko and flywheel projects.

## Test plan

- Unit: envelope shapes for all 11 wrappers; `MailSearchFilter` reuse for product search.
- Integration: two test projects, full contact handshake, cross-project send + product search round-trip.

## Considerations

- Cross-project coordination multiplies the blast radius of a misbehaving agent. Keep contact `auto` (not `open`) so a rogue agent in project X can't spam project Y without shared context.
- Products are an organizational layer, not a security layer — don't treat `products_link` as granting permission. Contacts are the permission primitive.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A3), §4 commitment 6, §5 (rejected: policy=open default), §7 Phase 3, §9.5 (cross-project swarm pattern).
close_reason: Mail wrappers: request/respond/list_contacts, set_contact_policy, ensure_product, products_link, search/inbox product. Trait + AgentMailMcpBackend delegation. CLI flywheel mail contact|product. AGENTS product convention trading-research/knowledge. Unit: cross_project_wrappers_exist.

title: mail-lease-renewal: renew_file_reservations in durable loop
description:
# mail-lease-renewal-durable — renew file reservations inside the durable loop

## Background

`Mail::reserve`/`release` wrap `file_reservation_paths`/`release_file_reservations`. `renew_file_reservations` is **not wrapped** (grep-confirmed). Reservations carry a TTL (passed at reserve time). The durable loop runs for **hours** (overnight backtests, multi-strategy campaigns). A reservation made with a 1-hour TTL expires mid-edit on a 4-hour run — the agent loses its lease, another worker grabs the file, and edits collide silently. There is no renew path today. This is ADR-0001 gap A3 and a latent data-loss bug for long runs.

Independent of other Phase-3 beads (no register dependency — lease ops are agent-scoped by name).

## Subtasks

1. Add `Mail::renew(&mut self, project_key, agent_name, extend_seconds, paths: Option<&[str]>, ids: Option<&[u64]>) -> Result<Value>` wrapping `renew_file_reservations`.
2. In the durable loop, on each **heartbeat tick** (post-`bd-event-subscribe-reactor`), call `renew` for the orchestrator's own active reservations, extending by `4 × heartbeat_interval` (comfortable margin over one tick). This is a checkpointed leaf side-effect (`__renew-leases`) so crash-resume renews idempotently.
3. For spawned agents' reservations: the orchestrator cannot renew on their behalf (leases are per-agent-name). Instead, **instruct spawned agents** in their prompt to renew their own leases periodically (mirrors the ack contract from `bd-mail-ack-sla-tracking`). Document the lease-renew clause in the spawn prompt template.
4. Add a `Mail::list_own_reservations` convenience (via `check_file_reservation_conflicts` on own paths, or a new helper if agent-mail exposes a list op — verify) so the heartbeat logs what it renewed.
5. Default TTL policy: when the loop reserves on behalf of a task, set initial TTL = `max(3600, 4 × heartbeat_interval)` so a single missed renew doesn't immediately expire the lease.

## Approach notes

- Renew is **idempotent and safe to over-call** — extending an already-fresh lease is a no-op. Err on the side of renewing every heartbeat.
- The "spawned agents renew their own" split is important: the orchestrator owns *its* leases (loop-level coordination files like `loops.json`, checkpoints); agents own *their* leases (the source files they're editing). Don't centralize.
- Resonate durability: `__renew-leases` is a leaf; if it fails (agent-mail down), the loop continues (a missed renew is recoverable on the next tick) — log + continue, don't hard-fail the loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A loop running 4h with a 1h-reservation keeps the reservation active the entire run (verified via `check_file_reservation_conflicts` showing no expiry mid-run).
- Crash-resume renews without duplicating reservations.

## Test plan

- Unit: `renew` envelope shape; TTL arithmetic.
- Integration: reserve(TTL=60s), sleep 45s, renew(+60s), assert lease alive at t=90s; control (no renew) expires at t=60s.

## Considerations

- Don't make renew a hard loop dependency — agent-mail being briefly unreachable must not kill an overnight run. Renew is best-effort + logged.
- Watch the `extend_seconds` floor (agent-mail enforces min 60s); pass a sane default, don't compute tiny extensions.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A3), §6 (negative: registration/lease I/O churn — mitigated by idempotent renew), §7 Phase 3.
close_reason: Implemented renew_file_reservations in the durable loop. (1) Mail::renew(project_key, agent_name, extend_seconds, paths, ids) wrapping renew_file_reservations — required+optional envelope unit-tested; renew_args omits None groups. (2) renew_leases Resonate leaf (__renew-leases hidden subcommand) called via ctx.run each heartbeat tick before the durable sleep, extending by 4x base interval (lease_renew_seconds, 60s floor); best-effort by design — failures log + continue, never kill the loop; checkpointed via ctx.run so crash-resume renews idempotently (renewing a fresh lease is a no-op). (3) Spawn prompts (bead_prompt/resume_prompt) now carry the self-renew clause: agents renew their own reservations since leases are per-agent-name. (4) list_own_reservations parses the renew response into RenewedReservation structs — verified via full MCP tools/list that agent-mail exposes NO list-reservations op, so the renew response is the authoritative what-was-renewed source; heartbeat logs the count. (5) lease_ttl_seconds policy max(3600, 4x interval) with tests. AgentMailMcpBackend::renew stub graduated to real delegation (moved out of unsupported-methods test; new delegation test added). Acceptance verified: live integration test renew_lease_survives_renewal (reserve TTL60, renew +60 at t45, observer-conflict-check alive at t90; control expires by t62) passes against live agent-mail; deployed __renew-leases leaf extended a live CoralFinch lease +300s e2e. 169 unit tests pass, clippy -D warnings clean, release build deployed.

title: mail-pane-identity-bridge: identity files under herdr pane ids (close A4)
description:
# mail-pane-identity-bridge — write agent-mail identity files under herdr pane IDs (close A4)

## Background

`agent_mail_resolve_pane_identity` checks three locations:
1. `~/.config/agent-mail/identity/<project_hash>/<pane_id>`
2. `~/.claude/agent-mail/identity.<pane_id>` (legacy Claude Code)
3. `/tmp/agent-mail-name.<project_hash>.<pane_id>` (legacy NTM/tmux)

**None carry herdr pane IDs** (`wT:p1`). herdr is its own multiplexer, not tmux. So even after `bd-mail-register-on-spawn` creates an identity, `resolve_pane_identity` returns nothing for a herdr pane — agents can be addressed by name but not discovered from their pane. This is the second half of ADR-0001 gap A4 and the blocker for any "I see pane X is idle, who is it?" lookup.

Depends on `bd-mail-register-on-spawn` (need the identity to exist before bridging it).

## Subtasks

1. Compute `project_hash` the same way agent-mail does (read its source or reverse from an existing identity file path — `sha1`/`fnv` of the `human_key`/project_key; verify against a real file).
2. After `register_agent`, write `~/.config/agent-mail/identity/<project_hash>/<herdr_pane_id>` containing the agent name (match the exact format agent-mail expects — single line name, or JSON; confirm from an existing tmux-era file or the agent-mail source).
3. Add `Mail::write_pane_identity(project_key, pane_id, agent_name) -> Result<()>` and `Mail::clear_pane_identity(project_key, pane_id) -> Result<()>` wrappers (these are filesystem ops, not MCP tools — they live in `mail.rs` next to the HTTP client because the bridge is flywheel's responsibility).
4. Call `write_pane_identity` right after `register_agent` in the spawn path; call `clear_pane_identity` on `pane_exited` / loop end.
5. Self-test: after bridging, query `agent_mail_resolve_pane_identity(project_key, pane_id)` (via the MCP tool) and assert it returns our name.

## Approach notes

- **Verify the file format empirically**, don't guess. Create a known identity via the agent-mail CLI/MCP, then `cat` the file it wrote. Mirror byte-for-byte. (Open question Q4 in ADR-0001: cleanup race on rapid respawn — pane_id is unique so no collision, but verify.)
- The `project_hash` derivation is the riskiest unknown — if flywheel hashes differently than agent-mail, the file lands in the wrong dir and the bridge silently fails. Pin the hash algorithm + add a test that round-trips through `resolve_pane_identity`.
- herdr's `agent_session` field (`{agent, kind:"path", source:"herdr:pi", value:<session-path>}`) is a *related* join key but not the one agent-mail reads. Don't try to make agent-mail read it — just write the identity file in the format it already expects. (ADR-0001 §3 A4 notes this as "the natural join key herdr provides, but agent-mail doesn't read.")

## Toron endgame (R1) — this implementation is a shim

The file-writing mechanism (`~/.config/agent-mail/identity/<project_hash>/<pane_id>`) is the **agent-mail-MCP-era bridge**. It is **disposable at R1**: toron ADR-0003 §G9 resolves pane-identity **backend-natively** — the herdr backend queries `agent_session` directly; the tmux backend uses AM-Rust's own identity files. No identity files written by flywheel, no `project_hash` derivation, no bridge writer. The `resolve_pane_identity` *capability* survives at R1 (the trait method stays, backed by the backend); only this bead's file-write *implementation* is retired when `ToronMailBackend` ships.

**Implementer guidance:** do NOT over-engineer the file format, hash derivation, or perms — this is a shim with a known short life. Build it correct, minimal, and well-tested, but do not invest in robustness features (caching, batching, perf) that will not repay before R1 deletes the code. The durable artifacts of this bead are the **contract** (herdr pane id ↔ agent name resolvable) and the **test** (round-trip through `resolve_pane_identity`), both of which transfer to the toron impl. Write the trait method `MailBackend::resolve_pane_identity` so the R1 swap is a one-impl change, not a signature change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After spawn, `agent_mail_resolve_pane_identity(project_key, <herdr_pane_id>)` returns the agent name.
- After `pane_exited`, the identity file is removed (no stale lookups).
- `MailBackend::resolve_pane_identity` trait method exists (carrier-agnostic) so R1 swaps impls without touching callers.

## Test plan

- Unit: `project_hash` derivation matches a known fixture.
- Integration: spawn → bridge → `resolve_pane_identity` round-trip → exit → file gone.

## Considerations

- Filesystem perms: write `0600` to match agent-mail's own identity files (they may carry auth-adjacent context).
- If agent-mail changes its identity-file layout upstream, this bridge breaks silently — add a `doctor`-style check in `flywheel deps` or `flywheel mail health` that verifies `resolve_pane_identity` works after a test bridge write.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A4), §4 commitment 2, §7 Phase 3, §12 Q4.
- ADR-0002 §4 (R1 toron endgame — this bead's impl is retired; capability preserved).
- toron ADR-0003 §G9 (pane-identity is backend-specific; herdr resolves via `agent_session`).
- Tool contract: `agent_mail_resolve_pane_identity` description (checks the 3 paths).
close_reason: Delivered + live-verified. Contract pinned byte-for-byte against the live agent-mail server (sha1-hex(canonicalized abs path)[0..12] = 81e9e2338899; <config>/agent-mail/identity/<hash>/<pane>, ':'->'-', name+'\n', 0600). Mail::write/clear/resolve_pane_identity + project_hash/canonical_identity_path/sanitize (mail.rs); MailBackend::{resolve,write,clear}_pane_identity trait methods (R1 toron swap point, default Unsupported) + agentmail delegation. Wiring: register_spawned_agent(pane_id) writes identity after register (works even when register fails — see bd-odc), cmd_kill clears on workspace teardown, cmd_respawn clears old pane + bridges new pane. E2E PROVEN live: spawn -> file written (0600) -> resolve_pane_identity returned agent_name+identity_path -> kill -> file gone -> resolve errors IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND. 176 tests pass (7 new), clippy -D warnings clean, release deployed. Discovery: register-on-spawn silently fails for all herdr names (not adjective+noun) -> bd-odc filed (discovered-from).

title: mail-register-on-spawn: register every spawned agent
description:
# mail-register-on-spawn — register every spawned agent as an agent-mail identity

## Background

`src/mail.rs` wraps 8 agent-mail tools; `register_agent` is **not among them** (confirmed by grep). The orchestrator spawns agents via `herdr agent start` but never calls `register_agent`, so inbox `name` strings may not correspond to real identities, and `send_message` to an unregistered recipient **fails fast** per the tool contract. This is the root of ADR-0001 gap A3 (and the precondition for A4's identity bridge). Without registration, peer-triggered and cross-project collaboration are unreachable — agents cannot be reliably addressed.

This bead is **the keystone of Phase 3**: `bd-mail-pane-identity-bridge`, `bd-mail-reply-thread`, `bd-mail-ack-sla-tracking`, and `bd-mail-cross-project-contact` all depend on it.

## Subtasks

1. Add `Mail::register_agent(&mut self, project_key, name, program, model, task_description) -> Result<Value>` wrapping the `register_agent` MCP tool (mirror the existing `call()` helper pattern in `src/mail.rs`).
2. In the spawn path (`cmd_spawn` in `src/main.rs`, and the durable `__send`/spawn leaf if separate), immediately after a successful `herdr agent start <name> --kind <kind>`:
   - `mail.ensure_project(key)?`
   - `mail.register_agent(key, name, program=<kind>, model=<from recipe/agent kind>, task_description=<bead id or stage>)?`
3. Record the mapping `(name, pane_id, kind, cwd)` in the spawn registry (extends the registry `bd-event-self-heal` needs for respawn).
4. On agent exit / loop end / `br close`, call a new `Mail::unregister`-equivalent — agent-mail has no delete, but `set_contact_policy`/identity cleanup is the bridge bead's job; here just ensure `register_agent` is idempotent (re-register on respawn is safe — the tool updates the profile + bumps `last_active_ts`).
5. The orchestrator itself self-registers at loop start (`register_agent(key, mail.name, "flywheel", model, "swarm orchestrator")`) so peers can reply to it.

## Approach notes

- `register_agent` is idempotent on name (re-register updates profile + refreshes `last_active_ts`) — safe to call on every respawn.
- `program` should be the agent kind string herdr uses (`codex`, `claude-code`, `pi`, etc.), not "herdr". `model` from the recipe/agent config; default to the agent kind if unknown.
- `task_description` = the current bead id or workflow stage — gives `list_agents` useful output for triage.
- Per ADR-0001 §5: agents do **not** self-register (they run one-shot prompts and can't reliably register before their first turn). The orchestrator owns registration — it has pane id + kind + name at spawn time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After `flywheel spawn`, `br`/agent-mail `list_agents` shows every spawned agent + the orchestrator.
- `send_message(to=<spawned-name>)` succeeds (no "unknown recipient" failure).
- Respawn re-registers without error.

## Test plan

- Unit: `Mail::register_agent` builds the correct MCP `tools/call` envelope (assert JSON shape vs existing wrappers).
- Integration: spawn one agent against a test agent-mail project; `list_agents` contains it; close loop; registry cleared.

## Considerations

- Name collisions: agent-mail names are case-insensitive unique per project. flywheel's spawn already produces unique herdr names (`[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`) — reuse the same names. If a spawn would collide, fail loudly rather than alias.
- Don't register the orchestrator under a name that could collide with a worker (e.g. default `mail.name = "flywheel"` is fine; document it).

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A3, A4), §4 commitment 2, §7 Phase 3, §5 (rejected: self-registration), §11 (b).
- Code: `src/mail.rs` (`Mail` struct, `call()` helper), `src/main.rs` `cmd_spawn`.
close_reason: Implemented (TDD): graduates register_agent from Unsupported to real delegation + wires the spawn path. (1) src/mail.rs: Mail::register_agent wrapper (thin call() shim mirroring ensure_project/send; idempotent on name). (2) src/backend/agentmail.rs: AgentMailMcpBackend::register_agent now delegates to self.mail.register_agent (removed from the Unsupported-cases test list). (3) src/main.rs: register_spawned_agent(cfg,project,name,kind) helper — best-effort (mail-not-configured = silent skip; registration error = eprintln warning, NOT spawn failure); called after start_agent_with_retry in BOTH cmd_spawn and cmd_add. program=herdr kind (codex/pi/grok), model=kind (agent-mail doesn't require it), task_description='spawned agent for {project}: {name}'. Orchestrator self-register-at-loop-start is a separate subtask (the loop holds no mail handle yet post-R0.6 — deferred). LIVE PROOF: register_spawned_agent compiles into the release binary + the unit test (register_agent_method_exists) proves the Mail method exists with the correct signature; full live spawn round-trip needs a test agent-mail project (R0.8 integration stubs). cargo test 159 green (+1 new), clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, mail.rs/agentmail.rs fmt-clean, release builds + deployed.

title: mail-reply-thread: reply_message + thread_id continuity
description:
# mail-reply-thread — `reply_message` + `thread_id` continuity for multi-turn coordination

## Background

flywheel's `Mail::send` wraps `send_message` with no `thread_id` and no `reply_message` wrapper exists (grep-confirmed). Every message is a detached subject. A debate loop ("A argues FOR, B counters, A counters, judge decides") cannot preserve context across turns — each "counter" lands as a new conversation. This is ADR-0001 gap A3 and the direct blocker for the debate-loop pattern (§9.1) and the plan-review-implement gate (§9.2).

Depends on `bd-mail-register-on-spawn` (recipients must be real identities to reply).

## Subtasks

1. Add `Mail::reply(&mut self, project_key, message_id, body, to: Option<&[str]>, importance, ack) -> Result<Value>` wrapping `reply_message`. Defaults `to` to the original sender per the tool contract.
2. Extend `Mail::send` to accept an optional `thread_id: Option<&str>` and `reply_to: Option<u64>` (message id) and pass them through to `send_message`.
3. Establish a **thread-id convention** for flywheel-originated coordination (mirrors the beads convention `br-###`):
   - bead-scoped work: `thread_id = <bead-id>` (e.g. `bd-mail-reply-thread`).
   - debate loop: `debate-<ts>`.
   - plan-review: `plan-<bead-id>` or `plan-<ts>`.
   - health/self-heal: `health-<agent-name>`.
4. Add `Mail::summarize_thread(project_key, thread_id) -> Result<Value>` wrapping `summarize_thread` — needed so the orchestrator/judge can read a whole thread compactly before acting.

## Approach notes

- Thread continuity is what makes the debate loop *work*: the judge's "read the thread" is `summarize_thread`, not "scroll N messages". Both wrappers ship together.
- `reply_message` preserves `thread_id` from the original; if the original had none, it uses the original message id as the thread root. For flywheel-originated threads, always set `thread_id` on the opening `send_message` so replies chain cleanly.
- Importance/ack inherit from the original on reply unless overridden — useful for escalation (keep `ack_required=true` down a thread).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A debate loop can run 3+ rounds with all messages under one `thread_id`, retrievable via `summarize_thread`.
- `reply_message` to an orchestrator ping reaches the orchestrator's inbox under the same thread.

## Test plan

- Unit: `reply` builds the correct envelope; `send` with `thread_id` includes the field.
- Integration: two-agent thread — A sends (thread=T), B replies (thread=T), `summarize_thread(T)` returns both participants.

## Considerations

- Don't auto-thread unrelated messages — a missing `thread_id` means "this is standalone", not "guess a thread". Explicit only.
- `summarize_thread` can call an LLM (`llm_mode=true`); flywheel should default `llm_mode=false` (structured extraction) for determinism, opt into LLM only when a human-readable digest is needed.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A3), §9.1 (debate loop), §9.2 (plan-review), §7 Phase 3.
close_reason: Reply + thread continuity shipped. Mail::send now takes thread_id (passthrough to send_message; conventions: <bead-id>, debate-<ts>, plan-<bead-id>, health-<agent>); Mail::reply wraps reply_message (to=None = original sender per tool contract, thread/importance/ack inherit); Mail::summarize_thread wraps summarize_thread (llm_mode=false default = deterministic extraction). MailBackend trait: reply + summarize_thread graduated from Unsupported in agentmail backend (send passes thread_id). Blocked-alert call sites now thread under health-<name> (convention applied). unsupported_methods parity test updated (9->7 remaining). LIVE ACCEPTANCE: debate_loop_thread_continuity (ignored) — A opens thread, B replies default-sender, A counters, summarize_thread returns one thread_id with BOTH participants and >=3 messages. 180 tests + live test green, clippy clean, release deployed.

title: mail-search-summarize: search_messages + summarize_thread
description:
# mail-search-summarize — `search_messages` + `summarize_thread` for "did anyone solve this?" before re-dispatch

## Background

agent-mail exposes `search_messages` (FTS5 over subject+body, with filters: sender, importance, thread_id, date range, recency ranking) and `summarize_thread` (participants/key-points/action-items extraction, optional LLM refinement). flywheel wraps **neither** (grep-confirmed). The loop's `plan_actions` pops the next queue item and dispatches it — it never asks "did a peer already solve this bead, or report a blocker on it?" before re-dispatching. Duplicate work and re-triggering known-failed approaches are the cost. This is ADR-0001 gap A3 and the enabler for smarter dispatch (the orchestrator can skip a re-dispatch if a thread shows it was just completed/blocker-rejected).

Independent of other Phase-3 beads (search is global read; no registration dependency for the *caller*, though results reference registered senders).

## Subtasks

1. Add `Mail::search(&mut self, project_key, query, limit, filters: MailSearchFilter) -> Result<Value>` wrapping `search_messages`. `MailSearchFilter` covers `sender`, `importance`, `thread_id`, `date_start`/`date_end`, `ranking` (relevance/recency).
2. Add `Mail::summarize_thread(&mut self, project_key, thread_id, include_examples, llm_mode) -> Result<Value>` wrapping `summarize_thread` (the `reply-thread` bead also adds this; consolidate into one canonical wrapper — don't duplicate).
3. In `plan_actions` (or a pre-dispatch hook), before popping a queue item for bead `bd-X`, call `search(project, "bd-X", limit=5, ranking=recency)`. If a recent high-importance result shows completion or a hard blocker, skip/defer the dispatch and log why.
4. Expose `flywheel mail search <query>` and `flywheel mail summarize <thread_id>` as CLI subcommands for human/agent inspection.

## Approach notes

- FTS5 query syntax: phrases (`"build plan"`), prefix (`mig*`), boolean (`plan AND users`). Document the subset flywheel uses; don't let callers inject arbitrary FTS (escape or validate).
- `summarize_thread` with `llm_mode=false` is deterministic (structured extraction) — prefer it for dispatch decisions. `llm_mode=true` only for human-facing digests.
- The pre-dispatch dedup is **advisory**, not blocking — if search times out or returns nothing, dispatch proceeds (fail-open). A false "already solved" skip is worse than a duplicate dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `flywheel mail search "bd-mail-reply-thread"` returns matching messages with recency ranking.
- A bead completed in the last hour is *surfaced* (not auto-skipped without a human/agent decision) before re-dispatch.
- CLI subcommands work end-to-end against a test project.

## Test plan

- Unit: `MailSearchFilter` serialization; query escaping.
- Integration: seed a project with 10 messages across 3 threads; assert search filters + summarize output shape.

## Considerations

- Don't auto-skip dispatch on search hits — too easy to skip legitimate re-work (a bead re-opened, a retry after a fix). Surface to the orchestrator/human; let them decide. The value is *visibility*, not automation.
- Search is read-heavy; cache nothing (FTS5 is fast, and stale cache could cause wrong skips).

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A3), §7 Phase 3.
- Tool contract: `agent_mail_search_messages` (FTS5 syntax reference in its description).
close_reason: evidence: Mail::search wrapper (grep pub fn search = 1) + search_wrapper_exists test (fn-pointer type check, passes); AgentMailMcpBackend::search graduated to delegation (grep filter.sender/Mail::search) + removed from Unsupported-cases (only request_contact/respond_contact remain). summarize_thread was already graduated by bd-mail-reply-thread. LIVE-VERIFIED: the exact search_messages envelope returned results against the running server (incl. tiered escalation messages — cross-bead evidence). cargo test --bin flywheel 228 green, clippy clean for mail.rs/agentmail.rs, fmt clean, release + deployed. Committed 2deddd1 (surgical staging). Bead acceptance met: search + summarize wrappers exist; the pre-dispatch 'did anyone solve this?' hook is the loop's to consume (the wrappers are the enabler).

description: Found while verifying bd-langgraph-b5-journal; pre-existing and unowned. tests/sc_bugfix_playbook.rs::bug_fix_cli_control_flow_reports_all_nodes fails: the bug-fix run reaches repair-until-verified node repair-1 and fails rendering with 'unresolved template ref {{inputs.bead_id}}', so the fix step errors, the crew expands to {} (empty), and the test's crew assertions get Null. This is the SAME class commit 7f9e117 fixed for {{inputs.coder_profile}} under bd-adv4: a workflow input ref with no declared default. Either declare a default for bead_id on the repair-until-verified input schema, or have the bug-fix caller supply it, or drop the ref if the recipe does not need it. Note bd-xmro (closed) previously fixed repair-until-verified expanding to an empty graph, so verify the expansion is not regressing again.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND, SOURCE FIX COMMITTED, TEST STILL RED ON THIS MACHINE.

Committed 8fc12cd: declared defaults for bead_id and ledger_path in the
repair-until-verified recipe. verify deliberately left with NO default (empty
verify passes vacuously; a missing VERIFY must keep failing loud).

The commit does NOT claim the test goes green, because it does not. Two further
defects sit between the source fix and a green test:

1. THE USER TIER SHADOWS THE BUILTIN.
   ~/.config/flywheel/workflows/repair-until-verified.yaml is a user-tier copy
   that wins resolution over the compiled-in builtin. It still carries the old
   inputs block, so the fix is inert.
   - `flywheel workflow drift` DOES detect this correctly: with a freshly built
     binary it reports repair-until-verified as `stale` (exactly 1 stale of 69).
     (An earlier reading of "current" was an artifact of the stale installed
     flywheel binary, not a catalog bug. Corrected.)
   - `flywheel workflow seed` will NOT refresh it: seed_user_catalog is
     non-destructive by contract (path.exists() -> kept), and there is a test
     named user_catalog_seed_is_non_destructive_and_drift_is_honest. This is
     coherent design, not a bug: a user copy always wins and drift is the honest
     signal.
   - So refreshing that tier is an OPERATOR decision about global config. Options:
     delete the stale copy and re-run `flywheel workflow seed` (reverts to the
     builtin), or hand-edit that one inputs block. Not doing it unilaterally.

2. THE TEST IS NOT HERMETIC.
   tests/sc_bugfix_playbook.rs drives the real binary, which resolves the AMBIENT
   user tier at ~/.config/flywheel/workflows/. So this test passes on a machine
   without that copy and fails on this one. A test whose result depends on
   operator-global config is a test defect regardless of the bug above. The fix
   is to make the catalog tier explicit in the test (or point the test at a
   fixture tier), so the suite is hermetic.

Also checked and cleared: run_call_workflow DOES call bind_input_defaults on the
child, so the nested call was never the problem; the shadowing was.

title: flywheel artifacts stitch errors on a composed run's outcome record (missing field path)
description:
Captured live while rewriting the guides: 'flywheel artifacts stitch fw-composed-2026-09-25T23:14:49Z --project toron' prints 'flywheel: missing field `path` at line 6 column 1'. The run dir holds only terminal.json (an outcome record: error, failed_step, leaf_preview, status) and has no path field, while stitch parses each file in artifacts/<run_id>/ as an ArtifactRecord. Reproduced on three consecutive composed runs (22:54:00Z, 23:04:13Z, 23:14:49Z), all the same error, so it is the record shape rather than one corrupt file.

The list form (flywheel artifacts <run_id> --project <project>) reads those runs fine, which is what the compound-engineering guide now uses.

title: Daemon unhosts auto-hosted loops with zero subscriptions
description: Reconcile adds loops but never removes: unsubscribing a workspace leaves its Brain sweeping forever. Design: reconcile drops hosted pairs that are not boot-configured and have zero referencing subscription rows (needs workspace-keyed loop tracking to send Shutdown + release the lease). Found via bd-kj2z testing litter. Stack follow-up.
close_reason: Implemented the design in the bead: hosted loops are tracked by project/workspace key (one HostedLoop table replacing three parallel Vecs), and reconcile retires a loop once no subscription references it and it is not boot-configured, sending BrainMsg::Shutdown and releasing the writer lease. Live-proven on the hosted daemon both directions, including the lease files on disk. Also fixed a re-entrant lock the refactor exposed (guard alive to end of statement + callee relocking = self-deadlock). make-operations-idempotent — reconcile now converges in both directions instead of only adding; fix-root-causes — the unretirable loop was a missing key, not a missing feature, so the keyed table is the fix rather than a bookkeeping list.

title: A standing registry ambiguity is audited every sweep: 52k rows a day naming one file
description:
FOUND 2026-09-28 while reproducing the Died storm. This is the chronic drip beside it, measured from the live journal.

SYMPTOM: registry_ambiguous fires at a steady ~36/min, every row naming the SAME file (flywheel-d5080499.json), all at executed.stage: sweep. Measured over 45 minutes: 1,657 rows, still firing (72 rows in the last 120 seconds). Extrapolated: ~52,000 rows/day, 1.2 MB/day of journal for one unchanging fact.

CAUSE: FileHost::registry_rows() sets pending_audit unconditionally whenever resolve_registry_file() reports ambiguity. The registry is never garbage-collected, so several hashed files routinely exist for one project slug (absolute vs relative spellings hash differently), the ambiguity never clears, and the sweep re-audits it on every pass.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ROWS: this is the loudest line in the journal and it says nothing new, which is exactly how a reader learns to skip a kind. It is the same failure the socket's own absent-audit already fixed: wake_sock_absent was deduped to one row per outage after it wrote 1,613 identical rows in one second.

FIX: one row per outage, keyed on the chosen file. A standing ambiguity is reported once and stays silent until it clears; when it clears the key resets, so a LATER ambiguity is a new outage and is audited again rather than silenced by the dedupe.

VERIFY: mbx +nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin test -p doorbell-rt registry_ambiguity. Red first: 36 sweeps of one ambiguity wrote 36 rows (the live cadence is 36/min). Green after: 1.
close_reason: done

title: main does not compile: 3596c64 spliced a #[test] fn into an assert! argument list, leaving doorbell-rt unbuildable
description:
main did not compile. 3596c64 ("fix(doorbell): classify the store skew on toron's declared code,
not its prose [bd-ogzg]") committed a syntactically broken crates/doorbell-rt/src/file_host.rs.

THE BREAK, verified against HEAD~1 and HEAD rather than inferred. 3596c64 added
inbox_fail_kind_matches_the_machine_marker by RELOCATING it, and the relocation landed in the wrong
place. At HEAD the file reads:

    2893        rt.block_on(async {
    2894            let _ = host.sweep_maintenance();
    2895        });
    2896        assert!(
    2897    /// bd-ogzg: the skew is a DECLARED code from another repo, ...
    ...
    2906    #[test]
    2907    fn inbox_fail_kind_matches_the_machine_marker() {
    ...
    2933    }
    2935            rx.try_recv().is_ok(),
    2936            "the herdr status change must reach the brain channel"
    2937        );

So a `#[test] fn` — doc comment and all — was spliced INTO the argument list of an `assert!`, which
consumed the macro's first argument and left the rest dangling after the spliced function closed.
rustc: "expected expression, found keyword `fn`" at 2907.

WHAT IT COST. `doorbell-rt` did not build, so `mbx clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` did
not build, and `mbx test --workspace` did not build. Every gate in this repo was red, and the
failure pointed at a syntax error rather than at the commit that introduced it, because the syntax
error and the intent were the same commit.

The test the commit ADDED does not exist at HEAD~1 at all (grep: 0 hits), so this was an addition
whose removal of the old tail took the neighbouring assert!'s close with it. The neighbour was a
real assertion — `rx.try_recv().is_ok(), "the herdr status change must reach the brain channel"` —
and it was silently reduced to a broken macro call rather than deleted.

THE REPAIR. Restored the assert to its HEAD~1 form, and moved the ogzg test out to its own `#[test]
fn` AFTER the enclosing function closes. Nothing about the test's body or intent was changed; only
its position. Verified by running both: `inbox_fail_kind_matches_the_machine_marker` passes, and the
neighbouring sweep test (4 passed) passes with its assertion intact.

NOT MINE, and recorded as such. This is not my defect and not my bead. I hit it because I was wiring
bd-3uqz into this file and could not get a green build, which is the only reason it surfaced before
someone's next commit piled on top of it. I am committing the repair rather than leaving main broken
because a broken main is worse than an unexpected commit, but the attribution belongs to
CopperWren/bd-ogzg and they should know their hunk split dropped a neighbouring assert.

THE LESSON, and it is the same one twice in one afternoon. Hunk-level staging is the right
instinct — 3596c64's own message says "Only this lane's hunks are in this commit", and that is
correct practice. But a split that MOVES a block has to apply both halves together, and a split
that only checks "are my hunks in?" cannot see that it dropped someone else's line in the gap. The
check that would have caught this is cheap and is the one I would add to the pre-commit gate:
after staging, compile the INDEX, not the working tree. Every one of my splits today verified the
working tree, which is exactly how this slipped past — and is why I twice believed I had preserved
another lane's work when I had in fact stopped looking at the index at all.
close_reason: main did not compile: 3596c64 relocated inbox_fail_kind_matches_the_machine_marker into a neighbouring assert! argument list, consuming the macro's first argument and leaving the rest dangling. Every gate in the repo was red. Repaired by restoring the assert to its HEAD~1 form and moving the ogzg test out to its own #[test] fn; both verified by running them. Defect belongs to CopperWren/bd-ogzg, found by me while wiring bd-3uqz.

title: wave-swarm stalls silently between gate.done and DISPATCH with no escalation
description: Run fw-composed-2026-10-23T04:21:54Z (and 04:28:43Z): GATE completed (wave-1-gate.done written by crew agent, grounding verified correct), then 30+ minutes of zero dispatch activity with both crew panes idle while the compose parent burned CPU in a poll loop. No error surfaced, no OBSERVE escalation (OBSERVE comes later in the pipeline), run row stayed 'running' until reconciled. The wedge is pre-DISPATCH: either await_gate polls a wrong label or the DISPATCH dispatch never fires. Evidence: marker mtimes (.flywheel/wave/wave-1-gate.done 04:51, no dispatch.done ever), pane revs frozen, wall-clock death at 3600s on three consecutive runs. For the engine lane; manual steering owns the lanes meanwhile.
close_reason: Root cause fixed: verify bypasses the journal (re-observes every evaluation), await echoes carry no ambiguity signals, three fences pin it. PRINCIPLES: fix-root-causes — the retry never polled because the journal replayed instead of re-invoking; prove-it-works — fail-then-succeed regression test plus template scan, all green

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE (journal evidence, corrects the wedge theory): every run's gate_marker row goes UNKNOWN with life_s 0 — the await evaluates ONCE, in the same second as the gate dispatch, before any agent could act. The 240x30s retry never polls; the engine parks on UNKNOWN (CPU-spinning poll/hang) until the wall-clock cap or a reconcile terminalizes it. That's why 3 runs died 'after 30 min of silence' — they were dead-or-parked from second 1, and the silence was never going to break. The gate agents' markers (written minutes later) arrive at a parked run. title: pane dispatch 429 annotates retryable but never takes the fallback hop

title: a held wave still dispatches, dispatches nothing, and the run reports success
description:
A held wave still dispatches, dispatches nothing, and the run reports success.

Live evidence, not inferred. A wave-swarm run on 2026-09-26 with
wave_label=wave-1 wrote this binding artifact and then carried on:

  .flywheel/wave/wave-1-ready.json
  {"blockers":["preflight:worktree (no project specified)",
               "preflight:playbook-files (no project specified)"],
   "held":true,
   "ready":[],
   "wave_label":"wave-1"}

`held: true`, blockers named, ready empty. The information was correct and
recorded. The run then ran DISPATCH, sent nothing, and exited 0. Three idle
coder panes, nine ready beads untouched, and a green run.

DEFECT 1 — DISPATCH never reads `held`. The gate's verdict is written into the
binding artifact as data, and the dispatch stage prompt says "Dispatch ONLY the
beads in <file>". It does not say "and refuse if held is true", so an empty or
held list is a valid instruction that happens to dispatch nothing. A hold that
does not stop the run is a comment, not a gate. This is the same shape as every
other false-green found this session (bd-uona's preflight, bd-523f's prompt-hop
reporting, bd-s913's zero-test fence): a door that reports success when the
operation it guards did nothing.

DEFECT 2 — the gate runs preflight WITHOUT `--project`, so two checks always
fail. `worktree` and `playbook-files` are project-scoped and fail when no
project is given. The gate stage task text says "preflight + scope `br ready`
to the label" and never says to pass `--project`, so the gate holds EVERY wave
for a reason that is the gate's own omission. Confirmed directly:
`flywheel preflight --mode workflow` fails exactly those two checks, and
`--project flywheel` turns both to pass (12/12).

DEFECT 3 — a label nothing carries is an empty ready set, not an error. No bead
in this project carries any wave value (all ten are unset), so wave-1 scopes to
nothing even with preflight fixed. The gate should fail loud naming that the
label matched zero beads, because an empty wave is indistinguishable downstream
from "the work is done". (The sibling artifact bd-fen3-live-ready.json DOES name
this: "no beads carry wave label bd-fen3-live" — so the gate can express it,
which makes the silent wave-1 case a consistency bug, not a missing feature.)

FIX. All three live in the wave-swarm GATE and DISPATCH stage prompts in
src/builtin_workflows.rs, and in the `wave-gate` / `wave-dispatch` stage
definitions they reference. Make the gate pass `--project`; make the hold
fail-closed so DISPATCH refuses on `held: true` with the blockers named; and
make a zero-bead label a loud gate failure rather than an empty artifact. A test
that a `held: true` binding artifact prevents dispatch is the row that would
have caught this, and it fails today.
close_reason: Done. DEFECT 3 closed: empty label is a loud gate failure. DEFECTS 1-2 verified by the crew's own tests. fix-root-causes — the gate names the blocker.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my own first write of this bead, recorded before anything shipped,
because I had it wrong and the wrong version was the more dramatic one.

I wrote "DISPATCH never reads `held`". That is FALSE and I should have read the
prompt before claiming it. src/stages.rs, the wave-dispatch prompt, says:

  FIRST read the gate artifact `.flywheel/wave/<wave-label>-ready.json` (...
  you dispatch ONLY beads the GATE wrote there; if the file is missing or
  "held": true, post `[dispatch] held` and STOP)

So the instruction to honour `held` is present and explicit. Correcting the
attribution matters because the real defect is worse, not milder.

THE REAL DEFECT: "STOP" in a stage prompt is not a gate.

Every wave-swarm step is a `dispatch_job` to an agent, with `on_error: fail_run`
wired to the STEP. A hold is carried by the agent POSTING `[dispatch] held` and
then stopping. That is a correct, obedient agent behaviour — and it is a
SUCCESSFUL step. The engine sees a completed dispatch_job, advances to EXECUTE,
REVIEW, COMPOUND and SIGNOFF, and the run reports success.

In other words the gate can only ever be expressed as an instruction to an
agent, and an instruction cannot fail a run. The engine has no path from "the
gate said held" to "the run failed": nothing inspects the binding artifact, and
the artifact is written by a prompt, not by code that can return an error.

That is the same failure family as everything else found this session — bd-uona's
preflight returning 12/12 PASS while dispatch was impossible, bd-523f reporting
prompt_hop "ok" with 19 of 20 pins unroutable, bd-s913's fence matching zero
tests. A door that reports success when the operation it guards did nothing.
Here the door is a prompt, so there is no code path to make it fail closed
without a structural change.

The live artifact from the idled run is the proof, and note that the GATE half
worked correctly:

  .flywheel/wave/wave-1-ready.json
  {"blockers":["preflight:worktree (no project specified)",
               "preflight:playbook-files (no project specified)"],
   "held":true,"ready":[],"wave_label":"wave-1"}

The gate named the blockers, set held, and produced an empty ready list. Both
halves behaved. The run continued anyway and exited 0.

WHAT A FIX ACTUALLY REQUIRES (not a prompt edit). The hold must become a value
the ENGINE can act on, not text an agent can obey. Options, cheapest first:

1. Make the gate step's verdict a real step output the engine branches on, and
   put the remaining steps behind a `when:` that excludes held. The compose
   grammar already has `when:`, so this is the intended shape; it needs the gate
   to return data rather than prose.
2. Add a step action that reads the binding artifact and fails the run when
   `held` is true. Small, local, and it puts the check in code where it can
   actually fail closed.
3. Have the gate artifact written by code rather than by a stage prompt, so its
   construction can return Err.

Option 2 is the smallest change that makes a hold a gate, and it is testable
without an agent: a held artifact must fail the step. That test does not exist
today and would fail today.

STILL TRUE AND SEPARATELY FIXABLE, verified: the wave-gate prompt says
`run \`flywheel preflight --mode workflow\`` with NO `--project`. `worktree` and
`playbook-files` are project-scoped and fail without one — confirmed directly,
those are exactly the two checks that fail bare and pass with `--project
flywheel` (12/12). So the gate holds EVERY wave for a reason that is the gate's
own omission. That one is a text fix plus a test pinning the flag.

title: find_workspace: duplicate swarm labels shadow live workspaces
description:
## Background

The durable loop (and all flywheel commands) resolve a project to a herdr workspace by matching the label via `find_workspace` (main.rs:601) — it returns the FIRST workspace whose label equals `swarm_label(project)`. Two workspaces with the same label (e.g. a dead scratch swarm and a fresh spawn of the same project) make the command resolve to the STALE one: `flywheel status <project>` then reports 'no agents' even though the fresh swarm is idle and healthy.

Observed live during bd-send-stall-escalation e2e: the probe-drop left workspace w14 with label flywheel-scratch-e2e; a respawn created w15 with the same label. `flywheel status scratch-e2e` kept resolving to w14 (no agents) until w14 was closed manually. Same failure mode bites the loop itself: a resumed workflow poll can silently target the wrong workspace.

## Why

One stale workspace makes every flywheel command (status, loop, send, spawn) mis-resolve — silent wrong-target behavior in the orchestrator's core name resolution.

## Technical approach

- In `find_workspace` (main.rs:601-610): prefer the workspace that actually contains managed agents (`flywheel-<project>-` named agents); fall back to first-match only when none has agents. Or: warn + pick the newest workspace on ambiguity.
- Keep resolution deterministic (no clock-based nondeterminism in the durable path).
- Unit test the resolver (pure fn over a workspace list).
- e2e: spawn, kill agent (drop), respawn — status must resolve to the live workspace without manual closes.

## Success criteria

- Two same-label workspaces: `flywheel status` resolves to the one with live agents.
- No behavior change when only one workspace exists.
- Deterministic resolution (no reliance on wall-clock).
close_reason:
find_workspace now disambiguates duplicate swarm labels. Pure herdr::resolve_workspace_id(matches, agents, prefix): single match wins; duplicates -> prefer the workspace holding MANAGED agents (names starting with flywheel-<base>-); else the first match — deterministic, no wall clock in the durable path. find_workspace (main.rs) gathers the label matches, and only when >1 does it query the agent list (the single-match fast path stays one round trip) and call the resolver with the prefix built from project_base. 137/137 tests (5 new: single match, duplicate with live managed agent -> live, duplicates both dead -> first, duplicates both live -> first deterministically, nameless managed record does not count).

Live e2e (the exact bd-nil scenario): spawned scratch-e2e oc swarm, killed the agent (record dropped -> stale workspace w23, label flywheel-scratch-e2e, agent_status unknown), spawned a fresh pi swarm (w24, same label, agent idle). `flywheel status scratch-e2e` resolved to w24 (the live workspace with the named agent) — previously it resolved to w23 and reported "no agents". Workspaces cleaned up after.

title: generator: flywheel integration <kind> [--out] + subagent templates
description:
# generator: `flywheel integration <kind> [--out]` + templates

## Background

The durable-loop semantics changed in the hardening epic (confirmed sends, escalation, state-file
context contract, dedup, adaptive cadence). The beads-agent instructions must stay current — a
generator makes the integration a build artifact instead of hand-edited copies.

## Technical approach (implemented)

- `integrations/beads-body.md.tpl` — the SHARED body: the bead lifecycle (triage → claim →
  reserve → announce → execute → verify → close → sync → handoff), skills list (br, bv,
  beads-workflow, beads-compliance, flywheel, agent-mail), discoveries rule (br create + dep add
  discovered-from), coordination rules (agent-mail identity, threads, blocked protocol), the
  **context contract** (write `{"context_pct", "ts"}` to `.flywheel/agent-state/<AGENT_NAME>.json`
  at ~80%, then finish + sync + reply CONTEXT_LIMIT; reader threshold 80%, 15-min freshness, dedup
  note), and the hard rules (never bare bv, never bd, --json everywhere, sync + commit .beads/).
  `{{KIND_NOTES}}` placeholder for per-kind notes.
- Per-kind wrappers with tool-specific frontmatter:
  - `integrations/opencode-beads.md.tpl` — name/description/mode: primary/temperature: 0.1/tools
    (mcp-agent-mail_*, read, write, edit, bash, grep, glob, task).
  - `integrations/pi-beads.md.tpl` — name/description/aliases (bead-executor, bead-worker,
    beads-executor)/thinking: high/systemPromptMode: replace/inheritProjectContext:
    true/inheritSkills: false/tools (read, grep, find, ls, bash, edit, write, mcp:agent-mail,
    contact_supervisor)/defaultContext: fork/defaultReads: context.md/defaultProgress: true.
  - `integrations/grok-beads.md.tpl` — name/description/prompt_mode: full/model: inherit/
    permission_mode: default/agents_md: true.
  - Each wrapper frontmatter carries a YAML comment stamp: `# flywheel beads agent — flywheel
    {{VERSION}}, generated {{GENERATED}}; source: integrations/<kind>-beads.md.tpl`.
- `flywheel integration [KIND] [--out PATH]` (main.rs): no kind → list the three targets +
  template note; kind accepted as opencode|pi|grok or shorts oc|pi|gk; renders via pure
  `render_integration(kind, version, generated)` (kind_notes per kind: config dirs
  ~/.config/opencode, ~/.pi, ~/.grok + per-kind quirks: opencode alternate-screen, pi session
  paths, grok landing latency); `--out` writes the file, else stdout.

## Success criteria (verified)

- `render_integration` produces a subagent file (frontmatter `name: beads` + shared body + kind
  notes), version + generated stamps present, no leftover placeholders.
- Unknown kind → error. All three kinds render with their config dir mentioned.
- 141/141 unit tests (4 integration_tests: subagent shape, per-kind config dirs, unknown kind,
  lifecycle + context contract presence).

## Test plan

- Unit (in-repo): integration_tests module — render shape, per-kind notes, unknown kind,
  lifecycle/context-contract content. All passing.

## Considerations

- Templates are embedded via include_str! — the generated output always matches the binary;
  edit `integrations/*.tpl`, rebuild, re-run the command.
- The version stamp in the frontmatter comment is the "is this current?" signal: after a rebuild
  the regenerated file's stamp changes.

## Status

IMPLEMENTED + CLOSED — commit d853ebd on the flywheel repo (with the AGENTS.md/README/stage
changes), 141/141 tests green.
close_reason: Generator implemented (commit d853ebd): flywheel integration [kind] [--out] renders the beads SUBAGENT from integrations/beads-body.md.tpl (shared lifecycle + coordination + context contract) + per-kind wrappers (opencode/pi/grok frontmatter, version-stamped). Shorts oc/pi/gk accepted; no kind lists targets; unknown kind errors. 141/141 tests (4 integration_tests: subagent shape, per-kind config dirs, unknown kind, lifecycle/context presence). Live-verified: renders for all three kinds with correct frontmatter + config-dir notes.

title: ledger check certifies an EMPTY commit, so a close reads LEGAL while proving nothing
description:
FOUND 2026-09-28, from walking through it myself.

WHAT HAPPENED. I staged five files, and a concurrent bare 'git reset' in this
shared repo unstaged the index between staging and committing. My commit
1275ebf landed EMPTY (0 files: git diff --name-only <parent> 1275ebf is empty).
I then gated and closed the bead against it, and 'flywheel ledger check
bd-watch-restart-metric-8dvf' printed LEGAL (sha 1275ebf), because the check
resolves the binding by grepping commit MESSAGES for the bead id and never asks
whether the commit changed anything. So the ledger's strongest word, LEGAL, was
given to a commit that could not have contained the fix.

The real fix was then 7096fd9 (4 files, 101 insertions), and the bead had to be
reopened, re-gated and re-closed: the documented manual repair, twice per
incident, because a closed bead has no legal gate transition.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND MY MISTAKE. An empty commit is the cheapest possible
false proof: any process that can run 'git commit --allow-empty -m "<message
citing bd-xxxx>"' can manufacture a LEGAL close for a bead nobody worked. The
same weakness is on the beads side: validate_close_sha (close.rs) accepts any
sha that resolves and whose message cites the bead, with no check that the
commit has content.

FIX DIRECTION. Reject a close sha whose tree is identical to its parent's, in
both the br close validation and flywheel ledger check, naming the empty commit
as the reason. A close is 'a PASS row plus a commit SHA' (ADR-0001 §5.3); a
commit that changed nothing is not that.

REPRODUCE: git commit --allow-empty -m 'bd-example' then br close <id>
--commit-sha <that sha>; today it closes, and with a PASS row it reads LEGAL.
close_reason: done
