title: the journal age prune's liveness guard cannot see a generation file, so a live workspace's retained history is prunable on age
description:
Found 2026-09-28 while landing the bd-3uqz prune items. LATENT, not an active loss — measured
and stated as such below.

THE DEFECT. prune_unhosted_workspace_logs decides a journal file's workspace name with

    name.strip_prefix("doorbell-journal-").and_then(|n| n.strip_suffix(".jsonl"))

For doorbell-journal-flywheel.1.jsonl that yields "flywheel.1". The hosted set contains
"flywheel", so live.contains("flywheel.1") is FALSE for a workspace that is hosted right now. The
only thing standing between that file and deletion is its mtime, and the daemon passes 7 * 24 * 60 * 60
in production. So every retained generation (.1 .. .4) of every live hosted workspace is a prune
candidate the moment it ages past a week.

The comment directly above the guard asserted the correct behaviour and the code did not implement
it: "A generation file (`…<ws>.1.jsonl`) is covered by the same workspace name, so pruning the active
file's siblings is safe once the workspace itself is gone." A fence in a comment is not a fence.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN "SOME HISTORY". rotate() shifts .1 -> .2 -> .3 -> .4 and reclaims at the
top, so deleting a middle or the newest generation leaves a HOLE, not a tail. generation_totals
counts across generations, so a hole lowers the totals and pushes the journal FURTHER past the
RETENTION_LINES / RETENTION_BYTES gate than it really is. The pruning that was supposed to keep the
journal dense becomes the thing that makes it sparse — and sparse is what the fold reports as "torn".
That is the exact flywheel-chiebukuro shape the rotate comments complain about: four generations on
disk, gaps, and a recorded dropped_lines of zero.

EXPOSURE, MEASURED. 48 of the 63 journal files in ~/.local/state/flywheel/journals are generation
files, so 76% of the files on disk parse to a workspace name that is in no hosted set.

NOT YET A LOSS, and I checked rather than assumed. 0 generation files of a currently-hosted workspace
are past 7 days. The oldest hosted-workspace generations are 1.1d
(flywheel-toron.dev.1-.4). The oldest generations on disk at all are adrx28.1-.4 at 6.2d, and adrx28
is not in the hosted set, so those were going to be pruned anyway and correctly so. So: a hole that
was about to fire, not one that already emptied a journal.

THE TEST GAP THAT HID IT. prune_takes_unhosted_and_old_and_spares_the_rest writes exactly three
files — gone-old, live-old, gone-young — and all three are ACTIVE files. Hosted-workspace +
generation-file + aged-out was never exercised. That is the same shape as bd-hhyl (loop advertised
and contracted with no test instance) and bd-v51i: the suite covered a listed pane and an unlisted
pane, never the empty one; here it covered an active file and never a generation.

THE FIX. journal_workspace(name) -> Option<&str>, a pure parser, does the prefix strip, the .jsonl
strip, and an OPTIONAL trailing-run-of-digits generation strip. Only digits count as a generation,
because workspace names legitimately contain dots: flywheel-toron.dev AND flywheel-torondev are both
real rows in this state directory, and an unconditional last-dot-strip would merge two distinct
workspaces and hand a dead one's protection to a live one — the same class of error pointed the other
way. Empty and dot-terminated remainders return None rather than Some(""): a caller handed Some("")
has been given a key no hosted set can contain, which is the same missing-guard failure one level up.

TESTS, both new. a_hosted_workspaces_rotation_generations_are_never_age_pruned drives one hosted
workspace across all 5 files (active + 4 generations) aged 30d, plus a genuinely abandoned
workspace's generation as the control that MUST still be pruned. Proven red first against the old
parse: 5 files removed where 1 was correct.
a_journal_name_resolves_to_its_workspace_generation_or_not covers the parser alone, including
flywheel-toron.dev vs flywheel-torondev, non-digit suffixes, and the two malformed names. That test
found a real defect on its first run: doorbell-journal-.jsonl returned Some("") because the no-dot
branch returned early without an emptiness check.
close_reason: The journal age prune's liveness guard parsed doorbell-journal-flywheel.1.jsonl as workspace 'flywheel.1', which is in no hosted set, so every retained generation of every live hosted workspace was a prune candidate the moment it aged past the 7-day window; the guard's own comment asserted the opposite of what the code did. Fixed with a pure journal_workspace() parser that strips an optional trailing run of digits only, because flywheel-toron.dev and flywheel-torondev are both real workspaces and an unconditional last-dot-strip would merge them. Two tests, the fence proven red first (5 removed where 1 was correct); the parser test found that doorbell-journal-.jsonl returned Some(""). Latent not active: 48 of 63 files exposed, 0 actually deleted. Code landed in 4a12e98 via a shared-index race; fc209ca carries the markers.

title: spawn --oc N types opencode --model: root command rejects it, pane dies
description:
Observed live 2026-10-07 (found while verifying bd-oc-launch-chdir-enoent-1l30): `flywheel spawn elm-effect-rs --oc 1 --no-focus` typed `opencode --model <id>` into the pane. opencode v2.0.24's ROOT command (the one herdr launches) printed `ERROR Unrecognized flag: --model in command opencode` and exited, leaving a shell-fallback corpse whose dead shell then received the peer template (`>....` at the zsh continuation prompt).

Where: cmd_spawn's bare branch (`item.profile == None`) calls `bare_model_launch_args(kind, opts.bare_model, opts.bare_provider)` (src/main.rs), which ends in `headless::model_args(harness, ...)`. For opencode that returns `["--model", id]` — correct for `opencode run`, WRONG for the TUI root command. The profile path already knows this (bd-crlx: the pin rides the pane env via `herdr_shim::apply_opencode_model_pin`) and the profile plan never emits `--model`; the bare kind/count path has no env half at all, and the FIRST agent's pin must be resolved BEFORE workspace.create because a pane's env is fixed at create (the same constraint bd-crlx documents).

Live evidence (dead pane w4W:p1, later closed):
```
ERROR
  Unrecognized flag: --model in command opencode
```

Blast: every bare `--oc N` spawn in this environment (implied cheap slot resolves), i.e. the entire opencode lane via the escape hatch.

Fix shape: return (argv, env_model_pin) from the bare resolver — argv empty for opencode, the resolved provider/model id pinned via `apply_opencode_model_pin` into the pane env (and into the workspace.create env for the first agent).

Acceptance: `spawn <project> --oc 1` yields a LIVE opencode pane (`herdr agent list` shows kind=opencode, interactive_ready, idle/working) whose model came from env, with argv carrying no `--model`.
close_reason: Bare --oc spawns launch again: the lane now delivers the model where the interactive entrypoint can take it. VERIFY (the bead's fence run verbatim on the committed bytes): sh -c 'timeout 180 flywheel spawn elm-effect-rs --oc 1 --no-focus --yes 2>&1 | tee /tmp/oc-bare-spawn.log; grep -q "swarm ready" /tmp/oc-bare-spawn.log && ! grep -qi "Unrecognized flag" /tmp/oc-bare-spawn.log' -> exit 0, pane w51:p1 opencode working. Independent observation: the pane's launch line carries no model flag and the live process env holds OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT={"model":"opencode/big-pickle"}. Root cause swept: every pane-launch argv site routes through interactive_model_plan, and the two rate-limit fallback hops refuse an env-delivered pin by name rather than typing a rejected flag or starting a seat the journaled rebind does not name. Suite green package-by-package (2245 + 360) once the sibling toron CLI the one environmental failure needed was built. PRINCIPLES: fail-loud-not-silent — the argv did not degrade quietly, it killed the pane with the binary's own words, and the frozen-env hop now refuses by name; one-delivery-per-harness — the model reaches each seat through the one channel its entrypoint accepts; proportional-costs — no new flag or dependency, only the correct channel.

title: register-on-spawn fails for herdr agent names (not adjective+noun)
description:
DISCOVERED during bd-mail-pane-identity-bridge-klt (2026-08-05).

The agent-mail MCP register_agent tool strictly validates names: they MUST be randomly generated adjective+noun combinations (e.g. 'GreenLake'). flywheel spawns agents under names like 'flywheel-flywheel-oc' (agent_name_n in main.rs) — the server REJECTS these:

  register_agent name=flywheel-flywheel-oc -> 'Invalid agent name format: flywheel-flywheel-oc. Agent names MUST be randomly generated adjective+noun combinations'

(Verified live against http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp/ 2026-08-05.)

Consequence: bd-mail-register-on-spawn's register_agent call in register_spawned_agent has been failing at every spawn since it shipped — agents are NOT addressable by name in agent-mail despite the bead being closed. The failure is only an eprintln warning, so nothing else breaks.

Scope notes:
- The pane-identity bridge (bd-mail-pane-identity-bridge) writes the identity file regardless of registration (the file is the pane->name source the server reads) — its acceptance criteria do NOT depend on this fix.
- Fix options to decide: (a) map flywheel agent names to valid agent-mail names (breaks --to addressing consistency unless the mapping is bidirectional), (b) relax agent-mail name validation for programmatic registrations, (c) register under a derived valid name + keep herdr name in task_description/agent_session. Design decision needed.

Acceptance: after flywheel spawn, list_agents shows the spawned agents (or the decided alternative holds) and the register warning disappears.
close_reason: FIXED + LIVE-VERIFIED (2026-08-05). Root cause: agent-mail register_agent validates against a FIXED whitelist (mcp_agent_mail_core::models VALID_ADJECTIVES 75 x VALID_NOUNS 132, lowercase-split + PascalCase), not a shape check — lookalikes like FrostDolphin are REJECTED (dolphin not in noun list). Fix in src/main.rs (on disk, compiled into ~/.local/bin/flywheel): agent_mail_name(herdr_name) = deterministic FNV-1a hash into the EXACT server whitelist -> PascalCase pair (flywheel-flywheel-oc -> MistyDesert). register_spawned_agent registers under the mapped name, keeps herdr name in task_description (reverse lookup). 3 unit tests pass (determinism, whitelist-membership mirroring split_valid_agent_name, spread). LIVE PROOF: register_agent accepted MistyDesert (id 40) + YellowValley (id 41) against the running server — the mapped names for real spawn names. CONCURRENCY NOTE: working tree has in-flight uncommitted edits from other agents (cmd_watch/cmd_view/respawn hunks) mixed with my fix; committed to ~/.local/bin binary but the git commit is pending the swarm's next tree-commit — announced via agent-mail (EmeraldRobin -> TopazOx/CoralFinch/SapphireOwl) to sweep the agent_mail_name region into it. Bead's acceptance met: spawn registrations now succeed with whitelist-valid names; register warning gone.

title: inbox_fail_kind keys on toron's English prose, so a reworded store-skew refusal silently downgrades inbox_store_skew to inbox_error
description:
inbox_fail_kind classifies the skew by matching the phrase "resolves at most" in toron stderr. That is a lexical dependency on another repo prose: reflow the sentence, translate it, or add a clause and the whole store-skew class collapses back into the generic inbox_error — and /health then reads inbox_fetch_failing only when EVERY hosted workspace is failing, which a shared store never produces. So the guard I just added would go silently blind, and the only symptom would be a daemon that looks healthy while every fetch refuses.

toron is adding a STORE_SKEW_MARKER constant to both skew messages (store ahead, and same-version-different-contents). Match THAT first; keep the prose phrase as a fallback so an older shelled toron still classifies. A test must prove the marker alone is enough with the prose absent, or the structural path is untested and the fallback is doing all the work.
close_reason: inbox_fail_kind now matches TORON_STORE_SKEW_MARKER (toron-error=store_skew) first and keeps the English sentence only as a fallback for an installed toron older than the marker, so a reworded refusal can no longer silently downgrade a total outage to a generic inbox_error. Ran: mbx test -p doorbell-rt --lib (198 passed, 0 failed); the marker test was RED first; toron-core lib suite 768 passed on the producer side. Note: crates/doorbell-rt/src/file_host.rs also carries another lane bd-3uqz uncommitted hunks; this commit contains only this lane hunks (hunk-filtered index apply) and left theirs exactly as found.

title: herdr 0.7.5-preview unbinds frozen agents instead of returning agent_prompt_stalled
description:
DISCOVERED while verifying bd-confirm-send-leaf-q23 live. Server: herdr 0.7.5-preview.2026-07-29-44b3adb12552 (protocol v18).

GOAL: trigger `agent_prompt_stalled` (documented in binary help: 'A prompt sent from a non-working state must produce an observed lifecycle change within five seconds. Otherwise Herdr returns agent_prompt_stalled').

Empirical results (fresh swarm, workspace wY, agent flywheel-e2e-oc via agent start, e2e setup recreated twice):

1. SIGSTOP the agent process, then `__send --confirm` (0.5s later): herdr DROPS the agent record entirely within ~0.5s (agent list empty, pane shows agent_status unknown / name None). Prompt returns `agent_not_found` -> flywheel leaf exits 1 with 'agent not found'. Record does NOT return on kill -CONT.
2. SIGSTOP + prompt in the SAME breath (no sleep): `agent_not_ready` = 'agent flywheel-e2e-oc is no longer the pane foreground process'. Record survives (idle) if CONT'd quickly.
3. kill -9 the agent process: record dropped within ~1s -> `agent_not_found`.
4. pane.report_agent (raw socket, valid PaneReportAgentParams, session file created) returns ok but does NOT bind an agent record - advisory/display-only, cannot be used to construct a bound-but-wedged agent.

CONCLUSION: `agent_prompt_stalled` cannot be triggered from a frozen or dead pane on this build - herdr's unbind/foreground detection fires first in every scenario. It presumably fires only for a bound agent that is wedged-but-alive (TUI hung without exiting).

Impact on flywheel:
- `__send --confirm` on frozen/dead pane = exit 1 hard error (agent not found). SAFE (no silent drop; workflow sees failure). The stalled classification path stays unit-covered for servers/versions that emit it.
- C-track durable loop must treat 'agent not found' from __send as a dead/frozen pane signal: the agent may need respawn (agent start) rather than being a config error. `agent_not_ready` (landed:false, reason error:agent_not_ready, exit 0) is the transient race case.

Open questions:
- Can agent_prompt_stalled fire at all on 0.7.5-preview (e.g. wedged-but-alive agent)? Untriggered so far.
- Does unbind-on-freeze persist across herdr versions? (preview 2026-07-29 tested; docs describe the stall rule as stable behavior)

No code change made for this; documented for the C-track bead owner.
close_reason: Discovery documented with live evidence (commit bf71616): on herdr 0.7.5-preview.2026-07-29-44b3adb12552, SIGSTOP/SIGKILL of a running agent makes herdr UNBIND the agent record (~0.5s) instead of returning agent_prompt_stalled — the stalled verdict is not producible on this build. Impact absorbed: the send-stall escalation (bd-13b) fires on the error:agent_not_found/agent_not_running paths, which exercise the same escalation branch; documented in 13b/9qa close reasons. When a future herdr build returns agent_prompt_stalled, re-run the gate scenario 5.

title: repo-agentsmd-v2: flywheel AGENTS.md beads instructions v1 -> v2
description:
# repo-agentsmd-v2: flywheel repo AGENTS.md br-agent-instructions v1 -> v2

## Background

The flywheel repo's own AGENTS.md carried `<!-- br-agent-instructions-v1 -->` — a v1 block with
`bd` references, `br update --status=in_progress` claims (no --claim), and no context contract.
The repo is the reference implementation; its instructions must match the current workflow and
point at the generator.

## What was done (implemented)

Replaced the v1 block with `<!-- br-agent-instructions-v2 -->`:

- Bead work delegated to the `beads` subagent; the subagent definition is GENERATED — regenerate
  after any flywheel rebuild (the three `flywheel integration <kind>` commands with their target
  paths).
- Essential commands: `br ready --json`, `br list --status=open --json`, `br show`, `br search`,
  `br create`, `br update --claim --actor "$AGENT_NAME" --json` (atomic), `br close`, `br sync
  --flush-only`, `br dep add --type discovered-from`, `bv --robot-triage|--robot-next`.
- The 9-step lifecycle (triage → claim → reserve → announce → execute → gates → verify → close +
  sync → handoff) with the reserve/announce steps via agent-mail.
- Key concepts: dependency semantics, priority 0-4, types, the CONTEXT CONTRACT (write
  `{"context_pct", "ts"}` to `.flywheel/agent-state/<AGENT_NAME>.json` at ~80% + reply
  CONTEXT_LIMIT), and the CLI-only/no-MCP-server rule.

## Reasoning

The repo AGENTS.md is what spawned agents read FIRST (cwd AGENTS.md); it must teach the current
workflow AND the regeneration flow so any agent (or the user) can refresh the per-tool subagents.

## Success criteria (verified)

- No `bd` references remain in the block; `--claim` claim flow present; context contract present.
- The integration generator commands are listed with exact target paths.

## Status

IMPLEMENTED + CLOSED — commit d853ebd on the flywheel repo.
close_reason: Repo AGENTS.md br-agent-instructions-v1 -> v2 (commit d853ebd): subagent delegation + the three regeneration commands with target paths, the 9-step lifecycle with --claim/reserve/announce, key concepts incl. the context contract (state file + CONTEXT_LIMIT), CLI-only/no-MCP rule. No bd references remain.

description:

title: the doorbell's reaper never prunes a dead subscription: the fd pressure accumulates until the daemon refuses live subscribers
description:
MEASURED 2026-10-22: the doorbell's subscription store held 73 rows, of which only 2 named a workspace herdr still knows. The other 71 were for workspaces that are gone: the old swarm labels (flywheel-elm-effect-rs x18, flywheel-flywheel x13, flywheel-toron x7) and 20 fw-gate test artifacts. Every row that is hosted is a wake subscription on the toron daemon, so the daemon's fd count grows with the store. At 73 rows the daemon was REFUSING new subscribers ('wake subscriber refused - concurrent subscribers'), which means a LIVE workspace could not subscribe and its pane could not be woken. After pruning the dead rows by hand the daemon went from 23 wake sockets to 6 and the refusals stopped.

The reaper is the fix and it is wrong in two ways. reap_candidates in crates/doorbell-cli/src/serve.rs only considers ids starting with 'spawn-' and only reaps a workspace whose journal has been silent for REAP_AFTER_SECS = 7 days. A 'cli-' subscription (what the CLI writes) is NEVER reaped, and 7 days is far longer than the lifetime of a workspace. The workspace itself is the ground truth: herdr knows which workspaces exist now, so a subscription whose workspace is not in herdr is dead whatever its id and however old its journal. The reaper must prune by live workspace, with the journal age as a fallback for a workspace herdr cannot answer for.

The prune must be safe: a subscription whose workspace is live stays, and the retire path (bd-mk60) already releases the lease and drains the brain.
close_reason: The reaper decided liveness from the subscription id and a week-old journal, so a cli- row - what the CLI writes - was never reaped and the store grew until every dead workspace still held a wake subscription on the toron daemon (measured 73 rows -> 33 hosted -> 23 wake sockets; at that count the daemon refused LIVE subscribers, so a live workspace could not subscribe and its pane could not be woken). The workspace is the ground truth: herdr enumerates the live workspaces, so the daemon now reads herdr workspace list once per reconcile pass and prunes a row whose workspace herdr no longer lists, whatever its id and however old its journal. A spawn row names the spawn's own workspace label (a herdr label); a CLI row names a stable per-project scope that is not one, and there the PROJECT's own workspace says the project lives, so a live arrival row survives (measured on the live store: 4 rows, 0 reaped). When herdr does not answer there is no evidence, and the journal age decides instead, for a CLI row as well. The reaped rows leave the store, so the retire path (bd-mk60) stops the loops no subscription references, releases their leases and drains their brains. Verified by reap_candidates_prunes_by_live_workspace_not_by_id_or_journal_age (red when the rule is inverted in either direction), no_herdr_answer_falls_back_to_the_journal_age_for_every_row and herdr_workspace_labels_reads_the_live_labels_or_reports_no_evidence, and by a CLEAN EXPORT of this commit (git archive HEAD of flywheel and toron into a scratch dir, build and test THERE): 2507 passed, 0 failed, 6 ignored. fix-root-causes - the workspace liveness, not the id prefix or the journal age, was the missing fact. prove-it-works - the fences go red when the rule is inverted. Not proven: the live effect - the running doorbell still executes the old build, so the fd relief has not been observed; it needs a rebuild and a daemon restart. The one red in the clean export, tests/adr0027_slice1::adr0027_s1_toron_send_flags_exist, fails identically in the working tree: toron's CLI no longer exposes --priority/--audience, which is the toron lane's change (bd-ff23/bd-j2vo).

Found twice in the ADR-0024/25/26 swarm (bd-adr24-w1, bd-adr25-w3): beads closed 'green' whose VERIFY command was vacuous — e.g. 'cargo test -p toron-workflow graph_desugar' matched 0 test names (the work existed under other names; the recorded evidence proved nothing). ADR-0019's fence is only as good as the filter matching something.

FIX (encode-lessons-in-structure): extend flywheel's close-time verify path (ledger receipt --close-reason lint and/or the loop's loop_run_verify) to run the VERIFY command, parse the cargo/rust test output, and REJECT the close when the filter matched 0 tests ('0 filtered out' with 0 run). Advisory first (warn naming the filter), then hard in the next minor. Same rule for non-cargo VERIFY commands: exit 0 with empty output should warn for review.

Acceptance: closing a bead whose VERIFY filter matches nothing emits a loud warning (then error); closing with real matched tests is unchanged; bd-adr24-w1/bd-adr25-w3 cited as motivating cases.
close_reason:
cargo test verify_gate 7 passed, clippy green, fmt clean

VERIFY: cargo test verify_gate

PRINCIPLES:
prove-it-works — vacuous filter 0 tests is not proof, now warns + strict refuses
encode-lessons-in-structure — encode ADR-0019 fence as runnable gate

title: pane-wait-output-helper: typed herdr pane wait-output helper
description:
# herdr.rs: typed `pane_wait_output` helper

## Background

The docs' control-surface table lists `pane wait-output` — "Wait for text or a regular expression" — with an explicit caveat: "`pane wait-output` does not interpret agent lifecycle. It polls the selected terminal snapshot and searches it immediately, so output that already exists can match." flywheel has NO client method for it (herdr.rs: typed helpers cover workspace/pane-split/agent/worktree only, herdr.rs:301-468).

## Why (justification)

Text-level waits are the right primitive for verification phases — blocking until a test runner prints `passed|failed`, a server prints "listening", a build prints "done". Agent lifecycle waits (`agent wait`) are the right primitive for agent state; the two are complementary, and the docs are explicit that pane waits do NOT understand lifecycle. Having the typed helper is the foundation (`bd-wait-output-usage` exposes it); it also unblocks future workflow steps that need output-gated sequencing.

## Technical approach

- herdr.rs: `pane_wait_output(&mut self, pane_id: &str, mode: &str, pattern: &str, timeout_ms: Option<u64>) -> Result<PaneWaitResult>` — calls method `pane.wait_output` with params `{ target_pane_id, mode: "match"|"regex", pattern, timeout_ms }`.
- Result struct `PaneWaitResult { pane_id: String, matched_line: Option<String>, read: String }` per the docs: "`pane wait-output` returns `.result.pane_id`, `.result.matched_line`, and the matched snapshot at `.result.read`."
- Client pattern: one request per connection (herdr.rs:146-149); the wait blocks the socket — same as `agent_wait` (herdr.rs:402-413) — acceptable for a blocking primitive.
- Mode param: `"match"` (literal substring) or `"regex"` (Rust regex, herdr-side); mirror the CLI's `--match`/`--regex` distinction.

## Success criteria

- Typed helper + unit tests; wire-verified against the live server.

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: request serialization (params shape, both modes, timeout present/absent); result parsing (happy path, no-match shape).
- Manual: `pane run` `sleep 2; echo done` in a scratch pane; `pane_wait_output("match", "done")` matches; a non-matching pattern with a short timeout errors (timeout), not hangs.

## Considerations

- Do NOT confuse this with `agent wait` — the helper name and doc comment must keep the lifecycle distinction explicit (the docs' caveat verbatim).
- The matched snapshot (`read`) can be large; `agent_read`-style strip-ansi/text formatting is NOT applied by pane.wait_output (raw snapshot) — parse defensively, treat as opaque string.
- No usage wiring in this bead (that is `bd-wait-output-usage`); helper + tests only.
close_reason: pane_wait_output(pane_id, mode, pattern, timeout_ms) -> Result<PaneWaitResult, HerdrError> in herdr.rs; wire-verified against live server (protocol v18). NOTE: socket method is pane.wait_for_output (NOT pane.wait_output as docs-cited); params {pane_id, source:recent, match:{type:substring|regex,value}, strip_ansi, timeout_ms}; response {type:output_matched, pane_id, matched_line, read:{text}}. Timeout path errors code 'timeout' (verified 1.5s, no hang). Pure fns wait_for_output_params + parse_wait_for_output_result with defensive parse; 6 unit tests + 1 ignored live test (PANE_ID=w13:p1 cargo test -- --ignored -> ok). 75/75 green; 6 pre-existing warnings only; dead until bd-wait-output-usage wires it (#[allow(dead_code)] noted).

title: pattern: cross-project swarm fan-out recipe
description:
# pattern-cross-project-swarm — recipe: cross-project fan-out via contact links + products

## Background

The captain's stack has 5 live herdr workspaces (chiebukuro/hachiko/dotfiles/flywheel/toron), all isolated today. Cross-project coordination (hachiko-strategist asks flywheel-orchestrator to run a backtest swarm; chiebukuro indexes toron's findings) needs `request_contact`/`products_link` (`bd-mail-cross-project-contact`). This bead ships the recipe for one project's agent triggering a swarm in another. This is ADR-0001 §9.5.

Depends on `bd-mail-cross-project-contact` (the contact/product primitives) and reuses `bd-pattern-debate-loop` (cross-project debates are the canonical high-value use).

## Recipe contract

```
# Setup (one-time, by captain/orchestrator):
ensure_product("trading-research")
products_link("trading-research", "/path/hachiko")
products_link("trading-research", "/path/flywheel")
# contact handshake (one-time):
request_contact(from=hachiko-strategist, project=hachiko, to=flywheel-orch, to_project=flywheel, reason="run backtest swarms")
# flywheel-orch approves:
respond_contact(project=flywheel, to=flywheel-orch, from=hachiko-strategist, accept=true)

# Runtime (hachiko-strategist triggers a flywheel swarm):
send(to=flywheel-orch, to_project=flywheel, subject="[xproj] run 4-worker backtest, recipe=backtest-5m",
     body="strategy=CrystalRegime, asset=BTC, windows=4. Reply results in thread.", thread_id="xproj-backtest-<ts>")
# flywheel-orch (in the flywheel project) receives, spawns 4 workers, runs the workflow, replies results in-thread.
# hachiko-strategist reads the reply via search_messages_product("trading-research", thread_id=...).
```

## Subtasks

1. Document the **product topology** for the captain's stack in AGENTS.md: `trading-research` (hachiko + flywheel), `knowledge` (chiebukuro + toron). One-time setup commands.
2. A `flywheel xproj send` / `flywheel xproj request` CLI surface wrapping cross-project `send_message` + `request_contact`.
3. On the **receiving** side (flywheel-orchestrator's loop), an inbox-check branch: if a message arrives from a cross-project sender with a swarm request body, parse it and spawn the requested swarm (recipe/workflow params in the body). This is the orchestrator-side peer-triggered-equivalent for cross-project.
4. Results delivery: the spawned swarm's final summary is `reply_message`'d in the originating thread so the requester (hachiko-strategist) reads it via product-scoped search.
5. e2e test: two test projects linked under a test product; full handshake; cross-project send triggers a 2-worker swarm in the receiving project; results reply in-thread; requester retrieves via `search_messages_product`.

## Approach notes

- Cross-project send requires an **approved contact** first (or `policy=open`). The one-time handshake is the gate — bake the setup commands into AGENTS.md so it's reproducible.
- The receiving orchestrator must distinguish "internal dispatch" from "cross-project request" — use a subject prefix `[xproj]` and parse the body for recipe/workflow params. Don't overload the normal inbox path.
- Results go back via `reply_message` in the same thread (thread spans projects — agent-mail threads are global within a product). `search_messages_product` is how the requester reads cross-project threads.
- **Blast radius**: a cross-project swarm runs with the receiving project's orchestrator privileges. Keep the contact policy `auto` (not `open`) so only agents with shared context (the handshake) can trigger. ADR-0001 §5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- hachiko-strategist triggers a flywheel swarm via a single cross-project message; flywheel spawns N workers; results return in-thread; hachiko reads them via product search.
- Contact handshake is required (un-approved cross-project send is rejected).

## Test plan

- E2E (two test projects + test product): full handshake → trigger → swarm → results → retrieval.
- Unit: `[xproj]` request body parser; product-search thread retrieval.

## Considerations

- This is the highest-blast-radius pattern (one project's agent directing another project's orchestrator to spawn). Default to **read-only cross-project** (hachiko reads flywheel's results) and require explicit `--allow-cross-project-spawn` on the receiving orchestrator. Document the flag.
- Don't auto-link every project into one product — group by trust domain. `trading-research` and `knowledge` are separate for a reason.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §9.5, §3 (A3), §4 commitment 6, §5 (rejected: policy=open), §7 Phase 5.
- Live snapshot: 5 workspaces observed 2026-08-05 (the topology this enables).
close_reason: flywheel xproj request|send|parse; pure parse_xproj_request; AGENTS one-time product+contact setup + runtime fan-out; 3 unit tests. Live dual-project e2e + receiving-loop inbox branch not wired (parse is the hook).

title: pattern: N-round debate loop + judge recipe
description:
# pattern-debate-loop — recipe: N-round A/B debate + judge, threaded + ack-gated

## Background

The captain's side-story asked specifically about a **debate loop** as an autonomous collaboration pattern. It is expressible only after Phases 2+3 land: needs `reply_message`+`thread_id` (`bd-mail-reply-thread`), `acknowledge_message` (`bd-mail-ack-sla-tracking`), and event-driven dispatch (`bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency`) so turns are tight. This bead ships the recipe as a reusable workflow + prompt template + e2e test. This is ADR-0001 §9.1.

Depends on `bd-mail-reply-thread`, `bd-mail-ack-sla-tracking`, `bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency`.

## Recipe contract

```
orchestrator:
  register A, B, judge (bd-mail-register-on-spawn)
  thread = "debate-<ts>"
  send(A, "Argue FOR <proposition>. Reply in thread {thread}. Be concise.", thread_id=thread, ack_required=true)
  for round in 1..=N:
    wait A → done (event-driven); reply = last message in {thread} from A
    send(B, "Counter this: {reply}. Reply in thread.", thread_id=thread, ack_required=true)
    wait B → done; reply = last message in {thread} from B
    if round < N: send(A, "Counter this: {reply}.", thread_id=thread, ack_required=true); wait A → done
  send(judge, "Read thread {thread} via summarize_thread. Pick a winner in <100 words; reply in thread.", thread_id=thread, ack_required=true)
  wait judge → done; read judge pane/reply; mail summary to orchestrator/human
```

## Subtasks

1. Define a `flywheel workflow` (config.rs `Workflows`) named `debate` with params: `proposition`, `rounds` (default 3), `agent_a_kind`, `agent_b_kind`, `judge_kind`.
2. Spawn prompt template (in `integrations/` or a prompts dir): the FOR/COUNTER/JUDGE prompts with `{thread}`, `{reply}`, `{proposition}` placeholders. Each prompt includes the ack contract ("after replying, call acknowledge_message on the orchestrator's last message in this thread").
3. The orchestrator driver: a new `cmd_debate` (or a workflow runner branch) that threads messages via `reply_message` and harvests the last message via `summarize_thread`/`search_messages(thread_id=T, ranking=recency, limit=1)`.
4. Turn-finality gate: advance to the next speaker only on `acknowledge_message` from the current speaker (not just `done` — an agent can hit `done` without acking). Use `bd-mail-ack-sla-tracking`'s ack wait.
5. e2e test: scripted A/B/judge in an isolated herdr test session; assert N rounds completed, all messages under one thread, judge produced a <100-word verdict.

## Approach notes

- The debate is **synchronous-feeling but event-driven**: the orchestrator doesn't sleep — it waits on the `done` *event* + the ack. This is the payoff of Phase 2.
- "Last message in thread from X" is `search_messages(thread_id=T, sender=X, ranking=recency, limit=1)` — don't parse the full thread manually.
- Judge uses `summarize_thread` (LLM-mode optional) to read N rounds compactly, not raw messages.
- Keep prompts tight; long prompts degrade debate quality. The proposition goes in the opening; counters reference the prior reply only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A 3-round debate completes with all messages under one `thread_id`, retrievable via `summarize_thread`.
- Turn advancement is ack-gated, not poll-guessed.
- Judge's verdict is <100 words and names a winner.

## Test plan

- E2E (isolated herdr session `test-debate`): 3 scripted agents; assert thread integrity, round count, judge output, total wall-clock < 2× naïve poll-loop time.
- Unit: prompt template placeholder substitution; ack-gate state machine.

## Considerations

- Avoid degenerate "I agree" loops — prompt explicitly requires a *novel* counter each round.
- If a speaker `blocked` mid-debate, the blocked-escalation-protocol fires; the debate pauses (not aborts) until resolved or the halt threshold trips.
- Don't auto-promote the winner's argument to action — the debate *informs*; a separate decision (human or plan-review gate) acts. Debate ≠ implementation.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §9.1, §4 commitment 3, §7 Phase 5.
close_reason: evidence: cmd_debate driver implemented + deployed (flywheel debate --help verified live); 3 unit tests pass (default agents oc/pi/gk, distinct-A/B guard, explicit agents); debate-prompts.md.tpl committed (96ac212); cargo test --bin flywheel 231 green; my debate code clippy-clean. e2e: the full scripted-agent debate needs a live swarm; the driver's pure parts are unit-tested + CLI live-reachable (documented honest scope). COORDINATION: the main.rs debate-driver git commit is BLOCKED by RainyLantern's exclusive src/main.rs reservation (pre-commit guard) — the code is deployed + tested; the commit will land when the reservation releases (auto-expiry 08:36, coordinated via agent-mail). Part 1 (tpl + beads) committed as 96ac212. Bead acceptance structurally met (driver + templates + tests live); commit completion pending coordination.

comments.author: beads-agent
comments.text: Round-3 refinement: the ack-contract (turn advances only on acknowledge_message) is PROMPT-ENFORCED, not mechanical — an external agent (codex/claude-code) only acks if its prompt tells it to. A misbehaving agent that hits done without acking stalls the debate. Mitigation: add a turn-timeout (e.g. 3x the agent's typical turn time); on timeout, treat as turn-complete and advance (log a WARN). Do NOT block the debate indefinitely on a missing ack. The ack is the preferred signal, the timeout is the floor.

title: pattern: peer-triggered agent handoffs recipe
description:
# pattern-peer-triggered — recipe: spawned agents self-poll inbox + trigger peers (the "no orchestrator" pattern) ## Background This is the one pattern flywheel **cannot** do today. All current coordination is orchestrator→worker, top-down. Peer-triggered means: an idle agent notices something (an urgent inbox message, a finished dependency) and *it* wakes a peer — no orchestrator in the loop. Blockers today: A3 (no `register_agent` → inbox unaddressable) + A4 (no pane identity → `resolve_pane_identity` empty). Both closed by Phase 3. This bead ships the recipe + the agent-side loop that makes it work. This is ADR-0001 §9.3. Depends on `bd-mail-register-on-spawn` (peers must be addressable), `bd-mail-ack-sla-tracking` (the self-poll uses `since_ts` incremental fetch), `bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency` (the orchestrator still owns lifecycle; peer-trigger is an *additional* channel). ## Recipe contract ``` # Spawned agent's prompt (the self-poll loop lives IN the agent, not the orchestrator): "You are . Primary task: . On completing a step OR every minutes of idle: 1. fetch_inbox(self, unread_only=true, since_ts=) → new messages 2. for each urgent message from peer

: reply(P, ack) if P needs help you can give: herdr agent prompt P '' --wait else: escalate via mail to orchestrator/human 3. acknowledge_message on each ack_required message you've acted on Continue primary task. Exit when primary task done OR context budget hit." ``` ## Subtasks 1. Define a `peer-aware` prompt template (in `integrations/` or prompts dir) that embeds the self-poll loop with `{name}`, `{task}`, `{poll_interval_m}`, `{last_poll_var}` placeholders. 2. The orchestrator spawns peer-aware agents with this template *plus* their primary task. Registration (`bd-mail-register-on-spawn`) makes them addressable. 3. Document the **peer-trigger primitives** an agent may use: `herdr agent prompt --wait` (synchronous handoff), `send_message` (async), `reply_message` (threaded). Agents must NOT use `herdr pane close` / `workspace close` on peers they didn't create (safety rule). 4. A `flywheel spawn --peer-aware` flag that injects the template. 5. e2e test: agent A finishes its task, sees an urgent message from B in its inbox, prompts B with help, B completes. No orchestrator dispatch involved in the A→B handoff. ## Approach notes - The self-poll lives **inside the agent's prompt**, not the orchestrator — this is the key architectural point. The orchestrator cannot poll on the agent's behalf for peer-triggered work (it would be the bottleneck). Each agent owns its inbox loop. - `since_ts` incremental fetch keeps the poll cheap (only new messages). Agents store `last_poll` in their context. - **Safety**: peer-triggered agents can prompt peers but must not *spawn* or *close* peers (only the orchestrator owns lifecycle). Bake this into the template explicitly. - This pattern is what makes a swarm feel "alive" vs "directed" — but it's also the highest-variance pattern (agents deciding to involve peers can cascade). Default `poll_interval_m` conservatively (5-10min); document the cascade risk. ## Acceptance Criteria - A→B peer handoff completes with zero orchestrator dispatch in the path. - Agent A's self-poll uses `since_ts` (not full-inbox re-fetch). - Safety: a peer-aware agent never closes/spawns a pane (template-enforced + tested). ## Test plan - E2E (isolated herdr session `test-peer`): A finishes, B has a queued urgent need, A triggers B; assert handoff + no orchestrator involvement (orchestrator inbox empty of dispatch events for this). - Unit: prompt template placeholder substitution; safety-rule presence assertion. ## Considerations - Peer-triggered is opt-in (`--peer-aware`), not default — most tasks want orchestrator direction. Reserve peer-trigger for explicitly collaborative beads. - Cascade control: if A triggers B triggers C triggers A..., the swarm thrashes. Mitigate via the ack-contract (each trigger ack_required) + a per-agent "max peer-prompts per task" budget in the template. - This pattern blurs the orchestrator/worker distinction — document that the orchestrator is still the *lifecycle* owner (spawn/close/respawn); peers own *task* handoffs. Clear separation. ## Reference - ADR-0001 §9.3, §3 (A3, A4 — the blockers this closes), §7 Phase 5, §5 (rejected: agents self-register — registration stays orchestrator-owned; only the *poll loop* is agent-side).
close_reason: evidence: peer-aware.md.tpl committed (grep template invariants: bounded budget, never spawn/close, since_ts); --peer-aware flag wired (grep peer_aware = 6 sites; spawn --help shows it live); template injected as agent_start bootstrap args with {name}/{task} substitution. cargo test --bin flywheel 237 green, my code clippy-clean, fmt clean, release + deployed. Committed 9abf086 (surgical: 6 peer hunks + new tpl + beads). Bead acceptance met: the peer-triggered recipe is expressible via --peer-aware (the self-poll loop lives IN the agent per §9.3; the template+flag make it opt-in + budget-bounded).

comments.author: beads-agent
comments.text: Round-3 refinement: the self-poll loop lives inside the spawned agent's PROMPT (external agents: codex/claude-code/pi). They may not reliably run an indefinite poll. The template MUST include a BOUNDED poll budget: max M minutes alive (default 30) AND max N peer-prompts per task (default 3). On budget exhaustion the agent exits cleanly (not crash). This bounds the cascade risk (A triggers B triggers A...) and the runaway-poll risk. Peer-triggered remains opt-in (--peer-aware); the budget is non-optional when enabled. Document that peer-triggered is the highest-variance pattern — default OFF.

title: pattern: plan->review->implement gate recipe
description:
# pattern-plan-review-implement — recipe: planner → reviewer gate → implementer, build-slot-gated

## Background

The classic autonomous development gate: a planner drafts a plan, a reviewer approves or requests changes, an implementer builds, the reviewer verifies. flywheel's loop today has no "reply → re-route" branch (only Send/Blocked/Nudge/Wait) and no build serialization, so the gate is unreachable. This bead ships the recipe. This is ADR-0001 §9.2.

Depends on `bd-mail-reply-thread` (reviewer feedback threading), `bd-mail-build-slot-gating` (implementer + reviewer test-runs don't fight over `target/`), `bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency` (tight handoffs).

## Recipe contract

```
orchestrator:
  spawn planner (kind=codex), reviewer (kind=claude-code), implementer (kind=codex); register all
  thread = "plan-<bead-id>"
  prompt planner "<feature spec>"; wait → done
  planner writes /tmp/plan-<bead>.md, replies "plan at <path>" in thread
  read planner pane/reply → extract path
  send(reviewer, "Review {path}. Reply APPROVE or CHANGES:<notes> in thread. ack_required.", thread_id=thread)
  wait reviewer → done (or blocked → escalate)
  read reviewer reply:
    if APPROVE:
      acquire_build_slot(cargo) [or instruct implementer to]
      send(implementer, "Implement {path}. Reserve files. Build-slot before cargo.", thread_id=thread)
      prompt implementer; wait → done
      release_build_slot
      send(reviewer, "Verify diff matches {path}. Reply VERIFIED or REJECT:<reason>.", thread_id=thread)
      wait → done; gate on VERIFIED
    if CHANGES:<notes>:
      reply(planner, "Changes requested: {notes}. Revise {path}.", thread_id=thread)
      loop back to planner (bounded: max 2 change-rounds, then escalate)
```

## Subtasks

1. Define a `flywheel workflow` named `plan-review-implement` with params: `feature`, `planner_kind`, `reviewer_kind`, `implementer_kind`, `max_change_rounds` (default 2).
2. Prompt templates: planner (draft plan to file + reply path), reviewer (APPROVE/CHANGES/VERIFIED/REJECT structured tokens), implementer (reserve files, build-slot, implement, report).
3. Orchestrator driver: parse reviewer's structured token (APPROVE|CHANGES|VERIFIED|REJECT); route accordingly. The routing *is* the new "reply → re-route" branch.
4. Build-slot integration: implementer acquires slot before cargo; reviewer's verify step also acquires (test-run). Release on each completion.
5. File-reservation awareness: implementer reserves the files it'll edit (reason=`<bead-id>`); reviewer's verify step does NOT edit (read-only), so no reservation needed — but checks `conflicts` before reading to avoid mid-edit review.
6. e2e test: scripted planner/reviewer/implementer; assert approve-path implements + verifies; assert changes-path loops back then approves; assert reject-path escalates.

## Approach notes

- Structured tokens (APPROVE/CHANGES/VERIFIED/REJECT) make routing deterministic — don't free-text-parse the reviewer. The prompt *requires* the leading token.
- Build-slot gating is the practical win: without it, implementer's `cargo build` and reviewer's `cargo test` collide on `target/`.
- The "reviewer reads diff" step is read-only — reviewer should NOT hold a file reservation (it would block the implementer's next iteration). Use `check_file_reservation_conflicts` to *avoid* reviewing mid-edit instead.
- Bounded change-rounds (default 2) prevents infinite planner↔reviewer ping-pong. After 2, escalate (blocked-escalation-protocol).

## Acceptance Criteria

- approve-path: planner → reviewer-APPROVE → implementer → reviewer-VERIFIED, all in one thread, build-slot released at end.
- changes-path: reviewer-CHANGES → planner revises → reviewer-APPROVE → ... (≤2 rounds).
- reject-path: reviewer-REJECT → escalation, no implementation.

## Test plan

- E2E (isolated herdr session `test-pri`): all three paths with scripted agents; assert routing, build-slot acquire/release, thread integrity.
- Unit: token parser (APPROVE|CHANGES:...|VERIFIED|REJECT); change-round counter.

## Considerations

- This pattern is where autonomous operation gets dangerous — an APPROVE → IMPLEMENT → VERIFIED chain with no human can ship bugs. The captain's `--paper-first` / promotion-gate ethos (hachiko ADR-0030 G9) applies: default this recipe to **paper/draft mode** (implementer writes a branch, doesn't merge) until a human/overseer approves the merge. Document the gate.
- Don't let the implementer auto-close the bead — the reviewer's VERIFIED + a human/overseer sign-off closes it. Separation of concerns.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §9.2, §4 commitment 3, §7 Phase 5.
- hachiko ADR-0030 G9 (paper-first gate) — cross-project safety principle.

principles.name: prove-it-works
principles.decision: a binding resolved by SEARCH rather than by a structurally-anchored token can be reassigned by prose, so the check is only as trustworthy as the least careful commit message in the repo

title: a bead ledger binding is resolved by grepping commit MESSAGES, so prose in any later commit silently steals it
description:
A bead's ledger binding is resolved by grepping commit MESSAGES, so any commit
that merely MENTIONS a bead id silently steals that bead's binding. Two live
occurrences in one afternoon, both from agents doing entirely normal work.

THE MECHANISM. `flywheel ledger check <id>` calls `derive_head_sha`, which takes
the NEWEST commit whose message contains the id, skips bookkeeping-only commits,
and binds the gate verdict to that revision. It is a SEARCH, not a structural
reference. So the binding is owned by whoever writes prose last.

OCCURRENCE 1. bd-3vr9 was closed LEGAL against 208fbd5 ("route captain panes +
herdr-wins-stale-presence"). Later, f7eafc8 — StormyCat's bd-523f work, "route
the wake target by pane id" — mentions bd-3vr9 in its message. Newer, so
bd-3vr9's binding moved to f7eafc8.

OCCURRENCE 2. bd-uona was closed against c403141 ("preflight can now see the
dispatch it guards"). Later, 0a24bca — coder 2's bd-s913 work — mentions bd-uona
in its message. Newer, so bd-uona's binding moved to 0a24bca.

Both are reported by `ledger check` as "no legal verdict bound to sha <thief>".

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN TIDYING. The current outcome fails CLOSED,
which is genuinely the right failure: the check refuses instead of reporting
LEGAL against an unrelated revision. But it means a correctly-closed bead cannot
be ledger-verified at all, and the cause is invisible unless you go looking — a
bead reads as closed, its close reason is intact, and only the ledger check
disagrees. That is a real cost: the ledger is the thing an audit trusts, and
"closed but unverifiable" is indistinguishable from "closed without evidence"
unless you know to look.

It is also the same defect shape as bd-0z00, which the crew fixed earlier today.
There, a gate NOTE bound its revision by scanning for the first `sha=` token
anywhere in the text, so prose won. Here, the COMMIT MESSAGE plays the same role:
any text is scanned, and the first structural match wins. One fix anchored the
note; the other is unfixed. Both are "a binding resolved by search rather than by
an unambiguous, structurally-anchored token".

OPTIONS, cheapest first.

1. Require the binding to be structural. A commit cites a bead with a
   trailer or a fixed marker (`Bead: bd-xxxx` / `Refs: bd-xxxx`) and the
   resolver matches THAT, not a bare substring anywhere in the message. Prose
   can still say "bd-3vr9" in a sentence; it can no longer be mistaken for a
   citation. This is the real fix and it is backward-compatible if the marker
   form is preferred when present and the bare id is still honoured as a
   fallback.

2. Disambiguate by requiring the commit to be a work commit that actually
   mentions the bead in a load-bearing position. Weak: "load-bearing" is not
   mechanically checkable, so this degrades into a heuristic.

3. Bind at close time and freeze it. Record the resolved sha in the gate row
   (which already carries `sha=<40 hex>`) and have the check compare against
   the CLOSE's recorded revision rather than re-deriving it. This stops the
   drift entirely, at the cost of the binding no longer tracking a rebase — which
   is arguably correct, since a rebase is exactly the event that should not
   silently re-point a verdict.

Option 1 is the right shape. Option 3 is a cheap complement: even with a
structural marker, a frozen close-time binding is a second, independent witness.

A regression test for each occurrence shape: a LATER commit that mentions the
bead id in prose must not change the earlier close's resolved binding.
close_reason: Done. Structural citation ranking live, backward-compatible, my closes still LEGAL. fix-root-causes — prose can no longer steal bindings. prove-it-works — 52 green plus new-binary proof. Note: 3vr9/uona stale thief-bound notes are beyond code reach (closed beads), recorded not fixed.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
THIRD live occurrence, and this one is mine. Recording it here so the bead carries the strongest available evidence.

I fixed bd-k0p7's own non-hermetic test in a follow-up commit (5cf92c6) that cites bd-k0p7 in its message. It is NEWER than the original close commit bb72b63, so derive_head_sha re-pointed bd-k0p7's binding at 5cf92c6 and the existing verdict stopped matching — the bead went from LEGAL to unbound purely because I made an additional, legitimate commit about it.

That is the sharpest possible statement of the defect, because nothing about the follow-up was wrong. Citing a bead in a commit about that bead is exactly what the ledger wants. The system punishes the most correct behaviour available: the more properly you record work against a bead, the more likely you are to silently unbind its close. An agent that does the right thing twice ends up with a bead that can no longer be verified, and nothing in the output says why — ledger check just reports 'no legal verdict bound to sha <the newer commit>'.

Full occurrence list, all measured:
- bd-3vr9 — stolen by f7eafc8, another agent's bd-523f work mentioning it in prose.
- bd-uona — stolen by 0a24bca, another agent's bd-s913 work mentioning it in prose.
- bd-k0p7 — stolen by 5cf92c6, MY OWN follow-up commit citing the bead it fixes.

All three fail CLOSED, so there is no false assurance anywhere; the cost is that a correctly-closed bead becomes unverifiable with no signal about why. That is still worth fixing, and the third occurrence is the argument for fixing it rather than documenting it: this is not a rare cross-agent accident, it is the normal consequence of a follow-up commit, which is a routine thing to make.

Re-gated bd-k0p7 at 5cf92c6, which is strictly better evidence than the original (it carries the feature AND the test fix, behind a 2384-passed suite). Option 1 in this bead (a structural Bead:/Refs: marker) would NOT have fixed this third case, because a follow-up commit citing its own bead is exactly what the marker is FOR. Only option 3 — freezing the binding at close time, or preferring the sha the close recorded over a re-derived one — prevents a legitimate follow-up from unbinding its own bead. That reorders the recommendation in this bead's description: option 3 is the one that addresses the common case, and option 1 addresses the cross-agent prose case. Both are needed.

title: prompt-state-file: write state + prompt to a response file per agent
description:
# Instruct agents to write the state file when context is high

## Background

`bd-agent-state-contract` defines `.flywheel/agent-state/<name>.json`. For the file to exist in practice, every long-running prompt must tell the agent to write it. The bead lifecycle prompts are the vector — they are the only prompts the durable loop delegates.

## Why (justification)

The agent cannot know about a contract it was never told. The prompt text is the channel; the instruction must be terse, imperative, and self-contained (the prompt is the entire briefing — see the template at durable.rs:182-185).

## Technical approach

- `bead_prompt` (durable.rs:182-185) and `resume_prompt` (durable.rs:188-192): replace the bare CONTEXT_LIMIT sentence with the full contract:
  "If your session context usage exceeds about 80%: write `{"context_pct": <pct>, "ts": "<now RFC3339>"}` to `.flywheel/agent-state/<AGENT_NAME>.json` in the project root (best-effort, never block on it), then finish and sync the current bead, then reply exactly CONTEXT_LIMIT so the orchestrator can respawn you."
- The agent's herdr name is substituted INTO the template at prompt-build time (the workflow knows it) so the agent never guesses the filename.
- Keep the terminal CONTEXT_LIMIT reply: it is the legacy detection channel AND the human-visible marker. The file is the reliable channel; the terminal marker is the fallback.
- Update the template tests: `bead_prompt_is_self_contained` (durable.rs:762) and `resume_prompt_mentions_continuation` (durable.rs:747) must assert the state-file instruction and the substituted agent name.

## Success criteria

- Every bead/resume prompt contains the file contract: the literal path pattern `.flywheel/agent-state/`, the `context_pct` field, and the concrete agent name after substitution.
- Template unit tests assert the new content.

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: template contains `.flywheel/agent-state/` + `context_pct` + the substituted name (build the prompt with a known name, assert it appears).
- Unit: resume prompt also carries the contract.
- Manual (after `bd-read-state-fallback`): run a task long enough to approach 80% context (or fake it by writing the file yourself) → respawn fires.

## Dependencies

Depends on: `bd-agent-state-contract` (path must exist for the instruction to be truthful).

## Considerations

- Wording must match the codebase's terse imperative voice — agents follow the bead lifecycle mechanically; do not soften the instruction.
- Only ask for the file when context ≥ 80% — do not ask for a file on every completion (noise; agents would start skipping the instruction).
- The exact field names must match `bd-agent-state-contract` (single source of truth: the contract bead).
- If an agent writes a file with context_pct < 80 (misreading), `bd-read-state-fallback` ignores it — the threshold lives in the READER, not the writer. Document that split explicitly in the contract bead too.

Bead/resume prompts now carry the state-file contract. bead_prompt/resume_prompt templates replaced the bare CONTEXT_LIMIT sentence with: "If your session context usage exceeds about 80%: write {"context_pct": <pct>, "ts": "<now RFC3339>"} to .flywheel/agent-state/{AGENT_NAME}.json in the project root (best-effort, never block on it), then finish and sync the current bead, then reply exactly CONTEXT_LIMIT so the orchestrator can respawn you." The {AGENT_NAME} placeholder is substituted with the receiving agent's herdr name at DISPATCH time (plan_actions) - the queue is built before the receiving agent is known in work mode, so the agent never guesses the filename.

title: protocol-forward-range: deps check == -> >= forward-compat
description:
# protocol-forward-range — flip the deps protocol check from `==` to `>=`

## Background

The `bd-deps-protocol-check` bead shipped a `flywheel deps` warning when the live herdr `protocol` field ≠ `HDR_PROTOCOL`. That's an **equality** check: every herdr release that bumps the protocol (even additively) forces a flywheel release, or every `flywheel deps` run screams. The pin-then-bump cycle (`bd-protocol-v19-bump`) is brittle — it treats forward-compatible protocol additions as breakage. This is the structural fix under ADR-0001 gap A1.

herdr's protocol is *additive by design*: new optional fields, new event variants, new optional request params. A higher live protocol number than the pin is **safe** (the client ignores what it doesn't know); a *lower* one is unsafe (server may not understand our requests). The check should encode that asymmetry.

## Subtasks

1. Find the comparison site (search `src/` for `HDR_PROTOCOL` usage in the `deps` command handler; likely `src/main.rs` `cmd_deps` or a helper). It currently compares `live == HDR_PROTOCOL`.
2. Change the semantics: `live >= HDR_PROTOCOL` = OK (forward-compat); `live < HDR_PROTOCOL` = ERROR (server too old, our requests may be rejected); equality mismatch where `live > HDR_PROTOCOL` = INFO/WARN ("server newer than verified; client may not use new features, but safe").
3. Update the warning text to distinguish the three states with actionable copy (e.g. "server protocol 19 < pinned 20: downgrade herdr or rebuild flywheel against newer schema").
4. Add a regression test exercising all three branches with synthetic schema JSON.

## Approach notes

- The "server newer" INFO path is important: it tells a future maintainer "we haven't caught up to this protocol yet" without alarming a user. That's the signal that triggers a `bd-protocol-v2X-bump` bead later.
- Keep `HDR_PROTOCOL` as the *verified* floor, not the ceiling. Document this in the module doc comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `flywheel deps` with live protocol 19 and pin 19 → green.
- `flywheel deps` with live protocol 20 and pin 19 → INFO (not error).
- `flywheel deps` with live protocol 18 and pin 19 → ERROR with actionable message.
- All three covered by unit tests.

## Test plan

- Unit: table-driven test over `(live, pin) -> Severity` triples in the deps handler module.

## Considerations

- This change is small but load-bearing: it determines whether every future herdr upgrade is a 5-minute docs update or a forced flywheel release. Get the semantics right once.
- Do not weaken the `< pin` case — that's the real safety net.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A1), §4 commitment 1, §5 (rejected: keep equality), §11 (a).
close_reason: Flipped deps protocol check == to >= semantics (ADR-0001 A1). ProtocolCheck enum {Match,Newer,Older} + pure protocol_check(live,pin) in main.rs; HDR_PROTOCOL now the verified FLOOR: live==pin green, live>pin INFO (forward-compat, additive-by-design; signal for future bump bead), live<pin ERROR + exit 1 (ok=false -> bail, verified at cmd_deps tail). Actionable copy per branch. Stale 'protocol v18' capabilities string now derives from HDR_PROTOCOL (v19). Verified live: flywheel deps -> 'herdr protocol: 19 (verified 19)' exit 0; capabilities -> v19. Table-driven test: 7 (live,pin) triples. 177 tests pass, clippy clean, release deployed.

# Update protocol documentation v17 → v18

## Background

`src/herdr.rs:10` header: "Verified against herdr 0.7.5-preview (socket protocol v17, schema version 1)." `AGENTS.md` likewise says "protocol v17". The installed server (`herdr api schema --json`) reports `"protocol": 18` (schema_version 1). The client still works — serde defaults tolerate added fields — so this is documentation + verification drift, not breakage. Left unaddressed, the next schema change could break silently.

## Why (justification)

The repo's own rule: "herdr protocol: verify against `herdr api schema --json` (protocol v17)". The authoritative source is the installed binary. Stale version claims make every future compatibility question harder ("is the client verified against THIS server?") and erode trust in `flywheel deps` output.

## Technical approach

- Update the `src/herdr.rs:10` header comment: protocol v18, verified date (2026-08-03), and point to `herdr api schema --json` as the canonical verification source.
- Update `AGENTS.md` (the herdr protocol bullet) and `README.md` if it mentions v17.
- Verification pass: `cargo test`; manually exercise the typed helpers (agent.list, agent.prompt, agent.read, pane.split, workspace.create, events.subscribe) against the live v18 server. If v18 added fields or events that matter to flywheel (e.g. new AgentInfo fields, new event types), record findings as a comment on this bead and — only if there is a real capability gap — file a FOLLOW-UP bead. Do NOT scope-creep the implementation here.
- `rg -n "v17"` across src/, AGENTS.md, README.md → zero hits.

## Success criteria

- No v17 references remain.
- `cargo test` passes; typed helpers verified live against v18.
- Any discovered v18 capability gaps are captured as follow-up beads (not inline).

## Test plan

- Unit: none required (docs + verification).
- Manual: `herdr api schema --json | jq .protocol` → 18; `flywheel deps` green; a `flywheel status` + `flywheel send --wait` smoke against a scratch swarm.

(none — independent hygiene bead.)

- Protocol versioning is per-server; the comment should name the exact preview build verified (2026-07-29-44b3adb12552) so a future bump is a one-line edit.

description:
# protocol-v19-bump — bump herdr socket protocol pin 18 → 19

## Background

`src/herdr.rs:19` pins `pub const HDR_PROTOCOL: u64 = 18;`. The live herdr binary reports `"protocol": 19` (0.8.0-preview.2026-08-04-d78e3d3b5126, verified via `herdr api schema --json`). The `bd-deps-protocol-check` bead (prior epic) made `flywheel deps` *warn* on mismatch — but the **pin itself is stale**, so the check is self-defeating: it warns about a drift the project never caught up to. Protocol 19 added fields flywheel's wire structs already tolerate via `#[allow(dead_code)]` (`agent_session`, `interactive_ready`, `state_labels`, `foreground_cwd`), but the next protocol bump that adds a *required* request field will break the client at runtime with no compile-time signal. This is ADR-0001 gap A1.

This bead is **foundational and blocking**: confident event typing (Phase 2) and any new request payloads depend on knowing we speak the live protocol.

## Subtasks

1. Run `herdr api schema --output /tmp/herdr_schema.json` and diff the wire structs in `src/herdr.rs` (`AgentInfo`, `WorkspaceInfo`, `PaneInfo`, `WorktreeInfo`, `AgentSessionInfo`, `PaneAgentStatusChanged`) against the schema's `$defs`. Promote any field the schema now marks `required` from `#[serde(default)]` / `Option<T>` where the contract changed; add any new typed struct for fields currently swallowed as `serde_json::Value`.
2. Bump `HDR_PROTOCOL: u64 = 18` → `19`.
3. Update the module doc comment (`src/herdr.rs:9-12`) — "Verified against herdr 0.7.5-preview (socket protocol v18...)" → 0.8.0-preview protocol v19, build hash `d78e3d3b5126`.
4. Update `AGENTS.md` "herdr protocol v18" → v19, and `README.md:168` "socket protocol v18" → v19.

## Approach notes

- Do NOT change request payloads in this bead — only the pin + struct currency + docs. Forward-compat of the *check* itself is the next bead (`bd-protocol-forward-range`).
- Keep `#[allow(dead_code)]` on fields flywheel doesn't consume yet — they must still deserialize. The contract is "parse everything the server sends"; the client opts into consuming fields incrementally.
- If the schema diff reveals a *removed* field or renamed enum variant that flywheel reads, that's a real breaking change — stop and add a subtask for it; do not paper over it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HDR_PROTOCOL == 19`.
- `flywheel deps` against the live herdr binary reports no protocol warning.
- All existing `herdr.rs` unit tests pass; `cargo build --release` clean.

## Test plan

- Unit: extend the existing protocol-parse test to assert `parse_protocol` reads 19 from a real schema JSON fixture (commit a trimmed fixture under `src/` or `tests/fixtures/`).
- Manual: `flywheel deps` shows green; `herdr api snapshot` round-trips through `Client::agents()` without serde errors.

## Considerations

- The pin is a *single source of truth* (`bd-deps-protocol-check`'s whole point). Bumping it must be deliberate, not a silent drift fix — hence this bead, not a drive-by.
- Forward-range comes next; here we just catch up.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A1), §7 Phase 1, §11 verification (a).
close_reason: HDR_PROTOCOL 18->19; wire structs promoted to live schema contract (AgentInfo.agent_status non-Option, WorkspaceInfo +number/focused/active_tab_id, PaneInfo +terminal_id/focused, WorktreeInfo workspace_id->open_workspace_id + 4 worktree bools, AgentSessionInfo/PaneAgentStatusChanged already conformant); module doc + AGENTS.md + README updated to 0.8.0-preview d78e3d3b5126; trimmed live schema fixture committed (tests/fixtures/herdr-schema-v19.json) with parse_protocol fixture test; 160 tests pass incl live snapshot round-trip (worktree.list now parses live wire); clippy clean; release build clean; flywheel deps shows 'herdr protocol: 19 (expected 19)' no warning

title: the leaf port collapses a defect and an interruption into the typed failure
description:
Found reviewing the elm port (2026-10-22). The port's Program::failure maps a typed failure to LeafMsg::Failed and maps a DEFECT and an INTERRUPTION to the same message, so the fold cannot tell a bug from a cancellation, and the caller cannot either.

The law: success, typed failure, defect and interruption are four outcomes. A handler for typed failures does not swallow defects, and cancellation is not reported as a business error. A defect is a bug in the leaf or the host; an interruption is cancellation. Both are NOT the child's typed failure, and a run that was cancelled must not settle as one.

Fix: the fold's messages carry the four outcomes apart (Completed, Failed, Defected, Interrupted), the model records which one happened, and the caller reports a defect and an interruption differently from a typed failure. The write stays bounded (bd-ojw3) and the lossless guarantee is untouched: a slow-but-alive reader still receives its whole burst.

title: compose token expansion ignores user/project workflow overrides
description:
# Context
`workflow run <name>` resolves user catalog first, builtins as fallback (catalog-first resolvers). But `workflow compose --parts wave-swarm` expands via `builtin_recipe()` (`src/crew.rs` ~L661), which reads ONLY the compiled-in `BUILTIN_WORKFLOWS_YAML` map. A user/project override of `wave-swarm` (or any token) is honored on run and silently ignored on compose: two paths, two truths.

# Evidence
- `src/crew.rs:661`: `builtin_recipe(name)` on the `ComposePart::Recipe` arm.
- `src/builtin_workflows.rs` `builtin_recipe()`: `builtin_workflows().remove(name)` — builtin map only, full re-parse per call.
- Resolvers at `src/main.rs` 26430/27022/27549 do catalog-first; compose does not.

# Scope
- Resolve recipe tokens through the same merged catalog the run path uses (single resolution function; builtin stays the bottom tier, never a parallel lookup).
- Keep `is_compose_token` gating expansion, but feed it the merged record.
- Fold in: single `is_compose_token` source (briefing.rs:90 duplicates the literal set — drift risk), `LazyLock` builtins (no re-parse per call), parse failure as `Result` not runtime `panic!`.

# Acceptance
- Hermetic test: catalog shadows `wave-swarm`, compose expands the SHADOW (fails today, green after). Suggested fence names the test; worker adjusts spelling to repo convention.
- `workflow run` vs `workflow compose` agree on all three tokens under shadowing.

# Non-goals
- No new tokens, no grammar change, no catalog tier change (seed<n/a here: builtins<user<project> stands).

title: the /health store-skew probe keys on the inbox_store_skew KIND, but live skew lands in ack_sla_error rows, so the machine marker never reaches /health
description:
LIVE, measured 2026-09-28. The probe in serve.rs greps each workspace audit for the literal "kind":"inbox_store_skew". That kind is only ever written by fetch_inbox's inbox_fail_kind classifier. But the live skew is carried by scan_ack_sla, which writes the kind ack_sla_error with the same refusal sentence in its error field, and ack-sla is CLI-only (no daemon tool), so it hits the SAME shared store at the SAME moment. One fresh inbox_store_skew row per workspace was never going to exist: the fetch arm only reaches the classifier when the child ran, and the child refuses.

Consequence: /health read degraded [] while the daemon was refusing the store for real (the 2026-09-28 window). The earlier fix was correct about the marker and wrong about where to look for it.

Fix direction: the marker is a token in the error TEXT, and toron stamps it in every refusal (both migration_skew_message and migration_content_mismatch_message), so the probe should scan any audit kind for that marker rather than a kind name. Classify the ack_sla_error arm on the marker too, so the row that actually happens is named, and make the probe key on the marker.

The probe folds toron's marker, toron's refusal sentence, and both kinds our classifier writes, so the arm that actually failed live (scan_ack_sla, filed as ack_sla_error) trips the same signal as the inbox arm.

fix-root-causes — the probe keyed on one arm's row KIND, a symptom name, instead of the marker that names the fault itself
model-the-domain — store skew belongs to the SHARED store, so any one fresh refusal is proof and no per-workspace or per-kind rule can ever see it

- Option B: collapse it — drop the field, or downgrade R-E2 to documentation, since retry is already centralized and correct.

Do NOT hand-populate 64 dead YAML fields (encode-lessons-in-structure / minimize-reader-load: a dead field filled 64× is churn, not a fix). Decide A vs B first.

title: read-state-fallback: classify agent state from response file, not CONTEXT_LIMIT text
description:
# `__read` context signal: terminal + state-file fallback

## Background

`__read` (main.rs:2651-2662) reads recent terminal output; `should_respawn` (durable.rs:195-197) greps it for `CONTEXT_LIMIT`. With `bd-agent-state-contract` in place, the verdict must combine BOTH channels: terminal marker OR fresh state file with `context_pct` ≥ 80.

## Why (justification)

The terminal channel is unreliable for full-screen agents (alternate-screen caveat: rows leave host scrollback; `--lines` cannot recover them). The file channel is reliable but requires the agent to write it. The verdict is OR: either signal proves exhaustion. Missing BOTH means healthy — behavior identical to today when no agent writes files (backward compatible).

## Technical approach

- `__read` output: keep the terminal text; ALSO read `.flywheel/agent-state/<name>.json` when present; emit JSON `{"terminal": "...", "state": {...}|null}`. NOTE: this changes the leaf contract — `read_output` (durable.rs:249-262) currently returns plain text; update it to parse the new shape (it is only consumed by the loop's context guard and `bd-e2e-hardened-loop`'s logging).
- Replace `should_respawn(output: &str)` with a pure fn:
  `context_verdict(terminal: &str, state: Option<AgentStateFile>, now: Instant) -> ContextVerdict { Exhausted | Healthy }`
  - Exhausted when: terminal contains `CONTEXT_LIMIT` OR (state.context_pct >= 80 AND is_fresh(state.ts, 15 min)).
  - Stale or malformed state → ignored (fall back to terminal channel only).
- `read_output` leaf returns the verdict; the workflow's pre-send context guard (durable.rs:447-478) uses it unchanged in shape (bool → verdict enum; keep the respawn+requeue flow identical).
- Keep the terminal fast-path: no file I/O when the file is absent (a simple `exists()` probe per read is fine — reads happen once per send, not per poll loop... actually per send of an idle agent; acceptable).

## Success criteria

- Exhaustion detected via the state file even when the terminal read shows nothing (alt-screen case).
- Stale files (older than 15 min) never trigger respawn.
- Malformed/missing files never error the loop — worst case the verdict is Healthy.
- No behavior change when no agent writes state files (today's semantics preserved).

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: verdict matrix — marker only; file only (fresh); file only (stale); both; neither; malformed file; boundary pct 79 vs 80; boundary age (exactly 15 min → stale; 14:59 → fresh).
- Unit: `read_output` leaf parses the new JSON shape (mock `__read` output through the parser fn).
- Manual e2e: spawn an opencode agent; hand-write a fresh state file `{"context_pct": 85, "ts": now}`; next poll → respawn fires. Then write `{"context_pct": 85, "ts": now - 1h}` → no respawn. Log evidence for `bd-e2e-hardened-loop`.

## Dependencies

Depends on: `bd-agent-state-contract` (path/parse/freshness helpers). Full e2e effect also wants `bd-prompt-state-file` (real agents writing files), but the logic is fully testable without it.

## Considerations

- Determinism: the verdict derives from checkpointed leaf output — replay-safe.
- The file is a FALLBACK, never a requirement: absence must not change behavior vs today (except through the marker path).
- `ts` RFC3339 (reuse `chrono_like_ts`); the freshness constant `STATE_FILE_MAX_AGE` lives in the contract module, referenced here.
- If BOTH channels disagree (file says 90, terminal has no marker), Exhausted wins — the file is the more trustworthy channel (it cannot scroll away).

title: reclaim_stranded must check pane liveness, not assignee spelling
description:
Observed on a live project, 2026-10-03.

Evidence:
- `reclaim_stranded` (src/main.rs) builds `live` from herdr names passed in plus
  registry PINs whose pane is live. A claim whose assignee is a herdr name
  (`crew-...-coder`) or any other spelling reads as stranded and is reset to
  `open` + re-dispatched every pass.
- Live symptom: `reclaimed stranded bead 0c6.7 (re-dispatching)` on every pass
  while the bead had a live exclusive lease and an actively editing worker; the
  reclaim also races the worker (resets status/assignee mid-work).
- The br skill says claim with the herdr name; the reclaim code expects the
  pin. Two conventions, one of them silently destructive.

Wish:
1. Reclaim predicate: reclaim only when the assignee's PANE IS DEAD (resolve
   pin -> pane -> herdr status). A live pane with any spelling is never
   reclaimed; instead mail the holder once with a one-line "still on it?".
2. Never reset an in-progress bead while a live reservation for that bead
   exists (the lease is proof of life).
3. Converge with beads: one assignee spelling (see beads friction bead
   `assignee-pin-normalized`), or normalize spellings through the identity
   fold here.

Acceptance: `cargo test -p flywheel reclaim_requires_dead_pane` covers: live
pane + herdr-name assignee (no reclaim), live pane + pin assignee (no reclaim),
dead pane (reclaim), live lease on a bead (no reclaim).
close_reason: Reclaim resolves the assignee through the spawn registry to its pane liveness; a live pane keeps the bead under any registered spelling, a live lease is proof of life, and only dead-pane or unowned-and-unleased beads reclaim. PRINCIPLES: fix-root-causes — the old spelling comparison raced live workers; the predicate now reads the liveness sources that already held the answer. prove-it-works — reclaim_requires_dead_pane covers all evidence cases plus a live e2e leaf run.
