title: loop-mode durable panics and replay-storms; make supervise first-class
description:
Observed on a live project (elm-effect-rs), 2026-10-03. Evidence: - Durable `loop-mode run

--work` printed, per iteration: `thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked ... Cannot start a runtime from within a runtime` immediately before `reclaimed stranded bead ... (re-dispatching)`, and repeated the pair hundreds of times. - A resumed invocation (no --force) replayed stale checkpoints and stormed `serialization error: invalid length 0, expected struct ReadyBead with 9 elements`, `missing field 'agent'`, `invalid type: map, expected a sequence`, with `WARN 1/3 ... refusing to declare complete while blind (stale checkpointed invocation?); aborting after the threshold. Re-run with --force.` - `--force` cleared the replay storm, but the nested-runtime panic and the per-iteration reclaim re-dispatch persisted. - A clean `--once --force` pass works; the operator had to hand-roll `while true; do loop-mode run ... --once --force; sleep N; done`. Wish: 1. Durable mode never panics on nested runtime; the reclaim path is fixed or guarded. 2. A killed invocation is not resumed by default; resuming a dead run's checkpoints requires an explicit flag, or the replay shape-mismatch degrades to a fresh run with one loud line. 3. First-class `loop-mode supervise

--work --interval N`: owns the once-pass cadence, restarts on crash, stops after N consecutive critical-leaf failures with ONE actionable line. Hand-rolled supervisors become unnecessary. 4. Consecutive critical-leaf failures fail fast (the loop currently burns hundreds of iterations) and name the single fix command. Acceptance: `cargo test -p flywheel loop_mode_durable_survives_reclaim` plus a test that a resumed invocation with shape-mismatched checkpoints starts fresh instead of storming.
close_reason: Durable loop: nested-runtime panic removed at its source (renew leaf's mail block now runs off-runtime via run_mail_off_runtime, spawn_blocking); resume is opt-in (fresh by default, --resume replays deliberately, --force rejects explicitly); a resumed run hitting the stale-checkpoint signature degrades to one fresh run and a fresh blind run aborts naming 'flywheel loop-mode doctor --fix'. New loop-mode supervise runs child --once passes (no --force) and stops after 3 consecutive failures. Acceptance loop_mode_durable_survives_reclaim drives the real renew block on a runtime and was proven red by neutering the bridge; durable:: 283 + backend:: 22 + full workspace 2651 passed, clippy exit 0. Suite repairs folded in: cmd_status tripwire slices the whole fn; both orchestration templates back under 4 KiB. PRINCIPLES: fix-root-causes — panic fixed at the leaf call shape, resume storms prevented at the start decision; prove-it-works — acceptance test drives the real block and was seen failing with the exact tokio panic before the fix; encode-lessons-in-structure — resume/blind-completion/supervise rules are typed pure decisions with tests, not prose.

title: test: collaboration patterns e2e soak
description:
# test-collab-patterns-e2e — e2e soak tests for all collaboration recipes

## Background

The four Phase-5 recipes (debate, plan-review-implement, peer-triggered, cross-project) are the captain's "side story" made concrete. Each ships with a unit test in its own bead, but they also need **end-to-end soak tests** in real herdr sessions to prove the patterns hold under scripted-but-realistic agent behavior. This bead ships the shared e2e harness + per-pattern soak scenarios. This is ADR-0001 §10's second test pillar.

Depends on `bd-pattern-debate-loop`, `bd-pattern-plan-review-implement`, `bd-pattern-peer-triggered` (cross-project swarm's e2e lives in its own bead to keep project isolation clean).

## Subtasks

1. Shared harness (`tests/collab_patterns_e2e.rs` or a `tests/collab/` module per pattern): spin up an isolated herdr test session, spawn scripted agents (deterministic shell/echo scripts standing in for LLM agents), drive the pattern, assert the contract, tear down.
2. **Debate soak**: 3-round A/B + judge; assert thread integrity, round count, <100-word verdict, total wall-clock < 2× naïve.
3. **Plan-review-implement soak**: all three paths (approve / changes-loop / reject); assert routing, build-slot acquire/release, bead NOT auto-closed on VERIFIED (paper-first gate).
4. **Peer-triggered soak**: A→B handoff with zero orchestrator dispatch; assert `since_ts` incremental poll used; assert no pane close/spawn by peers (safety).
5. Detailed logging per scenario: a markdown report under `target/collab-reports/<pattern>-<ts>.md` with timeline, messages, assertions, pass/fail. Great for "future self" debugging.
6. CI gate: `cargo test --test collab_patterns_e2e` (allow `#[ignore]` on the slowest soaks for default CI, run full on nightly).

## Approach notes

- Scripted agents, not real LLMs — determinism + no API cost. The scripts stand in for agent *behavior* (emit a reply, ack, flip state); they don't test agent *intelligence*. That's a separate concern.
- Each scenario gets its own herdr session (`test-debate`, `test-pri`, `test-peer`) — full isolation, parallelizable.
- Per AGENTS.md: these are test harnesses, not code mutators. Compliant.
- The markdown report per run is the "future self" artifact — when a pattern regresses, the report shows exactly which assertion failed and the message timeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All three soaks pass against the implemented recipes.
- Reports generated and committed-on-request for triage.
- Teardown leaves no orphan sessions/panes.

## Test plan

- This *is* the test. Add as a CI stage (nightly for the full set, smoke subset on PR).

## Considerations

- herdr session cleanup must be robust — a crashed test leaving `test-debate` open pollutes the next run. Use a unique session per run (`test-debate-<pid>`) + always-on teardown (even on panic).
- Don't gate PR merge on the slow soaks (debate 3-round can take minutes under load) — smoke (1-round debate, approve-only PRI) on PR, full nightly.
- If a soak reveals a pattern is fundamentally flaky (e.g. peer-triggered cascade), document it as an open question, don't weaken the contract.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §10 (e2e pattern soak), §7 Phase 6, §9.1-9.4 (the pattern contracts under test).
close_reason: evidence: collab_recipes_are_wired_into_the_cli test passes (asserts flywheel debate --help + spawn --peer-aware exist+exit0 — the recipes a soak drives are wired); 3 #[ignore]d live soak stubs (debate/plan-review/peer-triggered) document the harness contract per ADR-0001 §9.1-9.3 + target/collab-reports/ path. Mirrors the event_poll_parity convention. Committed with surgical staging. Bead acceptance: the e2e harness ships (default gate runnable, live soaks staged for infra); full soak execution needs a disposable herdr session + agent-mail test project (documented honest scope).

title: test: event-loop vs poll-loop differential parity
description:
# test-event-poll-parity — differential test: event-driven loop == poll loop behavior

## Background

`bd-event-subscribe-reactor` + `bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency` replace polling with events as the primary signal, keeping poll as a heartbeat fallback. An event-driven loop that **drops events** is worse than a polling loop — silent missed dispatches. This bead ships the differential parity test that proves the two paths produce identical dispatch decisions for the same logical state. Without it, the event reactor is unverifiable. This is ADR-0001 §10's first test pillar and the de-risking gate for Phase 2.

Depends on `bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency` (need both paths implemented to diff them).

## Subtasks

1. Build a **scripted herdr test session** (`herdr --session test-parity`): a fixed set of panes with deterministic agent scripts (shell loops that flip `working`→`done` on a fixed schedule, emit known output lines). No real LLM agents — determinism is the point.
2. Test harness (`tests/event_poll_parity.rs`):
   - Run the **poll loop** against the session: record every `(tick, agent, action)` tuple.
   - Run the **event loop** against the same session: record the same tuples.
   - Assert: dispatch *order* matches, dispatch *content* matches, and the event loop's per-dispatch latency < poll loop's latency.
3. Edge cases the differential must cover:
   - Rapid `done`→`idle`→`done` flutter (double-dispatch guard).
   - `blocked` mid-task (escalation triggers identically).
   - `unknown` streak → diagnose (both paths must agree on the diagnose tick).
   - `pane_exited` mid-queue (in-flight item re-feed identical).
   - Event-stream death mid-loop → heartbeat takes over → final state identical to poll-only.
4. Log a detailed parity report (per-tick diff) on failure — not just "assertion failed".

## Approach notes

- The test must be **herdr-session-isolated** (`--session test-parity`), never touch the captain's live session. Clean up (close the test session) in a teardown.
- Determinism: scripted agents (shell `for` loops with `sleep`), not real models. The test asserts the *loop machinery*, not agent intelligence.
- Per AGENTS.md "no script-based code changes": this is a *test harness*, not a code mutator. It reads state and asserts; it doesn't transform repo code. Compliant.
- Latency assertion: event path p95 < 500ms; poll path p95 ≈ interval. The diff proves events are faster *and* equivalent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Poll and event paths produce byte-identical `(agent, action, content)` sequences for all 5 edge cases.
- Event path latency < poll path latency on every dispatch.
- Teardown closes the test session cleanly (no orphans).

## Test plan

- This *is* the test. Add a CI gate: `cargo test --test event_poll_parity` must pass on every PR touching `src/durable.rs` or `src/herdr.rs`.

## Considerations

- Flakiness risk: herdr event timing under load. Use generous latency bounds (500ms not 50ms) and retry-once semantics in the harness, documented.
- If parity *cannot* be achieved for some edge case, that's a real finding (the event path has a semantic bug) — don't weaken the test to pass; fix the path or document the divergence in ADR-0001 §6.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §6 (negative: event determinism), §10 (differential parity), §7 Phase 6, §11 (c).

Fixed concurrent EscalationTier cast so suite compiles. Live session not run.

title: A failed mail init is memoised forever, poisoning every later call in the process
description: mail_shim::init_mailbox uses MAILBOX.get_or_init(build_mailbox_once) and runtime() uses RUNTIME.get_or_init(...). OnceLock::get_or_init stores the Err PERMANENTLY, so a single failed build makes mail unavailable for the rest of the process even after the cause is gone. Measured consequence in the suite: register_spawned_agent_pins_unique_adjnoun_identity and register_spawned_agent_folds_slug_to_pin in wake_identity_tests go red roughly 1 run in 3 under the module filter and green 4/4 in isolation. Chain, each link verified: those tests set TORON_DATA_DIR, and pin_test_mail_root_set() only pins a per-process root when BOTH TORON_MCP_DATA_DIR and TORON_DATA_DIR are unset -- so whichever test reaches Mail::from_config first builds the process-global mailbox on ITS OWN temp dir; PINNED is then set and no later test is ever pinned; that test ends with remove_dir_all(&data), deleting the directory the global mailbox lives on; the next init_mailbox hits the missing dir, fails, and get_or_init memoises the Err permanently. Confirmed not the operator environment: with FLYWHEEL_MAIL=toron and XDG_STATE_HOME pinned the flake still reproduces 2 runs in 6. Confirmed not XDG_STATE_HOME: a test_state_home() fix on the two tests was tried, did not hold (still 3/8 red), and was reverted. Fix at the shared function every caller routes through: memoise only success, so a transient failure self-heals. Extract the memoisation into a helper that takes the cell so the test drives a FRESH OnceLock instead of the process-global one, and prove the test red by reverting get_or_try_init to get_or_init.
notes: SECOND PASS on the same bead, after the first was closed and the flake was NOT fixed. Cause found verbatim: 'mail error ... (code: 1) no such table: bus_events' and 'no such table: agents'. The mailbox is a process-wide singleton on a per-process SQLite store; whichever test first reaches Mail::from_config owns that store for every later test in the process, and its closing remove_dir_all pulled the dir out from under live pooled connections. Two changes shipped: (1) cleanup_test_data_dir skips the singleton's root, comparing against BUILT_ROOTS (the roots the singleton actually captured) -- an earlier version compared against a fresh mailbox_roots() and made the flake WORSE, 5-in-10 vs a 2-in-8 baseline, because by the time a later test asks TORON_DATA_DIR points elsewhere. (2) pinned_mail_identity no longer discards the backend error; that silent None is why three theories were dead before it. Measured: 6-in-8 red before, 10-in-12 after, 0-in-6 with --test-threads=1. STILL OPEN: the residual 2-in-12 is the same no-such-table family, so a deleter remains unidentified; all 5 remove_dir_all(&data) sites in wake_identity_tests are converted, so the next step is to find the sixth deleter or a non-delete path to an empty store.

title: toron: ack_overdue_only is a schema field nothing reads (silent no-op), and the SLA scan's ack count is recipient-blind
description:
Found while wiring flywheel's ack-overdue read (bd-mail-ack-sla-tracking subtask 4, commit fbcb340). Two upstream facts, both verified by reading the sibling repo at HEAD:

1. `ack_overdue_only` is declared in the MCP tool schema (`crates/toron-mcp/src/tools/mail.rs:432`, `FetchInboxArgs`) and listed in the conformance arg set, but NO code reads it — `rg ack_overdue_only crates/toron-mcp/src/` returns the declaration alone. The shared inbox filter (`crates/toron-core/src/mailbox/filter_inbox_messages`, mailbox/messaging.rs:212) applies `urgent_only` / `since_ts` / `thread_id` only. So the flag is a silent no-op on every path: exactly the c3b.3 class (a filter that looks applied and is not).

2. toron's own SLA scan (`Mailbox::check_ack_sla_expired`, mailbox/messaging.rs:961) decides "has this post been handled?" with `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM message_reads WHERE message_id = ?1` — no `recipient` predicate. `message_reads` is per (message, recipient) by design (migration 0002, whose own header explains why a shared read_ts on `messages` would leak one recipient's state to co-recipients), so on a to/cc fan-out one reader's receipt silences the overdue wake for every other recipient.

flywheel's side no longer depends on either: `Mail::ack_overdue` reads the row projection per recipient and `MailInboxFilter.ack_overdue_only` is a real post-filter (src/mail_shim.rs). The upstream fix belongs here: give the core filter an ack branch (or delete the arg so the schema stops advertising it) and add `AND r.recipient = ?` to the scan's ack check — note the scan's audience list comes from `to_list`, so the recipient set is already in hand.

Refs: AGENTS.md (toron is a sibling repo, plane P must not fake its state); docs/agent-instructions/backends.md (the in-process-only read); ~/.agents/skills/toron/SKILL.md (the fetch_inbox row now carries the caveat).

title: toron embed doors accept a blank project spelling (agents answers [] silently; send/inbox garble the error)
description:
## Symptom (probed live, flywheel blank-project sweep residual)

```
flywheel toron agents --project ""                  -> exit 0, []        (silent empty roster)
flywheel toron mail send --project "" ...           -> exit 1, "unknown recipient: B (register it in project  first)"   (double space)
flywheel toron mail inbox --project "" --agent A    -> exit 1, "agent A has no local key in project  ..."               (double space)
```

## Mechanism

`flywheel toron` embeds the in-process mailbox and passes the project slug straight through (`toron_embed::dispatch` -> `Mail*` doors). Unlike the CLI doors there is no `project_dir` join, so `""` does NOT alias onto the workspace root — instead:

- `agents` answers `[]` for the degenerate "" project: a silently authoritative-looking empty roster (a real roster one spelling away is invisible).
- `send`/`inbox` fail (good) but the actionable error interpolates the blank slug: `project  first`.

Sibling of bd-empty-project-silently-retargets-workspace-bkr3 (mail doors) and bd-blank-project-spelling-non-mail-doors-76hi (non-mail CLI doors); this is the embed's own surface.

## Fix shape

Guard in `cmd_toron` (src/cmd/toron.rs) before the embed dispatch: `Agents { project }`, `Mail { cmd: Send { project, .. } }`, `Mail { cmd: Inbox { project, .. } }` each run `crate::check_project_spelling(project, "toron <door>")`. One choke point, no embed-side changes, message shape matches the house convention.

title: toron-superlogical-stubs: Unsupported stubs reserve env names
description:
# toron-superlogical-stubs — reserve env names + `Unsupported` stubs for unreleased/future backends

## Background

`FLYWHEEL_BACKEND=superlogical|tmux` and `FLYWHEEL_MAIL=toron` are documented future selections (ADR-0002 §3.1). superlogical is unreleased; toron-core isn't shipped as an embeddable crate yet; tmux is on hold (toron ADR-0003). If a user sets these env values today, they must get a **clear, actionable error**, not a silent fallback to herdr/agentmail (which would hide misconfiguration) nor a compile error (which would require the feature to exist). This bead ships `Unsupported`-returning stubs behind the cargo features so the env names are reserved, the config contract is stable, and the error message guides the user. ADR-0002 §3.5.

Depends on `backend-traits-define` (trait to implement) + `cargo-feature-flags` (features to gate behind).

## Subtasks

1. `src/backend/superlogical.rs` (behind `#[cfg(feature = "backend-superlogical")]`): `SuperlogicalBackend` implementing `MultiplexerBackend` with every method returning `Err(BackendError::Unsupported { backend: "superlogical", reason: "not yet released (superlogical.com beta); set FLYWHEEL_BACKEND=herdr" })`. `name()` returns `"superlogical"` (so `list_backends` can enumerate it).
2. `src/backend/tmux.rs` (behind `backend-tmux`): `TmuxBackend` stub, mirroring toron ADR-0003's "tmux returns Unsupported until un-held". Same `Unsupported` pattern; reason references toron ADR-0003.
3. `src/backend/toron_mail.rs` (behind `mail-toron`): `ToronMailBackend` implementing `MailBackend`, every method `Unsupported { backend: "toron", reason: "toron-core not yet embedded; set FLYWHEEL_MAIL=agentmail (toron ADR-0003 R1)" }`. `name()` → `"toron"`.
4. A `BackendError` enum (in `src/backend/mod.rs`): `Unsupported { backend, reason }`, `NotCompiled { feature }`, plus a passthrough `Other(anyhow::Error)`. `Display` prints actionable copy.
5. `flywheel backend list` CLI subcommand: enumerates compiled-in backends (`name + status: ready|stub`), so a user can see what's available without reading Cargo.toml.

## Approach notes

- **Stubs return errors, never panic, never silently succeed.** A stub that returns `Ok(())` would hide that the backend isn't real. `Unsupported` is the honest signal.
- The stubs exist *so the env names are reserved* — a user reading `.env.example` or AGENTS.md sees `FLYWHEEL_BACKEND=superlogical` documented, sets it, and gets a clear "not yet released" message rather than a "no such backend" crash. This makes the config contract forward-stable.
- Mirror toron ADR-0003's tmux framing exactly ("returns Unsupported until un-held") so when toron-core ships its tmux impl, the semantics match.
- `BackendError::Unsupported` should include a link/hint to the relevant ADR (toron ADR-0003 / superlogical.com / this ADR-0002) in its `Display`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `FLYWHEEL_BACKEND=superlogical` (with the feature on) → every multiplexer call returns `Unsupported` with the "not yet released" message; `flywheel backend list` shows `superlogical: stub`.
- `FLYWHEEL_MAIL=toron` (feature on) → every mail call returns `Unsupported` with the "R1" message.
- With features off, the factory returns `NotCompiled` (actionable: which feature to enable).
- No stub ever returns `Ok` or panics.

## Test plan

- Unit: every stub method returns `Unsupported` (table-driven over all trait methods × all stubs).
- Unit: `flywheel backend list` output shape.
- The parity test (R0.8) excludes stubs (they can't pass parity — they're not real).

## Considerations

- Don't implement even partial superlogical/tmux/toron behavior — a half-stub is worse than a clean `Unsupported` (it implies capability that isn't there).
- When toron-core ships (R1), `ToronMailBackend` graduates from stub to real impl in-place (same file, same struct, real delegation) — the env name + feature are unchanged, so user config is stable.
- `flywheel backend list` is the user-facing discovery tool — keep its output clig.dev-disciplined (stdout=data/`--json`, stderr=messages).

## Reference
- ADR-0002 §3.5 (stubs), §11 Q1 (superlogical protocol unknown — stub must be extensible), §6 (no silent fallback).
- toron ADR-0003 §architecture layer 5 (tmux "returns Unsupported until un-held").

Committed 3f3af17 (surgical staging: 3 new stubs + factory.rs + mod.rs + beads; concurrent in-flight files untouched).

title: routing: there is no default-HARNESS concept, and a profile naming a concrete model with no harness can only fail
description:
THE GAP. resolve_profile_route bails when a profile carries a concrete (non-slot) model and an EMPTY harness, and there is no default-harness concept anywhere in the tree — a search for default_harness over src/ returns nothing but the unrelated slot-level fallback_harness, which is a different mechanism (it names which harness to TRY, and never hands one a model).

WHY IT IS NOT "JUST ADD A DEFAULT". Choosing a default harness IS the policy: whichever harness a bare profile lands on becomes the fleet's de facto default for every profile that omits one, silently, and there is no evidence about which one that should be. The current behaviour is a loud, explanatory bail on a genuinely unconfigured profile, which is the honest outcome. A default added here would replace a truthful failure with a plausible one — the same trade this session has been refusing throughout, in the direction that hides rather than reveals.

WHAT IS ALREADY DYNAMIC, so the gap is narrower than it looks. The model side now has a dynamic default (bd-ziy9), and the bare-harness spawn path has had one since bd-88m4 via coupled_default_model plus the harness's implied slot. A profile that names a SLOT and no harness therefore resolves on every Open-tier harness today. The only unrouted shape is a CONCRETE model plus no harness, which is arguably not a routing problem at all — it is a profile that has not said where it runs.

WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD. The bail now names both real fixes, and points at the slot form as the one that matches the dynamic-with-a-default shape, because a slot carries a harness AND a model together and both can then detour per harness.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD IS WAITING FOR. Either (a) a configured default harness in models.toml, consulted only when a profile names none AND its model is concrete, with the resolved harness recorded in the spawn ledger so the choice is visible; or (b) leave it a bail, on the grounds that a profile omitting its harness is a configuration error worth surfacing. (a) is a new config key, so it wants an ADR rather than a code change smuggled into a routing fix.

NOT DONE. No default harness, no new config surface, no test asserting a default exists. The bail is loud and both fixes are named.

title: doorbell autohost: persist the armed host set so a plain 'restart' keeps hosting and keeps launchd supervision
description:
The armed host set must be STATE, not argv. Today it exists only in the command line, which is why
a routine restart can silently stop every wake.

THE MECHANISM, re-confirmed live. `doorbell restart` builds its expected config from ITS OWN argv,
its own argv has no `--host`, it compares that against the installed launchd unit, finds a mismatch,
and falls back to "starting detached" — using its OWN hostless config rather than the unit's. Two
harms: no wakes are delivered (injection falls to 0/0/0) and launchd supervision is lost, so nothing
restarts the daemon if it dies. Reproduced four times on 2026-09-28. Tracked as bd-jbz1; this bead is
the fix.

Note the trap in "just add --host to the plist": I did that, reloaded launchd, confirmed the
supervised daemon came up hosted with degraded: [], and `restart` STILL produced standby. The plist
fix is necessary and not sufficient, which is why the fix has to be in the daemon's own config
resolution rather than in the unit file.

THE INVARIANT, which is the whole design:

    effective_hosts = persisted_hosts  merged-under  argv_hosts

Never argv alone. Concretely:
  - `start --host A --host B`  -> persist {A,B}, serve {A,B}
  - `start` (no --host)        -> serve the persisted set; do NOT silently become standby
  - `restart` (no --host)      -> restart with the SAME hosts. This is the case that is broken and
                                  the case everyone means when they type it.
  - `restart --host A`         -> re-arm to exactly {A}
  - `restart --unhost`         -> explicitly go standby and persist an EMPTY set, so standby is a
                                  decision that is recorded rather than an accident

That last one is the important half. Today the only way to reach standby is to omit `--host`, which
is also what a bug does. Making standby require an explicit verb means "no wakes are delivered"
becomes a state someone chose, and `doorbell status` can then say whether it was chosen.

WHERE THE STATE LIVES. `~/.local/state/doorbell/hosts.json`, written atomically (temp + rename —
the same discipline the journal rotation just gained in 92df8f2) on every successful arm, and read
by `start`/`restart`. It is per state-dir, so a test with its own state dir gets its own host set
and cannot inherit the operator's. That matters: a test that called `restart` with no args would
otherwise re-arm the live daemon's hosts.

THE UNIT MATCH, second. Once the effective config includes persisted hosts, the comparison against
the installed unit uses the EFFECTIVE config, so a plain `restart` matches the plist and keeps
launchd supervision. A genuine mismatch (different binary, different state dir) should still fall
back to detached — that fallback is correct — but it must then report the hosts it is serving, not
go quiet about them.

HONESTY, which is the part that makes this safe to operate. Every arm and re-arm prints the
EFFECTIVE set and where it came from:

    doorbell: armed on flywheel/flywheel-flywheel, opencode/flywheel-opencode,
              toron/flywheel-toron (3 from persisted state)

so "why is nobody waking up" is answerable from the log without reading the source. bd-jbz1's
failure mode was not that it was silent in the health output — `standby_with_known_workspaces` said
so — it was that `restart` itself printed "started" and exited 0 on the way there.

FENCE. bd-jbz1's verify is already written and already proven RED against the live bug:

    doorbell restart --host flywheel/flywheel-flywheel >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 6;
    doorbell status | assert mode == hosted and degraded == []

Extend it with the no-argument form, because that is the case that is actually broken:

    doorbell restart >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 6;
    doorbell status | assert mode == hosted and degraded == []
    launchctl list | grep com.doorbell.serve   # supervision survived
close_reason: The armed host set is now state, not argv: effective_hosts = persisted merged-under argv, applied in main.rs right after the state dir is known so one resolution covers both start and restart. hosts.json is per state dir, written temp-then-rename, and load() splits MISSING (a first arm, reads empty) from CORRUPT (an ERROR, never an empty set, because treating unreadable state as 'no hosts' would reproduce this bug one layer down silently). --unhost wins over both inputs, so standby becomes a recorded decision rather than an accident. THE ROOT CAUSE WAS NOT THIS BEAD: the mismatch was a BYTE comparison over a hand-editable unit file, and the installed unit had tab indentation while the template emits eight spaces, so restart reported a mismatch forever with every host correct — bd-jbz1 blamed the config and the config was fine. The comparison is now over the parsed argv, with serve_args the single source for both renderer and comparison. A host-only difference re-renders the unit and stays supervised instead of falling back to detached and leaving a stale unit that would re-host everything on next login; a different binary/state-dir/port/flywheel-state still falls back, pinned by its own test. Adopting is not arming, and warn_if_arm_diverges names the divergence on all three adopt sites — found live when a re-arm reported 3 workspaces hosted while hosts.json still read empty. Proven live in order: plain restart -> hosted+supervised (was standby); --unhost -> re-rendered, supervised, hosts.json empty; plain restart -> STILL STANDBY, so the decision persisted; re-arm -> hosted, clean, restored. Also fixed downstream: the installed toron resolved migration 13 against a store at 14 (migration 0014 came from my own bd-v51i), rebuilt from a clean worktree, clearing the last inbox_store_skew. Gate caveat recorded honestly: one earlier run showed 96/1 on stop_target_falls_back_to_the_live_health_owner, caused by restarting the live daemon during the suite, passing 5/5 and 3/3 on a quiet daemon.

title: Engine kind-aware fail_run + R-E lint (ADR-0024 Spec 1 shall-rules missing in control_flow)
description:
GS-pack verified: control_flow.rs has ZERO kind/retryable handling — run_step (~:394-405) and run_graph (~:801-817) abort any ok==false, so a rate_limit or timeout kills a fail_run step that Spec 1 says must retry the same node. FIX: (1) run_step + run_graph: on {ok:false} with kind in (rate_limit, timeout) under fail_run, retry the SAME node with backoff — honor retry_after_ms, else 1s x 2^(attempt-1) cap 60s — bound: enclosing Retry.max_attempts else 3 — then escalate (failed outcome carries disposition). auth/blocked/cancelled/unknown keep today's abort. (2) lint.rs: R-E1 retry-on-blocked/auth = error; R-E2 missing kind on fail_run step = warning; R-E3 spawn+fail_run without enclosing Retry = warning. (3) Tests: rate_limit same-node retry then success; bound exhausted escalates; R-E rows. Existing pins stay green (failure_kind_ok_false..., park test). Verify filter: kind_aware.

title: send_shutdowns is an unbounded await ahead of the bounded drain — SIGKILL lands mid-drain before the straggler note can print
description: Observed during the bd-pf3b load-test setup (2026-09-24 22:5x, QUIET machine): restart exit=0 elapsed=21s ≈ full 20s grace + boot, daemon log shows 'shutdown sent, joining loops' (line 1143) then NOTHING — no straggler note, no 'loops joined', no 'shutting down' — straight to the new daemon's boot (1145). Mechanism: send_shutdowns walks the 7 loop channels SERIALLY with tx.send().await and NO timeout; a brain mid run_cli (up to 15s CLI_TIMEOUT_SECS) or mid-backlog doesn't recv, the channel (BRAIN_CAP) fills, the send blocks, and the serial walk accumulates multiple such stalls. The 10s DRAIN_BUDGET only starts AFTER all sends return, so send-phase + drain > 20s grace → stop escalates SIGKILL mid-drain → the probe/verdict/note never runs. Complementary to bd-y40k executor-starvation and possibly the ORIGINAL restart-flakiness mechanism (bd-pf3b incident shape). Effect law: bound every wait — send_shutdowns must share the stop budget (timeout per send or overall, count unsent keys, report them as failed sends like bd-burk did for closed channels). Evidence: doorbell.log lines 1143-1145, restart elapsed 21s, two brains logged full exit chains (1130-1142) proving Shutdown was in flight while later sends stalled.
close_reason: done

title: sc_d1_live_kind9_channel_post_rings fails (watch --once times out) and it is in the CI slices shard
description:
Found while adding an unrelated e2e to the same file (bd-swad), and proved pre-existing: `git stash push -- crates/ src/ tests/` then `mbx test -p flywheel --all-features --test sc_doorbell_adr0005 sc_d1_live_kind9_channel_post_rings` fails identically at HEAD.

Symptom: the test's toron channel post succeeds (mentions + npub assertions all pass), then `toron watch --once --timeout-ms 15000` exits non-zero with stderr 'watch: timeout' and the assertion at tests/sc_doorbell_adr0005.rs:590 fires. ~38s per run, dominated by that timeout.

What I ruled out: it is not caused by my change (stash above); it is not the ambient TORON_MCP_URL gotcha — the first run printed toron's own warning ('TORON_MCP_URL and TORON_MCP_DATA_DIR are both set, and the DAEMON wins — the data-dir pin is being IGNORED'), so I re-ran with `env -u TORON_MCP_URL` and then with a minimal `env -i` (PATH + HOME only): it fails the same way with no TORON_* variable set at all.

So the pinned TORON_MCP_DATA_DIR is not where the watch looks, or the watch never sees the post. Two candidates, not distinguished here: (a) a toron-side regression in the watch path — the toron repo currently has red tests in crates/toron-cli/tests/cli_robot.rs from bd-qpm0, which is the same watch/robot surface; (b) this test needs a live toron daemon and the post/read split lands on different stores.

Why it matters even though it is not mine: sc_doorbell_adr0005 is one of the three files the CI 'slices' shard runs explicitly, so it is a red test inside a sharded gate, and the gate has been billing-dark since 2026-09-25 (bd-whie) — meaning nobody has seen this fail in CI and nobody will until billing is restored. A test that fails on a developer's machine is the cheapest place to catch it.

Next step for whoever takes it: run the same flow by hand (`toron channel post` then `toron watch --once --timeout-ms 15000` with TORON_MCP_DATA_DIR pinned and TORON_MCP_URL unset) on a host with no flywheel involved, and check whether the failure survives outside flywheel. If it does, it is toron's, and this bead becomes a pointer.
close_reason: done

comments.author: CopperWren
comments.text: DIAGNOSED at b91a595ee68e2e3aa1ee5c9631942dcdfeba6a44 — it is toron's socket DISCOVERY, not the store and not flywheel. wake_sock::discover_sock_path resolves $XDG_STATE_HOME/toron/wake.sock through toron_core::config::state_dir(), which reads only XDG_STATE_HOME/HOME and DELIBERATELY never consults TORON_MCP_DATA_DIR (producer and consumers share one derivation, ADR-0036 Spec 2). So on a host with a live 'toron serve' holding that socket (here pid 6344), a data-dir-pinned 'watch --once' attaches to the MACHINE daemon: the project filter matches nothing, the whole budget burns, and the socket branch returns 'watch: timeout' before the in-process replay over the pinned store is ever reached. Reproduced OUTSIDE flywheel (two agents registered in a temp store, kind-9 post verified present via 'channel read'), so flywheel is not involved. DECISIVE EXPERIMENT — same dir, same argv, only TORON_WAKE_SOCK differs: (a) ambient socket -> 15.0s, 'watch: timeout', exit 1; (b) TORON_WAKE_SOCK=<absent> -> the stored kind-9 line in 39ms, exit 0, and the loud line 'wake.sock absent ... degrading to in-process replay+live'. The tell is that the attach is INVISIBLE: 'watching kinds=9' is byte-identical on both paths; only the ABSENCE of the socket is loud. Instrumented phases on the fixed test: live_mailbox 10.1s, channel create+join 13.0s, channel post 6.4s, watch 0.04s — so the watch is now 39ms where it used to be the whole 15s budget, and the residue is CLI/migration startup on a loaded host, not the watch. FIX: toron_run pins TORON_WAKE_SOCK into the test's own data dir (no daemon there), which is the path these assertions were always written for.

title: Respawn agents stuck in `unknown` for N consecutive polls
description:
# Respawn agents stuck in `unknown` for N consecutive polls

## Background

After `bd-unknown-skip-dispatch`, unknown agents are ignored. But a persistently unknown agent is a dead pane — the swarm is permanently down one worker and the loop never settles (unknown is not a settled state), so `--work` mode hangs forever waiting for nothing. The docs treat unknown as classification uncertainty, not proof of death; the repair must therefore wait a grace period, then act.

## Why (justification)

The skip alone trades silent loss for a hung loop. A grace period distinguishes transient classification flicker (unknown → idle → unknown) from a genuinely dead session (unknown → unknown → unknown). Once the grace elapses, respawn is the same repair the loop already uses for context exhaustion and (per `bd-send-stall-escalation`) stalled sends — one repair primitive, three triggers.

## Technical approach

- `swarm_loop` keeps `unknown_seen: HashMap<String, u64>` (workflow-local; deterministic — reconstructable from checkpointed poll results, like `assigned` at durable.rs:360).
- Each poll: status == unknown → `count += 1`; any other status → remove from map (reset).
- Pure fn `unknown_decision(status, counts, threshold=2) -> UnknownAction { None | Respawn }`: Respawn when count reaches threshold; None otherwise (and the map maintenance is done by the caller).
- On Respawn: use the SHARED respawn helper from `bd-send-stall-escalation` (one respawn path in the workflow; both triggers must funnel through it so an agent can never be double-respawned in one iteration).
- Log event `reason=unknown-stuck` with the agent name and the count.
- Threshold constant: 2 consecutive polls. At the settled interval (300s) that is ~10 min before repair; with `bd-adaptive-interval` the cadence is active while the swarm is unsettled, so the repair typically fires within ~1 min. No coupling between the beads — document the interplay only.

## Success criteria

- An agent unknown for 2+ consecutive polls is respawned; a fresh instance appears under the same name.
- An agent that flickers unknown → idle → unknown is NEVER respawned (counter resets on idle).
- Exactly one respawn per stuck agent (shared helper).

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: `unknown_decision` transitions — count 0→1→2 (Respawn at 2), reset on idle, threshold boundary (2 = respawn, 1 = wait).
- Unit: integration-style test over a fake state sequence (unknown, unknown → one Respawn; unknown, idle, unknown → zero respawns) driving the workflow's per-poll logic via the pure fns.
- Manual e2e: kill an agent process in its pane; observe skip-dispatch for 2 polls, then respawn; log evidence for `bd-e2e-hardened-loop`.

## Dependencies

Depends on: `bd-unknown-skip-dispatch`. Uses the shared respawn helper agreed in `bd-send-stall-escalation`.

## Considerations

- Never respawn on a confirmed-working agent; the counter only advances on `unknown`.
- The threshold is a named constant, not magic: `UNKNOWN_RESPAWN_THRESHOLD: u64 = 2` with a doc comment explaining the tradeoff (transient flicker vs dead pane).
- Do not close the pane of a merely-unclassified agent — the respawn helper already splits a fresh pane BEFORE closing the old one (main.rs:2676-2686), which keeps the workspace alive; preserve that ordering.
close_reason:
Unknown-status repair implemented via the shared respawn helper. UNKNOWN_RESPAWN_THRESHOLD=2 const (doc'd tradeoff: flicker vs dead pane); pure unknown_decision(status,count,threshold) + per-poll driver track_unknown (unknown -> +1, any other status -> reset, respawn -> clean episode so exactly one respawn per stuck episode); workflow-local unknown_seen map rebuilt from checkpointed polls (deterministic replays). Respawn goes through respawn_and_requeue (now text: Option<&str> — unknown repair has nothing to requeue), logging EventKind::Respawn with reason=unknown-stuck and the count. Split-before-close pane ordering preserved.

97/97 tests (5 new: decision transitions/boundary, classified-status never fires, two-unknown sequence -> one respawn + episode reset, unknown->idle->unknown flicker -> zero respawns, per-agent independence).

E2E limitation (live-verified): on this herdr build a persistent per-agent 'unknown' status is NOT producible — SIGKILL/SIGSTOP of a running agent -> record dropped (ABSENT) in ~0.5s; freeze mid-launch -> (idle, launch_pending) then dropped; failed/timed-out agent start -> record cleaned up; the only unknown sighting is the ~0.5s launch window. Same class as bd-ojx's un-producible stalled verdict. Negative live e2e: real loop + real idle agent, queue t1..t3 -> 2 landed sends, zero respawn events, unknown branch silent. The decision->respawn wiring is unit/integration-tested per the bead's own test plan; the respawn machinery itself (respawn_and_requeue -> __respawn -> fresh pane + same-name agent) was live-proven in bd-send-stall-escalation-13b. Full live unknown e2e becomes possible once bd-read-state-fallback-zwa can classify agent state from response files (noted in handoff for that bead).

title: plan_actions: never dispatch work to `unknown` agents
description:
# plan_actions: never dispatch work to `unknown` agents

## Background

`plan_actions` (durable.rs:326-349) treats any non-working, non-blocked status as dispatchable: the catch-all arm `_ => { if !queue.is_empty() { Send } else if nudge { Nudge } else { Wait } }` covers idle, done, AND unknown. The herdr preview docs are explicit about `unknown`: "an agent is present but Herdr cannot classify its lifecycle confidently; it does not prove successful completion. Use exact `--until` states when that distinction matters."

## Why (justification)

Dispatching to an unclassified agent can deliver a prompt into a half-dead session (agent process exited, TUI crashed, detection failed, pane replaced). The queue item is consumed by an agent that may never execute it — silent loss, exactly what the epic forbids. Skipping one poll costs nothing (the loop already tolerates `Wait` actions); the swarm is only ever down one delegation, never down one queue item.

## Technical approach

- In `plan_actions` (durable.rs:326-349), match `"unknown"` EXPLICITLY → `LoopAction::Wait` (never pop the queue, never nudge). Keep the catch-all for idle/done.
- Update the fn doc comment to state the contract: unknown is not dispatchable, by design.
- Add a regression test: an unknown agent does NOT count toward "all settled" — the completion guard (durable.rs:540-546) already only matches `idle | done`, so an unknown agent keeps the loop alive. Assert it.

## Success criteria

- Unknown agents never receive queue items or nudges.
- Queue integrity: an unknown agent never consumes queue items.
- Unknown agent keeps the loop alive (completion guard regression test).

## Test plan (TDD — RED first)

- Unit: `unknown_agent_keeps_queue` — states=[unknown], queue=[p1] → queue still len 1, action is Wait.
- Unit: `unknown_with_nudge_no_send` — states=[unknown], queue=[], nudge=Some → Wait, no Nudge action.
- Unit: `unknown_not_settled` — states=[unknown], empty queue → `all_settled` false (loop does not complete).
- Manual: kill an agent process in its pane (status becomes unknown); poll with a non-empty queue → queue intact on the next poll.

## Considerations

- This bead is the SKIP half. The repair half (respawn after N consecutive unknowns) is `bd-unknown-respawn`.
- Do not conflate `done` with `unknown`: `done` is "idle after background work" (docs) and remains dispatchable.
- Interaction with `bd-adaptive-interval`: an unknown agent keeps the loop from settling, so the loop stays on the active cadence while a repair may be pending — correct and desirable.

## Project fit

"Never feed work to a session you cannot trust" — the second pillar of the epic's no-silent-loss guarantee.

LEDGER BINDING STOLEN BY PROSE — do not read this close as ledger-legal.

This bead was closed against c4031417a212ddc27f4c4c46adf6bc08f18f48d8, which is its real work commit. A LATER commit by another agent, 0a24bca (owner bd-s913's work), MENTIONS this bead id in its commit-message prose. 'flywheel ledger check' resolves a binding by taking the NEWEST commit whose message mentions the id, so the binding now resolves to 0a24bca instead.

Consequence, measured: 'flywheel ledger check bd-uona' reports 'no legal verdict bound to sha <thief>'. Note that this FAILS CLOSED. That is the correct behaviour for a hijacked binding and it is why this was not 'fixed' by recording a verdict against the thief commit: doing so would manufacture a green verdict about a revision that has nothing to do with this bead's close.

Why it was not repaired by rewriting the offending commit message: both offending commits are local and unpushed and both agents have finished, so a message-only amend plus a rebase is mechanically possible. I did not do it. A bind-by-grep is the wrong shape, and editing messages until a grep is satisfied treats the symptom; the fix belongs where the binding is resolved. See the filed bead for that.

Verified directly, not assumed: the real close commit c4031417a212ddc27f4c4c46adf6bc08f18f48d8 still exists and carries this bead's work; the close reason and the bead's own evidence are intact; only the MACHINE-READABLE BINDING is displaced.

title: Seed user config with builtin workflow/stage/compose-token copies + a drift detector
description:
Ask: user config should hold a copy of every builtin workflow/stage/compose-token so the operator can override or create custom ones without editing source.

The mechanism ALREADY WORKS and was proven live this session: "flywheel slot set premium --harness pi --model opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor" wrote a user overlay that overrode the compiled-in premium slot (omp/glm-5.3) and repointed every @premium profile (oracle/planner/reviewer) to pi/muse, with "flywheel slot remove premium" as the revert. That is exactly the override-without-source-edit property being asked for, applied to slots. This bead generalizes it to workflows + stages + compose tokens.

The hard part is NOT the copy; it is precedence + freshness. Copying without a drift detector just relocates staleness. Design must settle: (1) seed command (a "flywheel catalog seed"-style command that writes the user tier, never overwriting existing user copies); (2) precedence when a builtin improves and a user copy is stale (shadow + version pin, or user copy always wins?); (3) a drift detector that reports "this user copy is behind builtin X" the way the slot list already reports source=user vs compiled-in; (4) resolution stays ONE path so a user override and a builtin never disagree (the catalog already layers builtins < user < project for workflows — extend the same rule to stages/tokens). title: StageReport drops leaf detail, so a composed judgment's own verdict is unreachable
description:
Found live, not theorised. A caller that runs a composed Stage and reads report.detail gets a FLATTENED summary of id=signal pairs, not the leaf's verdict.

StageReport (src/stage.rs:145) has exactly id, placement, signal, detail. There is no children field. combine() (src/stage.rs:260) joins the child reports' own id=signal strings and REPLACES each child's detail. So a Stage::Compose whose leaf is a Stage::Jev loses the Jev verdict entirely: the label 'wedged: wedged=0.95 working=0.05' exists for microseconds inside read() and is then discarded.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A NOTE. A judgment whose label no caller can read is not a judgment. It is a silent-success shape identical to the one bd-7wah just closed, one layer up: a real answer computed, then thrown away, with a green signal reported. My own first live run of bd-hj53 did exactly this - it parsed the verdict 'health' out of 'health:has-counters=Holds, stuck-vs-busy:noul=Holds' and printed a confident, completely fictional answer. Only because the verdict field existed and read as nonsense did it get caught.

Note that unanswered_triage escaped this by running the Jev leaf DIRECTLY rather than the compose, which is why it worked. So today the safe pattern is 'know your stage shape and reach past the compose' - which is a trap for the next composed judgment, not a design.

THE FIX, if taken: add pub children: Vec<StageReport> to StageReport, have combine() return the reports alongside the combined signal, and have the Compose arm attach them. Callers then read a named leaf instead of parsing a string. That is a change to a shared type with many call sites, so it wants its own bead rather than being folded into a judgment's bead.

UNTIL THEN: assert on the leaf, not the compose, and pin that shape in a test. bd-hj53's test the_composed_detail_does_not_carry_the_verdict_so_the_leaf_must_be_run exists for this and will FAIL LOUDLY if the compose ever starts carrying the verdict, at which point the callers can be simplified.

NOT DONE. No fix attempted here. The bead is the finding.
close_reason: Done. Red-first proof, pure-core fix, workaround test simplified per its own instruction. prove-it-works — failed before, green after, 44 in blast radius. fix-root-causes — leaf verdict preserved, not re-fetched.

description: doorbell serve hands every retiring hosted loop its Shutdown by walking the table in order under a single shared deadline (send_shutdowns, SEND_BUDGET 2s). If the first loop's channel is full because its brain is mid-dispatch, that send parks until the deadline and EVERY key behind it is reported BudgetExhausted without ever being tried. drain_loops was already cured of exactly this head-of-line defect (bd-zzgb: joins race the budget concurrently, and the old note claimed '6 of 6' missed when the ones behind the hung one had already exited); the send walk kept it. Observed live on the 2026-09-28 restart: 'shutdown send FAILED (send budget exhausted)' for all three hosted workspaces, so all three brains died with the process instead of draining their sinks and journaling undelivered intents. Fix: race every send against the shared deadline with futures::future::join_all, so each loop gets the full budget independently, total wall time stays bounded by SEND_BUDGET (lifecycle::STOP_GRACE still covers it), and a key is BudgetExhausted only if its OWN send did not land.
close_reason: send_shutdowns races each loop Shutdown against the shared deadline (futures::future::join_all + timeout_at per key) instead of walking the table in order, so a full channel parks only its OWN key. Ran: mbx test -p doorbell-cli --bin doorbell (79 passed, 0 failed); red-first serve::tests::send_shutdowns_races_so_one_blocked_brain_cannot_starve_the_rest; bash scripts/verify-clippy.sh exit 0.

description:

A green working tree is not a green HEAD. The general rule: verify a gate against the COMMITTED state, not the state you happen to be holding.

Standing rule recorded in the commit: a bead id belongs to exactly ONE commit, the one that closes it. Root cause is that the ledger resolves identity by SEARCHING commit messages rather than by an explicit record, so any later mention silently takes the binding; bd-close-without-gate-row-sfz9 is the adjacent defect where a legal close can leave no row at all.

principles.decision: one gap, one count

title: the doorbell's gap counter fans out: one herdr status-stream gap is counted by every hosted workspace
description:
Measured on the live doorbell (2026-10-22, after the clean deploy): every hosted workspace's wake-brain counter moved by +1 in the same 75-second window - 19 workspaces at once, adrx2728 included (its real drop counter moved too, 826 -> 827). One upstream gap therefore reaches EVERY subscriber of the same herdr status ring.

What is known: the gap is the herdr socket's typed 'events_lost' frame ('subscriber fell behind'), surfaced by the toron herdr backend and counted by the doorbell's wake brain (note_events_lost). The recovery path clears coverage and re-reconciles from session.snapshot, so STATUS facts are recovered and no mail is lost - but the counter degrades /health the way a drop does, and the real drop on one workspace is not recovered.

What is not yet known: WHY the subscribers fall behind. The suspect is the shape - one subscription per hosted workspace over a shared bounded ring, each with its own sweep cadence - so a burst outruns every subscriber at once. The fix belongs where the ring is read (flywheel's doorbell host) or where it is written (herdr), not in the counter: the counter is honest, the loss is not.

Done means: a gap on one ring is not counted by every subscriber that reads it, the /health degradation reflects a real loss, and the test goes red when the fix is inverted.
close_reason: The herdr subscription path treated a gap as the end of the stream: the reader thread broke on the typed events_lost error (the socket is still open - toron-core's read_event returns a typed error and leaves the reader on the stream) and the forwarder cleared its coverage, reconciled and exited so the next sweep re-subscribed. That cost a socket per gap (the daemon reclaims the old subscriber's socket only on its next heartbeat write, so its socket count grew at gap-rate x heartbeat-interval, and at 256 fds its accept loop spins on EMFILE and the MCP plane stops accepting - the guard's roster read, toron mail send and toron reserve acquire all failed against 127.0.0.1:18080) and it made a gap beget a gap (the fresh subscriber starts with no position on the ring, so it is behind the bounded ring and is told events_lost again - one upstream gap fanning out into a gap and a socket per subscriber, which is why 19 hosted workspaces' counters moved in the same 75s window). The fix is at the source, not in the counter: a gap is delivered IN BAND and the stream keeps reading, and the forwarder reconciles the status facts and KEEPS its subscription. Verified by a_gap_is_delivered_in_band_and_the_stream_keeps_reading (red when the fix is inverted) and a CLEAN EXPORT of this commit (git archive HEAD of flywheel and toron into a scratch dir, build and test THERE): 2507 passed, 0 failed, 6 ignored. fix-root-causes - the fatal gap handling, not the counter, was the defect. prove-it-works - the test goes red when the fix is inverted. Residual: crates/doorbell-rt/src/wake_sock.rs does not move the client's resume cursor past a gap (the shed path overwrites it, so the change was unobservable and unprovable); the daemon-side half of the fd ceiling is the toron crew's lane (bd-j2vo). The one red in the clean export, tests/adr0027_slice1::adr0027_s1_toron_send_flags_exist, fails identically in the working tree: toron's CLI no longer exposes --priority/--audience, which is the toron lane's change.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text: MEASURED 2026-10-22 (captain): the fan-out is the fd leak's SOURCE, so this one fix covers three symptoms. The gap counter moved +1 across 19 workspaces in the same 75s window, and the daemon's wake sockets grew 44 -> 61 in 100s (~10/min, matching the gap rate). Every gap makes the doorbell's forwarder exit and the sweep re-subscribe, and the daemon's old subscriber socket is not reclaimed until its next heartbeat write (~30s), so the count grows at (gap rate x heartbeat interval). At 256 fds the daemon's accept loop fails with EMFILE, the MCP plane stops accepting, and toron mail send / toron reserve acquire / the guard's roster read all fail against 127.0.0.1:18080 - the daemon wedged again at 04:27Z today with 266 fds (229 of them wake.sock). So: fix the fan-out and the daemon survives; the fd ceiling is the amplifier, not the cause.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text: mold correction (2026-10-03): the bead says a linker swap 'needs an install'. mold 2.42.1 is now installed via Homebrew and MEASURED UNUSABLE on this platform, so this is not a pending install any more. Three measured facts: (1) Apple clang rejects '-fuse-ld=mold' AND '-fuse-ld=ld.mold' by name with 'invalid linker name'; (2) given a full path ('-fuse-ld=/opt/homebrew/bin/ld.mold') clang does launch mold, but mold then fatals on the ld64 flags clang injects -- first '-no_deduplicate', and behind that '-dynamic'; (3) mold states the root cause itself: 'mold does not support macOS'. Homebrew's mold is the Linux/ELF build; its Mach-O support is not in the bottle, and 2.42.1 is the current stable release so there is no newer upstream to wait for. A wrapper that strips the flags was tried and is the wrong fix: stripping -dynamic and friends strips link semantics, not just spelling. Conclusion: the macOS linker lever is closed unless Homebrew LLVM's ld64.lld is installed instead (Apple clang accepts -fuse-ld=lld by name); that is the only remaining route and it was left alone pending the operator's call. Also recorded: '-B/opt/homebrew/bin -fuse-ld=ld' LOOKS like it works and silently uses Apple ld64, because /opt/homebrew/bin contains only ld.mold and no ld -- a measurement trap worth naming.

title: Swarm registry write failure: panes created but list/send read an empty registry
description:
# Swarm registry write failure: panes created but list/send read an empty registry

## Problem (live e2e, 2026-08-09)

During a crew dispatch, an agent ran `flywheel spawn toron-review --oc 2 --label "ADR-0008-debate"` (wrong project name). The failure surfaced as:

```
Flywheel swarm registry write failed
(spawn made herdr panes but list/send read a registry that's empty).
Driving opencode panes directly via herdr.
```

Root cause chain (from herdr 0.8.0-preview strings + flywheel behavior):
1. herdr persists the swarm/session registry to `session.json`; on a read failure it prints `failed to read session file` / `failed to parse session file, ignoring` and starts with an EMPTY registry.
2. A spawn that created panes while the registry write/read failed leaves the panes LIVE in herdr but INVISIBLE to `flywheel list` / `send` / `status` (which query the registry).
3. flywheel does not verify post-spawn that the workspace it just created is actually visible to list/send — the spawn "succeeds", then every subsequent command sees nothing.
4. The wrong project name (`toron-review` vs `toron`) is a skills/command-usage issue — the agent invented a project; flywheel's spawn either did not validate the project dir or the error was not surfaced loudly enough.

## Fixes proposed

### A. flywheel spawn: post-spawn visibility verification (primary)
After creating the workspace + agents, verify the new workspace appears in `workspace.list` (or `agent.list`) from the same client view list/send will use. If it does NOT:
- Fail with a LOUD error naming the registry path, the workspace id, and exact recovery steps (restart herdr: `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.herdr...` or `herdr restart`; or `HERDR_SESSION` path check).
- Do NOT silently succeed (current behavior). Consider a `--no-verify` escape hatch for scripts.

### B. flywheel spawn: project-dir validation BEFORE creating panes
- Validate the project dir exists (and is initialized: has .beads/ or is a git repo) BEFORE any herdr workspace/pane is created. `flywheel spawn nonexistent-project` must exit non-zero with "project dir missing: X (run: flywheel init X)" and NO side effects.
- This turns the wrong-command case into a fast, safe failure — the agent's `toron-review` mistake becomes a clear error naming the real projects available (suggest `flywheel list` / the project dirs).

### C. Label validation (the ADR-0008-debate case)
- Decide + enforce a slug convention: labels are used in workspace metadata; hyphenated/uppercase labels (ADR-0008-debate) should either be normalized (lowercase, hyphens allowed) or rejected with guidance. Document the convention in the spawn help + the flywheel skill.

### D. Skills/template hardening (the command-usage half)
- The flywheel skill + beads templates should state the spawn contract explicitly: `flywheel spawn <project> --oc N` where <project> is the DIRECTORY NAME in ~/workspace (toron, flywheel, hachiko...), never an invented name; label is optional + slug-safe. A one-line "common mistakes" note (wrong project name; --oc with space vs =; hyphenated labels).
- This is the agent-facing fix; A-C are the code guard rails that make the mistake cheap.

## Success criteria

1. `flywheel spawn nonexistent-project --oc 2` exits non-zero, creates ZERO panes, and prints a message naming the valid projects (or the init command).
2. After a spawn, `flywheel list` ALWAYS shows the new workspace, or spawn fails loudly with recovery steps (never silent success + empty registry).
3. `--label ADR-0008-debate` is either normalized to a slug or rejected with the convention explained.
4. Unit tests: spawn validation (project exists), label normalization, post-spawn visibility check (mock/real herdr).
5. e2e T2/T3 (bd-i8x) pass against this fix.
6. Full `cargo test` green; no regression on the happy-path spawn.

## Considerations

- The registry read is herdr-side (session.json). flywheel cannot fix herdr's silent-ignore, but it CAN verify what list/send will see and fail loudly — that is the contract flywheel owns.
- The post-spawn check should be cheap (one workspace.list call) and must not add a race: verify the workspace_id returned by spawn is present, not just "any workspace".
- Coordinate with bd-a7j (reply-verification) and bd-i8x (e2e confirmation) — the T2/T3 tests there are this bead's acceptance tests.
- Skills edits live outside the repo (~/.agents/skills/flywheel/SKILL.md + integrations/*.tpl) — the code guard rails are the committed deliverable; the skill note is the companion.
close_reason: A: post-spawn visibility check (workspace.list contains the exact created ws id; loud failure with herdr-restart recovery steps; --no-verify escape). B: project-dir validated before any pane (exit 1, zero panes, lists available projects). C: --label slug-normalized (ADR-0008-debate -> adr-0008-debate, warning, empty rejected) + meta fallback so project commands still resolve custom-label swarms. D: skill spawn contract note. Unit tests: slugify_label_normalizes (+ spawn_registry_roundtrip earlier). Live-verified all three code paths on scratch swarms. Suite green; clippy clean.

title: blocked status not producible via __send on this herdr build
description:
## Background

The e2e gate (bd-e2e-hardened-loop) scenario 4 drives an agent into herdr blocked (approval prompt) via __send prompts to verify the --on-blocked mail latency bound. On this build (herdr 0.7.5-preview), opencode agents auto-approve/execute ordinary prompts — none of the tested prompts (rm -rf /nonexistent, sudo -n true, etc.) produced an approval gate; the agent stayed working/idle.

## Why

The blocked-alert path (on-blocked mail within ~2x active interval) is unit-tested (next_interval_secs treats blocked as active) and wired (notify_blocked leaf), but never e2e-verified. A real blocked signal is the one herdr state this project cannot yet produce deterministically.

## Technical approach

- Try driving blocked via herdr agent send-keys into an opencode permission prompt, or a restricted-mode agent config (deny bash + request approval), or herdr's own blocked simulation if any (check herdr api schema for a state-forcing method).
- Alternatively verify the mail path end-to-end with a FAKE blocked: register the scratch project in agent-mail, then invoke __mail-blocked directly and assert delivery (the latency bound itself is already unit-covered).
close_reason: Discovery documented: herdr 0.7.5-preview cannot be driven into blocked via __send prompts (opencode auto-approves; rm/sudo prompts verified). The blocked-alert latency bound is unit-tested (next_interval_secs treats blocked as active) and the mail path is wired (notify_blocked leaf). The e2e gate (9qa) scenario 4 records this as its single FAIL with the precise reproduction; the gate script remains the runbook — when blocked becomes producible (or the __mail-blocked direct verification lands), scenario 4 flips green.

title: pi agents spawn nameless: name-based resolution fails until manual rename
description:
## Background

`flywheel spawn --pi 1` calls herdr agent.start with a name (`flywheel-<project>-pi`), but the resulting agent record frequently has NO name field (herdr's pi integration does not register the name — unlike opencode agents which carry it). Name-based resolution then fails:

- `flywheel __send <project> <name>` -> 'agent not found'
- `--to pi` / resolve_agents matching by name -> no match
- the durable loop's `agent_target` falls back to the PANE ID, which breaks `read_output`/poll_kind lookups (the pane-id name does not resolve either)

Observed live during bd-send-stall-escalation e2e: the w18 pi agent came up nameless; the loop's CONTEXT_LIMIT guard then called poll_kind with the pane-id fallback name and crashed ('__kind failed: agent w18:p1 not found'). Renaming manually (`herdr agent rename <pane> <name>`) fixes it, and sometimes a fresh spawn registers the name correctly (w19 did) — the behavior is inconsistent.

## Why

The loop targets agents by name everywhere. A nameless agent makes the swarm unusable (send/status/loop all fail or misbehave).

## Technical approach

title: wait-output-usage: use wait-output for send-receipt + stall detection
description:
# `__wait-output` leaf + documented recipe

## Background

`bd-pane-wait-output-helper` adds the client method. This bead exposes it as a hidden leaf (consistent with the `__*` leaf pattern: shell-out boundary so the blocking client never runs on the async executor, durable.rs:9-11) and documents the recipe — docs-first discipline: usage guides the design.

## Why (justification)

The primitive is only useful if reachable from automation and understood. A hidden leaf keeps the automation surface uniform (`__poll`/`__send`/`__wait-output`), and the README recipe teaches the pane-vs-agent distinction the docs emphasize.

## Technical approach

- Hidden subcommand `__wait-output <project> <agent-or-pane> <pattern> [--regex] [--timeout-ms N]`:
  - Resolve the target to a pane id (agent name → `agent.list` lookup, same as `__send` main.rs:2558-2562; or accept a raw pane id).
  - Call `pane_wait_output`; print JSON `{"matched": bool, "matched_line": ..., "pane_id": ...}`; exit 1 on timeout / agent-not-found.
- README automation section: recipe "block on a test run" — `pane run` the test watcher, then `__wait-output --regex "passed|failed"`; plus the docs' caveat: use `agent wait` when you need LIFECYCLE semantics, `__wait-output` for raw output.
- Do NOT add a new workflow-step type (`run_workflow`/`run_pipeline`, main.rs:1785-1834) in this bead — note it as a future option in a comment; avoid scope creep.

## Success criteria

- Leaf works end-to-end (match + timeout paths); README recipe present and accurate.

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: argv/params building pure fn (agent-name vs pane-id resolution, --regex flag, timeout) + JSON shape.
- Manual: follow the README recipe in a scratch workspace; verify match and timeout paths; log evidence.

## Dependencies

Depends on: `bd-pane-wait-output-helper`.

## Considerations

- Hidden leaf discipline: never invoke `__*` commands from interactive workflows; the durable workflow does not use this leaf yet (it is for scripts/automation) — that is fine; the recipe is the contract.
- Keep the output machine-parseable (`--json`-style single object); stderr for messages.
- The pane/agent target resolution must reuse the existing helpers (`resolve_agents`/`agent_target` in main.rs) — no duplicate lookup logic.
close_reason:
Hidden __wait-output leaf wired to the pane-wait-output helper (efq). cmd_internal_wait_output: target resolution via pure resolve_pane_id (agent name -> pane from the project's ws-filtered agent list; raw pane id accepted; unknown -> matched:false + exit 1), wait_output_mode maps --regex to herdr's regex mode (literal substring is the leaf's "match" -> client maps to "substring"), pane_wait_output call with optional timeout; stdout {"matched", "matched_line", "pane_id"} on every path, exit 0 on match, 1 on timeout/unknown (stderr messages). The 4 efq #[allow(dead_code)] markers removed (helpers now wired). No workflow-step type added — noted as a future option in a comment (scope discipline per the bead).

README "Durable backend" gains the recipe: herdr pane run a test watcher, then __wait-output --regex 'passed|failed'; caveat: __wait-output waits on raw pane OUTPUT, herdr agent wait for lifecycle semantics. Clarified that raw panes must live in the swarm's workspace (the leaf resolves the project's workspace first).

128/128 tests (6 new: resolve_pane_id name/raw/unknown, wait_output_mode, JSON shape incl. null matched_line, PaneWaitResult rendering).

Live e2e (scratch oc swarm + split pane): match on raw pane (TEST-MARKER-READY, exit 0, matched_line from the pane), timeout path (matched:false + stderr + exit 1), agent-name positive match (matched_line from the agent's pane), agent-name resolution to the right pane, unknown target (matched:false + exit 1).

title: Wake banners cite ids the toron daemon never registered (id-vocabulary drift)
description:
# Wake banners cite ids the toron daemon never registered (id-vocabulary drift)

Repro (2026-08-21, SandySparrow session, 13+ consecutive wakes):

- Banner repeatedly cited "Most recent urgent: id c43357a1… / thread 9844e931…" ([request-release] crates/toron-cli/**) against a read-empty inbox (0 unread, 0 rows <15min old).
- The request was answered hours earlier: `toron_reply_message` with `release_decision=agreed` + `request_message_id=c43357a1…` accepted, delivery event d4172200 to TealDune confirmed.
- Re-keying the response on the thread/reservation id failed: daemon returns "no request-release message with id 9844e931… addressed to SandySparrow" — i.e. the banner's cited id was NEVER a registered request id. Only the rumor id registers.
- One wake also surfaced under the WRONG PIN (TealDune), citing TealDune's inbox row of my own reply — see bd-captain-alias-0g8a for the alias class.

Root cause hypothesis: flywheel's wake banner generation and toron's request-release state machine use different id vocabularies (reservation/thread id vs rumor event id), so a responded request can never be recognized as terminal by whatever emits the banner.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every id a wake banner cites resolves through the mail surface before emission (unresolvable ids are dropped, not printed)
- [ ] A request-release that has received a release_decision response never re-fires a wake
- [ ] Contract test: respond to a synthetic request-release, assert zero subsequent wake emissions cite it

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test -p flywheel --bin flywheel -- --test-threads=1
```

Shipped: toron 14878ce + flywheel a5e616b.

Clause 2 (never re-fires): respond_request_release now records the responder's READ receipt on the request rumor (toron-core, best-effort after the decision DM). The bd-dbre wake filter (read rows do not wake) then drops the decided request permanently — CONTRACT TEST: synthetic request-release; pre-response the request is an unread urgent row in the holder's projection (wake candidate); post-response zero wake-citing rows remain.

Clause 1 (cited ids resolve): urgent_wake_prompt gates both citations through citable_wake_id — non-empty hex event id only. Reservation paths, thread labels, npubs, placeholders are dropped from the banner (wake still fires; no phantom reply key). Tests: unresolvable-ids-dropped (the exact repro shape: reservation-30078 / thread-9844e931), resolvable-hex-kept, id table. Existing fixtures moved to hex handles.

title: RestartWatch journaling is one row per Died MESSAGE, so watch_restart_loop counts deaths not restarts
description:
FOUND 2026-09-28 while deploying the alive fix. Two measurements of the SAME workspace over the SAME window disagree by ~40x, and the health signal is driven by the wrong one.

  journal doorbell-journal-flywheel-flywheel.jsonl: 1412 RestartWatch rows with ts inside a 300s window
  audit   flywheel-flywheel.audit.jsonl, same 600s: 35 "watch" rows (one real watch cycle per ~17s), 20 wake_consumer_dropped

MECHANISM (read, not guessed): brain.rs on_died() journals exactly ONE row per BrainMsg::Died it dispatches, and journal() derives actions from the effects, so the row actions are ["RestartWatch"]. doorbell-core tick maps DoorbellMsg::WatchDied -> DoorbellAction::RestartWatch, and doorbell-rt/host.rs maps BrainMsg::Died -> DoorbellMsg::WatchDied. So RestartWatch rows == Died messages, NOT restarts. There is exactly one Died sender (msg.rs deliver_died_blocking, GS062-ADV-5). Meanwhile the audit DEDUPES a repeated absence to one row per outage (file_host.rs absent_rows, bd-lorot), which is why the audit looks calm while the journal does not.

CONSEQUENCE: serve.rs health_body counts the string "RestartWatch" in the journal (tailprobe::count_matches_within_across) and degrades above WATCH_RESTARTS_ALLOWED_PER_WS (6) x hosted workspaces. So watch_restart_loop fires on a flux of Died messages and cannot distinguish (a) a real restart storm from (b) a consumer dying repeatedly without ever being respawned, or (c) a burst from a steady loop. The number a reader sees is not the thing the name says.

SEPARATE, ALSO OPEN, AND I DID NOT FIX IT: a real burst hit this workspace at 02:55-02:58Z (171 / 50 / 727 / 631 rows per UTC minute, ~12 per second at the peak, then dead). The daemon stayed calm throughout (3.1% CPU, 40 MB RSS), so it is not a spin. With single-flight in restart_wake (file_host.rs) collapsing scheduled restarts, a 12/s Died rate needs ~12 concurrent or rapid-fire consumers, and I could not derive that from reading. DO NOT FIX BLIND: reproduce it first, because the previous fix in this area was the missing single-flight guard and its absence was only visible from a live rate.

VERIFY: a test that pins the metric to restarts (a counter incremented where a restart is actually performed) and fails on a window containing Died rows but no restarts.
close_reason: done

title: ADR-0013 Wave C remainder: resolve the profile half of 'one routing source' (decide or retire)
description:
ADR-0013 P0-5 / ADR-0032 Spec 9 remainder.

WHAT LANDED (5bdc903 code, 417c318 docs): the routing table is now the one source for a primitive's trigger — decide_trigger_for derives matchers[0] and the duplicate 32-arm match is deleted; UNROUTED_PRIMITIVES is the single 'not routed' declaration; load is loud (check_catalog, check_workflow_routes) and the decide CLI cross-checks the merged workflow catalog. See src/decide.rs and the decide_router_* tests.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN — the 'profiles' half of ADR-0013 §7's Wave C line. The table carries decide_trigger / matcher / primitive / argv / topology, but NOT the profile/role affinity a route dispatches to. RouteArgv::WorkflowRun names a workflow; the @role lives in that workflow's steps and in stages.rs seed role affinities. So 'flywheel decide' cannot say which profile a route will run as, and nothing answers 'what does this primitive run as?' in one place.

TWO ACCEPTED SHAPES — pick one, do not split the difference:
(a) ADD the affinity: a route row (or the one catalog) carries the profile role a primitive dispatches to, READ from the workflow's steps rather than re-declared, with a loud load check that the named role exists in the profile catalog. Acceptance: flywheel decide --json (and briefing) name the role and a table-wide test pins it.
(b) RETIRE the framing: ADR-0013 §7's 'profiles + workflow matchers' wording is out of scope for Spec 9, which scopes the table to flywheel-owned routing metadata and says it is not added to toron-workflow::Workflow. Write the rationale into ADR-0013 §6/§7, leave P0-5 CHANGED with the profile half explicitly out of scope, and keep verify-0013.sh green.

WHY NOT A ONE-LINER: profile.rs is a runtime-tiered catalog (compiled-ins < profiles.toml) keyed by role, while ROUTING_TABLE is a compiled constant keyed by matcher. Shape (a) must not re-introduce a second truth — the role must be derived from workflow/stage data, never re-typed into a routing row.

NOT IN SCOPE: portable ProfileDef codec (P2-11) and dead_code / profile-CLI cleanup (P2-14) — those stay their own items.
close_reason: P0-5 folded as option (a): affinity READ from workflow steps via decide::workflow_role_from_steps, gated by check_profile_routes, proven by decide_router_profile_affinity (15/15 router tests green). Commit 9f50c92. PRINCIPLES: model-the-domain — affinity derived from steps, never re-declared; prove-it-works — table test pins real catalog

title: wave gating: read br's typed wave field; retire the label path
description:
Observed on a live project, 2026-10-03.

Evidence:
- br's typed `--wave N` field natively holds every wave>=1 bead until all lower
  waves close; `br ready` returned exactly one bead at a time as waves
  advanced. This worked perfectly and was discovered empirically.
- flywheel's wave-gate stage duplicates the logic label-based ("intersect br
  ready with the wave label; hold on any lower open wave") and wrote
  `.flywheel/wave/wave-1-ready.json` with `ready: []` mid-wave, a snapshot the
  dispatch stage reads.
- The br skill still documents the label path as "transitional until schema-18
  ships the typed wave field"; schema-18 has shipped.

Wish:
1. flywheel's gate reads the typed wave field (no label intersection), and the
   gate artifact is regenerated at dispatch time (or dispatch reads br ready
   live).
2. An empty ready set while in-flight beads exist is "gate passes, work in
   flight", not a held/empty wave.
3. br skill updated: typed field is the authority; labels are legacy.

Acceptance: `cargo test -p flywheel wave_gate_reads_typed_field`.
close_reason: Wave gating now reads br's typed `wave` field as the authority (schema-18): ReadyBead carries `wave` from all three br JSON parsers, bead_wave is typed-first with the legacy wave-N label as fallback (a stale label can never overrule the tracker), --wave-label scopes by the same rule, and progress groups by it. The wave-swarm chain carries the refined semantics: GATE writes in_flight[] and treats an empty ready with in-flight beads as WORK IN FLIGHT (held:false, marker written, no re-dispatch) while a truly empty wave stays the loud bd-mvy4 failure; DISPATCH re-reads br ready live instead of trusting the artifact snapshot; EXECUTE waits out in-flight closes and refuses to green a wave that ran nothing. Live evidence: in a scratch tracker br ready returned only the wave-1 bead, then [] while wave 1 was in_progress — br's native hold. VERIFY: mbx +nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin test -p flywheel wave_gate_reads_typed_field -> ok (1 passed). Evidence: 9 new tests across durable/main/stages, each mutation-proven red (typed read dropped; ready-parser wave dropped; WORK IN FLIGHT deleted) then re-greened; full suite 2673 passed / 0 failed; clippy exit 0; fmt applied. PRINCIPLES: prove-it-works — the authority claim was measured in a live scratch tracker and every gate claim is pinned by a mutation-proven test before the label path was touched; subtract-before-you-add — the gate stops re-deriving what br already enforces natively, and the label survives only as a fallback; boundary-discipline — the typed field is parsed once at the JSON boundary into ReadyBead and every consumer reads the one decision function.
